title: feat: generic Nango OAuth integration flow (Google Calendar first)
body:
# feat: Generic Nango OAuth integration flow (Google Calendar first)


Implements the OAuth connect flow for Nango-based calendar integrations, starting with Google Calendar. The flow is designed to be **provider-agnostic** — adding Outlook or another Nango integration requires only a config entry in `shared.tsx` and optionally a display entry in the web integration page, with no new components or routes needed.

Users can initiate a Google Calendar connection from desktop **Settings → Calendar** or **Onboarding**, complete OAuth via the web app's Nango Connect UI, and return to the desktop app via deeplink. Connection status is fetched from the API and displayed inline.

**Backend (Rust):**
- Separated integration routes (`/nango/*`, `/calendar/*`) from `pro_routes` into their own `integration_routes` group with basic auth (no PRO entitlement required)
- Added `GET /nango/connections` endpoint that lists **all** active connections for the authenticated user via Supabase PostgREST with RLS — no `integration_id` parameter required
- Shared `NangoConnectionRow` struct in `supabase.rs` replaces one-off `Row` structs in `status.rs` and `extractor.rs`
- Extended `SupabaseClient` with `anon_query()` for user-scoped RLS queries using the caller's JWT
- `SupabaseClient::new()` now requires `supabase_anon_key` parameter
- `create_connect_session` forwards caller's email, sets `end_user_id` / `end_user_email` connection tags per [Nango best practices](https://nango.dev/docs/implementation-guides/platform/auth/connection-tags). `allowed_integrations` is unscoped (`None`) — the web flow scopes per-integration via the `allowedIntegrations` param
- Fixed `#[serde(default)]` on `NangoConnectionRow::updated_at` to prevent deserialization failures when PostgREST omits the field

**Web (TypeScript):**
- `/_view/app/integration.tsx` accepts `integration_id` as a search param (defaults to `google-calendar`), with a display config map (`INTEGRATION_DISPLAY`) for provider-specific UI copy. No provider-specific code in the component itself.
- `/_view/callback/integration.tsx` handles post-OAuth redirect generically with typed deeplink construction (`buildDeeplinkUrl` + `IntegrationDeeplinkParams`)
- `nangoCreateConnectSession` server function validates the user server-side via `getSupabaseServerClient().auth.getUser()` — no longer trusts client-provided `userId`/`userEmail`

**Desktop (TypeScript):**
- Added `nangoIntegrationId` field to `CalendarProvider` type — each provider declares its Nango integration ID (Apple has none since it's native)
- Generic `OAuthProviderCard` component (`oauth.tsx`) for settings — takes provider config as prop, replaces the old Google-specific card
- Generic `OAuthCalendarConnect` component for onboarding — parameterized by provider config
- `configure/index.tsx` routes to `OAuthProviderCard` for any provider with a `nangoIntegrationId`, eliminating per-provider if/else chains
- Added `/integration/callback` deeplink type in `deeplink2` plugin (Rust types + generated JS bindings)
- `useDeeplinkHandler` handles the new deeplink generically — invalidates `["integration-status"]` query cache on success
- **New `useConnections` hook**: Calls `listConnections` from the generated api-client, returns all connections for the authenticated user. Used by both settings and onboarding to show connection status.
- **Connection status UI**: Both `OAuthProviderCard` (settings) and `OAuthCalendarConnect` (onboarding) now display connection state — "Connected" badge when connected, "Reconnect" vs "Connect" button text, different button styling (gray for reconnect, black for initial connect)
- Enabled Google Calendar provider in settings (`shared.tsx`: `disabled: false`, badge: "Beta")
- Google Calendar is now shown in onboarding on all platforms (not just settings)
- `buildWebAppUrl` helper now accepts optional `params` for passing `integration_id` and other query params

- **Replaced per-integration status endpoint with list-all**: Changed from `GET /nango/connection-status?integration_id=X` (single connection) to `GET /nango/connections` (list all connections). The UI no longer needs to know which integrations to check — one call returns everything.
- **Wired up connection status display**: Created `useConnections` hook that calls the generated `listConnections` client function. Both settings (`OAuthProviderCard`) and onboarding (`OAuthCalendarConnect`) now show connection state inline — "Connected" badge, "Reconnect" button when already connected.
- **Google Calendar back in onboarding**: The onboarding calendar step now shows Google Calendar (with OAuth connect) on all platforms, not just Apple Calendar on macOS. Connection status is displayed if the user has already connected.
- **Shared `NangoConnectionRow` type**: Extracted shared struct in `supabase.rs` to replace one-off `Row` structs in `status.rs` and `extractor.rs`. Includes `integration_id` field with `#[serde(default)]`.
- **`allowed_integrations: None`**: The `create_connect_session` endpoint no longer restricts which integrations can be connected (was hardcoded to `["google-calendar"]`). The web flow scopes per-integration via the `allowedIntegrations` param.
- Previous: Generic integration flow, parameterized web integration page, Rust endpoint unscoped, server-side auth for Nango sessions, type-safe URL construction, typed navigation, connection tags, error handling, lazy Nango SDK init


- [ ] **CRITICAL: `useConnections` hook wiring**: The `useConnections` hook was created following the pattern from `billing.tsx` but was not tested in a running desktop app. Verify that the hook correctly fetches connections, that the `["integration-status"]` query key matches the deeplink invalidation, and that the UI updates after OAuth completion.
- [ ] **Connection status UI display**: The "Connected" badge and "Reconnect" button styling changes are untested in a real UI. Verify the visual appearance and that the connection state correctly reflects the API response.
- [ ] **`NangoConnectionRow` `#[serde(default)]` on `integration_id`**: The shared struct has `#[serde(default)]` on `integration_id`, which means if a PostgREST query doesn't select `integration_id`, it'll silently default to empty string. The extractor path only selects `connection_id` and `updated_at`, so it'll get an empty `integration_id`. Verify this doesn't cause issues (it shouldn't since the extractor doesn't use that field).
- [ ] **`allowed_integrations: None` security**: The `create_connect_session` endpoint no longer restricts which integrations can be connected. Any Nango integration could potentially be connected via the web flow. Verify this is acceptable from a security/product perspective.
- [ ] **Google Calendar in onboarding**: The onboarding calendar step now shows Google Calendar on all platforms (not just Apple on macOS). Verify this is the intended UX — previous revision explicitly removed it from onboarding.
- [ ] **End-to-end OAuth flow**: Test desktop Settings → Calendar → Google Calendar → "Connect Google Calendar" → browser OAuth → callback → deeplink back → desktop state refresh with a real Google account. Verify connection tags appear in Nango dashboard and that the desktop app's integration status updates correctly (including the "Connected" badge appearing).
- [ ] **Access control change**: `/calendar/*` routes moved from PRO-gated to basic auth. Any authenticated user (including free-tier) can now call calendar endpoints. Verify this is intentional.
- [ ] **Desktop flow browser session**: The `nangoCreateConnectSession` server function calls `getSupabaseServerClient().auth.getUser()` via cookies. If the user hasn't logged into the web app in that browser, the OAuth flow will fail. Test with a fresh browser profile to verify the auth redirect handles this gracefully.


1. **Desktop → Web flow (fresh browser profile)**
   - Desktop → Settings → Calendar → Google Calendar → "Connect Google Calendar"
   - Browser opens to `/app/integration?integration_id=google-calendar` — verify user is authenticated (or redirected to login)
   - Complete Google OAuth in Nango Connect UI
   - Verify redirect to `/callback/integration?integration_id=google-calendar&status=success` and "Open Char" deeplink works
   - Check Nango dashboard: connection should show `end_user_id` and `end_user_email` tags
   - **Verify desktop UI updates**: "Connected" badge should appear, button should change to "Reconnect" with gray styling

2. **Onboarding flow**
   - Start onboarding → Calendar step
   - On macOS: verify both Apple Calendar and Google Calendar are shown
   - On Windows/Linux: verify Google Calendar is shown
   - If already connected: verify "Connected" badge and "Reconnect" button appear
   - Click Continue and verify onboarding proceeds normally

3. **Connection status endpoint**
   - After connecting: call `GET /nango/connections` with user JWT
   - Verify response includes `{ connections: [{ integration_id: "google-calendar", connection_id: "...", updated_at: "..." }] }`

4. **Error handling**
   - Simulate `getSessionToken` failure (e.g., network error)
   - Verify error UI appears and persists when modal is closed

5. **Verify existing routes still work**
   - Test `/calendar/calendars` and `/calendar/events` endpoints after connecting Google Calendar
   - Verify no 500 errors due to deserialization failures


- **CI Status**: All checks passing (fmt, ci, desktop_ci for all platforms)

title: feat: Add streaming speech transcription support via @react-native-ai/apple (closes #21)
body:
# feat: Add streaming speech transcription via @react-native-ai/apple

Adds a new `@react-native-ai/apple` Expo module package (`packages/react-native-ai-apple/`) that provides on-device speech transcription with real-time streaming partial results, addressing issue #21.

**TypeScript layer:**
- `useStreamingTranscription()` React hook with `startListening`/`stopListening`, `transcript`, `isFinal`, `state`, `error`, `isAvailable`
- `NativeAppleTranscription` native module bridge with graceful `null` fallback on Android/Web
- Full type definitions for segments, events, options, and state

**Native Swift layer (iOS):**
- `AppleTranscriptionModule.swift` — Expo module exposing batch `transcribe()`, streaming `start/stop`, `isAvailable()`, `requestPermissions()`
- `StreamingTranscriptionSession.swift` — Manages `AVAudioEngine` + `SFSpeechRecognizer` with partial results, configurable locale, punctuation, on-device mode, and task hints

**Note:** Uses `SFSpeechRecognizer` (iOS 10+) rather than Apple's newer `SpeechAnalyzer` (iOS 26+) for broader device compatibility. The issue specifically mentions SpeechAnalyzer — this was a deliberate pragmatic trade-off.

- **Stop native streaming on component unmount**: `useEffect` cleanup now calls `stopStreamingTranscription()` in addition to removing JS event subscriptions, preventing microphone and recognition resource leaks when the user navigates away mid-session.
- **Early return after `isFinal` in Swift callback**: The `recognitionTask` result handler now returns immediately after calling `stop()` on a final result, preventing a spurious `onError` event when Apple delivers both a result and an error in the same callback invocation.
- **Locale-aware availability check**: `checkAvailability()` now accepts an optional `locale` parameter (defaults to `'en-US'`). `startListening` re-checks availability for the requested locale so `isAvailable` reflects the correct state for non-English locales.
- *(Previous)* `hasSettled` guard in batch `transcribe()` to prevent promise double-resolution.
- *(Previous)* Permission denial handling — `startListening` checks `requestPermissions()` return value and surfaces a clear error instead of attempting to start the audio engine without authorization.
- *(Previous)* Added 2 tests for permission denial scenarios. Total: 16 tests passing.

- [ ] **Swift compilation with ExpoModulesCore**: The native Swift code was written without being compiled. Verify that `AppleTranscriptionModule.swift` and `StreamingTranscriptionSession.swift` actually compile against the ExpoModulesCore `Module` API (particularly `promise.reject(enum, string)` signature, `sendEvent` dictionary syntax, and `AsyncFunction` closure parameter types). **This is the highest-risk item in this PR.**
- [ ] **Audio session lifecycle**: `StreamingTranscriptionSession` sets category `.record` with `.duckOthers` and fully deactivates on stop — verify this doesn't disrupt other audio in the host app. No guard against calling `start()` twice on the same session.
- [ ] **SFSpeechRecognizer vs SpeechAnalyzer**: Issue #21 specifically requests SpeechAnalyzer (iOS 26+). This PR uses SFSpeechRecognizer instead. Confirm this is acceptable scope or if SpeechAnalyzer support is needed.
- [ ] **Test on a real iOS device**: All 16 tests pass but only cover the TypeScript mock layer. The hook tests use `capturedSetters[index]` which is dependent on `useState` call order — fragile if hook internals change. No native behavior has been tested.

1. Install the package in the main app: `cd app && npm install ../packages/react-native-ai-apple`
2. Add usage to a screen:
   ```tsx
   import { useStreamingTranscription } from '@react-native-ai/apple';
   
   const { startListening, stopListening, transcript, state } = useStreamingTranscription();
   // Add buttons to call startListening() / stopListening()
   // Display transcript text
3. Run on iOS device (not simulator — microphone required)
4. Grant microphone + speech recognition permissions
5. Tap "Start" → speak → verify partial results appear in real-time → tap "Stop" → verify final transcript
6. Deny permissions when prompted and verify a clear error is shown (not a native crash)
7. **New:** Navigate away from the screen mid-session and verify the microphone indicator turns off (no resource leak)
8. **New:** Test with a non-English locale (e.g., `startListening({ locale: 'ja-JP' })`) and verify `isAvailable` updates correctly

- This is a standalone package under `packages/` — not yet integrated into the main app
- 16 TypeScript tests pass (module loading, hook interface, options forwarding, event subscriptions, permission denial)
- TypeScript compiles cleanly (`tsc --noEmit`)
- No native iOS testing was possible in this environment


**Requested by:** bot_apk

feat: add streaming speech transcription support via @react-native-ai/apple

Implements on-device streaming speech transcription using Apple's
SFSpeechRecognizer (iOS 10+) with real-time partial results.

Resolves #21

New package: packages/react-native-ai-apple/

Native Swift:
- AppleTranscriptionModule.swift: Expo module exposing batch transcribe(),
  streaming start/stop, isAvailable(), and requestPermissions()
- StreamingTranscriptionSession.swift: Manages AVAudioEngine + SFSpeechRecognizer
  session with partial results, configurable locale, punctuation, on-device mode,
  and task hints (dictation/search/confirmation)

TypeScript:
- AppleTranscription.types.ts: Full type definitions for segments, events, options
- AppleTranscriptionModule.ts: Native module bridge with platform fallback (null on Android/Web)
- useStreamingTranscription.ts: React hook with startListening/stopListening,
  transcript, isFinal, state, error, isAvailable
- index.ts: Public API exports

Tests: 15 tests covering module loading, hook interface, default/custom options,
event subscription, and graceful fallback on unsupported platforms

Co-Authored-By: bot_apk <apk@cognition.ai>
fix: address Devin Review findings - Guard against promise double-resolution in batch transcribe() with hasSettled flag - Check permission result before starting streaming (handle denied/microphone_denied) - Add tests for permission denial scenarios (16 tests passing)

Co-Authored-By: bot_apk <apk@cognition.ai>
fix: address Devin Review round 2 - Stop native streaming on component unmount (prevent microphone/resource leak) - Return early after isFinal in Swift callback to prevent spurious error events - Accept locale param in checkAvailability() for accurate non-en-US availability

Co-Authored-By: bot_apk <apk@cognition.ai>
fix: add thread safety and idle state emission to StreamingTranscriptionSession

- Add serial DispatchQueue to synchronize access to mutable state
- Add isStopped flag to make stop() idempotent (no double-cleanup)
- Wrap recognition callback in queue.async for thread-safe access
- Emit onStateChange('idle') from stopInternal() so hook transitions
  to idle on natural isFinal completion
- Remove duplicate state event from module's stopStreamingTranscription
  (now handled by the session itself)

Co-Authored-By: bot_apk <apk@cognition.ai>
fix: separate requiresOnDeviceRecognition (iOS 13+) from addsPunctuation (iOS 16+)

requiresOnDeviceRecognition is available since iOS 13, not iOS 16.
Bundling it with addsPunctuation caused it to be silently ignored on
iOS 13-15, potentially sending audio to Apple servers when the user
explicitly requested on-device-only recognition.

Co-Authored-By: bot_apk <apk@cognition.ai>
fix: prevent resource leak on unmount during async startListening + fix event subscription ordering

- Add isMountedRef to track component lifecycle; check after each await
  in startListening to abort if component unmounted during permission
  dialog or native session startup
- Move event subscriptions to AFTER startStreamingTranscription resolves
  to avoid receiving stale 'idle' events from old session teardown when
  restarting a session
- Update useRef mock in tests to pass through initial values

Co-Authored-By: bot_apk <apk@cognition.ai>
fix: subscribe to events before native call + generation counter to discard stale events

- Move addListener calls back to before startStreamingTranscription()
  so the synchronous 'listening' event from session.start() is captured
- Add sessionGeneration counter in native module: each new session bumps
  the counter and callbacks compare their captured generation, becoming
  no-ops if they belong to a superseded session
- Keeps isMountedRef guards for unmount-during-async safety

Co-Authored-By: bot_apk <apk@cognition.ai>
fix: check result before error in batch transcribe() callback

Apple's SFSpeechRecognizer often delivers both a final result and an
error in the same callback invocation. Checking error first discarded
valid transcriptions. Now matches the streaming code pattern: check
result first, return early on isFinal, only then check error.

Co-Authored-By: bot_apk <apk@cognition.ai>
fix: add defer cleanup in start() for audioEngine.start() failure

If audioEngine.start() throws after audio session activation, recognition
task creation, and audio tap installation, the defer block now cleans up
all resources: cancels recognition task, ends recognition request, removes
audio tap, and deactivates audio session. Uses a started flag that is only
set to true after audioEngine.start() succeeds.

Co-Authored-By: bot_apk <apk@cognition.ai>
fix: move removeTap outside isRunning guard in stopInternal()

removeTap should be called regardless of whether the audio engine is
running, since a tap can remain installed on a stopped engine (e.g.,
after an audio session interruption). Matches the pattern already used
in the defer cleanup block in start().

title: Fix flaky threaded client lifespan test by using thread-safe counters
body:
Fixes flaky `test_client_context_lifespan_is_robust_to_threaded_concurrency` which failed in [this workflow run](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/21868579285) with:
AssertionError: assert 99 == 100
  +  where 99 = <MagicMock>.call_count   # startup
  +  and   100 = <MagicMock>.call_count  # shutdown

**Root cause:** `MagicMock.call_count` internally does `self.call_count += 1`, a non-atomic read-modify-write. When 100 threads call `startup()` concurrently, increments are lost due to the race on the counter.

**Fix:** Replace `MagicMock` with a `ThreadSafeCounter` that protects the count with a `threading.Lock` in the two multi-threaded tests. The purely async test (`test_client_context_lifespan_is_robust_to_high_async_concurrency`) is single-threaded and retains `MagicMock`.

Verified by running the previously-flaky test 20 times locally with zero failures, plus the full test module (all 3 tests passing).


  - No existing issue; this is a small flaky-test fix.

- [ ] Confirm `ThreadSafeCounter` exposes the same interface (`__call__` + `call_count`) that `make_lifespan` and the assertions rely on
- [ ] Verify the mixed-concurrency test (10 threads × 50 async tasks) also warrants `ThreadSafeCounter` rather than `MagicMock`
- [ ] Confirm the `MagicMock` import is still needed (yes — the async-only test still uses it)

title: Fix flaky E2E sorting test by isolating test data
body:
Fixes the consistently failing `should sort variables by name Z to A` E2E test in `ui-v2/e2e/variables/variables.spec.ts`.

**Root cause:** With `fullyParallel: true` and `workers: 4` in CI, the global `beforeEach` hook runs `cleanupVariables(apiClient, "e2e-test-")` before every test across all workers. When sorting and pagination tests run concurrently, one test's cleanup deletes another test's variables mid-execution. The sorting test then sees pagination variables in the first row instead of its own `zzz-sort` variable.

**Fix:** Give the Sorting and Pagination test groups their own isolated prefixes (`e2e-sort-` and `e2e-page-`) that fall outside the global `e2e-test-` cleanup scope, and navigate with `?name=<prefix><suffix>` URL params so each group only sees its own variables on the page.

- [ ] Verify the renamed sort variable ordering: `e2e-sort-{ts}-aaa` vs `e2e-sort-{ts}-zzz` — since `{ts}` is identical, `-aaa` < `-zzz` alphabetically, so A-to-Z and Z-to-A assertions should hold
- [ ] Verify that navigating with `?name=...` still causes the route to populate default search params (e.g., `sort=CREATED_DESC`) so URL assertions pass
- [ ] Confirm that the global `beforeEach`/`afterEach` (which still uses `e2e-test-` prefix) won't inadvertently affect the new `e2e-sort-` / `e2e-page-` prefixed variables
commit_msgs:
Fix flaky E2E sorting test by isolating test data

The 'should sort variables by name Z to A' test was consistently failing
because parallel test execution caused cross-test interference:

- fullyParallel: true with 4 workers means all tests run concurrently
- The global beforeEach cleanup (cleanupVariables with 'e2e-test-' prefix)
  deleted variables created by other concurrent tests
- The pagination test's cleanup would delete the sorting test's variables,
  and vice versa

Fix: Give sorting and pagination tests their own isolated prefixes
('e2e-sort-' and 'e2e-page-') that are outside the global 'e2e-test-'
cleanup scope. Navigate with name filter URL params so each test group
only sees its own variables on the page.

title: Fix env var leakage between concurrent deployments in worker
body:
`BaseJobConfiguration.from_template_and_values()` takes `base_job_template["job_configuration"]` by reference and then mutates the `env` key during variable merging. Since the worker caches `self._work_pool` (and its `base_job_template`) across its lifetime, concurrent flow runs processed in the same poll cycle share the same dict — causing env vars from one deployment to leak into another.

The fix deep-copies `job_configuration` at the start of `from_template_and_values()` so each call works on an independent copy.




### Important review items

- Confirm `copy.deepcopy` is appropriate here vs. a shallow copy. `job_configuration` contains nested dicts (e.g. `env`), so a shallow copy would still share mutable nested references. Typical job configs are plain JSON-like structures so `deepcopy` should be safe and cheap.
- `variables_schema` (the other value read from `base_job_template`) is **not** deep-copied — it is consumed read-only by `_get_base_config_defaults()` which builds a fresh dict. Worth confirming this is safe.


**Link to Devin Session:** https://app.devin.ai/sessions/851d9981a77c48348eef89fc61601f40  
**Requested by:** @desertaxle
commit_msgs:
Fix env var leakage between concurrent deployments in worker

Deep-copy base_job_template['job_configuration'] in
BaseJobConfiguration.from_template_and_values() to prevent mutations
from propagating across concurrent flow runs that share the same
cached work pool template.

Closes #21043

title: Fix CSS loading by removing nested HTML structure in app layout
body:
# Fix CSS loading by removing nested HTML structure in app layout


Removes nested `<html>` and `<body>` tags from the app layout file (`/src/app/[locale]/app/layout.tsx`) to fix CSS loading issues in the portable Windows version. The layout was creating invalid nested HTML structure that violated Next.js App Router conventions and caused unpredictable CSS injection behavior in certain environments.

- Removed nested `<html>` and `<body>` tags from app layout
- Removed redundant CSS import (already in parent layout)  
- Removed redundant Analytics component (already in parent layout)
- Layout now returns `children` directly, following Next.js best practices

The parent layout (`/src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx`) already provides the HTML structure, CSS import, and Analytics component, so the app layout should not duplicate these.


**⚠️ Important:** I could not reproduce the original CSS loading issue in my test environment, so this fix is based on architectural analysis rather than confirmed reproduction.

- [ ] **Test in actual portable Windows environment** - Verify CSS loads correctly on landing page (`/en`) after applying this fix
- [ ] **Test both routes work correctly** - Verify `/en` (landing) and `/en/app` (main app) both display with proper styling
- [ ] **Check HTML source structure** - View page source to confirm no nested `<html>` or `<body>` tags exist
- [ ] **Verify no functional regressions** - Test that app interface still works correctly (video editing, AI generation, etc.)


**Root cause analysis:** The issue was caused by having two layouts with full HTML structures:
- `/src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx` (parent) - has `<html>` and `<body>` ✅ correct
- `/src/app/[locale]/app/layout.tsx` (child) - also had `<html>` and `<body>` ❌ incorrect

This created invalid nested HTML that could cause CSS injection to fail unpredictably in certain environments while working fine in others.

title: feat(dog): treat dogs as agents with delayed session start
body:
**Fixes race condition where dogs pick up wrong work on startup.**

When dispatching work to dogs, the session was starting before the hook was set. This caused dogs to run `gt prime` and pick up deacon patrol tasks instead of their assigned work (e.g., `mol-convoy-feed`).

### Key Changes

1. **Delayed session start for dogs** - Session now starts AFTER hook is set, ensuring dogs see their assigned work when `gt prime` runs during startup

2. **Canonical dog bead IDs** - Dogs now get proper agent beads with ID format `hq-dog-<name>` and `--type=agent`

3. **`dog:name` shorthand syntax** - Added `dog:alpha` as shorthand for `deacon/dogs/alpha` (like `rig:polecat` syntax)

4. **Old dog compatibility warning** - If hook update fails for old dogs, warns user to recreate with `gt dog rm <name> && gt dog add <name>`

### Files Changed

- `sling_dog.go` - Added `DogDispatchOptions.DelaySessionStart` and `StartDelayedSession()` method
- `sling.go` / `sling_formula.go` - Use delayed start when dispatching to dogs
- `beads_dog.go` - Create dog beads with canonical `--id=hq-dog-<name>` and `--type=agent`
- `sling_helpers.go` - Handle `deacon/dogs/*` in `agentIDToBeadID()`, add old dog warning


- [x] `go test ./internal/cmd/... -run TestIsDogTarget` - dog target parsing
- [x] `go test ./internal/cmd/... -run TestDogDispatch` - dispatch options and delayed session
- [ ] Manual: `gt sling mol-convoy-feed dog:alpha` - verify dog gets correct work

Fix gt ready using wrong beads path for rigs

The ready command was incorrectly using RigMayorPath() which resolves to

/home/baldvin/gt/jbrs/.beads.

called by gt ready, even though the database existed at the rig root.

redirect system at <rig>/.beads/redirect already handles routing to
mayor/rig/.beads when appropriate.

path consistently.

fix(mayor): run session from mayorDir instead of townRoot

Mayor's session was changed to run from ~/gt/ (townRoot) in commit 278b2f2d,
but settings were still created in ~/gt/mayor/. This caused settings to not
be found since Claude Code only looks in the exact working directory.

Rather than moving settings to townRoot (which could affect other agents if
Claude Code traverses parent directories), this fix reverts Mayor to run from
its natural home directory ~/gt/mayor/.

Tools like `gt prime` use workspace.FindFromCwd() which walks UP to find the
town root, so running from ~/gt/mayor/ still correctly finds ~/gt/.

title: fix: move rebase integrity check to after branch swap
body:
- The `gt dolt rebase` integrity check was running on the `compact-work` branch before the branch swap to `main`
- `information_schema.tables` reflects the current branch's schema state, so tables could appear missing on `compact-work` even though they exist in the final rebased result
- This caused false positive "integrity FAIL: table missing" errors that aborted otherwise successful rebases (observed with `wisp_events` table on the `hq` database)

- Moved the integrity check to run **after** the branch swap, so it reads from the new `main`
- Changed from hard abort to warning since the swap is already complete at that point — aborting post-swap would leave the database in an inconsistent state

- [x] Verified the bug: `gt dolt rebase hq` failed with `integrity FAIL: table "wisp_events" missing after rebase` despite the table existing on main
- [x] Build succeeds with `go build ./...`
- [x] Successfully compacted hq (1937→2) and beads (1054→2) using `gt dolt flatten` as workaround
commit_msgs:
fix: compactor-dog nothing-to-commit dead code + --set-upstream push

Two fixes:

1. DOLT_COMMIT "nothing to commit" was treated as error because
   dolt_exec sends stderr to LOGFILE — the check on stdout was dead
   code. Now checks LOGFILE for the message and treats it as a skip.

2. Force-push uses --set-upstream to restore branch tracking metadata
   that flatten destroys (fixes "no upstream branch" on subsequent pushes).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix: resolve prefix→rig mapping in doctor checks to prevent DB drops

Doctor assumed database name == rig name, but some rigs use their prefix
as the DB name (e.g., "lc" for laneassist, "gt" for gastown). This caused
multiple checks to misidentify prefix-named databases as orphaned.

Four fixes:

1. collectReferencedDatabases: add rigs.json prefix fallback so prefix-named
   DBs are always marked as referenced, even if metadata.json is missing.

2. DoltMetadataCheck: look up expected DB name via config.GetRigPrefix()
   instead of hardcoding rigName. Check .dolt-data/<prefix> when
   .dolt-data/<rigName> doesn't exist. Preserve existing dolt_database
   in writeDoltMetadata when it matches a known prefix.

3. cleanStaleBeadsFiles: skip metadata.json when it declares a valid
   dolt_database, preventing the stale-redirect fix from severing
   a rig's connection to its database.

4. StaleRuntimeFilesCheck: build a prefix set from rigs.json so PID
   files named with prefixes (e.g., lc-witness.pid) aren't flagged stale.

Fixes: gt-85w7

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Merge fix/doctor-prefix-db-mapping (PR #3034)
Merge fix/compactor-dog-integrity-tolerance (PR #3035)
fix(nudge): add flock-based cross-process lock to prevent interleaved delivery

NudgeSession's in-process channel semaphore doesn't serialize across OS
processes. Each `gt nudge` CLI invocation is a separate process, so
concurrent nudges to the same session interleave send-keys/Enter steps,
producing garbled or empty input.

Add flock(2)-based filesystem lock in NudgeSessionWithOpts, gated by a
new TownRoot field on NudgeOpts. Lock files live at
<townRoot>/.runtime/nudge_queue/<session>/.lock alongside the nudge queue.
The existing in-process lock remains as a fast path for goroutine
serialization within long-running processes (daemon, witness, etc.).

All NudgeSession calls in the gt nudge CLI path (deliverNudge and
watchAndDeliver) now pass TownRoot to enable cross-process locking.

Fixes: gt-ukl8

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Merge branch 'fix/nudge-cross-process-flock'
fix: compactor-dog log output to prevent dog agent over-escalation

Replace WARNING/ERROR prefixes with [handled]/[info] for non-fatal
cases that the script already recovers from. Dog agents (Claude)
interpret WARNING text as failures and create HIGH escalations,
causing a feedback loop of noise despite the script completing
successfully.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
feat: support .no-sync marker file to skip databases during sync

Databases with a `.no-sync` file in their data directory are skipped
by both SyncDatabases and SyncDatabasesSQL. This prevents the
auto-provisioning logic from creating DoltHub repos and pushing
local-only databases that should never leave the machine.

(upstream PR: steveyegge/gastown#3128)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix: escape backslashes in mol-refinery-patrol TOML sed expression

The sed command on line 617 used \( and \) which are invalid escape
sequences in TOML basic strings. Doubled the backslashes so TOML
parses them as literal backslashes for the sed command.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix: remove --no-history flag and other plugin fixes (#3027)

* fix: guard grep pipeline in dolt-archive against pipefail exit

grep -v returns exit code 1 when no matches are found. With set -euo
pipefail, this kills the script before completing the dolt push step.
Add || true to the two affected pipelines.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: github-sheriff dedup failure — bd commands missing --rig flag

The bd list and bd create calls didn't specify --rig, so dedup queried
HQ while beads were created in the rig database. Result: 183 duplicate
CI failure beads per run, Dolt commits growing from 662 to 3325.

Also: bump cooldown from 5m to 2h, and filter PRs to last 7 days to
avoid scanning stale PRs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: dolt-archive DEFAULT_DBS references non-existent 'bd' database

The database is called 'beads', not 'bd'. This caused export failures
on every archive cycle. Matches actual databases in .dolt-data/.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: remove --no-history flag from bd create/update calls

bd does not support --no-history. This caused polecat spawning to fail
in a retry loop when gt sling tried to create new agent beads. The flag
was intended to skip git commit overhead, but dolt-auto-commit is already
off by default, making the flag unnecessary.

Fixes gt-vmnu.

fix: set cmd.Dir in doltserver.Start() to prevent wrong-CWD server launches (#3029)

The CLI code path (gt dolt start) did not set cmd.Dir when spawning the
dolt sql-server process, causing it to inherit the caller's working
directory. If started from a rig subdirectory, the server would fail to
discover any databases despite them existing on disk.

instead of using Gas Town primitives (beads, sling, convoys). The root cause

New users' Mayors default to Claude Code's built-in filesystem auto-memory
(~/.claude/*/memory/MEMORY.md) which is invisible to other agents and not

The unparam linter flagged the receipts parameter as unused in the
human-readable output function. The JSON output function uses it but
the human formatter does not. This was causing CI lint failures on main.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix(test): update github-sheriff cooldown expectation from 5m to 2h

PR #3027 changed the github-sheriff plugin cooldown duration from 5m
to 2h, but the scanner test still expected the old value.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix: dolt-archive pruning crash + auto-discover databases

Two bugs in plugins/dolt-archive/run.sh:

1. Snapshot pruning crashes under `set -euo pipefail` when no snapshots
   exist for a database. The `ls -t ... | tail -n +25` pipeline fails
   because `ls` returns non-zero when the glob matches nothing, and
   `pipefail` propagates that through the pipeline. Replaced with
   `mapfile` + array slicing which handles empty results cleanly.

2. DEFAULT_DBS was hardcoded but the correct database names vary across
   deployments. This is the same bug fixed in PRs #2369, #2715, #2747,
   #2777, #2781 — the hardcoded list keeps drifting out of sync with
   production. Instead of picking yet another set of names, default to
   "auto" which discovers databases via SHOW DATABASES at runtime. The
   --databases flag still allows explicit override when needed.

Fix-merge of PR #2808 (KeithWyatt).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix: retry Dolt testcontainer on transient reaper 'removing' status (gas-5i9)

When Docker's Ryuk reaper container is still being cleaned up from a
previous test run, testcontainers-go returns 'unexpected container status
removing'. This is a transient race condition.

Add runDoltContainerWithRetry() that retries up to 3 times with
exponential backoff (2s, 4s) when this specific error is detected.
Non-reaper errors fail immediately without retry.
fix: repair PROJECT IDENTITY MISMATCH after crash or rig addition (gas-tc4)

EnsureMetadata now corrects wrong dolt_database values (not just empty),
which is the primary cause of identity mismatches after bd init writes
"beads_<prefix>" instead of the rig name.

Changes:
- EnsureMetadata: fix wrong dolt_database values, not just empty ones
- isDoltConfigError: detect "identity mismatch" and "Unknown database"
  for fast-fail instead of retrying 10 times
- CheckDoltHealth: include actionable recovery path in error messages
  ("run gt doctor --fix" instead of opaque error)
- gt rig add: post-init identity verification catches mismatches before
  polecats are spawned
- gt repair: new focused command for identity/config repair (subset of
  gt doctor --fix)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix: pass --branch to bare clone in gt rig add

When users specify --branch with gt rig add, the flag was being ignored
for the bare repo clone (.repo.git). The CloneBare* functions had no
branch parameter, so git always cloned the remote HEAD branch.

Add CloneBareWithBranch and related variants to git.go; refactor
manager.go clone logic into a cloneBareWith closure that passes the
user-specified branch through to all bare clone variants.

Add TestAddRig_BranchFlag to cover the scenario.

Fixes #2940
fix(polecat): provision CLAUDE.md in worktree so polecats know to call gt done

The polecat-CLAUDE.md template (with 3 separate gt done warnings) existed
but was never written to polecat worktrees. The comment said "full context
is injected ephemerally via SessionStart hook (gt prime)" — but gt prime
output scrolls past and gets lost after compaction. Result: every polecat
finishes work then sits idle instead of calling gt done.

Fix: embed the template and write it during spawn (and repair). CLAUDE.md
is always loaded by Claude Code, so polecats will see gt done instructions
persistently. Also add CLAUDE.md to gasTownIgnorePatterns so it doesn't
pollute git status in worktrees.

fix(tests): add CLAUDE.md to polecat worktree allowlists

Update TestAgentWorktreesStayClean and TestAddWithOptions_NoFilesAddedToRepo

by CreatePolecatCLAUDEmd.

title: Clean codebase consolidation and V2→Onetime namespace migration
body:
### **User description** This PR represents a major architectural consolidation following multiple authentication and session management improvements. The work moves the codebase toward a cleaner, more maintainable structure by eliminating redundant code, standardizing on modern patterns, and completing the V2→Onetime namespace migration. ## What Changed **Namespace Migration (V2 → Onetime)** Completed the migration from the temporary V2 namespace to the permanent Onetime namespace for all core models (Customer, Secret, Metadata, CustomDomain, Feedback, Organization, Team, SystemSettings). This creates a stable foundation for the v1.0 release. **Code Consolidation** Moved 120+ commits worth of incremental improvements into a single coherent state. Relocated experimental/deprecated code to `.purgatory/` while preserving git history for future reference. This includes the entire V1 API app, legacy session implementations, outdated specs, and prototype auth implementations. **Authentication Architecture** Standardized on Rack::Session + Rodauth pattern with three auth modes (basic/advanced/disabled) via adapter pattern. Integrated Otto authentication strategies for the V2 API. Added comprehensive session validation and CSRF protection via modern middleware. **Application Structure** Refactored apps to use unified BaseApplication pattern with MiddlewareStack helper. Created dedicated `app.rb` and `registry.rb` files for each application. Standardized route organization with advanced Otto syntax for better request handling. **Session Management** Replaced custom session implementations with Rack::Session::Redis + Familia. Created Onetime::Session middleware for unified session handling. Added IdentityResolution middleware for cross-app user tracking. Implemented proper session validation and security helpers. **Middleware Improvements** Created MiddlewareStack helper to reduce duplication across apps. Improved DomainStrategy middleware for better multi-domain handling. Added security middleware for timing attack prevention. Better startup readiness checks. **Controller Refactoring** Split monolithic controllers into focused, single-responsibility classes. Moved common patterns to SessionHelpers and ShrimpHelpers modules. Updated to use modern authentication adapter pattern. Better separation between API and Web controllers. **Model Improvements** Upgraded to Familia 2.0.0.pre17 with enhanced relationship support. Improved encryption patterns with proper IV handling. Better TTL management and counter field patterns. Enhanced safe_dump implementation for debugging. **Testing Infrastructure** Extracted comprehensive auth test coverage from orphan branches. Added timing attack prevention tests. Updated all tests to use new Onetime namespace. Better test isolation with fresh context mode. **Configuration Management** Added auth.defaults.yaml for Rodauth configuration. Better environment variable handling. Improved config validation patterns. More consistent defaults across environments. **Documentation** Added comprehensive auth database migration notes. Better inline documentation for complex middleware. Improved changelog tracking via Scriv fragments. More detailed error messages. **Files Moved to Purgatory**: 270+ - Complete V1 API app (apps/api/v1/) - Legacy session models - Outdated specs and test helpers - Prototype auth implementations - Deprecated migration files - Legacy public assets **New Files**: 50+ - apps/web/auth/ - Complete Rodauth auth service - lib/onetime/helpers/ - Session and CSRF helpers - lib/onetime/services/auth/ - Auth adapter pattern - lib/onetime/middleware/identity_resolution.rb - etc/defaults/auth.defaults.yaml **Dependency Updates** - Familia: 2.0.0.pre17 (major upgrade) - Otto: 2.0.0.pre1 (authentication strategies) - Rodauth: Latest (auth service foundation) ## Breaking Changes (most things) - v1 API is not working (moved temporarily to .purgatory) - v2 API is not working (controllers have been removed in favour of Otto's advanced routes file syntax, not configured properly yet) - web routes are not working (same reason as v2 API) Hey but it still boots. All existing test suites pass: - Tryouts: `FAMILIA_DEBUG=0 bundle exec try --agent` - RSpec: `bundle exec rspec` - Frontend: `pnpm test` New test coverage added for: - Authentication flows (E2E and security) - Session validation - Timing attack prevention - Auth adapter integration ## Migration Path No manual migration required. The code includes compatibility layers to handle the namespace transition transparently. Future PRs will complete the migration by updating remaining V1 references. ___ ### **PR Type** Enhancement, Other ___ ### **Description** • **Namespace Migration**: Completed migration from V2 to Onetime namespace for all core models (Customer, Secret, CustomDomain, Metadata, etc.) • **Authentication Architecture Overhaul**: Implemented unified authentication system with three modes (basic/advanced/disabled) using Rack::Session + Rodauth pattern • **Code Consolidation**: Moved 270+ legacy files to `.purgatory/` while preserving git history, including entire V1 API app and deprecated session implementations • **Session Management Modernization**: Replaced custom session implementations with Rack::Session::Redis + Familia, added IdentityResolution middleware • **Controller Refactoring**: Split monolithic controllers into focused classes, moved authentication/billing methods to dedicated controllers • **Security Enhancements**: Added timing attack prevention, CSRF protection via middleware, comprehensive authentication security tests • **Template Engine Migration**: Replaced Mustache with ERB for better maintainability • **Testing Infrastructure**: Extracted comprehensive auth test coverage from orphan branches, added 50+ new test files • **Middleware Improvements**: Created MiddlewareStack helper, enhanced DomainStrategy middleware, added security middleware • **Configuration Management**: Added auth.defaults.yaml for Rodauth configuration, improved environment variable handling ___ ### Diagram Walkthrough ```mermaid title: fix: implement notification deduplication to prevent duplicate messages
body:
- Implements backend notification deduplication to prevent duplicate messages from flooding the UI
- Addresses issue where identical notifications (like diskmanager errors) appear multiple times
- Uses content-based hashing to identify and merge duplicate notifications within a configurable time window

- **Content Hash Generation**: Added hash generation based on component, type, title, and message
- **Deduplication Logic**: Implemented in InMemoryStore with 5-minute default window
- **Occurrence Tracking**: Added occurrence count to track how many times a notification has been triggered
- **Priority Escalation**: Updates to highest priority when duplicates with higher priority arrive
- **Status Management**: Resets notifications to unread when duplicates occur
- **Comprehensive Tests**: Added full test coverage for deduplication scenarios

- Notifications are identified by a SHA256 hash of their content (component + type + title + message)
- Deduplication window is configurable (default: 5 minutes)
- Both `notifications` and `hashIndex` maps maintain proper pointer references
- Update method modified to update fields in-place rather than replacing pointers

- [x] Run `go test -race ./internal/notification` - all tests pass
- [x] Run `golangci-lint run -v` - no issues
- [x] Test with repeated diskmanager errors - should see single notification with occurrence count
- [ ] Verify frontend displays occurrence count correctly
- [ ] Test that notifications outside deduplication window create new entries

## Example
Before: Multiple identical "diskmanager: invalid audio filename format" notifications
After: Single notification with `occurrence_count: 5` showing it happened 5 times



  * Added automatic deduplication of notifications based on content within a configurable time window, preventing duplicate notifications and aggregating their occurrence counts.
  * Notifications now display how many times they have occurred and track the timestamp of the first occurrence.
  * Notification priority escalates if a duplicate with higher priority is received, and read status resets on new duplicates.

  * Improved notification storage to ensure unique notifications are not incorrectly deduplicated.

  * Introduced comprehensive tests covering deduplication logic, priority escalation, occurrence counting, error handling, metadata handling, and internal cleanup mechanisms.

title: feat: add auto-detection for Blackwell GPU architecture (sm_100a)
body:
Add automatic GPU architecture detection to properly set `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` for Blackwell GPUs (sm_100a/10.0a).

When building DeepEP on Blackwell GPUs, users encounter errors like:
Target SM ARCH unknown is not compatible
cudaErrorInsufficientDriver

This is because the default `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` is set to `9.0`, which doesn't match Blackwell's `sm_100a` architecture.

- Add `get_cuda_arch_from_device()` function to automatically detect GPU architecture
- Auto-detect `sm_100a` for Blackwell, `sm_90a` for Hopper
- Print detected architecture during build for user feedback
- Fall back to `9.0` if detection fails (maintains backward compatibility)

Users can still override with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` environment variable.

- [ ] Build on Blackwell GPU system
- [ ] Build on Hopper GPU system  
- [ ] Verify fallback works when GPU detection fails

Fixes #519

title: fix: reduce Claude OAuth keychain prompt frequency
body:
Caches Claude OAuth credentials in CodexBar's own keychain item to prevent repeated keychain prompts.

## Root Cause Analysis
The `Claude Code-credentials` keychain item is owned by **Claude CLI** (Team ID: `Q6L2SF6YDW`), not CodexBar (Team ID: `Y5PE65HELJ`). When Claude CLI updates the OAuth token, it may reset the keychain's ACL/partition_id, removing CodexBar's authorization. This causes macOS to prompt for permission on every access, even after users click "Always Allow".

Create a separate keychain item owned by CodexBar to cache the credentials:

1. **New cache keychain item**: `com.steipete.codexbar.claude-oauth-cache`
   - Owned by CodexBar, never prompts for permission
   - Uses `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly` for stability across code signature changes

2. **Load order** (no prompts until step 4):
   1. In-memory cache (30 min validity)
   2. CodexBar's keychain cache (persists across app restarts)
   3. File fallback (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`)
   4. Claude's keychain (may prompt, but only when token is actually expired)

3. **Simple expiry check**: Only access Claude's keychain when the cached token is actually expired. No proactive refresh since CodexBar can't refresh tokens itself - it only reads from Claude CLI.

## User Experience
| Scenario | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| First launch | Prompt | Prompt (once) |
| Subsequent launches | Prompt every refresh | No prompt |
| After "Always Allow" | Prompts within minutes | No prompts |
| Token expired | N/A | One prompt (to read refreshed token from Claude CLI) |

- [x] Build passes (`swift build`)
- [x] All Claude-related tests pass (`swift test --filter Claude`)
- [ ] Manual testing: verify first launch prompts once, subsequent launches don't prompt
- [ ] Verify expired token correctly triggers fallback to Claude's keychain
- [ ] Verify `invalidateCache()` clears both in-memory and keychain caches

- Cache keychain uses `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly` to avoid prompts on code signature changes
- `loadFromKeychain()` kept as legacy alias for backward compatibility
- Cache is best-effort: failures are logged but don't break functionality

Fixes #108

title: feat: [EXPERIMENTAL] Add cost-based optimizer (CBO) for Comet vs Spark execution
body:
This PR introduces an **experimental** lightweight cost-based optimizer (CBO) that estimates whether a Comet query plan will be faster than a Spark plan, falling back to Spark when Comet execution is estimated to be slower.

> **⚠️ EXPERIMENTAL**: This feature is disabled by default and should be considered experimental. The cost model parameters are initial estimates and should be tuned with real-world benchmarks before being used in production.


- **Heuristic-based cost model** with configurable weights for different operator types:
  - Scan, Filter, Project, Aggregate, Join, Sort
- **Configurable speedup factors** for each Comet operator type
- **Transition penalty** for columnar↔row conversions
- **Cardinality estimation** using Spark's logical plan statistics with fallbacks
- **CBO analysis in EXPLAIN output** when enabled

## Configuration Options

| Config | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `spark.comet.cbo.enabled` | `false` | Enable/disable CBO |
| `spark.comet.cbo.speedupThreshold` | `1.0` | Minimum estimated speedup required to use Comet |
| `spark.comet.cbo.explain.enabled` | `false` | Log CBO decision details |

Additional internal configs for tuning weights and speedup factors are available (see `CometConf.scala`).

## How It Works

1. After `CometExecRule` transforms operators to Comet equivalents, CBO analyzes the plan
2. Collects statistics: Comet operators, Spark operators, transitions
3. Estimates costs for both Spark-only and Comet execution
4. Calculates estimated speedup = sparkCost / cometCost
5. If speedup < threshold, falls back to original Spark plan

## Limitations

- **CBO only affects operator conversion** (filter, project, aggregate, join, sort)
- **Scan conversion is NOT affected** - handled separately by `CometScanRule`
- Cost model parameters are estimates and need tuning with benchmarks

## Example Usage

```scala
// Enable CBO with default threshold
spark.conf.set("spark.comet.cbo.enabled", "true")

// Or with custom threshold (use Comet only if 1.5x faster)
spark.conf.set("spark.comet.cbo.speedupThreshold", "1.5")

// Enable debug logging
spark.conf.set("spark.comet.cbo.explain.enabled", "true")


- **New**: `CometCostEstimator.scala` - Core cost estimation logic
- **New**: `CometCBOSuite.scala` - Unit tests
- **Modified**: `CometConf.scala` - Configuration options
- **Modified**: `CometExecRule.scala` - CBO integration
- **Modified**: `ExtendedExplainInfo.scala` - CBO info in EXPLAIN


- [x] New unit tests in `CometCBOSuite` (13 tests)
- [x] Existing `CometExecRuleSuite` tests pass
- [ ] Manual testing with TPC-H/TPC-DS benchmarks (future work)
- [ ] Tune default parameters based on benchmark results (future work)

title: fix(workflows): respect commit_docs config in auto-advance recovery paths
body:
- Auto-advance recovery blocks in `plan-phase.md` and `discuss-phase.md` run raw `git add .planning/` without checking the `commit_docs` config flag
- Users who set `commit_docs: false` still get `.planning/` files committed through these two paths
- Adds the same `git reset HEAD .planning/` guard that `complete-milestone.md` already uses


Both `plan-phase.md:475` and `discuss-phase.md:631` contain recovery blocks for deeply-nested executor agents that unconditionally stage `.planning/` files:

git add .planning/ src/ tests/ 2>/dev/null

The `gsd-tools.cjs commit` gate at `commands.cjs:224` correctly checks `commit_docs`, but these raw git commands bypass it entirely.


After `git add`, strip `.planning/` from staging when `commit_docs` is false — matching the existing pattern in `complete-milestone.md`:

if [ "$COMMIT_DOCS" = "false" ]; then
  git reset HEAD .planning/ 2>/dev/null || true
fi

Both workflows already parse `commit_docs` from init JSON (plan-phase line 21, discuss-phase line 119).


- [ ] Set `commit_docs: false` in `.planning/config.json`
- [ ] Run `/gsd:plan-phase` followed by `/gsd:execute-phase` with auto-advance enabled
- [ ] Verify `git log -- .planning/` shows no new commits from the recovery path
- [ ] Verify `src/` and `tests/` changes are still committed normally

Closes #790

## Refactor
* Streamlined channel management by removing per-version existence/validation from POST, PUT, and DELETE flows.
* Handlers now rely on plugin-version and channel override/default logic instead of per-version lookups; new-version paths preserved where applicable.
* Adjusted logging and error responses to match the simplified flow.
* Tests updated to remove server-side version-existence checks and assert default channel behavior.

title: Add gitresolver package for git:// skill references
body:
- The upcoming git-based skill install feature (`thv skill install git://...`) needs a package to parse git references, clone repos, resolve auth, and securely write extracted files. This PR adds that foundation as a self-contained package without wiring it into the skill service yet.
- New `pkg/skills/gitresolver/` package with four components: URL parsing with SSRF prevention, clone resolution with timeout, host-scoped credential resolution, and secure file writing with symlink/containment checks.
- Adds `HeadCommitHash` helper to `pkg/git/` for retrieving the HEAD commit hash after clone (used by the resolver to record provenance).

Relates to #4015

## Type of change

- [x] New feature

## Large PR Justification

This PR is 1268 lines but ~655 lines (over half) are unit tests. The remaining ~613 lines are a single self-contained package (`pkg/skills/gitresolver/`) with four tightly coupled components (URL parsing, clone resolution, auth, file writing) that share types and validation logic. Splitting these into separate PRs would create packages that don't compile independently and add review overhead without reducing risk. The 14-line `HeadCommitHash` addition to `pkg/git/` is the only change outside the new package.


- [x] Unit tests (`task test`)
- [x] Linting (`task lint-fix`)


| `pkg/skills/gitresolver/reference.go` | **New** — `git://` URL parsing with SSRF prevention (private IP/localhost rejection, absolute path/backslash rejection) |
| `pkg/skills/gitresolver/resolver.go` | **New** — `Resolver` interface: clones repo, extracts skill files, enforces 2-min clone timeout |
| `pkg/skills/gitresolver/auth.go` | **New** — host-scoped auth resolution (`GITHUB_TOKEN` only sent to github.com, etc.) |
| `pkg/skills/gitresolver/writer.go` | **New** — writes files to disk with symlink checks, containment validation, permission cap (0644) |
| `pkg/git/client.go` | **Modified** — added `HeadCommitHash` helper function |
| `*_test.go` | Comprehensive tests for all four components |

## Does this introduce a user-facing change?

No — this is a foundation package with no integration yet. The next PR will wire it into skillsvc.

## Special notes for reviewers

### Security design

- **Credential exfiltration prevented**: Tokens are host-scoped per-clone — `GITHUB_TOKEN` is only sent to `github.com`, `GITLAB_TOKEN` only to `gitlab.com`. `GIT_TOKEN` is an opt-in fallback for other hosts.
- **Clone timeout**: 2-minute `context.WithTimeout` in `Resolve()` prevents slowloris-style hangs.
- **Path validation hardened**: `validateSkillPath` rejects absolute paths and backslashes in addition to `..` traversal.
- **SSRF**: Static host validation rejects localhost/private IPs.
- **Resource limits**: `LimitedFs` caps clones at 10k files / 100MB.

### Known limitations for follow-up

- DNS rebinding not mitigated (needs custom `http.Transport` with `DialContext` hook)
- No host allowlist (denylist only)
- `collectFiles` reads only top-level files in the skill directory (flat structure)

This is PR 2 of 3 — split from #4042. PR 1 (#4045, merged) moved the git package. PR 3 will integrate gitresolver into skillsvc.

title: feat: energy optimization — reduce CPU, GPU, and memory consumption
body:
Reduces energy consumption across the app through three layers of changes, from zero-risk config tweaks to targeted refactors. Each layer can be shipped independently.

### Layer 1: Config values (zero risk)
- **macOS vibrancy**: `"active"` → `"followWindow"` — GPU savings when window unfocused
- **D3 alphaDecay**: `0.002` → `0.01` — simulation settles in ~10s instead of ~50s
- **Graph debounce**: `16ms` → `300ms` — reduces burst refetch during FS events
- **Binary cache**: LRU eviction at 5000 entries (evict oldest 20%)
- **Image cache**: 10MB total size limit with size-aware eviction
- **Canvas RPC**: cleanup pending promises on window close

### Layer 2: Conditional behavior (low risk)
- **D3 simulation stop**: stops when graph tile is hidden, re-energizes on show
- **cursorBlink setting**: configurable in Settings → Terminal (default: true)
- **scrollback setting**: configurable in Settings → Terminal (default: 200000)
- **Agent interval**: 1s → 3s re-render interval during agent sessions
- **Agent interactions**: ring buffer capped at 1000 entries per session

### Layer 3: Targeted refactors (medium risk, TDD)
- **PTY foreground check**: idle-based `lastDataTime` pattern — one timer per session instead of clear/restart per data byte. Cleanup on all 5 session exit paths
- **Watcher batching**: 200ms coalescing window with 2s safety flush, deduplication, immediate cache invalidation
- **Wikilink batching**: `batchUpdate()` with 500ms debounce, chunks of 20, `recentlyDeleted` guard against race conditions
- **File tree smart reload**: targeted reload on rename (1-2 dirs instead of all), folder rename edge case handled via React state cleanup


| Layer | Files | Commits |
|-------|-------|---------|
| L1 | `index.ts`, `forceGraph.ts`, `WorkspaceGraph.tsx`, `file-filter.ts`, `image-worker.ts`, `canvas-rpc.ts` | 6 |
| L2 | `ForceDirectedGraph.tsx`, `TerminalTab.tsx`, `terminal-tile/App.tsx`, `terminal/App.tsx`, `settings/App.tsx`, `WorkspaceGraph.tsx`, `agent-activity.ts` | 5 |
| L3 | `pty.ts`, `ipc.ts`, `wikilink-index.ts`, `useFileTree.ts` | 4 |


- [x] 35 automated tests pass across 6 test files
- [ ] Manual: open app with 3 terminals + graph tile
- [ ] Manual: run `find /tmp -type f` — no UI freezes
- [ ] Manual: switch git branch — file tree updates, graph updates, no stutter
- [ ] Manual: Settings → Terminal → cursorBlink and scrollback controls work
- [ ] Manual: hide graph tile → CPU drops; show → graph re-animates

## Energy measurement instructions

To measure before/after improvements, run on `main` and then on this branch:

**Setup:**
cd collab-electron && bun run dev

**Scenario A — Idle with graph tile visible** (wait 10s, then measure):
sudo powermetrics --samplers cpu_power -i 5000 -n 3

**Scenario B — Terminal burst** (run `find /tmp -type f` in terminal, measure simultaneously)

**Scenario C — Background idle** (switch focus to another window, wait 10s, measure)

Record CPU Power (mW) for each scenario and add results here:

| Scenario | main (mW) | this branch (mW) | Δ |
|----------|-----------|-------------------|---|
| A: idle + graph | _pending_ | _pending_ | — |
| B: terminal burst | _pending_ | _pending_ | — |
| C: background idle | _pending_ | _pending_ | — |

## Cross-branch note

This branch modifies `Settings/App.tsx` (adding terminal settings to existing Terminal pane). The [auto-update PR](#81) also modifies this file (adding About & Updates pane). Whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase — changes are non-overlapping.

## Design docs

- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-28-energy-optimization-design.md`
- Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-03-28-energy-optimization.md`

commit_msgs:
fix: remove duplicate bottom padding in fullscreen DiffView

adjust_scroll() already handles end-of-file scrolling by shifting
scroll_offset when selected_line is near the bottom. The render-side
padding (visible_height/2 empty lines) was doubling this effect,
causing the cursor to get buried and the display to jump mid-file.
SplitView did not have this render-side padding and worked correctly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix: unify scroll behavior between DiffView and SplitView

- Add scroll margin (visible_lines/2) to adjust_scroll so scrolling
  begins at viewport center instead of the edge
- Fix visible_lines calculation for SplitView: 65% is horizontal width,
  not vertical height — both variants use term_h - 8
- Slice cached lines from scroll_offset in render to avoid Wrap-induced
  logical/display row mismatch (markdown long lines)
- Remove broken end-of-file padding logic that caused cursor jumps
- Add comprehensive snapshot tests for scroll invariants

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix: restore viewport-bounded rendering and clamp scroll_offset for short diffs

- Bound render_cached_lines to visible_height + buffer instead of
  rendering from scroll_offset to EOF, restoring O(viewport) per frame
  in both fullscreen DiffView and SplitView
- Reset scroll_offset to 0 in adjust_scroll when diff fits within
  viewport, preventing stale scroll state from hiding lines after
  refresh or patch shrink
fix: clamp scroll_offset and selected_line when diff_line_count changes

When a refresh or patch change shrinks the currently viewed diff,
scroll_offset and selected_line could remain past the end of the new
diff, causing a blank diff pane until the next navigation key press.

Now update_diff_line_count() clamps both values immediately after
recalculating the line count, ensuring the viewport always stays valid.
fix: clamp scroll_offset to max scrollable position in renderers

When a diff shrinks below the viewport height, scroll_offset was only
clamped to line_count, which could leave most of the pane blank.
Now clamp to line_count.saturating_sub(visible_height) so the viewport
always shows as many lines as possible.

Applied to both DiffView and SplitView renderers.
fix: use layout-aware visible_lines when inline comment panel is open

When comment_panel_open is true, the diff body only receives a percentage
of the available height (50-55%), not the full terminal height. The
adjust_scroll() calculation now replicates the actual rendering layout
proportions so cursor movement and comment jumps stay correctly bounded
within the visible diff area in both split view and fullscreen modes.

title: Resolve USD asset references recursively
body:
Resolve USD asset references recursively in `resolve_usd_from_url` so that nested stages are fully downloaded. Previously only top-level references were fetched — if `scene.usd` referenced `robot.usd` which in turn referenced `collisions.usd`, only `robot.usd` would be downloaded.

Replaces the flat single-level reference loop with a BFS queue that scans each downloaded stage for its own references.

Closes #196


- [x] New or existing tests cover these changes
- [x] The documentation is up to date with these changes
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` has been updated (if user-facing change)


uv run --extra dev -m newton.tests -k TestResolveUsdFromUrl

Five new unit tests covering:
- Single-level references (baseline)
- Two-level recursive references
- Three-level deep recursive references
- Diamond dependencies (no duplicate downloads)
- Cyclic references (no infinite recursion)

## New feature / API change

No API change — `resolve_usd_from_url` signature and return value are unchanged. References in child stages are now automatically resolved.

from newton._src.utils.import_usd import resolve_usd_from_url

# Now recursively downloads all nested USD references
path = resolve_usd_from_url("https://example.com/assets/scene.usd")




  * Recursive USD reference resolution now fully downloads and processes nested stages, avoids duplicate downloads, handles cyclic references safely, preserves nested subdirectory placement, rejects path-traversal attempts, and improves error messages to reference actual local targets.

  * Added tests for single-level, recursive, deep-nesting, duplicate references, cyclic references, nested subdirectories, and path-traversal rejection.

  * Added changelog entry describing the fix.

title: Fix silent error handling in FTP listener
body:
- Add upfront regex pattern validation in FormatMethodsHolder
- Replace log.error with BError.printStackTrace for visible errors
- Remove redundant code in FtpListener

Native side `log.error()` calls are not visible to users, causing the FTP listener to silently fail in various error scenarios.

Changed to create `BError` and call `printStackTrace()` which outputs Ballerina-formatted errors that are visible to users.

Fixes: https://github.com/ballerina-platform/ballerina-library/issues/8655



This pull request improves error visibility and early configuration validation in the FTP listener so configuration and runtime problems are reported clearly to users instead of being silently lost.


- Error reporting: Replaced native-side log.error calls with Ballerina-formatted errors (FtpUtil.createError(...) and BError.printStackTrace()) across server and client native code (including FtpContentCallbackHandler, FtpListener, client helpers and related utilities) so native errors are surfaced to users in a consistent, visible format.
- Early validation: Added upfront regex validation for @ftp:FunctionConfig.fileNamePattern in FormatMethodsHolder during initialization to surface invalid patterns at startup and removed redundant runtime pattern exception handling.
- Cleanup: Removed or simplified redundant logging and error-checking paths and centralized error creation via FtpUtil to streamline error handling and reduce silent failures.
- Changelog: Added an unreleased note describing the fix for silent listener failures.

## Outcome

Improves stability and debuggability of the FTP listener by surfacing configuration and runtime errors in a consistent, user-visible format and by catching invalid filename patterns earlier during initialization.

fix: address review issues from PR #12

1. PromptContext.expandContextVariables: single-pass replacement to prevent
   user content containing {clipboard} or {text} from being expanded

   is captured before network round-trip delays
3. PromptContext.capture: mark @MainActor for NSPasteboard thread safety

   write-after-return when semaphore times out

   blocking cooperative thread pool on slow path

body:
- Fetches and resolves all `GlobalRole` effective permissions once per reconciler tick using Kahn's topological sort, handling chained `RoleRefs` and `PermissionsOmitted`
- Caches resolved tuples and permission maps on the `Reconciler` struct (behind `sync.RWMutex`) for reuse across all namespace workers in the same tick
- Composes namespace `Role` permissions from resolved `GlobalRole` inheritance when a `globalRolePerms` map is available
- Adds `GlobalRoleBinding` to the namespaced reconcile GVR list
- Adds comprehensive tests for `resolveAllGlobalRolePermissions` covering multi-level chains, multiple `RoleRefs`, diamond inheritance, self-reference and longer cycles, pure inheritance, omit-all, omit-non-existent, and key-collision deduplication

Zanzana: resolve GlobalRole permissions during reconciliation

Add GlobalRole resolution to the Unistore→Zanzana reconciler:
- Fetch and resolve all GlobalRole effective permissions once per tick
  (topological sort handles chained RoleRefs + PermissionsOmitted)
- Cache resolved tuples and permission maps for reuse across namespaces
- Compose namespace Role permissions from resolved GlobalRole inheritance
- Add GlobalRoleBinding to the namespaced reconcile GVR list
- Add comprehensive tests for resolveAllGlobalRolePermissions covering
  multi-level chains, multiple RoleRefs, diamond inheritance, cycles,
  omission edge cases, and key-collision deduplication

Zanzana: consolidate dual mutexes into a single globalRoleMu

Replace the separate globalRoleTuplesMu and globalRolePermsMu with a
single globalRoleMu that protects both fields together. Readers now
acquire one lock and get a consistent snapshot of both tuples and perms,
eliminating the window where a goroutine could observe new tuples paired
with stale perms (or vice versa).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Zanzana: per-namespace selective GlobalRole tuple injection

Remove GlobalRoleBinding reconciliation from the reconciler loop — those
resources should not be synced to Zanzana.

Change GlobalRole tuple injection from "seed all GlobalRole tuples into
every namespace unconditionally" to "inject standalone tuples only for
GlobalRoles that are NOT referenced by any namespace Role". GlobalRoles
that ARE referenced by namespace Roles already have their permissions
inlined into the Role's tuples via translateRoleToTuples composition, so
standalone tuples for them would be redundant.

- fetchAndTranslateClusterGVRs → fetchGlobalRolePerms (perms-only, no
  tuple generation)
- Remove globalRoleTuples from Reconciler struct
- Rename setGlobalRoleData/getGlobalRoleData → setGlobalRolePerms/getGlobalRolePerms
- Track referencedGlobalRoles per namespace in the roles translator
  closure; inject unlinked GlobalRole tuples after the GVR loop

title: fix: resolve PSBT signature mismatch in descriptor-based multisig (Closes #320)
body:
This PR fixes PSBT signature mismatch errors in descriptor-based multisig workflows by enabling sign wallets to derive child private keys at the correct address index.

**Root Cause**: Watch wallet generates descriptor-derived public keys at varying indices (e.g., m/49'/1'/1/0/5), but sign wallet was using static WIF keys stored at index 0, causing PSBT signature verification to fail.

**Solution**: Store account-level extended private keys (xpriv) during key generation, then dynamically derive child keys at the correct address index when signing PSBTs.


### Database Schema
- Added `account_extended_privkey` column to `auth_account_key` table
- Created Atlas migration (20260112065432_add_account_extended_privkey.sql)
- Updated SQLC queries and generated models

### Key Generation
- Added `CreateKeyWithAccountXpriv()` method to HDKey generator
- Modified sign wallet auth key generation to store account xpriv
- Maintained backward compatibility with legacy workflows

### BIP32 Derivation Helpers
- Created `bip32_derivation.go` with utility functions:
  - `ParseBIP32DerivationPath()` - extracts address index from derivation path
  - `DeriveChildPrivateKey()` - derives child keys at specific indices
  - `ExtractAddressIndexFromPSBTInput()` - parses PSBT derivation metadata
- Comprehensive test coverage (16 tests, 100% passing)

### Signing Logic
- Updated `signMultisigPSBT()` to derive keys at correct index
- Added `deriveWIFForPSBT()` method that:
  - Checks for account xpriv availability
  - Parses PSBT to extract address index from BIP32 derivation info
  - Derives child private key at matching address index
  - Falls back to stored WIF for legacy (non-descriptor) workflows
- Ensures signing key matches descriptor-derived public key


- [x] Database migration verified (docker compose up)
- [x] Build verification passed (make check-build)
- [x] BIP32 derivation tests passed (16/16 tests)
- [x] Sign transaction use case tests passed
- [x] Linting fixes applied (make go-lint)
- [x] Backward compatibility maintained for legacy workflows


**Derivation Path Example**:
Watch wallet generates: m/49'/1'/1/0/5 (BIP32 derivation path)
PSBT includes: BIP32 derivation metadata with address_index=5
Sign wallet derives: Child key at index 5 from account xpriv
Result: Matching keys, successful PSBT signature verification

**Workflow Compatibility**:
- **Descriptor workflow** (new): Uses account xpriv for dynamic derivation
- **Legacy workflow** (existing): Uses stored WIF directly (no xpriv)


- Closes #320 (PSBT signature mismatch)
- Builds on #321 (keygen key inclusion in descriptors)
- Implements solution designed in #322 (root cause analysis)

title: feat: Add WalletConnect integration: x402 auto-payment, trading, and transfers
body: Adds WalletConnect as an alternative signer for all transaction flows — x402 auto-payments, DEX trading, and token transfers. Users can sign with hardware wallets (Ledger/Trezor) or mobile wallets without exposing private keys to the CLI. ### x402 Auto-Payment - Automatically handle HTTP 402 responses when a WalletConnect session is active - Signs EIP-712 `TransferWithAuthorization` typed data via `walletconnect sign-typed-data` - Retries the request with `Payment-Signature` header - Manual `--x402-payment-signature` override still works ### Trading (`nansen trade quote/execute --wallet walletconnect`) - `--wallet walletconnect` (or `wc`) on quote fetches address from WC session - Execute signs and broadcasts via connected wallet - Handles both `txHash` (wallet broadcasts) and `signedTransaction` (we broadcast via Trading API) responses - ERC-20 approval flow supported via WalletConnect - EVM only — Solana rejected with clear error ### Transfers (`nansen wallet send --wallet walletconnect`) - Native ETH and ERC-20 transfers via WalletConnect - Supports `--max` and `--dry-run` flags - Skips password prompt when using WalletConnect - **`src/walletconnect-exec.js`** (new) — shared subprocess helper for WalletConnect CLI calls - **`src/walletconnect-x402.js`** (new) — x402 payment construction, EIP-712 typed data - **`src/walletconnect-trading.js`** (new) — `getWalletConnectAddress`, `sendTransactionViaWalletConnect`, `sendApprovalViaWalletConnect` - **`src/api.js`** — intercept 402 responses, auto-sign and retry when wallet connected - **`src/trading.js`** — WC support in quote (signerType tracking) and execute (approval, simulation, tx via WC) - **`src/transfer.js`** — `sendTokensViaWalletConnect` for native and ERC-20 transfers - **`src/wallet.js`** — send handler detects `--wallet walletconnect`, skips password - **`src/cli.js`** — schema descriptions updated for walletconnect option - **Tests** — 50+ new tests across 5 test files (672 total pass) ## How to test ### Prerequisites 1. Install the [walletconnect CLI](https://github.com/AcrossCodes/agent-sdk) 2. Connect a wallet: `walletconnect connect --chain eip155:8453` 3. Verify: `walletconnect whoami --json` ### Trading via WalletConnect # Quote node src/index.js trade quote --chain base \ --from 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE \ --to 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 \ --amount 100000000000000 \ --wallet walletconnect # Execute (approve in wallet when prompted) node src/index.js trade execute --quote ### Transfer via WalletConnect node src/index.js wallet send --wallet walletconnect \ --to 0x... --amount 0.00001 --chain base ### x402 Auto-Payment NANSEN_API_KEY="x402-test" node src/index.js profiler balance \ --address 0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045 \ --chain ethereum --no-retry ### Error cases - `--wallet walletconnect --chain solana` → "WalletConnect is only supported for EVM chains" - No WC session → "No WalletConnect session active. Run: walletconnect connect" - [x] All 672 tests pass (`npm test`) - [x] Tested end-to-end: trade quote + execute via WalletConnect on Base (ETH → USDC) - [x] Tested end-to-end: wallet send via WalletConnect on Base (ETH transfer) - [x] Tested x402 auto-payment with live wallet signing - [x] Solana + WalletConnect rejected with clear error - [x] Manual `--x402-payment-signature` override still works
