title: Add support for sync functions and context managers in `Depends`
body:
Enables dependency injection for both synchronous and asynchronous code, making it easier to:
- Write pure computation dependencies without async boilerplate
- Integrate with existing synchronous libraries
- Mix sync and async dependencies in the same task

**Important**: Sync dependencies should NOT include blocking I/O. Use async dependencies for any I/O operations.


- **Extended type support**: `Depends()` now accepts sync functions, sync context managers (`@contextmanager`), async functions, and async context managers (`@asynccontextmanager`)
- **Automatic detection**: The system automatically detects the return type and handles it appropriately
- **Proper cleanup**: Sync context managers clean up correctly even when tasks fail
- **Dependency caching**: Works seamlessly across both sync and async dependencies

## Examples

### Sync dependency - pure computation
# ✅ Good: In-memory config, no I/O
def get_config() -> dict:
    return {"api_url": "https://api.example.com", "timeout": 30}

# ✅ Good: Pure computation
def build_query_params(
    user_id: int = TaskArgument(),
    config: dict = Depends(get_config)
) -> dict:
    return {"user_id": user_id, "timeout": config["timeout"]}

async def my_task(params: dict = Depends(build_query_params)) -> None:
    # Params computed without blocking
    await make_api_call(params)

### Async dependency - I/O operations
# ✅ Good: Network I/O uses async
async def fetch_user_data(user_id: int = TaskArgument()) -> dict:
    return await api_client.get(f"/users/{user_id}")

async def my_task(user: dict = Depends(fetch_user_data)) -> None:
    await process_user(user)

### What NOT to do
# ❌ Bad: Blocking I/O in sync dependency
def load_config_from_file() -> dict:
    with open("config.json") as f:  # Blocks event loop!
        return json.load(f)

# ✅ Good: Use async for file I/O instead
async def load_config_from_file() -> dict:
    async with aiofiles.open("config.json") as f:
        return json.loads(await f.read())

## Use Cases

**Best for sync dependencies:**
- Configuration merging and transformations
- Data structure manipulations
- Pure computations
- In-memory cache lookups

**Use async dependencies for:**
- Database queries
- Network requests
- File I/O
- Any operation requiring `await`


- Added 8 comprehensive tests in `test_dependencies.py` covering all sync scenarios
- Added 6 tests in `test_fundamentals.py` to document the feature
- All 14 new tests passing ✅
- All existing tests continue to pass
- 100% backward compatible

All dependency types work seamlessly together with automatic detection

title: Fix brand code race condition with Firestore atomic counter

- Two concurrent jobs received the same brand code (`NOMADNP-0012`) because `get_next_brand_code()` scanned Dropbox state — a classic TOCTOU race condition (jobs processed 0.86s apart)
- New service uses `@firestore.transactional` for atomic allocation, consistent with existing patterns in `rate_limit_service.py`

title: [TRTLLM-10421][perf] Fuse and optimize DSA indexer gather/scatter kernels
body:
- **Fuse DSA indexer kernel ops**: Combines cat + FP8 quantization + scatter into a single `fusedCatFp8Scatter` kernel, and adds a dedicated `indexerKCacheGather` kernel, reducing kernel launch overhead in the DSA attention indexer path
- **Optimize integer arithmetic**: Replaces expensive 64-bit divmod operations in gather/scatter kernels with precomputed strides and direct pointer arithmetic for the paged K cache layout
- **Fold scale multiplication**: Extends `fusedCatFp8` with an `output_scale_factor` parameter to fold downstream weight-scale multiplications into the quantization kernel

- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/fusedCatFp8Scatter.{cu,h}` — new fused cat+FP8+scatter kernel
- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/indexerKCacheGather.{cu,h}` — new K-cache gather kernel
- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/fusedCatFp8.{cu,h}` — add `output_scale_factor` param
- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/thop/FusedCatFp8ScatterOp.cpp` — PyTorch C++ binding for scatter op
- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/thop/IndexerKCacheGatherOp.cpp` — PyTorch C++ binding for gather op
- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/thop/CMakeLists.txt` — register new ops
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/attention_backend/sparse/dsa.py` — use fused ops in Python
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/custom_ops/cpp_custom_ops.py` — register new custom op schemas
- `tests/unittest/_torch/attention/sparse/test_dsa_indexer.py` — correctness tests

- [ ] New unit tests in `test_dsa_indexer.py` cover gather and scatter correctness against reference implementations
- [ ] Existing DSA attention tests should pass unchanged
- [ ] Run DeepSeek V3 serving benchmark to validate end-to-end performance improvement




  * Added fused FP8 quantization and K-cache scatter operation for optimized attention computation
  * Introduced K-cache gather functionality for efficient data retrieval
  * Added output scaling parameter to FP8 quantization for enhanced control

  * Added comprehensive test coverage for new K-cache and quantization operations

[TRTLLM-10421][perf] Optimize DSA indexer gather/scatter kernels

- Fuse DSA indexer kernel ops for reduced launch overhead
- Optimize gather/scatter kernel integer arithmetic
- Remove unnecessary non-power-of-two fallback in gather
- Remove unnecessary power-of-2 checks for tokens_per_block
- Update tests to use 3-arg gather API

Signed-off-by: JunyiXu-nv <219237550+JunyiXu-nv@users.noreply.github.com>
[TRTLLM-10421][fix] Wire fused cat+quant+scatter into DSA pre_indexer_proj

Move the k_cache scatter into the graph-capturable Op 1
(pre_indexer_proj) by having fused_cat_fp8_scatter write k_cache
directly, and drop the separate _update_k_cache step from Op 2.

To keep CUDA-graph replay correct when the graph is captured with a
larger batch than the live iteration, the scatter path now takes an
optional num_tokens scalar device tensor. The kernel reads it at
launch time and skips slot_mapping rows beyond num_tokens, so stale
padded slots are no longer written back to k_cache. The contiguous
fp8/scale outputs are still produced unconditionally since they are
consumed by the downstream indexer gather which is itself bounded by
num_tokens.

DSAtrtllmAttentionMetadata manages the scalar as a (1,) int32 CUDA
tensor owned by cuda_graph_buffers with a pinned host mirror, and
copies num_tokens into it in prepare(). The indexer test helper is
updated to call the standalone scatter op directly since
_update_k_cache is removed.

Signed-off-by: JunyiXu-nv <219237550+JunyiXu-nv@users.noreply.github.com>
[TRTLLM-10421][fix] Align test_fused_cat_fp8_scatter with scatter op schema

indexer_k_cache_scatter_op now requires an int num_tokens parameter and
consumes the scatter inputs in their native dtypes (FP8 for k_fp8,
float32 for k_scale) rather than uint8 byte views. Pass k_fp8 / k_scale
through directly in the expected 2-D shape instead of reinterpret-casting
them to uint8, and provide num_tokens.

Also drop the non-power-of-two block-size test: the kv cache manager
always uses a power-of-two tokens_per_block, so the fused gather/scatter
kernels' pow2 precondition is always satisfied and the fallback path
tested here is not reachable in practice.

Signed-off-by: JunyiXu-nv <219237550+JunyiXu-nv@users.noreply.github.com>

title: Fix CANCEL_NEW strategy not cancelling late runs
body:
closes #21060

## summary

this PR fixes the `CANCEL_NEW` concurrency strategy not actually cancelling runs that go late when the deployment's concurrency limit is full. runs were accumulating in a `Late` state instead of being cancelled.

## the bug

the `CANCEL_NEW` strategy is only enforced by the `SecureFlowConcurrencySlots` orchestration rule, which fires on `* → PENDING` transitions. but when a runner/worker is at capacity, runs never reach that transition — they stay `SCHEDULED` until the `MarkLateRuns` service marks them `Late`. since `MarkLateRuns` had no awareness of deployment concurrency options, these runs were never cancelled.

## the fix

modified `mark_flow_run_late` in the `MarkLateRuns` service to check the deployment's concurrency options before deciding how to handle a late run. when the deployment uses `CANCEL_NEW` and its concurrency limit is fully occupied, the run is cancelled instead of marked `Late`.

<summary>reproduction script</summary>

import asyncio
import time

import prefect
from prefect import flow
from prefect.client.schemas.objects import (
    ConcurrencyLimitConfig,
    ConcurrencyLimitStrategy,
    StateType,
from prefect.runner import Runner


@flow
def blocking_flow():
    time.sleep(120)


async def main():
    runner = Runner(name="test-cancel-new", limit=1, pause_on_shutdown=False)
    async with runner:
        await runner.add_flow(
            blocking_flow,
            name="test-cancel-new-deployment",
            concurrency_limit=ConcurrencyLimitConfig(
                limit=1,
                collision_strategy=ConcurrencyLimitStrategy.CANCEL_NEW,
            ),
        runner_task = asyncio.create_task(runner.start())
        try:
            async with prefect.get_client() as client:
                deployment = None
                for _ in range(10):
                    await asyncio.sleep(1)
                    for d in await client.read_deployments():
                        if d.name == "test-cancel-new-deployment":
                            deployment = d
                            break
                    if deployment:
                        break
                assert deployment

                blocker = await client.create_flow_run_from_deployment(deployment.id)
                for _ in range(15):
                    await asyncio.sleep(2)
                    blocker = await client.read_flow_run(blocker.id)
                    if blocker.state.type == StateType.RUNNING:
                        break
                assert blocker.state.type == StateType.RUNNING

                excess_ids = []
                for _ in range(3):
                    run = await client.create_flow_run_from_deployment(deployment.id)
                    excess_ids.append(run.id)

                await asyncio.sleep(35)
                for rid in excess_ids:
                    run = await client.read_flow_run(rid)
                    # BUG: these are Late, not Cancelled
                    print(f"  {rid}: {run.state.type}/{run.state.name}")
        finally:
            await runner.astop()
            runner_task.cancel()


asyncio.run(main())


## test plan

- [x] unit test: cancels late run when deployment has CANCEL_NEW and limit is full
- [x] unit test: marks late (not cancelled) when CANCEL_NEW but limit has available slots
- [x] unit test: marks late (not cancelled) when deployment uses ENQUEUE strategy with full limit
- [x] all 9 existing + new tests pass
commit_msgs:
Fix CANCEL_NEW strategy not cancelling late runs when limit is full

The MarkLateRuns service now checks deployment concurrency options before
marking a run as Late. When a deployment uses CANCEL_NEW and its
concurrency limit is fully occupied, runs are cancelled instead of
accumulating in a Late state.

closes #21060

title: Fix plugin install EEXIST error
body:
- Rename plugin from `qmd` to `qmd-search` in `marketplace.json` to fix `EEXIST` error during installation

The plugin name `"qmd"` conflicts with the `qmd` executable file at the repo root. When Claude Code installs the plugin, it creates the path `cache/<marketplace>/<plugin-name>/` and copies repo contents into it. Since both the directory and the file are named `qmd`, `mkdir` fails with `EEXIST`.

Renaming the plugin to `qmd-search` avoids the conflict.

title: [Agent] feat(vulkan): implement Vulkan→Metal bridge in PVThinLibretroFrontend
body:
Implements the Vulkan→Metal frame delivery path in `PVThinLibretroFrontend` — the last stub piece from issue #2624.

The Vulkan context setup (VkInstance / VkDevice / VkQueue via MoltenVK) was already wired. What was missing was actually getting rendered frames onto the screen.

### What changed

**`PVThinLibretroFrontend.mm`**
- `thin_vulkan_set_command_buffers` — submits the core's `VkCommandBuffer`s to the MoltenVK queue via `vkQueueSubmit`, including optional signal semaphore
- `thin_vulkan_set_signal_semaphore` — stores the semaphore for use in the next `vkQueueSubmit`
- `thin_vulkan_wait_sync_index` — drains the queue via `vkQueueWaitIdle` so the core can safely reuse resources
- `thin_vulkan_set_image` — extracts the `MTLTexture` backing the core's `VkImage` using `vkGetMTLTextureMVK` (primary, works on all MoltenVK) or `vkExportMetalObjectsEXT` (preferred on MoltenVK ≥ 1.2), then delivers it to the render delegate
- Loads `vkQueueSubmit`, `vkQueueWaitIdle`, `vkGetMTLTextureMVK`, `vkExportMetalObjectsEXT` in `createVulkanDevice`

**`PVCoreBridge/Protocols/PVRenderDelegate.swift`**
- New `PVRenderDelegateMetal` `@objc` protocol with optional `didRenderFrameWithMTLTexture(_:)`

**`PVMetalViewController.swift`**
- Conforms to `PVRenderDelegateMetal`: `didRenderFrameWithMTLTexture(_:)` blits the Vulkan-rendered `MTLTexture` into the existing input-texture/draw pipeline and signals the front-buffer condition

### Rendering flow

Vulkan core renders into VkImage
  → set_command_buffers  : vkQueueSubmit to MoltenVK queue
  → set_image            : vkGetMTLTextureMVK(VkImage) → MTLTexture
  → didRenderFrameWithMTLTexture(_:)
  → blit MTLTexture → inputTexture
  → isFrontBufferReady = true
  → draw(in:) blits inputTexture to screen

### Notes
- The `vkGetMTLTextureMVK` function is deprecated in newer MoltenVK but works on all versions without any special image creation flags — it's used as the universal fallback
- `vkExportMetalObjectsEXT` is the preferred path but requires MoltenVK ≥ 1.2 and the VkImage to have been created with `VkExportMetalObjectCreateInfoEXT` (which well-behaved Vulkan cores should do)
- Single-buffer sync: `get_sync_index` returns 0, `get_sync_index_mask` returns 1; `wait_sync_index` calls `vkQueueWaitIdle`. Proper double-buffering with fences is a future improvement.

- [ ] Build with `Provenance-Lite` scheme (iOS Simulator) — no compile errors
- [ ] Test with a Vulkan libretro core (e.g. parallel-n64, vulkan ppsspp)
- [ ] Verify frames appear on screen (not black)
- [ ] Verify no GPU validation errors from MoltenVK

title: fix(build): reduce codegen-units for low-memory devices (fixes #395)
body:
Fixed OOM (out-of-memory) compilation failures on low-memory devices like Raspberry Pi 3 (1GB RAM) by reducing `codegen-units` from 8 to 1 in the release profile.

On devices with limited RAM (e.g., Raspberry Pi 3 with 1GB), the release build would fail with SIGKILL during compilation because the parallel codegen with 8 units consumed too much memory.

error: could not compile `zeroclaw` (lib)
...
(signal: 9, SIGKILL: kill)

Reduced `codegen-units` from 8 to 1 in `[profile.release]`. This serializes compilation and significantly reduces memory usage during the build process.

### Trade-offs
- ✅ Enables compilation on low-memory devices (1GB RAM)
- ❌ Compilation is slower (sequential vs parallel)
- ✅ Binary size unchanged
- ✅ Runtime performance unchanged

- [x] All library tests pass (1 pre-existing flaky test unrelated to this change)
- [x] Release build completes successfully
- [x] Binary size unchanged (~6.3MB)

## Related Issue
Fixes #395

fix(build): reduce codegen-units for low-memory devices

Reduced codegen-units from 8 to 1 in the release profile to prevent
OOM (out-of-memory) compilation failures on low-memory devices like
Raspberry Pi 3 (1GB RAM).

The previous setting of 8 parallel codegen units consumed too much
memory during compilation, causing the process to be killed with
SIGKILL on memory-constrained devices.

With codegen-units = 1, compilation is serialized and uses significantly
less RAM, enabling successful builds on devices with limited memory.

Trade-offs:
- Compilation is slower (sequential vs parallel)
- Binary size and runtime performance are unchanged

title: [e2e-framework] Fix kindvm DDA deployment check for nil slice
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fix a bug in the kindvm scenario where the DDA (DatadogAgent) was deployed even when no DDA options were provided.


This bug was discovered while migrating the datadog-operator e2e tests from `test-infra-definitions` to `e2e-framework` (see [datadog-operator#2503](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-operator/pull/2503)).

When using the kindvm scenario with `WithDeployOperator()` but without `WithOperatorDDAOptions()`, a DDA was incorrectly deployed with the default namespace "datadog", causing test failures.

## The Bug

1. `operatorDDAOptions` was initialized as an empty slice `[]Option{}` in `GetRunParams()`
2. The check `params.operatorDDAOptions != nil` at `run.go:265` passes for empty slice (Go: `[]T{} != nil` is `true`)
3. This caused DDA deployment with default namespace "datadog" even when no options were provided

```go
// Go behavior:
var emptySlice []string = []string{}
var nilSlice []string = nil

fmt.Println(emptySlice != nil)  // true - empty slice is NOT nil!
fmt.Println(nilSlice != nil)    // false

## The Fix

1. Initialize `operatorDDAOptions` as `nil` instead of empty slice
2. Change the check from `!= nil` to `len() > 0`
3. Add `WithoutDDA()` function for explicit DDA removal (aligns with EKS scenario)


### `run_args.go`
- Changed initialization: `operatorDDAOptions: nil` (was `[]Option{}`)
- Added `WithoutDDA()` function (like EKS scenario has)
- Updated `WithOperatorDDAOptions()` to handle nil initialization

### `run.go`
- Changed condition: `len(params.operatorDDAOptions) > 0` (was `!= nil`)
- Changed env.Agent nil check accordingly

## Comparison with EKS scenario

| Feature | EKS Scenario | kindvm (before) | kindvm (after) |
|---------|--------------|-----------------|----------------|
| `WithoutDDA()` | ✅ Yes | ❌ No | ✅ Yes |
| Default `operatorDDAOptions` | `[]Option{}` | `[]Option{}` | `nil` |
| DDA deployment check | N/A | `!= nil` (buggy) | `len() > 0` |


- [x] Code compiles successfully
- [ ] CI tests pass

## Related PRs

- [datadog-operator#2503](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-operator/pull/2503) - Migration that discovered this bug

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix(e2e-framework): use AND instead of OR for env.Agent nil check

Fix bug where env.Agent was incorrectly set to nil even when an agent
was deployed via Helm (not operator). The condition should set env.Agent
to nil only when NEITHER the Helm agent NOR the DDA with operator is
deployed (AND), not when either one is missing (OR).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix(e2e-framework): refresh field values after provisioning to detect nil assignments

When provisioners set env fields to nil (e.g., env.Agent = nil when no agent
is deployed), the cached reflect.Value in retainedValues doesn't see this change.
This causes buildEnvFromResources to fail with "resource named Agent has no
import key set and no annotation" because it still sees the non-nil zero value
that was set by CreateEnv.

This fix re-reads the field values from the env struct after provisioning
completes, ensuring buildEnvFromResources sees the current state of the fields,
including any that were set to nil by the provisioners.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix(e2e-framework): initialize agentOptions as nil instead of empty slice

The condition `params.agentOptions == nil` was always false because
agentOptions was initialized as an empty slice `[]kubernetesagentparams.Option{}`
instead of `nil`. In Go, an empty slice is not equal to nil.

This is the same pattern fixed for operatorDDAOptions in commit 47e4bc1576.

The fix ensures that when no agent options are provided and no DDA
options are provided, the condition in run.go:281 correctly triggers
and sets env.Agent = nil, preventing the "resource named Agent has
no import key set" error during teardown.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix(e2e-framework): use len() checks for agentOptions slice

The previous commit (8b71a5b8b2) changed agentOptions initialization from
empty slice to nil, but broke CI because run.go still used != nil checks.

Changes:
- Replace `params.agentOptions != nil` with `len(params.agentOptions) > 0`
  at lines 79, 159, 228 in run.go
- Replace `params.agentOptions == nil` with `len(params.agentOptions) == 0`
  at line 281 in run.go
- Update kind_test.go to explicitly request agent deployment with
  WithAgentOptions() since agent is no longer deployed by default

fix(e2e-framework): change WithClusterName to accept StringInput

Change WithClusterName parameter type from pulumi.StringOutput to
pulumi.StringInput, allowing callers to pass either:
- pulumi.String("value") for plain strings
- pulumi.StringOutput for dynamic values

Update kind_test.go to use pulumi.String("kind-test").

title: Add --pro and --rsc flags to install generator
body:
Adds `--pro` and `--rsc` flags to `rails g react_on_rails:install`, plus standalone generators for upgrading existing apps.

**New commands:**
# Fresh install with Pro
rails g react_on_rails:install --pro

# Fresh install with RSC (includes Pro)
rails g react_on_rails:install --rsc

# Upgrade existing React on Rails app to Pro
rails g react_on_rails:pro

# Upgrade existing Pro app to RSC
rails g react_on_rails:rsc

Closes #2277

## What's Included

### Pro Generator (`--pro`)
- Creates `config/initializers/react_on_rails_pro.rb` with Node Renderer config
- Creates `client/node-renderer.js` bootstrap file
- Appends node-renderer process to `Procfile.dev`
- Installs `react-on-rails-pro` and `react-on-rails-pro-node-renderer` npm packages
- Handles upgrade from base React on Rails (removes `react-on-rails` package when installing Pro)

### RSC Generator (`--rsc`)
- Creates `config/webpack/rscWebpackConfig.js` for React Server Components bundle
- Creates HelloServer example component (JSX and TypeScript variants)
- Creates `HelloServerController` and view
- Adds RSC routes (`rsc_payload_route`, `hello_server`)
- Installs `react-on-rails-rsc` npm package
- Pins React to `~19.0.4` (security: CVE-2025-55182, CVE-2025-67779, CVE-2026-23864)
- Adds RSC config to `react_on_rails_pro.rb` initializer

### Standalone Generators
- `react_on_rails:pro` — upgrades an existing React on Rails app to Pro
- `react_on_rails:rsc` — upgrades an existing Pro app to RSC
- Reuses the same setup modules as the install generator flags
- Prerequisite validation (Pro gem required, React version check for RSC)

### Webpack Config Transforms
- Renames `generateWebpackConfigs.js` → `ServerClientOrBoth.js` with RSC bundle support
- Adds `rscBundle` parameter to `serverWebpackConfig.js` for RSC builds
- Adds client/server webpack config conditionals for Pro

- USAGE files for standalone Pro and RSC generators
- Generator details in `docs/api-reference/generator-details.md`
- Pro installation guide additions in `react_on_rails_pro/docs/installation.md`

- Unit tests for Pro/RSC prerequisite validation
- Integration tests for `--pro`, `--rsc`, and all flag combinations (`--typescript`, `--redux`, `--rspack`)
- Integration tests for standalone `pro` and `rsc` generators
- Idempotency tests
- Regression test for webpack config transforms

## Design Decisions
- **Reusable modules**: Pro and RSC setup logic lives in `ProSetup` and `RscSetup` modules, shared between install flags and standalone generators
- **Idempotent**: All generators are safe to run multiple times — existing files aren't overwritten, Procfile entries aren't duplicated
- **Flag combinations**: Works with `--typescript`, `--redux`, `--rspack`
- **React version pinning**: RSC pins to `~19.0.4` (not latest 19.x) because RSC support requires 19.0.x specifically


- [x] `bundle exec rspec spec/react_on_rails/generators/` — all generator tests pass
- [x] Manual verification in test app — Pro and RSC setup works end-to-end
- [ ] CI: `rspec-package-tests`, `markdown-link-check`, pre-commit hooks



  - Added --pro and --rsc generator flags and standalone generators; auto-sets up Node Renderer, Procfile.dev entries, webpack transforms, and dependency changes.
  - Scaffolds React Server Components (HelloServer + client LikeButton), routes, controller, views, and RSC webpack bundle.

  - Expanded generator docs, Pro installation/usage, Node Renderer guide, and RSC usage/prerequisites.

  - Expanded generator and integration specs covering Pro, RSC, TypeScript, Redux, Rspack, and idempotence.

Changes:
- Remove RSCPayloadRenderer (not needed, rsc_payload_route handles it)
- Remove AsyncRendering + enable_async_react_rendering (only needed
  for pages with multiple concurrent async_react_component calls)

- The streaming-server-rendering.md documentation

The spec is copied when `rails g react_on_rails:dev_tests --rsc` is run,
following the same pattern as hello_world_spec.rb.

The stream_view_containing_react_components method requires a template:

Skip HelloWorld entirely when using --rsc flag

RSC uses HelloServer as the example component, completely replacing HelloWorld.
Previously, HelloWorld controller/route/layout were created by base_generator
unconditionally, leaving a broken state (route exists but no view/components).

- base_generator.rb: Skip HelloWorld route, controller, layout, directory,
  and CSS when use_rsc? is true
- hello_server/index.html.erb: Remove broken comparison link to /hello_world
- install_generator_spec.rb: Expanded test to verify HelloWorld controller
  and route are NOT created with --rsc

Add RSC-required settings to node-renderer.js template

The Node Renderer VM requires these settings for RSC to work:
- additionalContext: { URL, AbortController } for async operations
- stubTimers: false to allow working timer functions
- replayServerAsyncOperationLogs for debugging

Without stubTimers: false, the RSC runtime hangs during VM
initialization because timer functions are stubbed by default.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Improve Procfile.dev naming to be bundler-agnostic

- Rename wp-client → dev-server (not webpack-specific)
- Rename wp-server → server-bundle (describes output)
- Rename rails-rsc-assets → rsc-bundle (consistent naming)
- Remove redundant WEBPACK_SERVE=true (set automatically by Shakapacker)
- Change RENDERER_LOG_LEVEL from info → debug for development

The old wp-* naming was misleading since Shakapacker supports both
webpack and rspack bundlers via the --rspack flag.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Pin Pro npm packages to exact gem version

Pro packages (react-on-rails-pro, react-on-rails-pro-node-renderer) were
being installed without version pinning, causing npm to install the latest
stable version instead of the version matching the gem.

This caused version mismatch errors when using pre-release gem versions,
as the version checker requires gem and npm package versions to match.

Uses VersionSyntaxConverter to convert Ruby gem format (16.2.0.rc.0) to
npm semver format (16.2.0-rc.0), with fallback to latest if conversion fails.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Fix running_generator? detection using defined?(Rails::Generators)

The previous ARGV-based check never worked because Rails replaces ARGV
with command-specific arguments before initializers run. When running
`rails generate foo`, ARGV contains `["foo"]`, not `["generate", "foo"]`.

This caused the Pro upgrade scenario to fail with a validation error,
requiring users to manually set REACT_ON_RAILS_SKIP_VALIDATION=true.

The fix uses `defined?(Rails::Generators)` which follows the same pattern
Rails uses for detecting Server and Console contexts. Rails only loads
the Generators module during generator commands.

Updated tests to:
- Stub running_generator? for skip_version_validation? tests (proper isolation)
- Verify running_generator? delegat

title: feat(ingest/kafka-connect): Kafka connect infer lineage from DataHub
body:
This PR adds **automatic lineage inference from DataHub** to the Kafka Connect source connector. Instead of relying solely on connector manifests, the ingestion can now query DataHub's metadata graph to resolve schemas and generate both table-level and column-level lineage.


Currently, Kafka Connect lineage extraction is limited by what's explicitly declared in connector configurations. This PR enables:

1. **Wildcard pattern expansion**: Connectors configured with patterns like `table.include.list: "database.*"` can now be resolved to actual table names by querying DataHub
2. **Column-level lineage**: Generate fine-grained lineage showing which source columns map to Kafka topic fields
3. **Schema-aware ingestion**: Leverage existing metadata in DataHub to enrich Kafka Connect lineage without requiring external database connections
4. **Auto-enabled for Confluent Cloud**: Schema resolver automatically enabled for Confluent Cloud environments where enhanced lineage is most valuable


### New Configuration Options

Added three new configuration fields to `KafkaConnectSourceConfig`:

source:
  type: kafka-connect
  config:
    # Enable DataHub schema resolution
    # Auto-enabled for Confluent Cloud, disabled for OSS by default
    use_schema_resolver: true
    
    # Expand wildcard patterns to concrete table names (default: true)
    schema_resolver_expand_patterns: true
    
    # Generate column-level lineage (default: true)
    schema_resolver_finegrained_lineage: true

### Auto-Enable for Confluent Cloud

**New behavior**: `use_schema_resolver` is automatically enabled when Confluent Cloud is detected via:
- `confluent_cloud_environment_id` + `confluent_cloud_cluster_id` configuration
- URI pattern matching (`api.confluent.cloud/connect/v1/`)

Users can opt-out by explicitly setting `use_schema_resolver: false`.

### Core Components

1. **SchemaResolver Integration** (`connector_registry.py`):
   - New `create_schema_resolver()` method to instantiate schema resolvers with platform-specific configurations
   - Automatically attaches resolvers to connector instances during creation
   - Passes pipeline context through the instantiation chain

2. **Fine-Grained Lineage Extraction** (`common.py`):
   - New `_extract_fine_grained_lineage()` method in `BaseConnector`
   - Assumes 1:1 column mapping between source tables and Kafka topics (typical for CDC connectors)
   - Generates `FineGrainedLineageClass` instances for column-level lineage

3. **Enhanced Source Connectors** (`source_connectors.py`):
   - **Snowflake Source Connector**: Pattern expansion support (e.g., `ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.*` → actual tables)
   - **Debezium Connectors**: Support for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB CDC
   - **JDBC Source Connector**: Generic JDBC source with pattern matching
   - **Mongo Source Connector**: MongoDB source with collection pattern expansion
   - **ConfigDriven Source Connector**: Generic connector for new/unsupported connector types

4. **Pattern Matching** (`pattern_matchers.py`):
   - New module for consistent pattern matching across all connectors
   - Supports database wildcards (`database.*`, `schema.table*`, etc.)
   - Handles platform-specific naming conventions

5. **Configuration Constants** (`config_constants.py`):
   - Centralized configuration key definitions
   - Reduces code duplication and typos
   - Easier maintenance and documentation

6. **Improved Topic Handling**:
   - Refactored topic extraction to distinguish between topics from API vs Kafka cluster
   - Better handling of Confluent Cloud scenarios (no direct Kafka access)
   - Improved sink connector topic filtering

### Code Quality Improvements

- Removed redundant connector instantiation in topic derivation
- Enhanced null safety with comprehensive checks before schema resolver access
- Improved error handling with detailed logging and graceful fallbacks
- Sanitized test data (removed real company names)
- Better separation of concerns (API topics vs Kafka topics)


### OSS Kafka Connect (Default Behavior)

source:
  type: kafka-connect
  config:
    connect_uri: "http://localhost:8083"
    # use_schema_resolver: false (default - no change in behavior)

### Confluent Cloud (Auto-Enabled)

source:
  type: kafka-connect
  config:
    confluent_cloud_environment_id: "env-123"
    confluent_cloud_cluster_id: "lkc-456"
    # use_schema_resolver: true (auto-enabled!)
    # Pattern expansion and column-level lineage work out of the box

### Confluent Cloud (Opt-Out)

source:
  type: kafka-connect
  config:
    confluent_cloud_environment_id: "env-123"
    confluent_cloud_cluster_id: "lkc-456"
    use_schema_resolver: false  # Explicitly disabled

### OSS with Schema Resolver (Explicit Enable)

source:
  type: kafka-connect
  config:
    connect_uri: "http://localhost:8083"
    use_schema_resolver: true
    schema_resolver_expand_patterns: true
    schema_resolver_finegrained_lineage: true


- ✅ **Comprehensive test coverage** across 15 unit test modules
- ✅ All linting checks pass (ruff)
- ✅ All type checks pass (mypy)
- ✅ Integration tests pass for OSS and Confluent Cloud scenarios

**Test modules:**
- `test_kafka_connect.py` - Core connector tests
- `test_kafka_connect_config_validation.py` - Auto-enable logic tests (8 new tests)
- `test_kafka_connect_schema_resolver.py` - Schema resolver integration
- `test_kafka_connect_snowflake_source.py` - Snowflake connector tests
- `test_kafka_connect_pattern_matchers.py` - Pattern matching tests
- `test_kafka_connect_config_constants.py` - Configuration validation
- `test_kafka_connect_connector_registry.py` - Connector registration tests
- Plus 8 additional test modules for specific features

## Documentation

- Updated `docs/sources/kafka-connect/kafka-connect.md` with:
  - Auto-enable behavior explanation
  - Configuration examples for OSS and Confluent Cloud
  - Prerequisites and recommended ingestion order
  - Opt-out instructions


**None** - All features are opt-in (or auto-enabled only for Confluent Cloud). Existing Kafka Connect ingestions continue to work unchanged.

**Default behavior:**
- OSS: `use_schema_resolver: false` (unchanged behavior)
- Confluent Cloud: `use_schema_resolver: true` (auto-enabled, can be disabled)
- No changes to existing connector behavior without explicit configuration

## Prerequisites for Schema Resolver

**IMPORTANT**: For schema resolver to work, source database tables must be ingested into DataHub **before** running Kafka Connect ingestion. Without prior database ingestion, schema resolver will not find table metadata.

**Recommended ingestion order:**
1. Ingest source databases (Postgres, MySQL, Snowflake, etc.) into DataHub
2. Run Kafka Connect ingestion (with schema resolver enabled/auto-enabled)
3. Enjoy enhanced lineage with column-level mappings!

title: Iris/CW: namespace-qualify RBAC and isolate canary lifecycle
body:
Fixes #3698 — multiple Iris instances on the same CKS cluster no longer interfere with each other's lifecycle.

**Problem:** ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding were hardcoded to `iris-controller` (cluster-scoped), so tearing down one Iris namespace destroyed RBAC for all others. The canary workflow also ran in the default `iris` namespace, so its nightly teardown would kill any persistent workloads there.

**Fix:**
1. Qualify cluster-scoped RBAC names with namespace (`iris-controller-{ns}`)
2. Move the canary to its own namespace (`iris-canary`) via a dedicated config, freeing `iris` for persistent use

## What changed

- **`coreweave.py`** — `ensure_rbac()` creates `iris-controller-{namespace}` ClusterRole/Binding; `stop_controller()` cleans them up
- **`coreweave-canary.yaml`** (new) — canary-specific config with `namespace: iris-canary`, `label_prefix: iris-canary`, separate `remote_state_dir`
- **`marin-canary-ferry-cw.yaml`** — points at `coreweave-canary.yaml`; concurrency group, teardown label, and diagnostics namespace all scoped to `iris-canary`
- **`coreweave.md`** — RBAC table updated

<summary>Why key on namespace, not label_prefix?</summary>

RBAC binds a ServiceAccount (namespaced) to a ClusterRole. Keying on namespace keeps the naming aligned with K8s's own isolation boundary. Two configs with the same namespace but different `label_prefix` should share one ClusterRole, not create two that grant the same SA identical permissions.

<summary>What already worked (no changes needed)</summary>

- **NodePool isolation** — already uses `label_prefix` for names and labels
- **Namespaced resources** (SA, Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, Secret) — already isolated by namespace
- **GCP platform** — doesn't use K8s RBAC


- [x] Existing `test_coreweave_platform.py` suite passes (47 tests)
- [x] New `test_rbac_isolation_across_namespaces` — two platforms create/teardown non-overlapping RBAC
- [x] `./infra/pre-commit.py --all-files --fix` passes
- [x] **Manual on CW** — verified end-to-end ([run 23119639900](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/23119639900))

<summary>Manual test details</summary>

Started default cluster (`namespace: iris`) from laptop, then triggered the canary workflow on this branch with `target_tokens=65536`.

**During canary run:** both ClusterRoles coexisted:
iris-controller-iris          2026-03-15T20:52:22Z
iris-controller-iris-canary   2026-03-15T21:29:19Z

**After canary teardown:**
| Check | Result |
| `iris-controller-iris` ClusterRole | Still exists |
| Default controller pod (`iris` namespace) | 1/1 Running |
| `iris-controller-iris-canary` ClusterRole | Gone (cleaned up) |
| Canary NodePools (`iris-canary-*`) | Gone (cleaned up) |
| Default NodePools (`iris-*`) | Unaffected |

The canary ferry itself failed at the training step (unrelated — likely 65k token edge case), but `Start CoreWeave cluster`, `Submit canary ferry`, and `Tear down CoreWeave cluster` all succeeded, which is what matters for the isolation test.

Note: a stale `iris-controller` ClusterRole from a pre-PR run (Feb 19) was found on the cluster — confirms the problem this PR fixes.

Iris/CW: namespace-qualify cluster-scoped RBAC to support isolated lifecycles

ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding names were hardcoded to "iris-controller",
causing collisions when multiple Iris instances shared a CKS cluster. Key on
namespace instead (e.g. "iris-controller-iris", "iris-controller-iris-canary")
so teardown of one cluster doesn't break another.

Adds a dedicated coreweave-canary.yaml config with namespace/label_prefix
"iris-canary" and points the canary workflow at it, so its nightly teardown
no longer interferes with persistent workloads in the default "iris" namespace.

Closes #3698

title: bun
body:
Complete migration from Yarn 4.6.0 to Bun 1.3.2 as the package manager for the Plate monorepo.

### Key Changes

- **Package Manager**: Upgraded from Yarn 4.6.0 to Bun 1.3.2
- **Lockfile**: Replaced `yarn.lock` with `bun.lock` (6,023 entries)
- **Configuration**: Removed Yarn-specific files (`.yarnrc.yml`, `.yarn/` directory)
- **Scripts**: Updated all `package.json` scripts to use `bun` commands
- **CI/CD**: Created new `bun-install` GitHub Action and updated all workflows
- **Documentation**: Updated `CLAUDE.md`, tech stack documentation, and README

### Files Changed

**Removed:**
- `.yarnrc.yml`
- `yarn.lock` (22,275 lines)
- `.yarn/plugins/` and `.yarn/releases/`
- `.github/actions/yarn-nm-install/`

**Created:**
- `bun.lock` (6,023 entries)
- `.github/actions/bun-install/action.yml`
- `.claude/docs/plans/yarn-to-bun-migration-plan.md`
- `ZOD_ISSUE.md` (documenting known issue)

**Modified:**
- Root `package.json` (packageManager, engines, all scripts)
- All 51 package `package.json` files
- All GitHub workflow files (`.github/workflows/*.yml`)
- `CLAUDE.md` (command documentation)
- `.cursor/rules/tech-stack.mdc`

### Benefits

- **Faster Installation**: Bun's native speed improvements
- **Faster Execution**: Built-in task runner performance
- **Simpler Configuration**: No custom Yarn plugins needed
- **Better Monorepo Support**: Native workspace support

### Verification

- ✅ All packages build successfully
- ✅ Type checking passes
- ✅ Linting passes
- ✅ All tests pass (2,233 tests, 32 snapshots)
- ✅ CI/CD workflows updated and validated

### Breaking Changes

**For Contributors:**
- Must install Bun 1.3.2 or later
- Replace all `yarn` commands with `bun`
- Replace `npx` with `bunx`

**For CI/CD:**
- GitHub workflows now use `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2` action
- Cache keys updated to use `bun.lock`

### Migration Commands

# Old (Yarn)
yarn install
yarn build
yarn test
yarn workspace @platejs/core build

# New (Bun)
bun install
bun build
bun test
bun workspace @platejs/core build

### Test Plan

- [x] Clean install: `rm -rf node_modules && bun install`
- [x] Build all packages: `bun build`
- [x] Type check: `bun typecheck`
- [x] Run linting: `bun check`
- [x] Run tests: `bun test`
- [x] Verify CI workflows syntax
- [x] Test individual package operations

### Known Issues

- **Zod Version Issue**: There's a known peer dependency warning with Zod (documented in `ZOD_ISSUE.md`)
  - Not blocking for this migration
  - Can be addressed in a follow-up PR

### Rollback Plan

If issues arise:
1. Revert the commit: `git revert ae6271b1e`
2. Restore Yarn: `yarn install` (will recreate `yarn.lock`)
3. Rebuild: `yarn build`

### References

- Migration plan: `.claude/docs/plans/yarn-to-bun-migration-plan.md`
- Bun Documentation: https://bun.sh/docs
- Setup Bun Action: https://github.com/oven-sh/setup-bun

title: feat(sdk): add runs.summaries() for bulk summary metrics retrieval
body:
- Adds `runs.summaries()` method to the `Runs` class, providing a simple way to collect summary metrics from all matching runs into a single DataFrame
- Supports polars, pandas, and list-of-dicts output formats, following the same pattern as `runs.configs()` from #11282
- Calls `upgrade_to_full()` for parallel pre-loading of lazy run data, avoiding the N+1 query problem when `lazy=True` (the default)

### API

title: Fix DeepSeek chat templates to handle tool call arguments type checking (#11700)
body:
This commit fixes the double JSON encoding issue in DeepSeek chat templates (v3, v3.1, v3.2) that was causing incorrect tool call formatting in multi-round function calling scenarios, particularly affecting BFCL_V3 evaluations.

Problem:
- Templates were applying `|tojson` filter unconditionally to tool arguments
- When arguments were already JSON strings (from previous model outputs), this caused double-escaping: '{"symbol": "NVDA"}' → '"{\\"symbol\\": \\"NVDA\\"}"'
- This broke multi-round function calling workflows

Solution:
- Added type checking: only apply `|tojson` when arguments are dict/object
- If arguments are already a string, use them as-is
- Pattern: `(arguments if arguments is string else arguments|tojson)`

Testing:
- Created comprehensive unit tests in test/srt/test_deepseek_chat_templates.py
- Tests cover dict arguments, string arguments, and mixed scenarios
- All tests pass for v3, v3.1, and v3.2 templates

Fixes #11700

Fixes `hypergraph(entity_types=['single'], direct=True)` to return empty DataFrame with proper column structure, enabling `get_degrees()` to work without KeyError across ALL engines (pandas, cudf, dask, dask_cudf).

## Core Fix
**Problem**: Single entity + direct mode returned empty DataFrame with NO columns  
**Impact**: `get_degrees()` failed with `KeyError: "None of [Index(['src', 'dst'])] are in the [columns]"`  
**Solution**: Empty edges DataFrame now has proper column structure (src, dst, edgeType, EventID, etc.)

- **`mt_series()`** - Properly creates empty Series for dask/dask_cudf by wrapping pandas Series
- **`format_direct_edges()`** - Uses `df_coercion()` pattern for cross-engine empty DataFrame creation
- **`get_indegrees()`** - Uses `.assign()` for cross-engine compatibility instead of direct assignment
- **`_safe_len()`** - Fixed dask_cudf meta parameter (`meta=pd.Series([], dtype='int64')` instead of `meta=int`)
- **Removed unnecessary persist()** - Dask_cudf no longer forces premature materialization, preserving lazy evaluation

- dask: `TestHypergraphDask::test_single_entity_direct_with_get_degrees()`

**Root cause fixed:**
The issue wasn't just empty DataFrame creation - it was that `get_indegrees()` and `get_outdegrees()`
perform groupby aggregations that fail on empty dask_cudf DataFrames with the error:

   - When edges are empty, all nodes have degree 0 by definition
   - Directly set degree columns to 0 instead of performing expensive groupby aggregation
3. Added materialization for dask_cudf DataFrames in hyper_dask.py to avoid lazy computation issues
   - Materialize entities after concat + drop_duplicates
   - Materialize empty edges in format_direct_edges()
   - Materialize event_entities in hypergraph()
   - Materialize final nodes in Hypergraph.__init__()

title: Fix CLI port mismatch and centralize local dev URLs
body:
`inkeep init --local` creates a CLI profile with `manageUi: 'http://localhost:3001'`, but the management dashboard runs on port **3000**. This causes the device-code authentication flow to fail for every new developer running local setup — the CLI directs the browser to `http://localhost:3001/device?user_code=XXX` which doesn't exist, resulting in ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED and eventually "Device code expired."

### How it happened

| Date | Commit | What happened |
|------|--------|---------------|
| Jan 8 | `112b5c765` (PR #1395) | Added `--local` flag. Created `LOCAL_REMOTE` constant in `types.ts` AND hardcoded `manageUi: 'http://localhost:3001'` inline in `init.ts`. Both used port 3001. No mismatch yet. |
| Jan 20 | `b63b786c7` (PR #1458) | Mono-API refactor. The hardcoded URL in `init.ts` survived untouched. |
| Feb 5 | `96de89839` (PR #1752) | Updated `LOCAL_REMOTE.manageUi` from 3001 → 3000. **Did not touch `init.ts`.** The inline hardcoded `'http://localhost:3001'` was missed. |

Root cause: `init.ts` hardcodes the URL inline instead of importing the `LOCAL_REMOTE` constant, so updating the constant had no effect on the actual profile creation.

Beyond the immediate bug, the same localhost URLs are hardcoded as string literals in 6+ files across the CLI package. `LOCAL_REMOTE` already exists in `types.ts` but was barely used, creating a class of bug where one file gets updated and others don't.


### 1. Fix the bug — use `LOCAL_REMOTE` in `init.ts`

Import `LOCAL_REMOTE` from the profiles barrel and replace all 4 hardcoded localhost URLs:
- Line 390: non-interactive API URL default
- Lines 423-424: interactive prompt placeholder + initialValue
- **Line 456: `manageUi: 'http://localhost:3001'` → `LOCAL_REMOTE.manageUi`** (the bug)

### 2. Centralize runtime fallbacks

`profile-config.ts` and `config.ts` both had hardcoded localhost URL fallbacks. Replaced with `LOCAL_REMOTE` references so they stay in sync with the constant.

### 3. Split `profile add` into Cloud/Local/Custom

The old "Custom" option served both local dev AND remote/staging users with conflicting defaults (pre-filled localhost URLs confused self-hosted users). Split into three options with audience-appropriate defaults:

| Path | Who | Prompt flow |
|------|-----|-------------|
| **Cloud** | Cloud deployments | name → environment ("production") → credential → done |
| **Local** | Local dev | name → environment ("development") → done (URLs from `LOCAL_REMOTE`, credential auto-set to `'none'`, no URL/credential prompts) |
| **Custom** | Self-hosted/staging | name → API URL → Manage UI URL → environment ("production") → credential → done |

Key decisions:
- **Local skips credential prompt** and auto-sets `'none'` — local dev servers don't require auth, and `init --local` already does this.
- **Custom uses placeholder hints** (`https://your-agents-api.example.com`) with no pre-filled default — prevents accidentally accepting wrong defaults. Validation rejects empty input.
- **Keychain warning skipped when `credential === 'none'`** — `'none'` is a sentinel meaning "no auth needed", warning about it missing from keychain is noise.

### 4. Remove dead `DEFAULT_LOCAL_PROFILE` constant

Exported from `types.ts` but never imported by any file since creation in PR #1395. Removed to avoid misleading future developers.

### 5. Tests

- Fix 3 init test expectations from `manageUi: 'http://localhost:3001'` to `'http://localhost:3000'`
- Use `LOCAL_REMOTE` constants consistently in all mock return values and assertions
- Add 9 tests for `profileAddCommand` covering all three paths (Local, Cloud, Custom)

### 6. Documentation

| File | What |
|------|------|
| `cli-reference.mdx` | Fix stale profile YAML example (`manageApi` → `api`, remove `runApi`, credential `none`). Add login/logout command sections. Update profile add description. Fix init --local description. Fix push options/env vars/CI table (`--agents-manage-api-url` → `--agents-api-url`, env vars updated). |
| `workspace-configuration.mdx` | Fix CLI flag, env vars table, and code examples to use current field names (`agentsApi.url`, `INKEEP_AGENTS_API_URL`, `--agents-api-url`). |
| `setup-profile.mdx` | Update Step 1 to describe Cloud/Local/Custom options. |
| `troubleshooting.mdx` | Add CLI Issues section covering login failures, device code expiry, and push auth errors. |

### Not changing

- **`utils/url.ts` line 34** — Dead code (`buildAgentViewUrl` has zero callers). Removal tracked in PR #1984.
- **`config.ts` lines 32, 37** — JSDoc `@default` annotations consumed by fumadocs-typescript for the docs site. Values are already correct (`localhost:3002`, `localhost:3000`). Can't reference constants in JSDoc tags (they're parsed as plain text).


### Automated
- [x] `pnpm test` — **632 tests pass** (5 skipped), 41 test files, 0 failures

### Manual end-to-end (built from source)
- [x] `inkeep init --local --no-interactive` → `manageUi: 'http://localhost:3000'` in profile, `agentsApi.url: 'http://localhost:3002'` in config
- [x] `inkeep profile add` → Local → no URL/credential prompts, env defaults to `development`, profile stored with `manageUi: http://localhost:3000`
- [x] `inkeep profile add` → Custom → placeholder hints visible, empty validation rejects with "URL is required", credential keychain warning shown
- [x] Device-code flow → `login.ts` constructs URL from `profile.remote.manageUi` → `http://localhost:3000/device?user_code=...` for local profiles

title: feat: support depth on array and anything derived from them
body:
Add `depthSize` and `maxDepth` constraints to array-based arbitraries (`array`, `uniqueArray`, `set`, `sparseArray`, `dictionary`, `map`) to support depth-aware length adjustment in recursive structures.

Closes #6344
commit_msgs:
feat: support depth on array and anything derived from them

Add `depthSize` and `maxDepth` constraints to array-based arbitraries
(`array`, `uniqueArray`, `set`, `sparseArray`, `dictionary`, `map`).

When used within recursive structures (e.g., via `letrec`), these
constraints allow arrays to generate fewer elements as depth increases,
preventing exponential blowup of generated structures.

- `maxDepth`: once this depth is reached, only arrays of `minLength`
  are generated
- `depthSize`: controls how aggressively depth reduces the generated
  length (uses the same scale as `oneof`/`option`)

The depth adjustment is only active when the user explicitly provides
`depthSize` or `maxDepth`, preserving full backward compatibility.

Closes #6344

title: fix: AppImage EGL crash on Arch Linux
body:
Fixes the AppImage crash on Arch Linux (and other rolling-release distros) caused by `EGL_BAD_ALLOC` when the system's `WebKitGPUProcess` loads bundled Ubuntu-compiled EGL/Mesa libraries via inherited `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.

### Root Cause

Tauri's AppImage bundler includes `libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0` but **not** `WebKitGPUProcess`. The system's GPU process inherits `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` from AppRun, loads the bundled (Ubuntu-compiled) EGL libs, and crashes due to ABI mismatch with the host's Mesa 26+ drivers.

### Fix (2-Layer Strategy)

- **Layer 1 — CI pipeline** (`updater-release.yml`): Post-process the AppImage after build to remove GPU-driver-dependent libs (`libEGL`, `libGLESv2`, `libgbm`, `libwayland-*`). This forces the AppImage to use the system's native EGL stack, which is compatible with the system's `WebKitGPUProcess`. The AppImage is then repackaged with `appimagetool` and re-signed for the Tauri updater.

- **Layer 2 — Rust code** (`lib.rs`): Set `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1` only when running inside an AppImage (`APPIMAGE` env var detection). This is defense-in-depth for edge cases like NVIDIA driver quirks. No effect on deb/rpm/native installs.

### Why not just env vars?

Setting `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1` globally disables GPU acceleration for **all** Linux users, including those on Ubuntu/Fedora where the AppImage works fine. The CI post-processing approach removes only the conflicting libs, preserving GPU acceleration on compatible systems.


- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — 0 warnings
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — formatted
- [x] `cargo test -- --test-threads=1` — 323 passed
- [x] lint-staged hooks passed on commit
- [ ] Verify Linux AppImage build succeeds in CI (post-processing + re-sign + upload)
- [ ] Verify `latest.json` includes `linux-x86_64` platform after release
- [ ] (Ideal) Test on Arch Linux with Mesa 26+ and AMD/NVIDIA GPU

Closes #186



  * Fixed EGL-related crashes on Linux AppImage by disabling a problematic graphics renderer mode and removing conflicting GPU driver libs for improved stability.

  * Updated release pipeline to post-process, re-sign, and upload Linux artifacts (AppImage, deb, rpm) and integrate these steps with metadata generation.

Layer 2 (Rust): Set WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1 in AppImage

Root cause: Tauri bundles libwebkit2gtk but not WebKitGPUProcess.
The system's GPU process inherits LD_LIBRARY_PATH from AppRun,

title: fix(livestream): Omit empty error field from request logs
commit_msgs:
fix(livestream): Omit empty error field from request logs

The default Echo logger middleware always includes an `error` field in
JSON logs, even when empty. This causes Grafana/Loki to incorrectly
categorize successful requests (200, 204) as errors because the `error`
key is present.

Switch from `middleware.Logger()` to `middleware.RequestLoggerWithConfig`
with a custom `LogValuesFunc` that only includes the `error` field when
there's actually an error.

The implementation is clean and follows existing patterns for other search providers. **SearXNG Implementation:** - Adds SearXNG metasearch engine support with no API key requirement (just needs a reachable instance URL) - Configuration via `tools.web.search.searxng.baseUrl` or `SEARXNG_URL` environment variable - Supports freshness filters (pd/pw/pm/py mapped to day/week/month/year) - Returns structured results matching Brave's format (title, url, description, siteName, engine) - Includes proper caching, error handling, and type definitions **Additional Changes (Unrelated to SearXNG):** - Adds customizable `greetingPrompt` configuration to SessionConfig, allowing users to override the default prompt when starting sessions with `/new` or `/reset` - Refactors `BARE_SESSION_RESET_PROMPT` to `DEFAULT_GREETING_PROMPT` with backward compatibility - Updates two integration points (`get-reply-run.ts` and `agent.ts`) to use the new configurable greeting prompt The code follows existing patterns for provider integration, includes proper TypeScript types, and maintains consistency with Brave/Perplexity/Grok implementations.

title: Improve C# code generation in decompiler
body:
- **Precedence-aware parenthesization** — replaces flat `NeedsParentheses` with `NeedsParenthesesInContext` that compares child vs parent operator precedence, reducing redundant parens
- **Constant folding** — eliminates identity operations (`x + 0`, `0 + x`, `x - 0`, `x * 1`, `1 * x`) with a side-effect guard to preserve call expressions
- **Boxing cleanup** — `box` emits `(object)expr` cast instead of `expr /* box T */` comment
- **conv.i8 + ulong fix** — negative constants with ulong return type emit `unchecked((ulong)-1)` instead of invalid `-1L`
- **IsLoadOf improvement** — handles `Ldloca_s`/`Ldloca` for compound assignment detection


- [x] All 177 decompiler tests pass
- [ ] Spot-check decompiled output on a few real assemblies for parenthesization correctness

title: fix(backend/chat): Include input schema in discovery and validate unknown fields
body:
Fixes two related issues that cause agent execution failures in AutoPilot (SECRT-1858):

1. `find_agent` and `find_library_agent` don't return input schemas, meaning AutoPilot never correctly provides agent inputs
2. `run_agent` silently ignores unknown input fields and falls back to defaults, masking errors

### Changes 🏗️

**Part 1: Include Input Schema in Discovery Tools**
- Added `inputs` field to `AgentInfo` model to include the agent's input schema
- Updated `find_agent` (marketplace) to fetch graph and include input schema for each agent
- Updated `find_library_agent` (library) to fetch graph and include input schema for each agent

**Part 2: Validate Unknown Input Fields**
- Added `INPUT_VALIDATION_ERROR` response type
- Added `InputValidationErrorResponse` model with `unrecognized_fields` and valid `inputs` schema
- Added validation in `run_agent` to reject unknown input fields with actionable error message
- Agent does NOT execute when unknown fields are provided

**Files Changed:**
- `agent_search.py` - Include input schema in discovery responses
- `models.py` - Add `inputs` field to AgentInfo, add InputValidationErrorResponse
- `run_agent.py` - Add validation for unknown input fields
- `run_agent_test.py` - Add test for input validation behavior

### Checklist 📋

- [x] I have clearly listed my changes in the PR description
- [x] I have made a test plan
- [x] I have tested my changes according to the test plan:
  - [x] Type checking passes (0 errors)
  - [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (linting, formatting)
  - [x] Run `find_agent` and verify input schema is included in response
  - [x] Run `find_library_agent` and verify input schema is included in response
  - [x] Call `run_agent` with unknown input fields and verify `input_validation_error` is returned
  - [x] Call `run_agent` with correct input fields and verify execution succeeds

#### For configuration changes:

- [x] `docker-compose.yml` is updated or already compatible with my changes
- [x] I have included a list of my configuration changes in the PR description (under **Changes**)

No configuration changes required.




> Changes response shapes for agent discovery and adds stricter input validation in `run_agent`, which may affect clients expecting previous behavior and can block executions that previously succeeded with ignored fields.
> Agent discovery (`find_agent`/`find_library_agent`) now **includes each agent’s input schema** by fetching the related graph (in parallel) and returning it as a new `AgentInfo.inputs` field.
> `run_agent` now **rejects unknown input keys** instead of silently ignoring them, returning a new `input_validation_error` response (`InputValidationErrorResponse`) that lists unrecognized fields and echoes the valid schema; coverage is added via a new test.
> <sup>Written by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) for commit 7b839b22a8a56dda8171e0a0433835309cb209eb. This will update automatically on new commits. Configure [here](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot).</sup>

title: Add Lean 4 LSP plugin for interactive theorem proving
body:
- Adds Lean 4 language server plugins (`lean4-lake-lsp` and `lean4-lean-lsp`) for interactive theorem proving in Claude Code
- Previously, Claude Code could only interact with `.lean` files by shelling out to `lake build` — a slow, non-native CLI approach that triggers full build cycles and produces unstructured terminal output Claude must parse
- This plugin connects Claude Code directly to Lean 4's built-in language server via LSP, providing real-time, structured diagnostics (type errors, unsolved goals, `sorry` markers), hover info, go-to-definition, and completions — the same feedback mathematicians rely on in VS Code
- Two modes: `lake serve` for Lake projects with dependencies (e.g., Mathlib), and `lean --server` for standalone `.lean` files


Mathematicians doing interactive theorem proving need a tight feedback loop: write a tactic, check the goal state, adjust, repeat. The CLI-based `lake build` approach breaks this loop — each invocation is slow, provides no incremental feedback, and loses structured error information. This LSP plugin restores that feedback loop inside Claude Code, dramatically reducing the effort for mathematicians and formal verification researchers.

## Plugin details

- **Repository**: https://github.com/LucianoXu/claude-lean4-lsp
- **License**: MIT
- **Category**: development
- **Tags**: lean, lean4, theorem-proving, mathematics, formal-verification

title: feat(visualizer): add visualizer selector with 6 visualization types
body:
![Screen Recording 2026-03-02 at 12 07 00 AM mov](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/045f2576-1c2a-42b1-8da7-f6a686286a30)

- Add a dropdown selector to switch between 6 visualizer types: Particles (existing), Waveform Bars, Circular Ring, Radial Spikes, Sound Lines, and Lissajous
- Refactor visualizer to Strategy Pattern with `VisualizerRenderer` interface for hot-swappable renderers
- Enrich audio data with 12 pitch classes, timbre, tempo, and beat phase from Spotify Audio Analysis API
- Fix canvas centering by using container dimensions instead of sketch.js window dimensions

This fixes https://github.com/trungvose/angular-spotify/issues/35

## Architecture

### Strategy Pattern

All visualizers implement a shared `VisualizerRenderer` interface, making it easy to add new types without touching existing code:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  VisualizerRenderer                     │
│  (interface)                                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  + setup(width, height): void                          │
│  + updateAudio(audioData: AudioData): void             │
│  + draw(ctx, width, height): void                      │
│  + destroy(): void                                     │
└──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
                       │ implements
       ┌───────────────┼───────────────┬──────────────────┐
       │               │               │                  │
       ▼               ▼               ▼                  ▼
┌──────────────┐┌──────────────┐┌──────────────┐┌──────────────┐
│  Particles   ││ WaveformBars ││ CircularRing ││ Lissajous    │
│  Renderer    ││ Renderer     ││ Renderer     ││ Renderer     │
└──────────────┘└──────────────┘└──────────────┘└──────────────┘
                                         ┌──────────────┐┌──────────────┐
                                         │ RadialSpikes ││ SoundLines   │
                                         │ Renderer     ││ Renderer     │
                                         └──────────────┘└──────────────┘

### AudioData Interface

Each renderer receives rich audio data from the Spotify Audio Analysis API:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              AudioData                   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  energy: number      ← mean(pitches)/2  │
│  pitches: number[]   ← 12 pitch classes │
│  timbre: number[]    ← 12 coefficients  │
│  tempo: number       ← BPM              │
│  beatPhase: number   ← 0-1 beat cycle   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────┘

### Component Flow

User selects type ──→ VisualizerStore ──→ Component subscribes
                      updates state       to visualizerType$
                                               │
                                               ▼
                                    renderer.destroy()
                                    createRenderer(newType)
                                    renderer.setup()
                                               │
                                               ▼
                                    sketch-js draw() loop
                                    calls new renderer

## New Visualizers

| Type | Description | Inspiration |
|------|-------------|-------------|
| Waveform Bars | 12 bars for pitch classes with glow, beat pulse, reflections | — |
| Circular Ring | Pulsing blob distorted by pitches with 3 layered rings | [CodePen](https://codepen.io/TimPietrusky/pen/QWEWLjm) |
| Lissajous | Oscilloscope-style morphing curves | [CodePen](https://codepen.io/worenga/pen/DpKVpw) |
| Radial Spikes | 48 spikes radiating from center | [CodePen](https://codepen.io/MyXoToD/pen/JYJGvG) |
| Sound Lines | Joy Division-style horizontal wave lines | [CodePen](https://codepen.io/soleneramis/pen/dQYwGa) |

- [ ] Verify all 6 visualizer types render correctly via the dropdown
- [ ] Verify visualizers are centered both horizontally and vertically
- [ ] Verify smooth transitions when switching between types
- [ ] Verify PiP mode works with all visualizer types
- [ ] Verify selected type persists when navigating away and back

title: perf: Optimize node store subscriptions to reduce re-renders
body:
## Performance Optimization: Reduce Re-renders in Node Editor Components

### Problem
Node editor components were subscribing to Zustand stores inefficiently, causing unnecessary re-renders:
- **BaseNode**: Made 5 separate `useResultsStore` calls, re-rendering on every result/chunk/toolCall/planningUpdate/task change
- **NodeInputs/Outputs**: Made multiple separate `useNodes` calls, re-rendering on every edges/nodes change
- **ReactFlowWrapper**: Made multiple separate metadata store calls, re-rendering on every metadata change

In workflows with 100+ nodes, this caused cascading re-renders and performance degradation.

### Solution
Combined multiple store subscriptions into single selectors with `useMemo` to prevent selector function recreation:

**BaseNode.tsx** (lines 394-457)
- Before: 5 separate `useResultsStore` calls for result, chunk, toolCall, planningUpdate, task
- After: 1 combined selector with all 5 values
- Impact: BaseNode only re-renders when relevant results change, not all results

**NodeInputs.tsx** (lines 155-166)
- Before: Separate `useNodes` calls for edges and findNode
- After: 1 combined selector with both values
- Impact: NodeInputs only re-renders when edges or node lookup changes

**NodeOutputs.tsx** (lines 26-37)
- Before: Separate `useNodes` calls for node lookup and updateNodeData
- After: 1 combined selector with both values
- Impact: NodeOutputs only re-renders when specific node changes

**ReactFlowWrapper.tsx** (lines 117-123, 265-282)
- Before: Multiple `useMetadataStore` calls for getMetadata and nodeTypes
- After: 1 combined selector with both values
- Before: Multiple `useNodePlacementStore` calls for pendingNodeType, cancelPlacement, label
- After: 1 combined selector with all 3 values
- Impact: ReactFlowWrapper only re-renders when relevant metadata changes

✅ TypeScript type checking passes
✅ All unit tests pass (84 tests in node components)
✅ ESLint passes

### Performance Impact
- Reduced component re-renders in node editor workflow
- Improved responsiveness when dragging/connecting nodes
- Better performance in workflows with 100+ nodes

### Files Changed
- `web/src/components/node/BaseNode.tsx`
- `web/src/components/node/NodeInputs.tsx`
- `web/src/components/node/NodeOutputs.tsx`
- `web/src/components/node/ReactFlowWrapper.tsx`

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit_msgs:
perf: Optimize node store subscriptions to reduce re-renders

Combine multiple Zustand store subscriptions into single selectors to prevent unnecessary component re-renders in critical node editor components.

Changes:
- BaseNode.tsx: Combine 5 separate useResultsStore calls into single selector (result, chunk, toolCall, planningUpdate, task)
- NodeInputs.tsx: Combine edges and findNode from useNodes into single selector
- NodeOutputs.tsx: Combine node lookup and updateNodeData from useNodes into single selector
- ReactFlowWrapper.tsx: Combine metadata store subscriptions (getMetadata, nodeTypes) and node placement store subscriptions (pendingNodeType, cancelPlacement, label)

Impact: Reduces re-renders in BaseNode (rendered on every node state change), NodeInputs/Outputs (rendered on every edges/nodes change), and ReactFlowWrapper (rendered on every workflow interaction)

title: fix: serialize all sendToAgent calls and use per-key canUseTool callbacks
body:
Fixes #488


- Remove `'heartbeat'` early-return from `acquireLock` — all convKeys including `'heartbeat'` now serialize via `processingKeys`
- Replace shared `currentCanUseTool` field with per-key `currentCanUseToolByKey` map and per-key factory function

## Bug 1: `acquireLock('heartbeat')` skips locking entirely (`bot.ts`)

`acquireLock` short-circuited for the `'heartbeat'` convKey, so concurrent `sendToAgent` calls (e.g. from `HeartbeatService` and `PollingService`) called `session.send()` on the same Session object simultaneously. The letta-code-sdk does not support concurrent sends on the same Session instance (shared `streamQueue`), causing responses to bleed between triggers.

## Bug 2: `currentCanUseTool` clobbered by concurrent `runSession` calls (`session-manager.ts`)

A single `currentCanUseTool` field was overwritten on every `runSession` call. Concurrent sessions for different convKeys (e.g. `'discord'` and `'heartbeat'`) would clobber each other's tool approval callback.


- [ ] Heartbeat and email polling can run concurrently without response bleeding
- [ ] Tool approval callbacks are invoked with the correct handler per session
- [ ] TypeScript compiles cleanly (`npx tsc --noEmit`)

fix(bluesky): prevent duplicate WebSocket connections causing doubled messages

Three-part fix for a race condition in the Jetstream connection lifecycle:

1. Guard in `connect()`: return early if `this.ws` already exists, preventing
   a second connection from being established during the startup race where
   `checkRuntimeState()` fires a deferred `reconnectJetstream()` concurrently
   with `start()`'s own `connect()` call.

2. `intentionalClose` flag in `reconnectJetstream()`: signals the close handler
   not to schedule another reconnect when the old connection is closed as part
   of an intentional reconnect.

3. ws identity check in close handler: capture the specific WebSocket instance
   in the closure and bail out if a newer connection has already replaced it.
   This prevents stale close events from nullifying the active `this.ws`
   reference, which was the core issue causing orphaned connections in
   subsequent reconnect scenarios.

title: fix: prevent CLI from leaking brief context across repos
body:
- **Scope auth context per-workspace**: AuthManager/ContextStore singletons now re-scope via `setProjectRoot()` in the AuthDomain constructor, preventing context leakage between projects
- **Route all CLI auth through TmCore**: Eliminated `AuthManager.getInstance()` and `setProjectRoot()` from the entire CLI layer — all commands use `tmCore.auth` (AuthDomain), scoped by construction
- **Honor selected brief over local files**: StorageFactory auto-detection now checks for an explicitly selected brief before falling back to solo-mode FileStorage
- **Fix clearUserContext re-merge bug**: `saveContext()` was re-merging the `selectedContext` that `clearUserContext()` was trying to remove


- [x] TypeScript: zero errors across `@tm/core` and `@tm/cli`
- [x] Unit tests: 164/164 CLI, 1181/1181 tm-core — all passing
- [x] Manual: `tm auth status`, `tm context`, `tm context clear`, `tm list` verified against live Hamster API
- [x] Manual: `tm list` correctly shows tasks from selected brief (API storage), not local files
- [ ] Manual: Cross-repo context isolation — select brief in repo A, verify repo B doesn't inherit it



> Changes how auth context is stored and how `auto` storage selects API vs file, which can affect which task backend a repo uses and could cause unexpected context/selection regressions across workspaces.
> Fixes cross-repo *brief/org context leakage* by scoping context storage to a per-workspace file (`~/.taskmaster/{projectId}/context.json`) via new workspace path helpers and `AuthDomain(projectRoot)` re-scoping of the `AuthManager` singleton.
> Updates CLI commands (`auth`, `context`, `briefs`, `export`, PRD-to-Hamster) and shared helpers (`auth-guard`, `org-selection`, `brief-selection`) to route all auth/context operations through `TmCore.auth`/`AuthDomain` (initialized from `getProjectRoot()`), and adds proper `TmCore` cleanup.
> Hardens `StorageFactory` `auto` mode to only switch to API storage when a brief is explicitly selected, otherwise preferring file storage for solo-mode repos detected by local task files; adds unit + real-filesystem integration tests covering this behavior and a `ContextStore.clearUserContext` fix to avoid re-merging cleared selections.

  * Scoped brief/context storage per-project to stop cross-workspace leaks (workspace-scoped context files).

  * Solo-mode projects with local task files now prefer local file storage.
  * CLI now lazily initializes core services and shows richer auth/session status; cleanup closes core resources.
  * Added workspace-path utilities for per-project storage locations.

  * Added unit and integration tests validating storage auto-selection and solo-mode behavior.

title: Add precompilation workloads for OrdinaryDiffEqSDIRK
body:
- Add `PrecompileTools.@compile_workload` to `OrdinaryDiffEqSDIRK` for `TRBDF2()` and `KenCarp4()`, following the same pattern used by OrdinaryDiffEqBDF and OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock
- Add `PrecompileTools` and `Preferences` as dependencies in Project.toml
- Support all four specialization modes via `Preferences.@load_preference` (DefaultSpecialize enabled by default, Auto/FunctionWrapper/NoSpecialize opt-in)

OrdinaryDiffEqSDIRK was the only major solver package with zero precompilation workloads, causing unnecessary TTFX overhead for widely-used methods like TRBDF2.

### Before (no precompilation)
When a second SDIRK solver is called after the first already paid shared infrastructure costs:
- TRBDF2 (1st after KenCarp4): **~3.0s**

### After (with precompilation)
- TRBDF2 (1st after KenCarp4): **~0.12s** (25x improvement)
- KenCarp4 (1st after TRBDF2): **~0.10s**

Note: the first solver called in a session still pays ~2.5s for shared OrdinaryDiffEqCore/LinearSolve infrastructure compilation. `--trace-compile` analysis confirms this is from broadcast fusion specialization for user-specific function bodies (especially ForwardDiff dual number types), not from solver method recompilation. The solver-specific precompilation added here IS effective.

Ref: SciML/DifferentialEquations.jl#1125

- [x] `Pkg.test()` passes (JET + Aqua tests)

title: feat: implement efficient range request support for chunks (PE-8334)
body:
This PR implements efficient range request support for reading Arweave chunks, allowing the gateway to seek directly to required chunks instead of streaming all data when serving HTTP range requests.

- **Merkle Path Parser**: Complete implementation with full Arweave compatibility including:
  - Support for all validation rulesets based on weave offset thresholds
  - Rebasing support (Arweave 2.7 feature)
  - Comprehensive property-based tests
  - Compatibility validation against arweave.js
  
- **Streaming Range Fetcher**: New `streamRangeData` function that:
  - Uses async generators for efficient memory usage
  - Seeks directly to chunks containing the requested byte range
  - Tracks chunks fetched for metrics
  
- **TxChunksDataSource Integration**:
  - Uses streaming approach for range requests
  - Falls back to original implementation for full data requests
  - Proper error handling and metrics tracking
  
- **Generalized Metrics**:
  - `dataRequestChunksHistogram` - tracks chunks fetched per request
  - `dataRequestFirstChunkLatency` - tracks time to first chunk
  - Added `request_type` label to existing metrics ('full' or 'range')

- Comprehensive unit tests for merkle-path-parser
- Property-based tests using fast-check
- Unit tests for stream-tx-range functionality
- Integration tests for TxChunksDataSource range requests
- All tests passing

## Performance Impact
This implementation significantly improves performance for range requests by:
- Reducing network usage (only fetching required chunks)
- Reducing memory usage (streaming instead of buffering all data)
- Reducing latency (seeking directly to target chunks)

  - Check `block.len() >= 2` before accessing `block[1]` for C3 commands

title: fix: pin base images, bump stale digests, add Rust cache mounts
body:
- **Pin 7 unpinned base images** to sha256 digests across Dockerfile, Dockerfile.runner, and Dockerfile.sandbox — prevents silent cache invalidation when Docker Hub pushes new tags
- **Bump stale golang:1.25 digest** in Dockerfile.ubuntu-helix from `ce63a16e` (2026-01-27) to `dfae6809` (current)
- **Add cargo cache mounts** to Dockerfile.ubuntu-helix rust-build-env stage and remove unnecessary `cargo clean` — saves ~180s on incremental Rust rebuilds


Unpinned `FROM` tags like `golang:1.25`, `ubuntu:25.04`, `node:23-alpine`, `debian:bookworm-slim`, and `alpine:latest` silently pull new images when Docker Hub updates them, invalidating every layer downstream. This causes full rebuilds with no obvious cause ("I swear I just built that").

The Rust cache mounts (`/root/.cargo/registry`, `/root/.cargo/git`, `/build/gst-pipewire-zerocopy/target`) match the pattern already used in Dockerfile.zed-build. Without them, every desktop rebuild downloads all crates and compiles from scratch.


- [ ] `./stack build-ubuntu` completes successfully
- [ ] Second run of `./stack build-ubuntu` (no code changes) shows all layers cached
- [ ] `./stack build-sandbox` completes successfully

title: Change williamson_condition default to false for 2N low-storage RK
body:
- Changes the default value of `williamson_condition` from `true` to `false` for all 10 low-storage 2N RK method constructors in `OrdinaryDiffEqLowStorageRK`
- The `williamson_condition` optimization fuses broadcast expressions with the function call using `ArrayFuse`, but it only works for `Array` types and can silently produce wrong results if the ODE RHS isn't implemented correctly
- This makes the optimization opt-in rather than opt-out, as discussed in #2310

Affected algorithms: `ORK256`, `DGLDDRK73_C`, `CarpenterKennedy2N54`, `NDBLSRK124`, `NDBLSRK144`, `DGLDDRK84_C`, `DGLDDRK84_F`, `SHLDDRK64`, `NDBLSRK134`, `HSLDDRK64`

## Breaking change
Users who relied on the default `williamson_condition = true` behavior will now need to explicitly pass `williamson_condition = true` to get the fused broadcast optimization. This is intentionally breaking for v7.

Fixes #2310

- [x] Ran `Pkg.test()` for `OrdinaryDiffEqLowStorageRK` locally - all 517 tests pass (28 pre-existing broken)
- Existing tests already explicitly set `williamson_condition` so no test changes needed
