title: feat: add --skip_quantification_merge for per-sample tximport
body:
Adds `--skip_quantification_merge` for per-sample pipeline operation at scale. When enabled, the pipeline switches from run-centric to sample-centric output organization, where each sample's results are self-contained under `<outdir>/<sample_id>/`.

Key changes:
- Per-sample tximport (individual gene/transcript-level TSVs per sample, no cross-sample merging)
- Per-sample MultiQC reports (one report per sample, not one merged report)
- Sample-centric output directory structure (all outputs nested under `<sample_id>/`)
- `rapid_quant` profile for minimal pseudo-alignment-only runs with per-sample QC

### Also included (upstream module sync)

Updating the quantification subworkflows in nf-core/modules required syncing dependent components to their latest versions. This brings in:

- **samtools** 1.22.1 → 1.23 (all samtools modules): unified `index` output replaces separate `bai`/`csi`/`crai` emits; `sort`/`stats`/`faidx` accept combined `[meta, fasta, fai]` tuples
- **picard/markduplicates**: merged `fasta`/`fai` input; output filename changed from `*.MarkDuplicates.metrics.txt` to `*.metrics.txt`
- **multiqc**: new meta-aware tuple input signature (`[meta, files, configs, logo, replace_names, sample_names]`)
- **custom/tx2gene, summarizedexperiment, tximeta/tximport**: topic-based version reporting
- **bam_dedup_stats_samtools_umitools**: new `umitools_dedup_primary_only` parameter for filtering to primary alignments before UMI dedup

## Related PRs

This PR depends on upstream changes in nf-core/modules:

- nf-core/modules#10928 - feat(quant subworkflows): add skip_merge for per-sample quantification (MERGED)
- nf-core/modules#10929 - fix(subworkflows): preserve meta in channel emits (MERGED)
- nf-core/modules#10931 - feat: add topic version emission to quant-related modules (MERGED)
- nf-core/modules#10927 - feat(tximeta/tximport): add tag directive (MERGED)


Large-cohort RNA-seq analyses (hundreds to thousands of samples) face two problems at scale:

1. **Memory**: Cross-sample aggregation steps (tximport `.collect()`, SummarizedExperiment, RSEM merge counts, merged MultiQC) collect all samples into single processes, which can exceed available memory
2. **Organization**: Run-centric output directories (`fastqc/`, `salmon/`, `multiqc/`) mix files from all samples together, making it difficult for e.g. sequencing facilities to locate, deliver, or archive results per sample

`--skip_quantification_merge` addresses both by switching to sample-centric operation: each sample is processed independently and all its outputs are organized under `<outdir>/<sample_id>/`.

## Output structure

**Normal mode** (unchanged):
results/
  fastqc/raw/          # all samples mixed
  trimgalore/          # all samples mixed  
  salmon/              # all samples mixed + merged counts
  multiqc/star_salmon/ # one merged report

**Per-sample mode** (`--skip_quantification_merge`):
results/
  RAP1_IAA_30M_REP1/
    fastqc/raw/        # this sample only
    fastqc/trim/
    trimgalore/
    bbsplit/
    fq_lint/
    salmon/            # quant + per-sample tximport TSVs
    multiqc/           # per-sample MultiQC report
  RAP1_UNINDUCED_REP1/
    ...
  pipeline_info/       # global (not per-sample)
  custom/out/          # reference files (not per-sample)

## Architecture

### Sample-centric output directories

A centralized `ext.publish_prefix` closure in `nextflow.config` controls per-sample path prefixing for sample-level processes. It uses `meta?.containsKey('single_end')` to distinguish sample-level meta from reference/genome meta, so genome preparation outputs and shared files (tx2gene, pipeline_info) remain at the top level. Sample-level publishDir paths reference `${task.ext.publish_prefix}` - the logic lives in exactly one place. Genome preparation processes (`prepare_genome`) don't use the prefix since they never carry sample-level meta. MULTIQC uses a direct `meta.id` check instead, since its meta is constructed in the workflow without the `single_end` key.

### Per-sample quantification

- **TX2GENE**: uses `.first()` instead of `.collect()` (only needs one sample for transcript ID discovery; this applies in both merged and per-sample modes)
- **TXIMETA_TXIMPORT**: receives individual `[meta, results]` tuples in per-sample mode (N invocations) vs collected `[['id':'all_samples'], all_results]` in merged mode (1 invocation)
- **SummarizedExperiment + RSEM merge counts**: completely skipped, emitting `channel.empty()`
- **DESeq2 QC**: gated with `!params.skip_quantification_merge`

### Per-sample MultiQC

- **Meta propagation**: `ch_multiqc_files` carries `[meta, file]` tuples throughout. Global files (workflow summary, versions, strand/mapping checks, DESeq2 outputs) are tagged with empty meta `[[:], file]`.
- **Branching at MULTIQC invocation**: files are branched into per-sample (`meta.id != null`) vs global (empty meta), grouped by sample ID, and each sample gets its own MultiQC report. In normal mode, all files are collected into one merged report as before.
- **MULTIQC module update**: updated to the new meta-aware tuple input signature, matching nf-core/modules upstream.

### rapid_quant profile

Bundles `skip_quantification_merge` with `skip_alignment` and alignment-dependent QC skips. Explicitly sets `skip_multiqc = false` to ensure per-sample MultiQC reports are produced even if a user's config previously disabled MultiQC.


- [x] `--pseudo_aligner salmon --skip_alignment --skip_quantification_merge` - per-sample outputs under `<sample_id>/` with per-sample MultiQC
- [ ] `-profile rapid_quant` - same as above via profile
- [ ] Default run (no flag) - existing behavior unchanged, run-centric output structure
- [ ] Existing nf-tests pass (stub snapshots updated for multiqc_plots/.stub)
- [ ] `--skip_quantification_merge` with alignment enabled - per-sample structure includes alignment outputs

title: Currency converter
body:
Currency Conversion System for ProjectForge

  Implementation of a complete currency conversion system with automatic exchange rate fetching and integration into existing invoice functionality.

  Overview

  This feature enables ProjectForge to manage invoices and financial statistics in multiple currencies and automatically convert them to the system currency. The system can
  automatically fetch exchange rates from online sources and supports historical rates for accurate accounting.

  Key Features

  1. Currency Pair & Rate Management

  - React-based UI for managing currency pairs (e.g. USD → EUR)
  - Historical exchange rates with validity date (validFrom)
  - Automatic rate fetching via ExchangeRateApiService from online sources
  - Inverse rates are automatically calculated and stored
  - Bidirectional conversion: EUR→USD works even if only USD→EUR is defined

  2. Cache System

  - CurrencyConversionCache for performant queries
  - Automatic cache invalidation on data changes
  - Intelligent lookup with automatic fallback to inverse rates

  3. Integration into Invoice Statistics

  - Automatic currency conversion in AbstractRechnungsStatistik
  - All amounts (gross, net, paid, open, etc.) are converted to system currency
  - Warning messages for missing conversion rates
  - Uses historical rates based on invoice date

  4. Invoice List Enhancements

  - Separate currency column in incoming invoice list (Wicket)
  - Amounts displayed without currency symbol
  - Fallback to system currency when no currency is set

  5. Import Improvements

  - Due date preservation when importing incoming invoice positions
  - Enrichment logic prevents unwanted field deletion

  Technical Details

  New Components

  - CurrencyPairDO / CurrencyConversionRateDO - Domain Objects
  - CurrencyPairDao - DAO with UserRight FIBU_CURRENCY_CONVERSION
  - CurrencyConversionService - Service layer for conversions
  - CurrencyConversionServiceSupport - Shared logic for service
  - CurrencyConversionCache - Cache with bidirectional lookup
  - ExchangeRateApiService - Integration with exchangerate-api.com
  - CurrencyPairPagesRest / CurrencyConversionRatePageRest - React REST APIs

  Database

  - Migration V8.0.15__RELEASE-Currency.sql
  - Tables: t_fibu_currency_pair, t_fibu_currency_conversion_rate
  - Foreign key constraints and indexes

  UI Components

  - UIInlineGroup - New UI element for grouped inline fields
  - DynamicInlineGroup.jsx - React component
  - CurrencyPropertyColumn - Extension with showCurrencySymbol flag

  Rights System

  - New UserRight: FIBU_CURRENCY_CONVERSION
  - Integration into menu system (FIBU menu)

  Test Coverage

  - CurrencyConversionServiceTest with 19 tests:
    - Basic conversion and null handling
    - Historical rates with multiple date values
    - Fallback to oldest rate
    - Inverse conversion (EUR→USD when only USD→EUR exists)
    - Cache behavior and performance
    - Custom scale and rounding

  Breaking Changes

  No breaking changes. All changes are backward compatible:
  - Existing invoices without currency use system currency
  - AbstractRechnungsStatistik detects missing conversions and shows warnings
  - CurrencyPropertyColumn maintains default behavior (showCurrencySymbol=true)

  Migration Notes

  After deployment, administrators should:
  1. Create standard currency pairs (e.g. USD→EUR, GBP→EUR)
  2. Import conversion rates for historical periods (if needed)
  3. Assign UserRight FIBU_CURRENCY_CONVERSION to finance group

  Additional Changes

  - BaseDao: baseDOChangedRegistry is now private
  - ValidationUtils: Extracted from AbstractPagesRest for reusability
  - EmployeePagesRest/VisitorbookPagesRest: dataType fixes

- All reviews are logged in GitHub Actions history

Refs #28. After some thinking, this tries for a 'best of both worlds'
approach. Simple arguments can be present essentially as the original
spec recommended. As discussed, we don't specify the args for `npx` and
friends directly, so a simple package is merely...

```yaml
- name: my-api-mcp
  # ...
  packages:
    - type: npm
      name: "@c4312/my-api-mcp"
      version: "0.0.1"
      arguments:
        # Named inputs in 'arguments' generate a `--name=<value>`
        - type: named
          name: "api-key"
          is_required: true
          is_secret: true
```

However, I think we need to be able to specify runtime args in some
cases, otherwise the registry eventually mirrors all docker configs and
options which is not a great situation to be in. So, I suggest a
`runtime_args` in the same format. Say I wanted that for npm, I could:

```yaml
- name: my-api-mcp
  # ...
  packages:
    - type: npm
      name: "@c4312/my-api-mcp"
      version: "0.0.1"
      runtime_arguments:
        # Arguments with a pre-specified `value` don't get prompted for input
        - type: positional
          value: "--experimental-eventsource"
```

But Docker mounts are... complex, and ultimately we may deal with cases
that need multiple inputs in an argument like that. So for that I suggest
the third kind of "templated" input that does basic replacements and has
`properties` that follow the same general input schema:

```yaml
- name: server-filesystem
  # ...
  packages:
    - type: docker
      name: "mcp/filesystem"
      version: "0.0.1"
      runtime_arguments:
        - type: template
          description: Mount paths to access.
          required: true
          repated: true
          template: "--mount=type=bind,src={host_path},dst={container_path}"
          values:
            host_path:
              description: Path to access on the local machine
              required: true
              format: filepath
            container_path:
              description: Path to mount in the container. It should be rooted in `/project` directory.
              required: true
              format: string
              default: "/project"

      arguments:
        - type: positional
          value: "/project"
```

And then client config ends up being pretty simple, for the above case
for example a client could have this config:

```
{
  "filesystem": {
    "server": "@modelcontextprotocol/servers/src/filesystem@1.0.2",
    "package": "docker",
    "settings": {
      "mount_config": [
        { "source_path": "/Users/username/Desktop", "target_path": "/project/desktop" },
        { "source_path": "/path/to/other/allowed/dir", "target_path": "//projects/other/allowed/dir,ro" },
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Which might generate a CLI:

```
docker run \
  --mount=type=bind,src=/Users/username/Desktop,dst=/project/desktop \
  --mount=type=bind,src=/path/to/other/allowed/dir,dst=/project/other/allowed/dir,ro \
  mcp/filesystem:1.0.2 \
  /project
```

I think this does a good job of accomplishing the goals we care about:

- We get nicely defined inputs that are easy to extend, easy to process,
  and easy for clients to configure.
- Versioning is enforced as we don't require the package to specify the
  identifier to npx/uvx/etc.
- We _usually_ can break away from a dependency on a specific runtime.
  This promise is broken a bit with `runtime_arguments`, most packages
  should not need this and those that do are those inherently more
  tightly coupled to a specific runtime like Docker (e.g. they would be
  pretty uncommon for Node or Python.)
- We don't have a suple complex template system with loops and fallbacks
  and conditionals, like we would if we tried to have a single template
  string for a command.

This PR delivers a comprehensive upgrade to the AI Data Science Team project with enterprise-grade features:

- **310 tests passing** (up from 0) with 70%+ coverage target
- **5 new major modules** for extensibility and scalability

### 1. Plugin System (`ai_data_science_team/plugins/`)
- Base classes: `AgentPlugin`, `ToolPlugin`, `WorkflowPlugin`
- Plugin registry with decorators (`@register_agent`, `@register_tool`)
- Dynamic plugin loader for files, directories, and Python modules

### 2. Caching Layer (`ai_data_science_team/cache/`)
- `MemoryBackend`: In-memory LRU cache with TTL support
- `DiskBackend`: Persistent disk-based cache with pickle serialization
- DataFrame-aware cache key generation for pandas operations
- Decorators: `@cached`, `@cache_result`, `@invalidate_cache`
- **25 unit tests**

### 3. Async/Parallel Execution (`ai_data_science_team/async_ops/`)
- `AsyncExecutor`: Async execution with concurrency control
- `ParallelExecutor`: Thread/process pool for CPU/IO-bound tasks
- `parallel_map`, `parallel_apply` for DataFrames
- `run_agents_parallel` for concurrent agent execution
- Utilities: `async_retry`, `timeout`, `RateLimiter`, `CircuitBreaker`
- **37 unit tests**

### 4. Cloud Connectors (`ai_data_science_team/connectors/`)
- `SnowflakeConnector`: Full Snowflake support
- `BigQueryConnector`: Google BigQuery with dataset management
- `RedshiftConnector`: Amazon Redshift with COPY from S3
- `PostgresConnector`: PostgreSQL with bulk operations
- `S3Connector`: AWS S3 for CSV/Parquet/JSON
- Connection pooling and URL-based creation
- **36 unit tests**

### 5. REST API Server (`ai_data_science_team/api/`)
- FastAPI application with OpenAPI docs at `/docs`
- Endpoints for all agents: `/agents/invoke`, `/agents/clean`, `/agents/eda`, `/agents/sql`, `/agents/visualize`

title: fix(subscriptions): prevent NRE when Ack races with Resubscribe
body:
- **Fix**: `Ack()` now captures `CheckpointCommitHandler` into a local variable and returns early if null, preventing NRE when `DisposeCommitHandler()` nulls it concurrently during resubscribe
- **Root cause**: `AsyncHandlingFilter` worker thread calls `Ack()` → `CheckpointCommitHandler!.Commit()` after `Resubscribe()` has already set the handler to null via `DisposeCommitHandler()`, causing a NRE cascade (NRE → Nack → Dropped → resubscribe → repeat)
- **Test**: Adds `Should_not_throw_nre_when_ack_races_with_resubscribe` that deterministically reproduces the race using a slow handler + triggered drop


- [x] New test reproduces the NRE before the fix (confirmed: `Assert.Fail` with NRE at `Nack` line 107)
- [x] New test passes after the fix (31/31 pass)
- [x] All existing subscription tests still pass
commit_msgs:
fix(subscriptions): prevent NRE when Ack races with Resubscribe

During resubscribe, DisposeCommitHandler() sets CheckpointCommitHandler
to null. If the AsyncHandlingFilter worker thread is still processing a
message, it calls Ack() → CheckpointCommitHandler!.Commit() and hits a
NullReferenceException. The NRE cascades through Nack → Dropped →
resubscribe in an infinite loop.

Fix: capture CheckpointCommitHandler into a local variable and return
early if null, using the standard pattern for concurrent null races.

title: UN-2888 [FIX] Add hook for setting default triad for invited users
body:
## What

- Add `setup_default_adapters_for_user()` hook method to `AuthenticationService` (raises `MethodNotImplemented`)
- Call the hook from `set_user_organization()` in `AuthenticationController` for non-new organizations (invited user flow)


- When an invited user accepts an invitation and joins an existing organization, the Default Triad (LLM, embedding, vector DB, x2text adapters) is not set for them
- This causes silent failures in API deployment creation because the `UserDefaultAdapter` record is missing
- The frictionless onboarding only creates default adapters for the org creator, not for subsequently invited users

## How

- Added `setup_default_adapters_for_user()` to the base `AuthenticationService` following the same plugin pattern as `frictionless_onboarding()` (raises `MethodNotImplemented` in base, implemented in cloud)
- In `set_user_organization()`, after `create_tenant_user()`, the hook is called in the `else` branch (non-new org) with a try/except for `MethodNotImplemented`
- The cloud repo implements the actual logic to find existing frictionless adapters and create `UserDefaultAdapter` for the invited user

## Can this PR break any existing features? If yes, please list possible items. If no, please explain why.

- No. The new hook raises `MethodNotImplemented` in the base implementation, which is caught and silently ignored. This is the same pattern used by `frictionless_onboarding()`. OSS deployments are unaffected.

## Database Migrations

- None

## Env Config

- None

## Related Issues or PRs

- UN-2888
- Companion PR: unstract-cloud `fix/set-default-triad-for-invited-user`

## Dependencies Versions

- None

## Notes on Testing

- Unit tests added in `pluggable_apps/platform_admin/tests/test_set_default_adapters.py` covering:
  - Default adapters created for invited user with all 4 types
  - Skips if user already has defaults (idempotent)
  - Skips if no OrganizationMember exists
  - Skips if no frictionless adapters in org
  - Skips if missing adapter types
  - Multiple invited users share same frictionless adapters

title: fix: use HF-style cache for model downloads, avoid iCloud eviction
body:
- **Root cause:** swift-transformers `Hub.snapshot()` downloaded models to `~/Documents/huggingface/` which is iCloud-synced on macOS — large safetensors files were evicted to cloud, causing timeouts and crashes on subsequent loads
- Replaced with `swift-huggingface` `HubClient.downloadSnapshot()` for Python-compatible HF-style cache at `~/.cache/huggingface/hub/` (shared with `mlx_lm`)
- Always validate/resume via HubClient before loading — handles partial downloads from interrupted sessions
- Simplified resolver: AFM cache (flat, side-loaded) → HF hub (HF-style, downloaded)

- Bump `swift-transformers` to 1.3.0, add `swift-huggingface` 0.8.1+ dependency
- `downloadModel()` uses `HubClient.downloadSnapshot()` instead of `Hub.snapshot()`
- Add `*.jinja` to download globs (`chat_template.jinja` was missing)
- Remove `applyEnvironment()` side effects (AFM cache is read-only)
- Show "resuming download" when partial cache detected
- Remove stale progress bar (HubClient `@MainActor` callbacks batch in CLI apps)

- [ ] `env -u MACAFM_MLX_MODEL_CACHE afm mlx -m mlx-community/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-4bit -s "hi"` — fresh download to `~/.cache/huggingface/hub/`
- [ ] Interrupt download (Ctrl-C), restart — resumes from partial, shows "resuming download"
- [ ] `MACAFM_MLX_MODEL_CACHE=... afm mlx -m <cached-model>` — loads from AFM cache, no download
- [ ] Verify `chat_template.jinja` is downloaded (no "No chat template" warning)
- [ ] Confirm `~/Documents/huggingface/` is no longer used

Closes #70


## Summary by Sourcery

Switch MLX model downloads to use Hugging Face hub-style caching and simplify cache resolution away from iCloud-synced locations.

New Features:
- Add support for resuming partial model downloads with explicit UI stage reporting.

Enhancements:
- Standardize model download destination on the Hugging Face hub cache shared with Python tooling.
- Simplify MLX cache resolution to prioritize a flat AFM cache and the HF hub cache, treating AFM as read-only for side-loaded models.
- Replace legacy progress bar output with a simpler spinner-based status line for model loading and downloads.
- Include Jinja chat template files in the set of downloaded model artifacts.
- Print resolved model and download paths to aid debugging of cache behavior.

Build:
- Bump swift-transformers to version 1.3.0 and add a dependency on swift-huggingface for HubClient-based downloads.
- Adjust MLX vendor patch script to align swift-transformers version expectations.
- Add a compiler flag to strip build machine path prefixes from release binaries for cleaner error paths.

Documentation:
- Add documentation describing MLX model path resolution, environment variables, lookup order, and download destinations.

title: feat: add --tree flag for tree-view output
body:
- Adds `--tree` flag that displays cloned file structure as a colored tree
- Color scheme:
  - **Bold cyan** — primary directory (header)
  - **Cyan** — subdirectories, symlink targets pointing to dirs
  - **No color** — regular files, symlink targets pointing to files
  - **Yellow** — symlink names
- Smart path header: `./` for cwd-relative, `~/` for home-relative, absolute otherwise
- Blob picks show just the file path (no redundant tree node)
- Works with `--dry-run` (clones to temp dir, prints tree, cleans up — no files left on disk)
- Suppresses all human-readable output (banner, spinner, success) when `--tree` is active
- Cross-platform: normalizes Windows backslashes to forward slashes

## Examples

```sh
# repo
$ gitpick nrjdalal/picksuite my-project --tree
./my-project              # bold cyan
├── file.txt              # no color
├── folder                # cyan
│   ├── deep              # cyan
│   │   └── file.txt
│   └── nested.txt
├── README.md
├── symdir -> folder      # yellow -> cyan (points to dir)
└── symlink.txt -> file.txt  # yellow -> white (points to file)

# folder
$ gitpick nrjdalal/picksuite/tree/main/folder ~/demo --tree
~/demo
├── deep
│   └── file.txt
└── nested.txt

# blob (just the path, no tree)
$ gitpick nrjdalal/picksuite/blob/main/file.txt --tree
./file.txt

# dry-run (no files left on disk)
$ gitpick nrjdalal/picksuite my-project --dry-run --tree
./my-project
├── file.txt
├── folder
│   ├── deep
│   │   └── file.txt
│   └── nested.txt
├── README.md
├── symdir -> folder
└── symlink.txt -> file.txt

title: fix(threading): protect source_target_map with lock
body:
`source_target_map` and `simple_map` in `modules/globals.py` are mutated from the UI thread (when the user configures face mappings) and read concurrently from `ThreadPoolExecutor` workers during frame processing. Without synchronization, this causes intermittent crashes or corrupted map state during live mode with map-faces enabled.

This adds a `threading.Lock()` to `globals.py` and wraps all mutations of these shared data structures in `face_analyser.py`.


- `modules/globals.py`: Add `MAP_LOCK = threading.Lock()`
- `modules/face_analyser.py`: Wrap mutations of `source_target_map` and `simple_map` with `MAP_LOCK`


- Map-faces mode: configure mappings while live preview is running
- Verify no crashes during concurrent map updates and frame processing
- Standard face swap (non-map mode) unaffected


## Summary by Sourcery

Protect global face-mapping state from concurrent modifications by introducing a shared lock and using it around all map mutations.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent race conditions and intermittent crashes when updating face-mapping data while it is being read during frame processing.

Enhancements:
- Guard global face-mapping structures with a dedicated lock to ensure thread-safe updates from UI and worker threads.

title: fix(engine): prevent pipeline premature exit when single execution path fails
body:
Fixes the bug where a pipeline with multiple parallel execution paths (e.g., Crew AI, Deep Agent, LangChain agents running simultaneously) would abort entirely when a single path encountered an error.

**Root cause**: The agent error handling code called `rocketlib.error()` (which maps to the C++ engine's `engLib.error()`) when an agent's `_run()` method threw an exception. The C++ engine interprets `error()` as a **fatal node failure signal**, causing it to terminate all parallel execution paths in the pipeline -- not just the one that failed.

**Fix**: Replaced `rocketlib.error()` with `rocketlib.warning()` in three agent error handling locations:

- **`packages/ai/src/ai/common/agent/agent.py`** -- `AgentBase.run_agent()` exception handler. This is the primary fix -- all agent framework drivers (CrewAI, Deep Agent, LangChain, RocketRide Wave) flow through this shared entrypoint. The error details are already captured in the answer payload and written to the answers lane, so downstream nodes and the UI retain full error context.

- **`nodes/src/nodes/agent_rocketride/rocketride_agent.py`** -- Wave planner failure handler. When `plan_wave()` raises, the error is now logged as a warning and the agent returns a graceful error message instead of signaling a fatal failure.

- **`nodes/src/nodes/agent_rocketride/executor.py`** -- Tool call and memory store failures within wave execution. Individual tool errors were already handled gracefully (returned as error dicts), but the `error()` log call was still triggering engine-level abort.

Additionally added `'status': 'error'` to the answer payload metadata in `AgentBase.run_agent()` so consumers can programmatically distinguish failed paths from successful ones.

**Behavior after fix**:
- If one execution path fails, only that path reports an error (via its answer payload)
- Other parallel paths continue executing normally
- The pipeline completes with partial results -- succeeded paths deliver their answers, failed paths deliver error context
- The failure is still visible in the job log as a warning

Closes #444

- [ ] Trigger a failure in one path (e.g., send a request that causes an LLM to return None/empty for one agent)
- [ ] Verify the failed path reports its error in the answer payload
- [ ] Verify the other paths complete successfully and deliver their answers
- [ ] Verify the failure appears as a warning (not error) in the job log
- [ ] Verify that a pipeline where ALL paths fail still reports all failures correctly
- [ ] Regression: verify a normal pipeline (no errors) still works identically

feat: Add OpenAPI tool infrastructure and vendor adapter pattern

This commit introduces a comprehensive OpenAPI 3.x tool generation system
with a clean vendor adapter pattern for domain-specific API integrations.

## Core Features

### OpenAPI Tool Infrastructure
- Generic OpenAPI 3.x specification parser with security validation
- Dynamic tool generation from OpenAPI operations
- Circuit breaker pattern for API resilience
- Rate limiting and timeout controls (configurable per tool)
- Domain allowlist for security (OPENAPI_ALLOWED_DOMAINS)

### Vendor Adapter Pattern
- Pluggable vendor-specific API transformations
- Clean separation: generic infrastructure in core, vendor logic in adapters
- Conditional loading with graceful fallback
- Example: `tools/vendor_adapters/ptengine.py` (not included in this commit)

### Role System Enhancements
- Dynamic role loading with vendor-specific roles
- Conditional imports allow optional vendor extensions
- Generic roles: generalist, analysis, research, writer, critic
- Vendor roles loaded via: `from .vendor/role import ROLE_PRESET`

### Configuration Improvements
- Config overlay pattern: base config + vendor overlays
- Environment variable support for secrets (${VAR_NAME})
- Dynamic header templating: `{{body.fieldName}}`
- Hot-reload configuration via SHANNON_CONFIG_PATH

### Orchestrator Improvements
- Generic field mirroring in agent.go (no hardcoded field lists)
- All request body fields automatically promoted to prompt_params
- Synthesis activity with tool restriction (allowed_tools: [])
- DAG workflow execution optimizations

### LLM Provider Fixes
- Fix Anthropic API conflict: remove top_p when temperature is set
- Consistent behavior across provider manager facade

### Rust Agent Core
- Enhanced gRPC tool execution
- Generic tool parameter handling

## Architecture

```
Generic Infrastructure (this commit):
├── config/shannon.yaml                    # Base config (vendor-agnostic)
├── go/orchestrator/
│   ├── activities/agent.go               # Generic field mirroring
│   ├── activities/synthesis.go           # Synthesis with tool control
│   └── workflows/strategies/dag.go       # DAG execution
├── python/llm-service/
│   ├── llm_provider/anthropic_provider.py
│   ├── providers/__init__.py
│   ├── api/agent.py                      # Template rendering
│   ├── api/tools.py                      # OpenAPI tool loader
│   ├── roles/presets.py                  # Generic roles + conditional imports
│   └── tools/
│       ├── openapi_parser.py             # OpenAPI 3.x parser
│       └── openapi_tool.py               # Generic tool generator
└── rust/agent-core/src/grpc_server.rs

Vendor Extensions (examples, not committed):
├── config/overlays/shannon.vendor.yaml   # Vendor-specific config
├── python/llm-service/llm_service/
│   ├── roles/vendor/custom_role.py       # Vendor-specific roles
│   └── tools/vendor_adapters/vendor.py   # API transformations
```

## Usage Example

1. **Base Shannon (generic)**:
```yaml
# config/shannon.yaml
openapi_tools: {}  # Vendor configs in overlays
```

2. **Vendor Extension**:
```yaml
# config/overlays/shannon.vendor.yaml
openapi_tools:
  my_api:
    spec_path: config/openapi_specs/my_api.yaml
    auth_type: bearer
    auth_config:
      vendor: my_vendor
      token: "${MY_API_TOKEN}"
```

3. **Vendor Adapter**:
```python
# tools/vendor_adapters/my_vendor.py
class MyVendorAdapter:
    def transform_body(self, body, operation_id, prompt_params):
        # Domain-specific transformations
        return body
```

4. **Vendor Role**:
```python
# roles/my_vendor/custom_role.py
CUSTOM_ROLE_PRESET = {
    "name": "custom_role",
    "system_prompt": "...",
    "allowed_tools": ["my_api_operation"]
}
```

## Security
- All secrets via environment variables (never hardcoded)
- Domain allowlist prevents SSRF attacks
- Private IP blocking in OpenAPI parser
- Circuit breaker protects against cascading failures

## Testing
- End-to-end test verified: decomposition → DAG → synthesis
- Vendor adapter integration confirmed working
- Role-based tool restriction validated
- Config overlay pattern tested

## Breaking Changes
None - this is additive infrastructure.

## Future Work
- Additional vendor adapters for other APIs
- Enhanced OpenAPI parameter validation
- Webhook support for async operations
- GraphQL tool generation

   - Synchronize workflow goroutine writes with query handler reads
   - Safe for Temporal: mutexes only affect memory safety, not determinism

5. Semaphore Panic Risk (grpc_server.rs)

   - Prevents server crashes from semaphore acquisition failures

### Stage 5: Cascade Confirmation
- Add cascade confirmation widget for Planning mode

title: Replace GATK with FreeBayes for variant calling; upgrade Java tools to eliminate CVEs
body:
This PR replaces the GATK variant caller with FreeBayes in the `refine_assembly` pipeline, removes GATK from the codebase entirely, upgrades Java bioinformatics tools, and adds a CVSS v4.0-aware Trivy vulnerability policy. Together these changes eliminate 5 CRITICAL and 33 HIGH CVEs.

## 1. GATK → FreeBayes migration

### Variant caller evaluation

We evaluated four options for replacing GATK3 UnifiedGenotyper:

| | UnifiedGenotyper (old) | HaplotypeCaller | Mutect2 | FreeBayes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Algorithm | Bayesian genotyper | Local reassembly + Bayesian | Somatic caller | Bayesian genotyper |
| EMIT_ALL_SITES | `-out_mode EMIT_ALL_SITES` | Unclear (`EMIT_ALL_CONFIDENT_SITES` may omit sites) | Not supported | `--report-monomorphic` (exact equivalent) |
| Output format | Standard VCF (AD, DP) | GVCF with `<NON_REF>` (BP_RESOLUTION) | Variants-only | Standard VCF (AD, DP) |
| Ploidy | `--ploidy N` | `--ploidy N` | No fixed ploidy | `--pooled-continuous` |
| Java fat JAR CVEs | N/A (old) | 14 HIGH | 14 HIGH | None (C++ binary) |
| Image size impact | N/A | +400MB | +400MB | ~2MB |

FreeBayes is the closest algorithmic match to UG — both are Bayesian pileup-based genotypers. Its `--report-monomorphic` flag is a direct equivalent of `EMIT_ALL_SITES`, emitting every position in standard VCF with per-base DP. The existing `vcfrow_parse_and_call_snps()` parser works unchanged. HaplotypeCaller uses local reassembly (a bigger behavioral change) and its GVCF output with `<NON_REF>` alleles would have required parser changes. Mutect2 is a somatic caller and doesn't support all-sites output.

### Code changes

- **Created** `src/viral_ngs/assemble/freebayes.py` — FreeBayes tool wrapper with bgzip+tabix support (FreeBayes writes plain VCF, so we compress and index after calling)
- **Deleted** `src/viral_ngs/core/gatk.py`
- **Removed** `gatk4` from conda deps; **added** `freebayes>=1.3.6` to assemble image
- **Removed** IndelRealigner step from `align_and_fix()` and `refine_assembly()`
- **Removed** CLI commands: `gatk_ug`, `gatk_realign`
- **Removed** CLI args: `--skipRealign`, `--GATK_PATH`

### Behavioral differences

Validated by running integration tests in Docker, aligning old vs new consensus with mafft, and examining read pileups with samtools:

**refine1 — 6bp insertion at position 1539:**
FreeBayes correctly calls a 6bp insertion (`ACGACT`) that GATK3 UG missed. Pileup shows 9/11 reads (82%) support the insertion (QUAL=300, AF=1.0, genotype 1/1). This is an improvement — the insertion is clearly real.

**refine2 — 49bp longer consensus (27bp at 5' + 22bp at 3'):**
Root cause is the test aligner change (novoalign → minimap2): minimap2 maps more reads to the terminal regions than novoalign, so coverage at the ends meets the `min_coverage=3` threshold and `strip('Nn')` trimming has fewer terminal N's to remove. One interior A→N at a position right at the DP=3 boundary.

### Breaking changes

- `gatk_ug` and `gatk_realign` CLI commands removed
- `--skipRealign` and `--GATK_PATH` arguments removed from `align_and_fix` and `refine_assembly`
- `viral_ngs.core.gatk` module deleted
- `refine_assembly()` no longer accepts `gatk_path` parameter

## 2. Java tool upgrades

- **Picard** → 3.4.0 (eliminates log4j CRITICAL CVEs)
- **fgbio** → 3.1.2
- **SnpEff** → 5.2 (OpenJDK 17)

## 3. Trivy vulnerability policy (CVSS v4.0 support)

Added `.trivy-ignore-policy.rego` with rules that filter out CVEs that are architecturally inapplicable to our deployment model (ephemeral batch containers on cloud PaaS, no inbound listeners, no interactive sessions). Each rule targets a specific CVSS vector pattern and documents its rationale:

| Rule | CVSS pattern | Rationale |
|------|-------------|-----------|
| Physical access | AV:P | Containers are cloud-hosted, never physically accessible |
| Adjacent network | AV:A | Containers run on orchestrated cloud infra, attacker cannot be on same network segment |
| Local + user interaction | AV:L + UI:R | Batch containers have no interactive sessions — no human clicking links or opening files |
| Local + high privileges | AV:L + PR:H | Containers run as non-root with dropped capabilities |
| Local + scope unchanged | AV:L + S:U | Attacker already has code execution inside an ephemeral container; vulnerability grants no additional capability |
| Availability-only + scope unchanged | C:N + I:N + S:U | DoS in a batch container = one failed job, container destroyed, no data leak or corruption. Operationally equivalent to a corrupted input file |

Each rule supports both CVSS v3.1 and v4.0 vector string formats. The v4.0 support is needed because Trivy is transitioning to v4.0 for newer advisories and some CVEs now only have v4.0 vectors.

Rules explicitly do NOT filter: scope-changed CVEs (container escapes), any CVE with confidentiality or integrity impact, or network-accessible vulnerabilities beyond the DoS-only case.

### Per-CVE exceptions (`.trivyignore`)

Two individual CVEs are excluded in `.trivyignore` because they cannot be addressed by version bumps or by the Rego policy rules above:

**CVE-2026-23949 — jaraco.context path traversal in tarball extraction (HIGH)**
- Package: `setuptools` (vendors `jaraco.context 5.3.0` internally)
- The vulnerable code path (`tarball()` context manager) is only used during `pip install` of source distributions, which happens at **build time only** from trusted sources (PyPI, conda-forge). No pip installs happen at runtime.
- Even if triggered, the path traversal writes files inside an ephemeral container that is destroyed when the job completes — no persistence, no lateral movement.
- NVD scored this AV:N/S:C, but this assumes a network-facing service extracting untrusted archives. In our deployment, there is no such service. The Rego policy cannot filter it because the NVD score uses AV:N rather than the more appropriate AV:L.
- Will self-resolve when setuptools updates its vendored jaraco.context to >= 6.1.0.

**CVE-2020-25649 — jackson-databind XXE in DOMDeserializer (HIGH)**
- Package: `jackson-databind 2.10.5` bundled inside `snpEff-5.2` fat JAR
- The vulnerability requires jackson-databind to deserialize **XML input** via `DOMDeserializer` without disabling external entity resolution.
- SnpEff uses jackson-databind for **JSON parsing only** (config metadata, database indices). Its inputs are VCF, GenBank, and properties files — it never parses XML through Jackson. The vulnerable code path is present in the JAR but never traversed.
- Cannot be fixed without an upstream snpEff release that updates its bundled jackson-databind.

## 4. Test changes

- Switched `refine_assembly` integration tests from novoalign to minimap2 (via `already_realigned_bam` path)
- Removed `@unittest.skipIf(IS_ARM)` guards — integration tests now run on ARM64
- New expected FASTA files generated from FreeBayes+minimap2 pipeline

## CVE impact

| Metric | main | This branch | Change |
|--------|------|-------------|--------|
| CRITICAL | 5 | **0** | **-5 eliminated** |
| HIGH | 34 | **1** | **-33 (97% reduction)** |

The remaining 1 HIGH is CVE-2026-27459 (pyOpenSSL DTLS) — unrelated to this branch. FreeBayes introduced zero CVEs.


- [x] CI unit tests pass (all images, amd64+arm64)
- [x] CI Trivy security scans pass
- [x] Local Docker integration tests with mafft alignment and pileup analysis
- [ ] Terra regression testing — `assemble_refbased` on known-good samples (in progress)

title: Fix G_K exponential degradation in damage model
body:
## **User description** - The continuous damage factor was applied to `G_K`/`G` inside the stress component loop (`do i = strxb, strxe`), causing the shear modulus to be compounded by the damage factor on each iteration - With N stress components, this produced an effective `G_K * damage^N` instead of the intended `G_K * damage` - Fix moves the damage application before the loop in both cons-to-prim and prim-to-cons paths - [ ] Verify damage model test cases produce physically correct stress degradation - [ ] Golden file regeneration likely needed for damage model cases ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** **Apply damage factor once to shear modulus to stop exponential weakening** ### What Changed - The damage multiplier is applied a single time to the shear modulus before iterating stress components instead of being multiplied inside the component loop. - Shear contribution to pressure and elastic stress now uses the correctly degraded shear modulus rather than an N-times compounded reduction. - No change to user-facing inputs; results for damage-model cases will change to the physically intended stress degradation. ### Impact `✅ Correcter stress degradation for damage cases` `✅ Restored shear strength in damaged cells` `✅ Fewer unexpected differences in damage-model outputs` 💡 Usage Guide ### Checking Your Pull Request Every time you make a pull request, our system automatically looks through it. We check for security issues, mistakes in how you're setting up your infrastructure, and common code problems. commit_msgs:
Fix G_K exponential degradation in damage model

The damage factor was applied inside the stress component loop, causing
G_K (and G) to be multiplied by the damage factor on every iteration.
With N stress components, the effective shear modulus was reduced by
damage^N instead of damage^1. Move the damage application before the
loop so it is applied exactly once per cell.

title: [Supersonic Page Speed] Dedicated homepage CSS bundle
body:
## Hackathon: Supersonic page speed optimizations


Create a lean homepage-specific CSS bundle that only includes the ~15 SCSS modules the homepage actually uses (out of 70+). The full bundle carries docs, registry, pricing, API reference, and event page styles that are never used on the homepage.

### How it works
- New `homepage.scss` entry point with only homepage-relevant imports (header, footer, hero, buttons, carousel, chooser, swiper, neo-mode, etc.)
- Pages set `css_bundle: homepage` in frontmatter to use it; pages without the field get the default full `bundle.css`
- `assets.html` reads the `css_bundle` param and loads the corresponding CSS file
- Production `minify-css.js` PurgeCSS pipeline processes the homepage bundle alongside the existing ones

### Results
- Homepage CSS: 659 KiB -> 260 KiB in dev (60% smaller)
- After gzip: **30 KiB** vs production's current 61 KiB (**-51%**)
- Other pages are unaffected (they continue to use `bundle.css`)

### Extensibility
Any page can set `css_bundle` in frontmatter to use a page-specific bundle. This pattern can be extended to other high-traffic pages (pricing, product, etc.) in the future.

title: fix(desktop): prevent StartView flash when deleting active workspace
body:
- Fixed bug where deleting the active workspace would sometimes cause the StartView ("select project" screen) to appear even when other workspaces exist
- Root cause: mismatch between backend workspace selection (all workspaces) and frontend cache (only visible projects)


**Backend (`db-helpers.ts`):**
- `selectNextActiveWorkspace()` now only selects from visible projects by joining with the projects table and filtering by `tabOrder != null`

**Frontend (`useDeleteWorkspace.ts`, `useCloseWorkspace.ts`):**
- Iterate through all remaining workspaces to find one with full data in `previousGrouped`, instead of only checking the first one
- Add fallback that sets minimal workspace data instead of `null` when cache is missing, preventing StartView flash


- [ ] Delete the active workspace when multiple workspaces exist in the same project
- [ ] Delete the active workspace when workspaces exist in different projects
- [ ] Verify no StartView flash occurs during workspace deletion
- [ ] Verify the next workspace becomes active correctly



> Aligns next-workspace selection to visible projects and hardens optimistic switching to avoid StartView flashes when closing/deleting the active workspace.
> - Backend: `selectNextActiveWorkspace()` now joins `projects` and filters by `projects.tabOrder != null`, selecting most-recent from visible projects only
> - Frontend (close/delete hooks): iterate remaining workspaces to find one present in `getAllGrouped` and optimistically set it active; add minimal-data fallback instead of `null` to prevent StartView flash; keep caches in sync and invalidate after ops (plus recents on close)

title: Add AVX-VNNI support for 256-bit VNNI without full AVX-512
body:
- Adds `HAVE_VNNI256` macro as a second tier below `HAVE_FANCY_SIMD`, enabling 256-bit VNNI instructions (`_mm256_dpbusd_epi32`, `_mm256_dpwssd_epi32`) on CPUs that have AVX-VNNI but lack full AVX-512
- New CMake option `GGML_AVX_VNNI` (adds `-mavxvnni` on GCC/Clang, defines `__AVXVNNI__` on MSVC)
- Converts 155 `#ifdef`/`#ifndef HAVE_FANCY_SIMD` blocks across 11 files to use `HAVE_VNNI256` where the block only uses 256-bit AVX2+VNNI intrinsics — blocks that use 512-bit intrinsics, AVX-512 mask operations, or AVX-512-only function references remain unchanged


Currently, VNNI dot-product intrinsics are gated behind `HAVE_FANCY_SIMD`, which requires the full AVX-512 ISA (`AVX512F` + `VL` + `BW` + `DQ` + `VNNI`). However, the same 256-bit VNNI instructions are available via AVX-VNNI (VEX-encoded) on many CPUs that lack full AVX-512:

- Intel Alder Lake / Raptor Lake / Meteor Lake

Without this change, these CPUs fall back to the 2-instruction `_mm256_maddubs_epi16` + `_mm256_madd_epi16` sequence instead of the single `_mm256_dpbusd_epi32`.

## Benchmark Results

Tested on Intel Meteor Lake:

### Upstream

| qwen35 0.8B Q4_K - Medium      | 696.32 MiB |     1.01 B | CPU        |       2 |         pp512 |    225.68 ± 6.76 |
| qwen35 0.8B Q4_K - Medium      | 696.32 MiB |     1.01 B | CPU        |       2 |         tg128 |     35.83 ± 4.51 |

build: edf54621 (4301)

### This PR

| qwen35 0.8B Q4_K - Medium      | 696.32 MiB |     1.01 B | CPU        |       2 |         pp512 |    275.14 ± 5.99 |
| qwen35 0.8B Q4_K - Medium      | 696.32 MiB |     1.01 B | CPU        |       2 |         tg128 |     38.21 ± 2.81 |

build: 56f4e9e6 (4302)

## Config

```c
// Tier 1: 256-bit VNNI (AVX-VNNI or AVX512-VL+VNNI)
#if defined(__AVXVNNI__) || (defined(__AVX512VNNI__) && defined(__AVX512VL__))
    #define HAVE_VNNI256
#endif

// Tier 2: Full AVX-512 + VNNI (unchanged)
#if defined(__AVX512F__) && defined(__AVX512VNNI__) && defined(__AVX512VL__) && defined(__AVX512BW__) && defined(__AVX512DQ__)
    #define HAVE_FANCY_SIMD
#endif

When `HAVE_FANCY_SIMD` is defined, `HAVE_VNNI256` is always also defined (superset).


# AVX-VNNI only (Intel Alder Lake+, no AVX-512)
cmake -B build -DGGML_AVX_VNNI=ON -DGGML_AVX2=ON

# Full AVX-512 + VNNI (unchanged, also enables HAVE_VNNI256)
cmake -B build -DGGML_AVX512=ON -DGGML_AVX512_VNNI=ON

# Auto-detect
cmake -B build -DGGML_NATIVE=ON

## What was not changed

- `ggml-quants.c` and `llamafile/sgemm.cpp` already had correct `__AVXVNNI__` guards
- 512-bit VNNI paths (`_mm512_dpbusd_epi32`, 97 calls) still require full AVX-512
- `fa/iqk_fa_templates.h` — all blocks use AVX-512 features


- [x] Builds cleanly with `-DGGML_AVX_VNNI=ON -DGGML_AVX2=ON -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF` (no warnings)
- [x] Benchmarked on AVX-VNNI hardware (Meteor Lake and Raptor Lake)
- [x] Verify no regression on full AVX-512 builds (`HAVE_FANCY_SIMD` path)

Add AVX-VNNI support for 256-bit VNNI without full AVX-512

title: feat: replace SummaryVec with HistogramVec for reconcile metrics
body:
Replace `promauto.NewSummaryVec` with `promauto.NewHistogramVec` for reconcile duration metrics. SummaryVec maintains sorted sliding-window quantile streams per label combination that grow unboundedly — with ~200-400 unique `{component, instance}` pairs, this consumed **521 MB of heap (64.7% of total)**. HistogramVec uses fixed-size bucket arrays costing only **3 MB** (174x improvement).

### Verified Results (Two Independent Experiment Runs)

| Metric | Baseline (SummaryVec) | Fix (HistogramVec) | Range Across Runs |
|--------|----------------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| **Go heap (pprof)** | 569–805 MB | 140–287 MB | **-64% to -75%** |
| **SummaryVec in heap** | 521 MB (64.7%) | 0 MB | **-100% (confirmed both runs)** |
| **HistogramVec cost** | 0 MB | 3 MB (1.2%) | 174x improvement |
| **Container memory** | 3.8–3.85 GB | 1.35–2.65 GB | **-31% to -65%** |
| **CPU** | 371–373% | 339–379% | **-9% to +2%** |

**Key finding**: Heap reduction is consistent (~64%) across both runs. Container memory and CPU vary with measurement timing — the 31% memory / +2% CPU from the revalidation run (15 min warmup, steady state) are the conservative, reproducible figures. The -65% memory / -9% CPU from the first run captured a transient favorable state early in warmup.

### What works
- SummaryVec quantile buffers fully eliminated (521 MB → 0 MB, confirmed by pprof in both runs)
- Heap stays bounded — HistogramVec uses fixed-size arrays, no growth with label cardinality
- Zero call site changes (`.Observe()` API identical), zero behavioral changes
- FSMv2 state identical between baseline and fix

### What doesn't improve
- **CPU**: +2% regression at steady state from 6.5x more frequent GC cycles on smaller heap. SummaryVec quantile computation was <0.5% of CPU — removing it doesn't save meaningful CPU. The first run's -9% was measured before GC overhead accumulated.
- **Container RSS varies**: 31-65% depending on Redpanda state, benthos worker count, and MADV_FREE page reclamation timing. Go heap (64%) is the authoritative metric.

### Data quality notes from revalidation
- Baseline Prometheus metrics file was accidentally captured from fix container (wrong port) — does not affect heap profiles or docker stats
- High-res CPU tracked s6-svscan (PID 1), not umh-core Go binary — nmap oscillation confirmed unaffected via pprof instead


1. `pkg/metrics/metrics.go` — SummaryVec → HistogramVec (5-line change)
2. `integration/metrics_parsing.go` — summary quantile parser → histogram bucket parser
3. `integration/metrics_parsing_test.go` — updated test fixtures

## Risk

- **Low**: Zero behavioral changes, zero call site changes
- **Note**: Breaks external Prometheus/Grafana queries using `quantile="..."` labels (need to update to `le="..."` bucket queries)
- **CPU trade-off**: +2% from increased GC frequency — acceptable for eliminating unbounded memory growth


- [x] EXP-1 first run: 82 S6 services, 15 min warmup, heap/memory/CPU captured
- [x] EXP-1 revalidation: 77 S6 services, 15 min warmup, full A/B with pprof + docker stats + Prometheus
- [x] Integration tests pass (metrics_parsing_test.go updated)

title: [2.x] Fix: strip pipelining scalacOptions before launching the REPL
body:
Fixes #8921

Note: I was able to reproduce issue in sbt 2.0.0-RC10.


When `usePipelining := true` in a multi-project build, sbt appends  
`-Ypickle-java` and `-Ypickle-write <path>/early.jar` to `scalacOptions`  
for fast parallel compilation. These flags were being leaked into the Scala  
REPL, causing failure on console


Strip pipelining flags before forwarding to the REPL  in Deafults.scala.

First build and publish your local sbt:
cd sbt
sbt publishLocal

and then create a scratch project:
mkdir -p /tmp/test8921/modules/subproject/src/main/scala
echo 'object Sub { val x = 42 }' > /tmp/test8921/modules/subproject/src/main/scala/Sub.scala
cat > /tmp/test8921/build.sbt <<'EOF'
ThisBuild / usePipelining := true
ThisBuild / scalaVersion  := "3.8.1"
lazy val subproject = project.in(file("modules/subproject"))
lazy val root = project.in(file(".")).dependsOn(subproject).aggregate(subproject)
EOF
mkdir /tmp/test8921/project
echo 'sbt.version=2.0.0-RC9-bin-SNAPSHOT' > /tmp/test8921/project/build.properties

launch it: cd /tmp/test8921 && sbt

Test:
>subproject/console
>Nil

Result: After "Nil", it was hanging before but now it doesn't hang, There is valid output.

title: fix: make browser sessions stateless for serverless
body:
Removes the in-memory session cache that caused "Session not found" errors on Vercel. Each request now connects to BrowserBase via CDP using the session ID — no shared state between function instances.


The browser module stored Playwright sessions in an in-memory `Map` with a `globalThis` hack. This works locally (single process), but on Vercel serverless each request can hit a different function instance with an empty Map. The `submit` request would fail with a 404 because the session created by `start` lived in a different instance's memory.


Design for stateless from the start:
- **Removed**: in-memory `Map`, `globalThis` session store, TTL reaper, `createdAt` tracking
- **Added**: `connectToSession()` and `fetchLiveViewUrl()` shared helpers
- **Changed**: `getSession()` now connects via CDP on every call — BrowserBase keeps the browser alive server-side, so reconnecting gives you the same page state
- **Simplified**: `BrowserSession` interface (single `sessionId` field instead of redundant `id` + `browserbaseSessionId`)

Net **-19 lines** across 2 files (browser.ts, route.ts).


- [ ] Start a session locally → submit credentials → verify full flow works
- [ ] Deploy to Vercel → verify "Session not found" error is gone
- [ ] Verify browser live-view iframe still loads correctly

fix: make browser sessions stateless for serverless compatibility

Remove in-memory session Map, globalThis cache, and TTL reaper.
Each request now connects to BrowserBase via CDP using the session ID,
making the design fully stateless and compatible with Vercel serverless
where requests may hit different function instances.

title: ttsim: skip test_reshape_oob on wormhole_b0 and blackhole
body:
`test_reshape_oob` allocates two 2^15x2^15 sentinel tensors and runs 10 iterations under TTSim, taking ~150s in serial. Under parallel xdist execution it intermittently exceeds the 320s job timeout — especially after PR #34905 added `test_narrow` cases to the same xdist group, increasing resource contention.

This has been causing `sanity-tests.yaml` to flap on `main` since Mar 27.

The skip list passes each entry as `--deselect=<path>` to pytest, and pytest `--deselect` supports `file::test_name` granularity — so only `test_reshape_oob` is excluded. The other 31 tests in `test_reshape.py` continue to run normally.

- [x] yamllint passes (pre-commit)
- [ ] sanity workflow green on main after merge

## 🔐 Security Enhancements

## 🛠️ Development Tools

- **ESLint Config**: Modern flat config with Next.js and TypeScript rules

**Deletions**: -9,484 lines  

This represents a complete modernization of the codebase while maintaining backward compatibility for existing projects.

This is a major version upgrade that requires:

- Updated Clerk configuration for third-party auth
- Supabase migration to new RLS patterns

## 🎉 Ready for Production

This v2 release provides a solid foundation for modern web applications with:
- Enterprise-grade authentication and database integration
- AI capabilities out of the box
- Mobile-first responsive design
- Comprehensive developer documentation
- Modern development tooling and practices

title: feat(backup): support workload identity and configurable S3 provider for backup credentials
body:
- Make `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` optional in the `s3-backup-credentials` Secret. When omitted, rclone uses `--s3-env-auth=true` to authenticate via the provider's native credential chain (AWS IRSA, GKE Workload Identity, etc.)
- Add configurable `S3_PROVIDER` key (default: `Other`) to enable provider-specific credential chains and optimizations (e.g., `AWS`, `GCS`, `Ceph`)
- Add `spec.backup.serviceAccountName` CRD field so backup/restore Jobs can use a workload identity-enabled ServiceAccount on any cloud
- Applies to all backup Job types: pre-delete, pre-update, periodic CronJob, and restore

Closes #320

## Multi-cloud support

| Cloud | `S3_PROVIDER` | Workload Identity | How it works |
|-------|---------------|-------------------|--------------|
| **AWS EKS** | `AWS` | IRSA / Pod Identity | `--s3-env-auth=true` uses AWS SDK chain |
| **GKE** | `GCS` | Workload Identity Federation | `--s3-env-auth=true` + GCS S3-compatible endpoint |
| **AKS** | (any compatible) | Workload Identity | Static HMAC keys or compatible S3 provider |
| **Any S3** | `Other` (default) | N/A | Static `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` |


- **CRD types**: Add `serviceAccountName` to `BackupSpec`
- **`s3Credentials`**: Add `Provider` and `EnvAuth` fields
- **`getS3Credentials()`**: Make AK/SK optional, set `EnvAuth=true` when empty, read `S3_PROVIDER` with `Other` default
- **`buildRcloneJob()`**: Use `--s3-env-auth=true` instead of static credential flags when `EnvAuth` is set; use configurable `--s3-provider`; accept and set `ServiceAccountName` on pod spec
- **`buildBackupCronJob()`**: Same env-auth, provider, and SA logic for the periodic CronJob
- **Callers** (backup.go, restore.go, autoupdate.go): Pass `serviceAccountName` through
- **Tests**: Unit tests for env-auth mode, provider passthrough, and ServiceAccountName on both Job and CronJob
- **E2E tests**: Verify ServiceAccountName propagation and env-auth CronJob creation
- **Docs**: Update README.md and docs/api-reference.md with cloud-agnostic workload identity guide

## Backward compatibility

Fully backward compatible:
- Existing Secrets with `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` continue to work as before
- `S3_PROVIDER` defaults to `Other` (the previously hardcoded value)
- `serviceAccountName` defaults to empty (no change to Job pod spec)


- [ ] Unit tests pass for `buildRcloneJob` with env-auth creds and `--s3-provider=AWS`
- [ ] Unit tests pass for `buildRcloneJob` with ServiceAccountName
- [ ] Unit tests pass for `buildBackupCronJob` with env-auth creds and provider passthrough
- [ ] Unit tests pass for `buildBackupCronJob` with ServiceAccountName
- [ ] E2E: CronJob created with ServiceAccountName when `spec.backup.serviceAccountName` is set
- [ ] E2E: CronJob uses `--s3-env-auth=true` when static credentials are omitted from Secret
- [ ] Existing tests continue to pass (backward compat with `Provider: "Other"`)

title: fix: prevent duplicate logical experts on same GPU
body:
This PR fixes a bug where the expert packing algorithm could place multiple physical replicas of the same logical expert on the same GPU, which defeats the purpose of expert replication for load balancing.


As reported in #22, when distributing 256 logical experts + 32 redundant experts across 32 GPUs, the algorithm could produce mappings like:
dup expert layer 0 rank 16, [200, 226, 236, 236, 12, 204, 156, 229, 184]
where expert 236 appears twice on the same GPU.


The `balanced_packing` function in Step 3 only considered load balancing when packing physical experts to GPUs. It did not check whether multiple physical experts mapping to the same logical expert would end up on the same GPU.


- Add optional `logical_ids` parameter to `balanced_packing` function
- When packing, prefer packs (GPUs) that don't already contain the same logical expert ID
- Pass the `phy2mlog` mapping to `balanced_packing` in Step 3 of `rebalance_experts_hierarchical`

The fix is backward compatible - existing code without the `logical_ids` parameter continues to work.


- `eplb.py`: Modified `balanced_packing` to accept and use logical ID constraints
- `test_eplb.py`: Added comprehensive test suite including:
  - README example validation
  - Regression test for issue #22
  - High replication scenario test
  - Global load balancing test
  - Single replica per expert test

fix: prevent duplicate logical experts on same GPU

When packing physical experts to GPUs, the `balanced_packing` function

This is inefficient and defeats the purpose of expert replication.

Changes:
- Add optional `logical_ids` parameter to `balanced_packing` function
- When packing, prefer packs that don't already contain the same logical ID

title: feat(bex): complete garbage collector implementation
body:
Complete the BEX garbage collector implementation by closing 5 identified gaps in the engine-level integration:

- **Gap 1**: Parked VM roots now collected via VM pointer registry
- **Gap 2**: VM stacks updated with forwarding pointers after GC  
- **Gap 3**: TLABs invalidated after GC space swap
- **Gap 6**: Handle race condition fixed with EpochGuard


### VM Pointer Registry (Phase 1-2)
- Add `parked_vms: Mutex<Vec<VmPtr>>` to `EpochState` for tracking VMs at safepoints
- VMs register pointers before parking, unregister after GC completes
- GC collects roots from all parked VM stacks

### Stack Updates & TLAB Invalidation (Phase 3)
- Add `collect_garbage_with_forwarding()` that returns the forwarding map
- Update parked VM stacks with new object indices after GC moves objects
- Invalidate TLABs so VMs allocate from the new space

### Handle Race Condition Fixes (Phase 4)
- Remove cached `ObjectIndex` from `Handle` - always resolve through table
- Add `gc_in_progress` flag to synchronize new calls with GC
- New `call_function` invocations wait for in-progress GC before resolving handles

### EpochGuard & Accessor API (Phase 6)
- Add `EpochGuard` token type for compile-time epoch protection enforcement
- `Handle::object_index()` now requires `&EpochGuard<'_>` parameter
- Add heap accessor API (`read_string`, `read_array`, `with_object`) for safe external access

title: Example(nextjs): add FSRS parameter optimizer with client and server-side training
body:
This PR adds a comprehensive Next.js example demonstrating FSRS parameter optimization with both client-side and server-side training approaches.


### Dual Training Modes
- **Client-Side Training**: Runs FSRS optimization directly in the browser using WebAssembly
  - No server load for computation
  - Real-time progress tracking
  - Memory-efficient implementation
- **Server-Side Training**: Offloads computation to the server with SSE for real-time updates
  - Better for large datasets
  - Reduces client resource usage

### Core Functionality
- CSV file upload for review history data
- Configurable timezone settings with automatic detection
- Adjustable parameters (next day start time, relearning steps)
- Real-time progress tracking for both optimization modes
- Dual optimization (with/without short-term memory)
- Dark mode support with responsive design

## Important Configuration

### Package Manager (pnpm)
  "pnpm": {
    "supportedArchitectures": {
      "cpu": ["current", "wasm32"]
Required for downloading WebAssembly dependencies.

### Next.js Configuration
1. **serverExternalPackages**: Prevents bundling issues with WebAssembly modules
2. **Cross-Origin Isolation Headers**: Enables `SharedArrayBuffer` for client-side WebAssembly training

## Project Structure
examples/nextjs/
├── src/
│   ├── app/                 # Next.js App Router
│   │   ├── api/
│   │   │   ├── timezone/    # Timezone API
│   │   │   └── train/       # SSE training endpoint
│   ├── components/
│   │   ├── ClientTraining.tsx
│   │   └── ServerTraining.tsx
│   ├── hooks/
│   │   └── useSSETraining.tsx
│   ├── types/
│   └── utils/

## Technology Stack
- Next.js 16 with App Router
- React 19
- Tailwind CSS 4
- @open-spaced-repetition/binding (WebAssembly)
- Hono for SSE endpoints
- TypeScript
- Biome for linting

## Deployment Notes
⚠️ When deployed to Vercel, server-side training may not work with large CSV files due to serverless function limitations. Client-side training is recommended for production on Vercel.

title: Replace blocking Redis KEYS with non-blocking SCAN in Colonel API
body:
### **User description** Fixes #2211 - replaces 9 blocking Redis `KEYS` operations in the Colonel admin API with non-blocking alternatives to prevent Redis lock-up under load. The Colonel API used `dbclient.keys('pattern')` calls which are O(N) and block Redis during execution. With a growing database, this caused admin panel timeouts and risked production degradation. **Count operations** (`get_colonel_info.rb`, `get_database_metrics.rb`): - Replaced `dbclient.keys('secret*:object').count` with `Onetime::Secret.count` - These use Familia's O(1) ZCARD-based counting instead of scanning the keyspace **Iteration operations** (4 files): - `list_users.rb`: Extracted KEYS from the per-user loop (was O(N*M)) into a single SCAN pass that builds an owner_id→count index - `export_usage.rb`, `get_user_details.rb`, `list_secrets.rb`: Replaced KEYS with cursor-based SCAN iteration All SCAN implementations include a 10K item memory bound to prevent OOM on large datasets. - Verified no `.keys('pattern')` calls remain in colonel logic - QA reviewed all 6 files for correctness and Ruby 3.4 compatibility - Existing colonel tryouts pass (2/2) ## Notes for Reviewers The `list_secrets.rb` pagination is still in-memory (loads up to 10K secrets, then slices). title: perf: Optimize Zustand store subscriptions with selective selectors
body:
## Performance Optimization: Zustand Store Selector Improvements

### 🎯 Objective

Fix performance bottlenecks caused by components subscribing to entire Zustand stores instead of specific state slices, preventing unnecessary re-renders.

### 📊 Problem

Components were using `useStore()` without selectors, causing them to re-render whenever **any** property in the store changed, even if the component didn't use that property. This is particularly problematic in:
- Node editor with 100+ nodes
- Asset management with 1000+ files  
- Real-time collaboration features

### ✅ Solution

Converted all non-selector Zustand subscriptions to use **selective selectors**:

#### Before (❌ Causes unnecessary re-renders)
const { setSelectedPath } = useNodeMenuStore();
// Component re-renders when ANY store property changes

#### After (✅ Only re-renders when needed)
const setSelectedPath = useNodeMenuStore((state) => state.setSelectedPath);
// Component only re-renders when setSelectedPath changes

### 📝 Files Changed (18 files)

**Components:**
- `NamespaceItem.tsx` - Node menu namespace items
- `ModelFiltersBar.tsx` - Model filter controls
- `VibeCodingPanel.tsx` - VibeCoding UI panel
- `VibeCodingChat.tsx` - VibeCoding chat interface
- `CollectionList.tsx` - Workflow collections list
- `NotificationButton.tsx` - Notification panel button
- `DataframeProperty.tsx` - Dataframe property editor
- `SwatchPanel.tsx` - Color swatch panel
- `ColorPickerModal.tsx` - Color picker modal
- `RemoteSettingsMenu.tsx` - Remote settings menu
- `FoldersSettingsMenu.tsx` - Folders settings menu
- `WorkspaceTree.tsx` - Workspace tree view
- `VersionHistoryPanel.tsx` - Version history panel
- `ModelListHeader.tsx` - Model list header
- `ModelListIndex.tsx` - Model list index

**Hooks:**
- `useModels.ts` - Models hook
- `useFileHandling.ts` - File handling hook

**Tests:**
- `RemoteSettingsMenu.test.tsx` - Updated mock to handle selectors

### 🚀 Performance Impact

- ✅ **Reduced re-renders**: Components only re-render when their specific dependencies change
- ✅ **Better scalability**: Critical for large workflows (100+ nodes)
- ✅ **Follows best practices**: Aligns with project's ZUSTAND_BEST_PRACTICES.md
- ✅ **No API changes**: Pure optimization, behavior unchanged

### 🧪 Testing

- ✅ TypeScript compilation: No errors
- ✅ ESLint: Passes (4 pre-existing warnings unrelated to changes)
- ✅ Single test passes: RemoteSettingsMenu "should not display secret settings"
- ⚠️  Note: Full test suite has pre-existing test fragility in RemoteSettingsMenu (tests timeout on main branch as well)

### 📚 Documentation

This change implements the best practices documented in `/web/src/stores/ZUSTAND_BEST_PRACTICES.md`:

> ## Selector Patterns
> ### Use Selectors to Prevent Unnecessary Re-renders
> ```typescript
> // ❌ BAD: Subscribing to entire store
> const store = useMyStore();  // Re-renders on any state change
> // ✅ GOOD: Selective subscription
> const count = useMyStore((state) => state.count);  // Only re-renders when count changes
> ```

### 🔗 Related Work

- Similar optimization completed on 2026-01-11 (WorkflowAssistantChat, AppHeader, WelcomePanel)
- Project context: `.memory/project-context.md` documents "Zustand Subscription Optimization" as recent improvement

title: perf(ci): optimize pipeline — merge jobs, build once, parallelize Docker
body:
5 CI optimizations to reduce wall-clock time from ~15 min to ~8-10 min.

| # | Optimization | Savings |
|---|-------------|---------|
| 1 | Merge lint + test into one job | ~30s (eliminate duplicate setup) |
| 2 | E2E setup builds once, shards download artifacts | ~30-45s per shard |
| 3 | E2E uses `next start` (production) vs `next dev` | ~30-60s (no per-page compilation) |
| 4 | Docker build parallel with E2E (`needs: [lint-and-test]`) | ~5-7 min off critical path |
| 5 | Concurrency: cancel-in-progress on new push | Saves runner minutes |

### Pipeline diagram
lint-and-test (~2m) ──┬── e2e-setup (~2m) ── 3 shards (~4m each)
                      └── docker (~5m, parallel)

### Before vs After
| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Jobs | 6 (lint, test, 3×e2e, docker) | 6 (lint-and-test, e2e-setup, 3×e2e, docker) |
| Setup cycles | 6× pnpm install | 3× pnpm install (lint, setup, docker) |
| E2E web server | dev mode (compile on visit) | production mode (pre-compiled) |
| Docker blocks on | lint + test + e2e | lint-and-test only |
| Stale run handling | None | Cancel-in-progress |
commit_msgs:
perf(ci): optimize CI pipeline — merge jobs, build once, parallelize

5 optimizations to reduce CI wall-clock time:

1. Merge lint + test into one job — eliminates duplicate setup (checkout,
   pnpm install, prisma generate, shared build). Was 2 jobs, now 1.

2. E2E setup job builds once, uploads artifacts — shards download
   pre-built .next/, prisma client, shared dist, and test DB instead
   of each shard rebuilding from scratch.

3. E2E shards use `next start` (production) instead of `next dev` —
   eliminates per-page compilation delay (2-5s per page visit in dev).

4. Docker build runs parallel with E2E — changed from
   `needs: [lint, test, e2e]` to `needs: [lint-and-test]`. Docker
   builds from source, doesn't depend on E2E results.

5. Concurrency with cancel-in-progress — new pushes cancel stale runs,
   saving runner minutes.

Expected pipeline:
  lint-and-test (~2 min) → e2e-setup (~2 min) → 3 shards (~4 min each)
  lint-and-test (~2 min) → docker (~5 min, parallel with E2E)
  Total wall clock: ~8-10 min (was ~15 min)

title: refactor: convert all file I/O operations to async using aiofiles
body:
This PR converts all synchronous file I/O operations to async using `aiofiles`, significantly improving UI responsiveness in the TUI by preventing blocking operations.

## Changes Overview

### Dependencies Added
- ✅ `aiofiles>=24.0.0` - async file operations library
- ✅ `types-aiofiles>=24.0.0` - type stubs for mypy

### Files Converted (12 modules)

**Core Managers (HIGH PRIORITY - blocks TUI)**
- ✅ `conversation_manager.py` - async save/load/clear with atomic backups
- ✅ `usage_manager.py` - async persist/restore (called after every agent run)
- ✅ `config_manager.py` - all 10 config methods now async

**Agent Tools & Utilities**
- ✅ `common.py` - async TOC extraction from markdown files
- ✅ `tools/file_management.py` - async read/write for .shotgun files
- ✅ `tools/codebase/file_read.py` - async file content retrieval

**TUI Utilities**
- ✅ `tui/utils/mode_progress.py` - async content checking for mode hints

**Codebase Infrastructure (MEDIUM/LOW priority)**
- ✅ `codebase/core/ingestor.py` - async file parsing during indexing
- ✅ `codebase/core/code_retrieval.py` - async code snippet extraction
- ✅ `codebase/core/change_detector.py` - async file hash calculation
- ✅ `agents/history/token_counting/tokenizer_cache.py` - async cache writes


- 🚀 Non-blocking TUI during conversation save/load
- ⚡ Smooth UI during configuration changes
- 🎯 No lag after agent runs (usage tracking now async)
- ✨ Better overall application responsiveness
- 🔧 Foundation for future async optimizations


⚠️ **IMPORTANT**: This is a breaking change that requires follow-up work.

All callers of the converted async methods must be updated to properly await them. This affects:
- TUI screens and services (ConversationService, config screens, etc.)
- CLI commands using these managers
- Test files - need `async def` and `await`
- Agent system prompt builders

**Next Steps**: A follow-up PR will systematically update all callers throughout the codebase by:
1. Running tests to identify broken callers
2. Updating TUI screens/services to await file operations
3. Converting tests to async
4. Ensuring proper error handling


- [ ] Run full test suite to identify broken callers
- [ ] Update TUI screens to await async operations
- [ ] Verify conversation save/load works in TUI
- [ ] Test config changes in TUI
- [ ] Verify agent file operations still work
- [ ] Run mypy type checking

## Technical Notes

- Used `aiofiles` for async file I/O (read, write, append)
- Used `asyncio.to_thread()` for operations without aiofiles support (unlink)
- Preserved atomic file operations (temp file + rename pattern)
- All file operations maintain error handling and logging
- Type hints preserved with mypy type stubs

title: fix(amplitude-session): fix 0-second sessions on iOS
body:
Fix AmplitudeSessionPlugin producing 0-second sessions (`session_start` + `session_end` at the same timestamp) on iOS. Addresses customer escalation from v0.4.2 rewrite (PR #1104).

**Root cause:** The plugin ignored iOS's `inactive` AppState. On iOS, the lifecycle is `active → inactive → background`, but the plugin only handled `background`, so the `active → inactive` transition was a no-op. This meant `lastEventTime` was never updated on backgrounding, causing immediate session expiration when the app resumed.


### Handle iOS `inactive` AppState (primary fix)
Track `_previousAppState` and treat `inactive` the same as `background` for session timeout, matching the core library's pattern at `analytics.ts:771`. Without this, every iOS background/foreground cycle produces a spurious `session_end` + `session_start`.

### Await `onForeground`
`onForeground` was fire-and-forget, so the session transition could race with incoming events. Now awaited.

### Replace `resetPending` with `_sessionTransition` promise
The `resetPending` flag was cleared asynchronously via the event pipeline when `session_start` flowed back through `track()`. Between the flag being set and cleared, a race window existed where concurrent `execute()` calls could skip the transition check. The promise lets concurrent callers await the same in-flight transition.

### Remove dual-ID concept (`eventSessionId`)
The v0.4.2 rewrite added `eventSessionId` as a separate ID for event enrichment, intended to let events keep the old session ID during transitions. But `track()` overwrote it when session events flowed back through the pipeline — by that point the transition had already completed, so `eventSessionId` held the new value anyway. With the transition promise serializing access (no event can be enriched mid-transition), the second ID is unnecessary. Removed `_eventSessionId`, `EVENT_SESSION_ID_KEY`, and related getter/setter.

### Fix `track()` to preserve existing `session_id`
When `session_start`/`session_end` events flow back through `track()`, preserve the `session_id` already set by `performSessionTransition` instead of overwriting it with the current `sessionId`.

### Fix `reset()` to fire `session_end`
`reset()` now fires `session_end` before clearing state, matching the Swift SDK behavior. Uses `multiRemove` for atomic cleanup.

### Batch persistence
Use `AsyncStorage.multiSet` in transitions instead of individual fire-and-forget `setItem` calls. Removes `sessionId` setter's persistence side-effect (now only persisted in `performSessionTransition` and `reset()`).

### Cleanup
Remove 3 unconditional `console.log` debug statements and a dead `//await this.saveSessionData()` comment left from the v0.4.2 rewrite.

- [x] All 23 plugin tests pass (including new concurrency, app state, and persistence tests)
- [x] Full test suite passes (66 suites, 363 tests, 0 failures)
- [ ] Manual verification on iOS device: background/foreground cycles no longer produce 0-second sessions

title: fix(security): Sanitize error responses, add rate limiting, improve atomicity
body:
- **Error message sanitization**: Replace `$e->getMessage()` in `RelayerController` API responses with generic messages, log details server-side to prevent information disclosure
- **Rate limiting**: Add `throttle:60,1` to Privacy/Merkle read endpoints, `throttle:10,1` to write endpoints (merkle-path, verify-commitment), tighten passkey auth from 10/min to 5/min
- **Error sanitization in connectors**: `SimpleBitcoinConnector` no longer exposes raw HTTP response body to callers
- **Exception logging**: `TransactionQueryAnalyzerService` now logs previously-swallowed date parsing exceptions at debug level
- **Atomic operations**: `GasStationService::sponsorTransaction` now wraps bundler submit + fee deduction in `DB::transaction()` for consistency
- **Code style**: Minor whitespace alignment fixes in AI tool tests

## Security Fixes

| Issue | Severity | Fix |
|-------|----------|-----|
| `$e->getMessage()` exposed in RelayerController responses | CRITICAL | Generic messages, server-side logging |
| No rate limiting on Privacy/Merkle endpoints | CRITICAL | `throttle:60,1` reads, `throttle:10,1` writes |
| Passkey rate limit too permissive (10/min) | HIGH | Reduced to 5/min |
| Raw HTTP body in SimpleBitcoinConnector errors | HIGH | Log details, throw generic message |

## Code Quality Fixes

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| Swallowed exceptions in date parsing | Added `Log::debug()` for observability |
| Non-atomic bundler submit + fee deduction | Wrapped in `DB::transaction()` |
