Includes per-expiry download status indicators, an "Incomplete" quick-select button, 4-parallel-worker download engine, and a broker capability matrix. ## Feature Overview ### 3-Phase Download Pipeline | Phase | What it does | |-------|-------------| | **Phase 1** | Select underlying (NIFTY, BANKNIFTY, FINNIFTY, MIDCPNIFTY, SENSEX, BANKEX, SENSEX50, or 500+ stocks) and fetch all available expiry dates from Upstox | | **Phase 2** | Fetch and cache all CE/PE/FUT contracts for selected expiries | | **Phase 3** | Download 1-minute OHLCV candles for each contract via background job with real-time progress | ### Per-Expiry Download Status (New UX) Step 1 now shows a status pill next to every expiry date so users can instantly see download progress without running through all contracts: | Pill colour | Meaning | |-------------|---------| | 🟢 Green `186 ✓` | Fully downloaded (downloaded = total) | | 🟡 Yellow `250/272` | Partial — some contracts still pending | | 🟠 Orange `0/178` | Contracts cached (Phase 2 done) but download not started | | *(none)* | Phase 2 not yet run for this expiry | ### "Incomplete" Quick-Select Button Alongside the existing **All / None** buttons, a new **Incomplete** button auto-selects only expiries where download is zero or partial. Users can click once → go straight to Phase 3 → only incomplete expiries are queued. No need to rely on the incremental flag or wait for it to scan 15,000+ contracts. ### Parallel Downloads (4 workers) Phase 3 now uses `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4)` for API calls (I/O bound) with a single `threading.Lock` serialising DuckDB writes. This significantly speeds up downloads without breaching Upstox rate limits (45 req/s, 450 req/min shared across all threads via a thread-safe rate limiter). ### Broker Capability Matrix A new capability matrix shows which brokers support expired F&O data. Currently only **Upstox Plus Plan** is supported. All 24+ broker `plugin.json` files updated with structured `historify_capabilities` field. ### Stats Dashboard Live stats at the top of the Expired F&O tab: - Expiries cached - Contracts cached - Downloaded contracts - Total candles stored ### New Files | File | Description | |------|-------------| | `broker/upstox/api/expired_data.py` | Thread-safe Upstox expired-instruments API client with rate limiter | | `services/expired_fno_service.py` | Full service layer: 3-phase pipeline, job management, parallel downloader | | `frontend/src/api/expiredFno.ts` | TypeScript API client for all expired F&O endpoints | | `frontend/src/pages/historify/ExpiredFnoTab.tsx` | React component: full 3-phase UI with status pills | | `frontend/e2e/expired-fno.spec.ts` | Playwright end-to-end tests | ### Modified Files | `blueprints/historify.py` | +244 lines: all expired F&O API routes | | `database/historify_db.py` | +590 lines: DuckDB schema, CRUD, `get_expired_fno_expiry_stats()` | | `app.py` | Register historify blueprint | | `utils/plugin_loader.py` | Load `historify_capabilities` from broker plugins | | `frontend/src/pages/Historify.tsx` | Add Expired F&O tab | | `broker/upstox/plugin.json` | Add `historify_capabilities` with `expired_contracts: full` | | All other `broker/*/plugin.json` | Add `historify_capabilities` (none/limited as appropriate) | ## Database Schema (DuckDB) Two new tables in `db/historify.duckdb`: ```sql CREATE TABLE expired_fno_expiries ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, upstox_key VARCHAR, -- e.g. NSE_INDEX|NIFTY50 openalgo_symbol VARCHAR, -- e.g. NIFTY exchange VARCHAR, expiry_date DATE, is_weekly BOOLEAN, contracts_fetched BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE, data_fetched BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE, fetched_at TIMESTAMP ); CREATE TABLE expired_fno_contracts ( expired_instrument_key VARCHAR PRIMARY KEY, -- Upstox key upstox_key VARCHAR, openalgo_symbol VARCHAR, -- e.g. NIFTY28MAR2420800CE exchange VARCHAR, expiry_date DATE, contract_type VARCHAR, -- CE / PE / FUT strike_price DOUBLE, trading_symbol VARCHAR, lot_size INTEGER, data_fetched BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE, candle_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0, created_at TIMESTAMP ); CREATE TABLE expired_fno_jobs ( id VARCHAR PRIMARY KEY, underlying VARCHAR, exchange VARCHAR, expiry_date VARCHAR, contract_types VARCHAR, interval VARCHAR, status VARCHAR, -- pending / running / completed / failed / cancelled total_contracts INTEGER, completed_contracts INTEGER, failed_contracts INTEGER, error_message VARCHAR, created_at TIMESTAMP, started_at TIMESTAMP, completed_at TIMESTAMP ); ## Bug Fixes & Thread-Safety All issues found during code review have been resolved: | # | Issue | Fix | |---|-------|-----| | 1 | `_SyncUpstoxRateLimiter.on_response()` mutated `_error_count`/`_backoff_factor` without holding `self._lock` | Added `with self._lock:` in `on_response()` | | 2 | `_cancelled_jobs` set leaked on normal completion | Added `finally: _cancelled_jobs.discard(job_id)` wrapping entire job | | 3 | `_get_executor()` had TOCTOU race (lazy init + global) | Replaced with module-level `ThreadPoolExecutor` initialised at import | | 4 | Local imports inside functions (`threading`, `concurrent.futures`, `get_all_expired_fno_jobs`) | Moved all imports to top of file | | 5 | `cancel_job()` wrote `status=cancelled` to DB, racing with thread writing `status=completed` | Thread final-status write now guarded by `if job_id not in _cancelled_jobs` | | 6 | `upsert_expired_fno_contracts()` only marked `contracts[0]["expiry_date"]` as `contracts_fetched` in multi-expiry batches | Now iterates all unique `(upstox_key, expiry_date)` pairs in the batch | | 7 | "No candles" contracts (illiquid OTM options) never marked `data_fetched=True` | Now calls `mark_expired_fno_contract_done(key, 0)` so incremental runs skip them | ## API Endpoints All endpoints under `/historify/api/expired/`: | Method | Path | Description | |--------|------|-------------| | `GET` | `/capability` | Check if active broker supports expired F&O | | `POST` | `/expiries` | Phase 1: fetch & cache expiry dates from Upstox | | `GET` | `/expiries?underlying=NIFTY` | Get cached expiries (now includes `total_contracts`, `downloaded_contracts` per expiry) | | `POST` | `/contracts` | Phase 2: fetch & cache contracts for expiries | | `GET` | `/contracts?underlying=NIFTY&expiry_dates=...` | Get cached contracts | | `POST` | `/jobs` | Phase 3: start background download job | | `GET` | `/jobs` | List recent jobs | | `GET` | `/jobs/{id}` | Get job status + progress % | | `POST` | `/jobs/{id}/cancel` | Request cancellation | | `GET` | `/stats` | Summary stats (expiries, contracts, candles) | | `GET` | `/broker/capabilities` | Capability matrix for all brokers | **Expired F&O tab — live download in progress (NIFTY, 47M+ candles stored)** ![Expired F&O Tab](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/placeholder-tab) **Step 1 — Per-expiry status pills (green = complete, yellow = partial, orange = not started)** Shows 219 expiries with per-expiry download counts. Users click "Incomplete" to auto-select only expiries needing work. **Broker capability matrix** Structured `historify_capabilities` in every broker's `plugin.json`: "historify_capabilities": { "futures_historical": "full", "options_historical": "full", "expired_contracts": "full" Upstox is the only broker with `expired_contracts: full` (requires Plus Plan). - [x] Phase 1: Select NIFTY → Fetch Expiries → expiry list populates with status pills - [x] Phase 2: Select expiries → Fetch Contracts → contracts cached, orange `0/N` pills appear - [x] Phase 3: Start Download → real-time progress bar via Socket.IO → green `N ✓` pills after completion - [x] "Incomplete" button selects only non-complete expiries - [x] Cancel mid-job → job stops at next contract boundary, no partial data - [x] Incremental re-run skips already-downloaded contracts and "no candles" contracts - [x] Stocks tab: select RELIANCE / TCS / etc. → same 3-phase flow works - [x] Non-Upstox broker → capability check shows unsupported message - [x] Playwright e2e tests: `frontend/e2e/expired-fno.spec.ts` Adds an Expired F&O download flow to Historify powered by Upstox’s expired-instruments API, plus a searchable F&O stock combobox for quick symbol selection. This includes a new tab, per-expiry progress, and a 4‑worker downloader that writes safely to `DuckDB`. - New Expired F&O tab with a 3‑phase pipeline (fetch expiries → cache contracts → download 1m candles), per‑expiry status pills, and an Incomplete quick‑select. - 4‑worker downloads with a shared rate limiter, serialized `DuckDB` writes, resumable jobs, live stats, and REST routes under `/historify/api/expired/*` and `/historify/api/broker/capabilities`; broker capability matrix read from plugin `capabilities` with fallback to `historify_capabilities` (Upstox Plus supported). - NSE F&O equity stock list API (`GET /historify/api/fno/stocks`) and UI: the Expired F&O tab uses a searchable stock combobox backed by this API. - **Bug Fixes** - Rate limiter: lock updates in responses and move sleeps outside the mutex to avoid stalls. - Job/data integrity: guard final‑status writes on cancel, mark all expiries in multi‑expiry batches and “no candles” contracts as done, record partial downloads in `error_message`, and prevent empty `contract_types` from generating invalid SQL. - UI/tests/misc: fix socket callback closure, clean polling, prevent checkbox double events; remove the Historify watchlist F&O‑stocks bulk‑import (combobox retained in the Expired tab); E2E skips when Flask isn’t running and asserts non‑200 auth responses; move imports to module top‑level; set `allow_unsafe_werkzeug=True`; normalize broker capability keys. - Upstream merge: accept updated `mstock` `supported_exchanges` (remove BCD/MCX) and rebuild frontend dist. Written for commit 4623f79a8f4bd86366c34356a70c8bbee473dda5. Summary will update on new commits.

title: perf(linux): add memfd optimizations and typed flags
body:
- Add `MemfdFlags` enum to replace raw integer flags for `memfd_create`, providing semantic clarity for different use cases (`executable`, `non_executable`, `cross_process`)

- Use memfd + `/proc/self/fd/{fd}` path for loading embedded `.node` files in standalone builds, avoiding disk writes entirely on Linux

title: refactor: Replace local iGenomes STAR modules with nf-core aliases
body:
- Remove duplicate local STAR modules (`star_align_igenomes`, `star_genomegenerate_igenomes`) that were near-identical copies of nf-core equivalents differing only in container version (STAR 2.6.1d vs 2.7.11b)
- Replace with nf-core module aliases (`STAR_ALIGN as STAR_ALIGN_IGENOMES`, `STAR_GENOMEGENERATE as STAR_GENOMEGENERATE_IGENOMES`) pinned to STAR 2.6.1d via config-based container/conda overrides
- Merge the two duplicated ext.args blocks in `align_star/nextflow.config` into a single block, using `task.process` introspection to select the correct transcriptome ban flag
- Net removal of ~2,600 lines of duplicated code

## What changed

| File | Action |
| `modules/local/star_align_igenomes/` | **deleted** (entire directory) |
| `modules/local/star_genomegenerate_igenomes/` | **deleted** (entire directory) |
| `conf/igenomes_star.config` | **new** - amd64 container overrides for STAR 2.6.1d |
| `nextflow.config` | include `conf/igenomes_star.config` unconditionally; add `params.arm` flag |
| `nextflow_schema.json` | add hidden `arm` boolean param |
| `subworkflows/local/align_star/main.nf` | import changed to nf-core alias |
| `subworkflows/local/align_star/nextflow.config` | merged two near-identical ext.args blocks into one |
| `subworkflows/local/prepare_genome/main.nf` | import changed to nf-core alias + meta tuple calling convention |
| `subworkflows/local/align_star/tests/nextflow.igenomes.config` | **new** - test-specific config for bare STAR_GENOMEGENERATE in nf-test setup blocks |
| `subworkflows/local/align_star/tests/main.nf.test` | updated igenomes tests to use nf-core setup |
| `subworkflows/local/align_star/tests/main.nf.test.snap` | updated snapshots |

## Design

The STAR 2.6.1d container is needed for compatibility with pre-built AWS iGenomes STAR indices. Rather than maintaining local module copies, we use:

1. **nf-core module aliases** - `STAR_ALIGN as STAR_ALIGN_IGENOMES` etc. in the workflow includes, creating distinct process names for config targeting
2. **Config-based container overrides** - `conf/igenomes_star.config` pins STAR 2.6.1d for the aliased process names via `withName` selectors
3. **Unified ext.args** - a single config block handles all three STAR variants (`STAR_ALIGN`, `STAR_ALIGN_IGENOMES`, `SENTIEON_STAR_ALIGN`), using `task.process.endsWith(':STAR_ALIGN')` to select the STAR 2.7+ flag (`--quantTranscriptomeSAMoutput BanSingleEnd`) vs the STAR 2.6 flag (`--quantTranscriptomeBan Singleend`). All other args (rsem vs salmon, prokaryotic, save_unaligned, extra_star_align_args) are shared

### ARM handling

- **Production**: `conf/igenomes_star.config` (loaded before profiles) sets amd64 containers. The `arm64` profile loads `conf/arm.config`, whose `withName` selectors for `STAR_ALIGN_IGENOMES` and `STAR_GENOMEGENERATE_IGENOMES` override with ARM-specific STAR 2.6.1d containers
- **nf-test**: The pipeline's config chain handles IGENOMES-suffixed processes automatically. The test config (`nextflow.igenomes.config`) only provides a bare `STAR_GENOMEGENERATE` override for nf-test setup blocks, using a `params.arm`-aware closure to select the correct container at runtime


- [x] CI: "star - no igenomes" and "star - no igenomes - stub" tests pass (unchanged)
- [x] CI: "star - with igenomes" and "star - with igenomes - stub" tests pass with regenerated snapshots
- [x] CI: Pipeline-level tests pass (full config chain loads `conf/igenomes_star.config`)
- [x] CI: ARM tests pass (arm.config overrides verified with `nextflow config -flat -profile test,arm64`)
- [x] Nextflow lint passes

title: research: macOS sandbox-exec capabilities and limitations
body:
- Comprehensive research on macOS sandbox-exec for polecat isolation (gt-6qt)
- Confirms sandbox-exec is fully functional on Sequoia despite deprecation
- Documents SBPL syntax, Node.js compatibility, and a complete working profile template
- Blocks gt-2pb (Spike: macOS sandbox-exec polecat isolation)

## Key Findings
- Filesystem, network, and process restrictions all work as expected
- Node.js requires specific SBPL rules (file-ioctl, mach-host*, pseudo-tty, etc.)
- No code signing / Gatekeeper interference
- No viable alternatives — sandbox-exec is the only practical option for CLI sandboxing

- [x] Local testing on macOS Sequoia confirmed all sandbox capabilities
- [x] Node.js v25.6.0 runs successfully under sandbox with CPUs detected

title: feat(cache): prevent bots from writing to cache
body:
- Bots can **read** from cache but must **not write** or trigger background revalidation
- Bots often hit arbitrary URLs with unique query params that would pollute all cache tiers with one-hit entries
- Uses existing `isBot()` utility (UA-based detection)
- Stale responses are still served to bots (read-only, no revalidation triggered)

- [ ] Send request with bot UA — verify cache hit/stale works but no new entries are written
- [ ] Send request with normal UA — verify cache write works as before
- [ ] Monitor `loader_cache` metric — bot requests should show as hits/stale but never miss→write


**PR 5 of 5** — split from #1122. Merge order: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5

Prevent bots from writing to the loader cache, triggering background revalidation, or leading non-bot singleFlight work. Bots can still read cached/stale responses and now deduplicate via a separate singleFlight key.

  - Detect bots via `isBot` (User-Agent).
  - Skip `cache.put` and background revalidation for bots.
  - Use a separate singleFlight key for bot requests to dedupe bot traffic without affecting non-bot callers.
  - No behavior changes for normal users.

<sup>Written for commit 844cac8671e71a4b6d9871fca25a3e28be053844. Summary will update on new commits.</sup>



  * Prevented automated/bot traffic from triggering cache writes and background revalidations, reducing redundant processing and load.
  * Bots can still read cached content to ensure consistent responses.
  * Bot requests are deduplicated separately from regular traffic to avoid interfering with normal cache behavior.
commit_msgs:
feat(cache): prevent bots from writing to cache or triggering revalidation

Bots can read from cache but must not write to it or trigger background
revalidation. They often hit arbitrary URLs with unique query params
that would pollute all cache tiers with one-hit entries.

- Detect bot requests via User-Agent (existing isBot utility)
- Skip cache.put() for bot requests
- Skip background revalidation for bot requests
- Bots still get served stale/cached responses (read-only)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix(cache): prevent bot requests from leading shared singleFlight

Bot requests skip cache writes and revalidation. If a bot became the
singleFlight leader, concurrent non-bot callers would inherit that
behavior and miss their cache write. Fix: bots bypass singleFlight
entirely and run staleWhileRevalidate directly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix(cache): use separate singleFlight keys for bot vs non-bot requests

Instead of bypassing singleFlight entirely (which wastes CPU on duplicate
bot requests), use a prefixed flight key so bots still deduplicate among
themselves but never become leader for non-bot callers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: fix(weixin): fix channel mode model selection and Google OAuth fallback
body:
- Fix channel-configured model not being applied for gemini-cli and non-claude ACP backends
- Allow reuse of Google OAuth credentials (from `~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json`) in channel mode, so users who have logged in via Gemini CLI don't need a separate API key
- When no model is explicitly saved for the WeChat channel, automatically fall back to Google OAuth credentials if available — preventing "Could not load the default credentials" (ADC) errors
- Construct Google Auth provider directly in channel mode instead of relying on the synthetic frontend provider
- Hide the "Continue?" tool confirmation prompt in WeChat channel (WeChat already runs in yoloMode so the prompt is auto-approved in the background — showing it without interactive buttons is confusing)


- [ ] With no model saved for the WeChat channel and Google OAuth creds present (`~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json`), send a WeChat message — should use Google Auth instead of crashing with ADC error
- [ ] With a saved model explicitly set to Google Auth provider, channel mode should still use the correct OAuth credentials
- [ ] With a regular API key provider saved, channel should use that API key as before
- [ ] Tool calls in WeChat channel should auto-approve without showing "Continue?" to the user
commit_msgs:
fix: apply channel-configured model for gemini-cli and other non-claude ACP backends

Previously, model selection in channel settings was ignored for gemini-cli sessions
because `setModel` was only called for the `claude` backend. The channel's configured
model (from `assistant.weixin.defaultModel`) was never forwarded to the ACP subprocess.

- Pass `c.model?.useModel` from the conversation record into `AcpAgentManager` as the
  initial `currentModelId` so it reaches `persistedModelId` in the constructor.
- Thread `currentModelId` from `AcpAgentManager` into `AcpAgent.extra` when creating
  the agent subprocess.
- In `AcpAgent.start()`, call `setModel` for non-claude backends when `currentModelId`
  is set (covers gemini-cli and any future ACP-based backends).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix: allow Google OAuth credentials in channel mode when local creds exist

Previously getChannelDefaultModel() unconditionally skipped the Google Auth
provider in channel mode, falling back to a hardcoded empty-key provider which
caused "Could not load the default credentials" errors.

If the user has already logged in with `gemini auth login` on the desktop,
the credentials are cached in ~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json. Channel mode can
reuse those local credentials without a browser flow, so we now check for
the credentials file before deciding to skip the Google Auth provider.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix(weixin): hide tool confirmation prompt in WeChat channel

WeChat uses yoloMode so tool confirmations are auto-approved in the
background. Sending "Continue?" without interactive buttons is confusing
to the user. Show plain tool progress lines instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix(weixin): construct Google Auth provider directly for channel mode

The google-auth-gemini provider is a frontend-only synthetic entry built
in useModelProviderList.ts and never stored in model.config. Looking it
up via providerList.find() always returned undefined, causing the code to
fall through to an API-key Gemini provider with an empty key.

With an empty key, GeminiAgentManager used ADC which fails on a non-GCE
server ("Could not load default credentials"), causing agent.send() to
hang indefinitely. ChannelMessageService.sendMessage never resolved, and
the WeChat 5-minute timeout fired with no reply sent.

Fix: when oauth_creds.json exists, construct the provider object directly
with platform='gemini-with-google-auth' so getProviderAuthType() returns
AuthType.LOGIN_WITH_GOOGLE and GeminiAgentManager reads the local OAuth
credentials instead of falling back to ADC/API-key.

title: Fix clipboard race condition with speech-to-text paste
body:
- When a speech-to-text tool (e.g. MacWhisper) updates the clipboard and immediately triggers Cmd+V / Ctrl+V, the paste keystroke can arrive at the server before the clipboard content has been written — pasting stale/empty content
- Root cause: `update_clipboard()` spawns a fire-and-forget background thread, so the server processes the next message (the paste keystroke) before the clipboard write completes
- Fix: add an awaitable `update_clipboard_blocking()` variant using `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`, and use it on the server side so the clipboard write completes before the next message is processed


The race condition flow:
1. Client clipboard changes → `MultiClipboards` message sent to server
2. Client keystroke (Cmd+V) → `KeyEvent` message sent to server
3. Server receives `MultiClipboards` → spawns background thread to write clipboard → **immediately moves on**
4. Server receives `KeyEvent` (paste) → injects keystroke → OS pastes from clipboard that hasn't been written yet

The fix ensures step 3 completes before step 4 begins, by awaiting the clipboard write on the server's async message loop. The client side remains unchanged (fire-and-forget) since the race only affects the controlled machine.

This is a minimal, ~10-line change touching only two files with no protocol or behavioral changes for normal usage.


- [ ] Verify normal clipboard copy-paste between client and server works unchanged
- [ ] Test with a speech-to-text tool that uses clipboard + paste (e.g. MacWhisper) — text should now arrive correctly on the remote machine
- [ ] Confirm no noticeable latency increase during regular remote desktop usage
- [ ] Test on macOS, Windows, and Linux server targets
commit_msgs:
Fix clipboard race condition with speech-to-text paste

When a speech-to-text tool (e.g. MacWhisper) updates the clipboard and
immediately triggers Cmd+V/Ctrl+V, the paste keystroke can arrive at the
server before the clipboard content has been written, because
update_clipboard() spawns a fire-and-forget background thread.

Replace the server-side update_clipboard() calls with an awaitable
variant (update_clipboard_blocking) that uses spawn_blocking to ensure
the clipboard write completes before the next message — typically the
paste keystroke — is processed. The client side is unchanged since the
race only affects the controlled (server) machine.

title: Fix flaky test_sqlite_kill_query/test_cancel_query under MSan
body:
- Fix `test_cancel_query` in `test_sqlite_kill_query` flaking under MSan due to stale log line matching
- `wait_for_log_line("Generate a chuck")` was matching a leftover log line from the preceding `test_kill_query`, causing the test to send SIGINT before the client entered the query loop
- Under MSan (3-5x slower), the client exited without sending a Cancel packet, so the server never logged the expected exception
- Fix: use `look_behind_lines=0` so `tail` only follows new lines

CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=98361&sha=8369a24c6bd7f4bda13cef73619d83980543b56c&name_0=PR&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_msan%2C%205%2F6%29

commit_msgs:
Fix flaky test_sqlite_kill_query/test_cancel_query under MSan

The test_cancel_query was flaky under MSan because
wait_for_log_line("Generate a chuck") matched a stale log line from the
preceding test_kill_query. This caused the test to proceed before the
clickhouse client query actually started reading data. Under MSan (3-5x
slower), when SIGINT was sent, the client hadn't entered the query loop
yet and exited without sending a Cancel packet, so the server never
logged the expected exception.

Fix: use look_behind_lines=0 so tail only sees new log lines.
Also simplify the grep pattern for the cancel message.

- **Session persistence**: Conversations are saved per workspace directory
- **Workspace switching**: Change working directory with folder picker
- **Streaming responses**: Real-time text streaming from Claude API
- **API timeout control**: 60-second timeout with cancel button
- **Third-party proxy support**: Reads API key from environment variables or `~/.claude/settings.json`
- **Dark/light theme**: Follows system theme preferences
- **Auto-cleanup**: Removes sessions older than 30 days


### New Files
- `src/ask-panel.html` - Floating panel UI (560 lines)
- `src/preload-ask.js` - IPC bridge for panel
- `src/session-manager.js` - Session persistence with auto-cleanup

- `src/hit-renderer.js` - Double-click detection (2-3 clicks → open panel, 4+ clicks → reaction)
- `src/preload-hit.js` - Added `openAskPanel()` IPC call
- `package.json` - Added `@anthropic-ai/sdk` dependency

- ✅ Removed plaintext API key storage (only uses env vars or Claude Code settings)
- ✅ Added automatic cleanup of sessions older than 30 days
- ✅ Added 60-second timeout for API calls with cancel button
- ✅ Updated error messages to guide users to secure config sources

## API Key Configuration

The panel reads API keys from (in order):
1. Environment variable `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
2. `~/.claude/settings.json` (supports `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` for third-party proxies)

For third-party proxies, set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` in the same location.

title: mark used resources in pytest
body:
requires https://github.com/imbue-ai/mng/pull/652



- Adds a resource guard system that enforces pytest marks for external tool dependencies (tmux, rsync, unison)
- PATH wrapper scripts intercept binary calls during the test call phase and block unmarked tests
- Must-use enforcement catches superfluous marks (tests marked but never invoking the resource)
- Blocked-invocation tracking catches tests that handle the guard's exit code gracefully
- Marks added to ~330 tests across 40+ files
- Fixes a CPython posix_spawn bug where `subprocess.Popen` intermittently uses stale environment (cpython#113119)
- **Found and fixed a real bug in `UnisonSyncer.is_running`** (see below)

## Bug found: UnisonSyncer.is_running was lying

The must-use enforcement caught a real bug: `UnisonSyncer.is_running` returned `True` as soon as `subprocess.Popen` created the OS process, before unison had actually initialized. Tests that called `start()` then immediately checked `is_running` and called `stop()` were killing the process within ~4ms of spawning -- before the unison binary even loaded. These tests appeared to pass but were testing nothing.

**Fix:** `is_running` now requires that unison has produced at least one line of output (tracked via a `threading.Event` set by the `on_output` callback). This ensures unison has actually started before callers can observe it as "running."


1. At session start, bash wrapper scripts are created for each guarded binary and prepended to PATH
2. During the test call phase (not fixture setup/teardown), wrappers check env vars to allow/block
3. If a test invokes a resource without `@pytest.mark.<resource>`, the wrapper writes a `blocked_<resource>` tracking file and exits 127
4. After the test, `makereport` checks for blocked tracking files (missing mark) and unused allowed resources (superfluous mark), failing the test in either case

The blocked-invocation tracking is important: without it, a test that expects a failure (e.g., checking `is_running` returns False) could silently pass by handling the guard's exit 127 as a legitimate error. The tracking file ensures `makereport` catches it regardless. This caught additional tests that were missing marks across unit, integration, and acceptance tests.

## Demo

Five test scenarios showing the guard system in action:

def test_no_mark_no_call():
    """No mark, no call -- should pass."""
    assert 1 + 1 == 2

@pytest.mark.tmux
def test_has_mark_and_calls_tmux():
    """Has @pytest.mark.tmux and actually calls tmux -- should pass."""
    result = subprocess.run(["tmux", "-V"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert result.returncode == 0

def test_no_mark_but_calls_tmux():
    """Missing @pytest.mark.tmux but calls tmux -- should FAIL (guard blocks it)."""
    result = subprocess.run(["tmux", "-V"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert result.returncode == 0

def test_no_mark_handles_error_gracefully():
    """Missing mark, but test handles the 127 -- should still FAIL via makereport."""
    result = subprocess.run(["tmux", "-V"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert result.returncode != 0

@pytest.mark.tmux
def test_has_mark_but_never_calls_tmux():
    """Has @pytest.mark.tmux but never calls tmux -- should FAIL (superfluous mark)."""
    assert 1 + 1 == 2

Results: 2 passed, 3 failed -- exactly as expected:

PASSED  test_no_mark_no_call
PASSED  test_has_mark_and_calls_tmux
FAILED  test_no_mark_but_calls_tmux
FAILED  test_no_mark_handles_error_gracefully
FAILED  test_has_mark_but_never_calls_tmux

**Missing mark (assertion failure)** -- the wrapper intercepts the call and exits 127:
_________________________ test_no_mark_but_calls_tmux __________________________

    def test_no_mark_but_calls_tmux():
        result = subprocess.run(["tmux", "-V"], capture_output=True, text=True)
>       assert result.returncode == 0
E       assert 127 == 0
E        +  where 127 = CompletedProcess(
E              args=['tmux', '-V'], returncode=127, stdout='',
E              stderr="RESOURCE GUARD: Test invoked 'tmux' without @pytest.mark.tmux mark.\n
E                      Add @pytest.mark.tmux to the test, or remove the tmux usage.\n"
E            ).returncode

**Missing mark (error handled gracefully)** -- the test's own assertion passes, but makereport catches the blocked tracking file:
____________________ test_no_mark_handles_error_gracefully _____________________
Test invoked 'tmux' without @pytest.mark.tmux.
Add @pytest.mark.tmux to the test, or remove the tmux usage.

**Superfluous mark** -- the tracking file was never created, so the test is failed after the call phase:
______________________ test_has_mark_but_never_calls_tmux ______________________
Test marked with @pytest.mark.tmux but never invoked tmux.
Remove the mark or ensure the test exercises tmux.


- [x] All 3010 tests pass with guards active
- [x] Blocking catches tests that use resources without marks
- [x] Blocked-invocation tracking catches tests that handle the exit code gracefully
- [x] Must-use catches tests with superfluous marks
- [x] Guards only active during call phase (fixtures can use tools freely)
- [x] Works with xdist parallel workers
- [x] UnisonSyncer.is_running fix verified with 10/10 passes on previously-failing tests

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Add pytest resource marks to integration test files

Add @pytest.mark.git, @pytest.mark.rsync, @pytest.mark.tmux, and
@pytest.mark.unison to integration test functions based on what
resources each test uses during its call phase:

- test_push.py: 26 marks (rsync for file sync, git for stash/commit ops)
- test_pull.py: 28 marks (rsync for file sync, git for stash/commit/fetch ops)
- test_create.py: 16 marks (tmux for agent creation, git for worktrees, rsync for copies)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Remove superfluous @pytest.mark.git from 6 tests that don't invoke heavy git subcommands

The resource guard system enforces that tests marked with @pytest.mark.git
actually invoke the git binary with a heavy subcommand (init, clone, commit,
worktree, etc.) during the call phase. These 6 tests were marked with
@pytest.mark.git but never triggered the guard because:

- test_ensure_clean_rejects_dirty_worktree_by_default: Uses CliRunner
  in-process; internal git status call is a lightweight subcommand
- test_ensure_clean_skipped_with_explicit_base_branch: Uses CliRunner
  in-process; subprocess git branch is not a heavy subcommand
- test_destroy_remove_created_branch_deletes_branch: Uses CliRunner
  in-process; git commands use -C flag so $1 is not a heavy subcommand
- test_destroy_without_remove_created_branch_leaves_branch: Same as above
- test_push_files_does_not_modify_host_directory[clobber]: CLOBBER mode
  skips git stash/pop, only stash and merge variants need @pytest.mark.git
- test_pair_files_starts_and_stops_syncer: Both repos have same commit,
  so no git sync occurs; only lightweight rev-parse commands are used

For the parametrized push test, moved @pytest.mark.git from the function
level to individual pytest.param entries for stash and merge variants only.

Also commits the resource guard system in conftest_hooks.py which was
previously uncommitted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Improve git guard to skip global flags and find actual subcommand

The git wrapper script previously checked $1 against the heavy subcommands
list, but git -C /path worktree add has -C as $1, not worktree. Now the
wrapper skips global flags (-C, -c, --git-dir, --work-tree, etc.) to find
the actual subcommand before matching against the heavy list.

Re-added @pytest.mark.git to tests that use git worktree operations through
the CLI runner, which the improved detection now correctly catches.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Fix git guard flag-skipping, disable unreliable must-use enforcement

The git wrapper now skips global flags (-C, --git-dir, etc.) to find the
actual subcommand. This correctly catches `git -C /path worktree add` as
a heavy operation, re-enabling @pytest.mark.git on destroy tests that use
worktree operations through the CLI runner.

Disabled the must-use enforcement (marked test must invoke resource)
because subprocess.Popen on macOS does not reliably resolve binaries
through a modified PATH (posix_spawn behavior). The blocking direction
(unmarked test blocked from using resource) still works correctly since
it causes the wrapper to exit 127.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Add @pytest.mark.git to 140 tests that invoke git via lightweight commands

The resource guard now blocks ALL git invocations (not just heavy
subcommands like init/commit/push). This removes the heavy-subcommand
filtering from conftest_hooks.py and adds @pytest.mark.git to every
test that invokes git through any path:

- Ratchet tests (98 tests across 2 files): use git ls-files via the
  ratchet framework. Applied via pytestmark module-level mark.
- Config/CLI tests (23 tests across 5 files): use git rev-parse to
  find repo root for project config resolution.
- Push/pull tests (12 tests across 2 files): use git status to check
  for uncommitted changes.
- Git utils, create, pair, and deploy tests (8 tests across 4 files):
  use git config, git status, or git rev-parse.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Remove git subcommand filtering, disable must-use enforcement

Git guard no longer filters by subcommand -- all git invocations during the
call phase trigger the guard. This treats git as a dependency (any test using
git needs @pytest.mark.git) rather than filtering by operation weight.

Disabled must-use enforcement (marked test must invoke resource) because it
has too many false negatives: LRU-cached subprocess calls (ratchet tests
cache git ls-files results across tests), in-process invocations via Click
CliRunner, and library code that caches binary resolution. The blocking
direction (unmarked test blocked from using resource) remains the primary
enforcement mechanism.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Remove git subcommand filtering, disable must-use enforcement

Git guard now treats all git invocations equally (no special handling for
"heavy" vs "lightweight" subcommands). This correctly models git as a
binary dependency - any test that calls git for any reason should declare
@pytest.mark.git.

Disabled must-use enforcement (failing tests that have a mark but never
invoke the resource binary). This direction has too many false negatives:
- LRU-cached subprocess calls (ratchet tests cache git ls-files results)
- In-process invocations via Click CliRunner (no subprocess spawned)
- Module-level pytestmark (mark is a dependency declaration, not per-test)

The blocking direction (catching unmarked tests that invoke a resource)
remains fully active and is the primary enforcement mechanism.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Disable must-use enforcement in resource guard

The must-use direction (failing tests that have a mark but never invoke
the resource binary) has too many false negatives to be reliable:
- LRU-cached subprocess calls (ratchet tests cache git ls-files)
- In-process invocations via Click CliRunner (no subprocess spawned)
- Module-level pytestmark (mark is a dependency declaration, not per-test)

The blocking direction (unmarked test blocked from invoking resource)
remains the primary enforcement mechanism.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Remove git subcommand filtering, re-enable must-use enforcement

- Git guard no longer filters by subcommand weight. Any git invocation
  during the call phase triggers the guard, treating git as a binary
  dependency rather than filtering by operation type.

- Must-use enforcement re-enabled: tests marked with @pytest.mark.<resource>
  that never invoke the resource binary are failed. This catches superfluous
  marks that would slow down filtered test runs.

- Ratchet tests are exempt from must-use enforcement via xdist_group check.
  The ratchet framework caches git ls-files results with @lru_cache, so only
  the first test in the group actually spawns the binary.

- Removed the library-path-based exemption (_GUARD_EXEMPT_PATH_SEGMENTS).
  All libraries including imbue_common are now subject to guards.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Fix posix_spawn stale env bug by explicitly passing os.environ.copy()

On macOS, subprocess.Popen with env=None uses posix_spawn which reads
the process environment via _NSGetEnviron(). This can return a stale
pointer if env vars were modified since process start (CPython #113119).

Pass os.environ.copy() explicitly when env is None so Popen always uses
the current environment dict rather than the potentially-stale pointer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Merge branch 'mng/bad-popen-local' into mng/color-local
Remove skip_must_use_check now that posix_spawn env bug is fixed

The subprocess_utils.py fix (passing os.environ.copy() explicitly to
Popen) resolves the intermittent environment propagation issue that
caused the unison wrapper tracking to fail for this test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Remove duplicate @pytest.mark.rsync decorator

Problem: test_pull_files_fail_mode_with_no_uncommitted_changes_succeeds in
libs/mng/imbue/mng/api/test_pull.py had @pytest.mark.rsync applied twice.
Fix: Removed the duplicate decorator, keeping one instance.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Fix UnisonSyncer.is_running to require actual unison initialization

is_running previously returned True as soon as the OS process was spawned
(subprocess.Popen returned). This meant callers could immediately stop
the syncer before unison had even loaded, resulting in tests that appeared
to start and stop unison but never actually ran it.

Now is_running requires that unison has produced at least one line of
output, which signals that the binary has initialized. This is tracked
via a threading.Event set by the on_output callback.

This was caught by the resource guard must-use enforcement: tests marked
@pytest.mark.unison were failing because the guard wrapper script's
touch command never executed -- the process was killed within milliseconds
of spawning, before bash could parse and execute the wrapper.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into mng/color-local

# Conflicts:
#	libs/mng/imbue/mng/hosts/test_host.py
Add missing resource marks caught by CI

- test_create_work_dir_copy_excludes_git_when_disabled: new test from
  main merge, needs @pytest.mark.git and @pytest.mark.rsync
- test_sync_acceptance.py: all acceptance tests need @pytest.mark.tmux,
  @pytest.mark.git, and @pytest.mark.rsync (they create agents and do
  git/rsync sync operations)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Remove @pytest.mark.tmux from sync acceptance tests

These tests create agents via run_mng_subprocess (a child process), not
by calling tmux directly. The tmux wrapper in the test process's PATH
is never invoked, causing must-use failures.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Set guard env vars during setup phase so fixtures capture them

Previously all guard env vars were set in _pytest_runtest_call (the call
phase). Fixtures that snapshot os.environ during setup (like
get_subprocess_test_env) would miss the guard configuration, causing
child processes spawned by those fixtures to bypass the wrappers.

Now the allow/block and tracking dir env vars are set in
_pytest_runtest_setup (before fixtures run), while _PYTEST_GUARD_PHASE
is still only set during _pytest_runtest_call. This means:
- Fixtures see the guard vars and pass them to child processes
- Wrappers still only enforce during the call phase (not setup/teardown)
- Cleanup happens in _pytest_runtest_teardown

title: feat: Finalize C API and regular API
body:
This PR finalizes the C API and regular API for Guillotine EVM, providing comprehensive configuration options and a clean, ergonomic interface for both C and Zig consumers.

### Key Changes

- **Comprehensive Build Configuration**: Added extensive build-time configuration options for EIPs, hardforks, memory management, tracer settings, and system contracts
- **Enhanced EVM Configuration System**: Implemented runtime parsing for EIP overrides and tracer presets with full type safety
- **Streamlined Module Structure**: Simplified root.zig to expose only essential types, removing redundant re-exports
- **C API Improvements**: Updated C API implementation with better alignment to simplified module structure
- **Code Cleanup**: Removed obsolete files and improved code formatting

### Configuration Features

#### Build Options Added
- EIP override support (e.g., `3855:true,1153:false`)
- Call/stack limits (max_input_size, max_call_depth, stack_size)
- Memory configuration (initial capacity, limits, arena settings)
- Tracer configuration with presets (disabled, debug, full)
- System contract toggles (beacon roots, historical hashes, validator deposits/withdrawals)
- SIMD vector length configuration
- Loop safety quota settings
- Block info compact types option

#### API Improvements
- Type-safe configuration parsing
- Build-time EIP customization
- Flexible tracer configuration
- Comprehensive memory management options

### Files Changed

- `build.zig` - Expanded with organized configuration options
- `src/evm_config.zig` - Enhanced with parsing logic and build integration
- `src/root.zig` - Streamlined to essential exports
- `src/root_c.zig` - Updated C API implementation
- `src/evm_c_api.zig` - Code formatting improvements
- Removed obsolete `src/main.zig` and `src/_test_utils/README.md`

### Test Plan

- [ ] Verify all build configurations compile successfully
- [ ] Test EIP override parsing with various combinations
- [ ] Validate tracer presets (disabled, debug, full)
- [ ] Confirm C API compatibility with existing consumers
- [ ] Run full test suite: `zig build test`
- [ ] Test with different optimization levels
- [ ] Verify system contract toggles work correctly


*Note: This action was performed by Claude AI assistant, not @roninjin10 or @fucory*

title: Fix #291: Support multiple xpubs per auth key to fix duplicate addresses
body:
Implement support for exporting and storing separate extended public keys (xpubs) for each BIP purpose (44, 49, 84, 86) per auth key. This fixes the duplicate address issue where different address types (Taproot, Bech32, P2SH-SegWit, Legacy) derived from the same xpub, causing database constraint violations.


The current implementation exports and stores only ONE xpub per auth key at m/49'/1' level. This causes all address types to derive from the same xpub, resulting in duplicate addresses at the same index and database constraint violations.


Export and store **separate xpubs for EACH BIP purpose**:
- m/44'/1' for BIP44 (Legacy/P2PKH)
- m/49'/1' for BIP49 (P2SH-SegWit)  
- m/84'/1' for BIP84 (Native SegWit/Bech32)
- m/86'/1' for BIP86 (Taproot)


### Database Layer
- Add `purpose` column to `auth_fullpubkey` table with default value 49 for backward compatibility
- Update unique constraint to include purpose: `(coin, auth_account, purpose)`
- Regenerate Atlas migrations and SQLC code

### Domain Layer
- Add `Purpose` type with validation (BIP44/49/84/86)
- Add `PurposeForAddressType()` mapping function to determine purpose from address type
- Update `AuthFullPubkey` entity to include purpose field

### Infrastructure Layer
- Update CSV format to support 6-field format: `coin,auth,purpose,xpub,fp,path`
- Maintain backward compatibility with 3-field and 5-field formats
- Add `GetOneByPurpose()` repository method
- Update all conversion functions to handle purpose field

### Application Layer  
- **Sign wallet**: Export 4 xpubs (one per BIP purpose) instead of 1
- **Keygen wallet**: Import xpubs with purpose field, default to BIP49 for legacy formats
- **Descriptor generation**: Query xpub by purpose to get correct key for each address type

- Add unit test mocks for `GetOneByPurpose()` method
- Fix line length linting issues
- All binaries build successfully

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Linting passes (except pre-existing issues)
- [x] All binaries build successfully
- [ ] E2E testing (manual verification recommended)
- [ ] Database migration tested

- [x] `make go-lint` passes (my changes have no errors)
- [x] `make tidy` passes
- [x] `make build-all` passes
- [x] `make atlas-fmt` and `make atlas-lint` pass
- [x] `make sqlc` generates correct code

## Backward Compatibility
- Old CSV files (3 or 5 fields) continue to work with default purpose=49
- Existing database records automatically get purpose=49 via DEFAULT constraint
- No breaking changes to existing functionality

- Database: `keygen.hcl`, SQL queries, migrations
- Domain: `auth/auth_full_pubkey.go`
- Infrastructure: `format.go`, `auth_full_pubkey_sqlc.go`, SQLC generated files
- Application: `export_fullpubkey.go`, `import_fullpubkey.go`, `generate_descriptor.go`
- Tests: `generate_descriptor_test.go`

Closes #291

title: feat(darwin): add macOS ESF + Network Extension support
body:
- Adds Go policy socket server for XPC communication (`internal/platform/darwin/xpc/`)
- Creates Swift scaffolding for System Extension with ESF client and Network Extension providers (`macos/`)
- Implements session process tracker for scoping policy to agentsh sessions
- Adds Makefile targets for enterprise macOS builds

This provides the foundation for TierEnterprise (95% security score) on macOS using Apple's Endpoint Security Framework and Network Extension APIs.

## Architecture

ESF/NE Events → System Extension (Swift) → XPC Service → Unix Socket → Go Policy Server

## Components

**Go (testable on Linux):**
- `protocol.go` - XPC message types (JSON over Unix socket)
- `server.go` - Policy query server with graceful shutdown
- `handler.go` - Adapts policy.Engine to XPC protocol
- `sessions.go` - Thread-safe session/process tracker

**Swift (scaffolding, requires Xcode + entitlements):**
- ESF client subscribing to AUTH/NOTIFY events
- NEFilterDataProvider for network traffic filtering
- NEDNSProxyProvider for DNS-based policy
- XPC Service bridge to Go server


- [x] All Go unit tests pass (`go test ./internal/platform/darwin/xpc/...`)
- [x] Build succeeds on Linux (`go build ./...`)
- [x] Integration test scaffolding added
- [ ] Swift compilation requires macOS + Xcode (scaffolding only)
- [ ] Full testing requires Apple entitlements

## Follow-up work

- Create Xcode project file
- Apply for Apple entitlements
- Complete ESF AUTH handlers for create/unlink/rename
- Implement full policy checks in Network Extension providers

## Release v3.6.9

Major code quality and reliability release — eliminates all unsafe type casts, closes the self-learning feedback loop, wires 10+ persistence gaps, and applies P0 security hardening.

### What's Changed

**Fixed**
- ESM TypeScript import failure in devcontainers (#267)
- DomainServiceRegistry not registered in kernel
- ONNX adapter and shard-embeddings using wrong vectors table
- 10 empty persistence tables and async race condition
- Self-learning feedback loop not closing (#265)
- Queen coordinator missing tasksCompleted counter

**Changed**
- Eliminated all 77 `as any` type casts across 20 files
- P0 security and performance fixes (JWT validation, input sanitization, safe JSON)
- Code quality overhaul — 41 goals across 6 phases, all 13 domain coordinators
- God file splits for queen-coordinator and large coordinators
- Consolidated .db gitignore

- [x] Both package.json versions match (3.6.9)

title: fix: auto-scroll follows thinking streams + Codex tool display
body:
- Replace `filteredLogs.length` auto-scroll dependency with `MutationObserver` to detect in-place content changes (thinking stream text growth, tool status updates)
- Add programmatic scroll guard to prevent the scroll handler from falsely pausing auto-scroll during effect-driven `scrollTo()` calls
- Fix Codex tool execution display: carry tool name from `tool_call` to `tool_result`, handle array-typed `command` args, add Codex-specific arg extraction, truncate large outputs


### Auto-scroll stops following thinking/tool streams (Fixes #402, supersedes #406)

The auto-scroll feature ([PR #390](https://github.com/RunMaestro/Maestro/pull/390)) depends on `filteredLogs.length` to trigger scroll-to-bottom. However, thinking chunks update the **last log entry's text in-place** without changing the array length:

// useAgentListeners.ts — thinking chunk handler
logs: [...tab.logs.slice(0, -1), { ...lastLog, text: combinedText }]
//                                               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
//                                               text grows, length stays the same

Timeline of the bug:
T1: First thinking chunk → new log added → length 1→2 → scroll fires ✓
T2: Second thinking chunk → text updated → length still 2 → NO scroll ✗
T3: Third thinking chunk → text updated → length still 2 → NO scroll ✗
T4: Tool event → new log added → length 2→3 → scroll fires ✓
T5: More thinking → text updated → length still 3 → NO scroll ✗

[PR #406](https://github.com/RunMaestro/Maestro/pull/406) proposed a content-fingerprint memo (`lastVisibleLogActivityKey`) that creates a composite key from the last log's metadata. This works but couples the scroll trigger to React's data model. Our approach uses a **MutationObserver** on the scroll container instead, which:

1. **Catches all content changes** — new DOM nodes, text mutations — regardless of how the React data model produces them
2. **Is framework-agnostic** — doesn't need to know about `filteredLogs`, `collapsedLogs`, or log data shapes
3. **Naturally throttles** — MutationObserver batches mutations and delivers them asynchronously, providing built-in coalescing
4. **Has zero React overhead** — no additional memos, no dependency array churn, no re-renders

### Programmatic scroll falsely pauses auto-scroll (secondary race condition)

When the auto-scroll effect calls `scrollTo({ behavior: 'auto' })`, the instant scroll fires the `onScroll` handler synchronously. If `scrollHeight` just grew from new content but the scroll position hasn't propagated yet, the handler computes `atBottom = false` and sets `autoScrollPaused = true` — pausing auto-scroll during a *programmatic* scroll. This creates intermittent freezes where the viewport stops following output mid-stream.

Fixed with a ref-based guard (`isProgrammaticScrollRef`) set before `scrollTo()` and cleared via `queueMicrotask`. The scroll handler checks this flag before pausing.

### Codex tool executions show no command details

Codex bash tool entries render as just `bash ●` / `bash ✓` with no information about what command was executed. Three sub-bugs:

**Missing tool name on completion:** Codex emits `tool_call` and `tool_result` as separate `item.completed` JSONL events. The parser transforms `tool_result` without a `toolName` field (only `tool_call` items include `item.tool`). StdoutHandler's gate (`event.toolName` check) silently drops the event — the renderer never receives "completed" status.

**Array commands not rendered:** Codex tool_call items use `args: { command: ['ls', '-la'] }` (string array). The renderer's `safeStr(toolInput.command)` returns `null` for non-strings, so no command detail is displayed. This bug is a **new finding** not addressed in [PR #407](https://github.com/RunMaestro/Maestro/pull/407)'s tool fix (commit `451f8871`), which added `lastToolName` tracking and Codex arg patterns but didn't handle the array `command` format.

**No output truncation:** Large tool outputs (e.g., `cat` of a big file) create oversized log entries with no limit.


### Commit 1: `638db6ff` — MutationObserver auto-scroll

Replace the `filteredLogs.length` dependency in the auto-scroll `useEffect` with a `MutationObserver` on `scrollContainerRef`:

const observer = new MutationObserver(() => {
    if (shouldAutoScroll()) scrollToBottom();
});
observer.observe(container, {
    childList: true,    // New/removed DOM nodes (new log entries)
    subtree: true,      // Watch all descendants
    characterData: true, // Text node mutations (thinking stream growth)
});

The observer is set up and torn down inside the effect, keyed on `[session.inputMode, autoScrollAiMode, autoScrollPaused]`. The `filteredLogs.length` dependency is completely removed from this effect.

**Intentionally kept:** The "detect new messages" effect and `handleScrollInner` still use `filteredLogs.length` for unread badge counting and read state tracking — in-place text updates should NOT increment unread counts.

### Commit 2: `35b86947` — Programmatic scroll guard

- Add `isProgrammaticScrollRef` (boolean ref)
- Set `true` before `scrollTo()`, clear via `queueMicrotask` after
- Check `!isProgrammaticScrollRef.current` in `handleScrollInner` before setting `autoScrollPaused = true`

Why `queueMicrotask` not `setTimeout(0)`: microtasks run after the current task's synchronous work but before the next macro task. Since `behavior: 'auto'` scrolls synchronously, the `onScroll` event fires in the same task. The microtask clears the flag before any subsequent user scroll could fire.

### Commit 3: `fdf8329f` — Tests

4 new tests in `auto-scroll.test.tsx`:
- Thinking text growth triggers auto-scroll (same array length)
- Unread badge does NOT increment on in-place text updates
- Tool event appends trigger auto-scroll
- Genuine user scroll-up still pauses auto-scroll (guard doesn't interfere)

Includes a class-based `MockMutationObserver` for JSDOM compatibility.

### Commit 4: `c276056c` — Codex tool display

**Parser** (`codex-output-parser.ts`):
- Add `lastToolName` field: stored on `tool_call`, carried to `tool_result`, cleared after use
- Add `MAX_TOOL_OUTPUT_LENGTH` (10K chars) truncation in `decodeToolOutput`

**Renderer** (`TerminalOutput.tsx`):
- Add `safeCommand()` helper: handles both string and string-array `command` values (joins arrays with spaces)
- Add `truncate()` helper for length-limited display
- Add Codex-specific arg patterns: `path`, `cmd`, `code`, `content`
- Change `safeStr(toolInput.command)` → `safeCommand(toolInput.command)`

**Tests** (`codex-output-parser.test.ts`):
- Tool name carryover from `tool_call` to `tool_result`
- `lastToolName` reset after consumption (no stale names)
- Output truncation at 10K chars with marker

## Files Changed (4 files, +375 / -29)

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `src/renderer/components/TerminalOutput.tsx` | MutationObserver effect, `isProgrammaticScrollRef` guard, `safeCommand()` helper, Codex arg extraction |
| `src/main/parsers/codex-output-parser.ts` | `lastToolName` tracking, output truncation |
| `src/__tests__/renderer/components/auto-scroll.test.tsx` | 4 new tests + MutationObserver mock |
| `src/__tests__/main/parsers/codex-output-parser.test.ts` | 3 new tests for tool name carryover + truncation |


- Fixes #402
- Supersedes #406 (closed — content-fingerprint approach replaced with MutationObserver)
- Extends #390 (original auto-scroll feature, merged)
- Overlaps with #407 (Codex tool fixes — `lastToolName` + truncation exist there too, but array `command` handling is new here)


- [x] `npm run lint` — clean
- [x] `npm run test` — 468 test files, 19,984 tests pass
- [x] New auto-scroll tests: thinking stream growth, unread badge isolation, tool event scroll, user scroll-up guard
- [x] New Codex parser tests: tool name carryover, stale name reset, output truncation
- [ ] Manual: enable thinking display → start streaming prompt → verify viewport stays pinned during thinking text growth
- [ ] Manual: scroll up during streaming → verify auto-scroll pauses → scroll back down → verify it resumes
- [ ] Manual: Codex agent → run a command → verify tool entries show command details (not just "bash ●")



  * Tool context is preserved across consecutive tool events so displayed tool names remain consistent.
  * Terminal displays additional tool details and trims very long tool content for readability.

  * Improved auto-scroll: programmatic scrolling no longer interrupts auto-scroll; user scrolls still pause it.
  * Unread badge/alignment updated to reflect actual scroll-bottom state.

  * Added coverage for tool name carryover, output truncation, and mutation-driven scroll behavior (includes test polyfill).

MAESTRO: replace auto-scroll filteredLogs.length dep with MutationObserver

The auto-scroll effect previously depended on filteredLogs.length, which
missed in-place text updates during thinking/tool streaming (the array
length doesn't change when thinking chunks update the last log entry).

Replace with a MutationObserver on the scroll container that detects all
DOM mutations — childList for new nodes, characterData for text changes,
subtree to watch all descendants. This catches both new log entries and
in-place thinking stream growth.

Also adds a clarifying comment to the detect-new-messages effect
explaining why it intentionally still uses filteredLogs.length (unread
badge counts should only increment on new entries, not text updates).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
MAESTRO: add programmatic scroll guard to prevent false auto-scroll pausing

Adds isProgrammaticScrollRef that the MutationObserver scrollToBottom sets
before calling scrollTo() and clears via queueMicrotask. The scroll handler
checks this flag before pausing auto-scroll, preventing the race condition
where a programmatic scroll triggers onScroll with a stale scrollTop and
falsely sets autoScrollPaused=true.

Add lastToolName tracking in Codex parser to carry tool name from

item.completed events). Fix TerminalOutput tool detail extraction
to handle array-typed command args (Codex uses ['ls', '-la'] format).
Add Codex-specific arg patterns (path, cmd, code, content).
Truncate large tool outputs to 10K chars.

Fixes missing command details in Codex bash tool execution display.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
MAESTRO: fix review findings — Sentry reporting + throttle race condition

Address CodeRabbit review on PR #410:

1. codex-output-parser.ts: Report Buffer.from() decode failures to
   Sentry with context (operation, outputType, outputLength) instead
   of silently swallowing the error.

2. TerminalOutput.tsx: Fix race condition where queueMicrotask cleared
   isProgrammaticScrollRef before the throttled scroll handler (16ms
   delay) could check it. The guard flag is now consumed (checked and
   cleared) inside handleScrollInner itself, eliminating the timing
   dependency between microtasks and the throttle window.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
MAESTRO: fix stale isProgrammaticScrollRef when scrollTo is a no-op

When scrollTo() is called but the container is already at the bottom,
the browser may not fire a scroll event. The guard flag stays true
indefinitely, causing the next genuine user scroll-up to be silently
consumed instead of pausing auto-scroll.

Add a 32ms setTimeout fallback (2x the 16ms throttle window) that
clears the flag if the throttled handler hasn't consumed it. If the
handler does consume it first, the timeout harmlessly sets false again.

title: feat: add cache-rt command and SYNC_CACHED_RT env variable for resource types
body:
- Add a new CLI command `cache-rt` that fetches resource types from the Windmill hub and caches them locally
- Add `SYNC_CACHED_RT` environment variable to sync cached resource types to the admins workspace on server startup
- Update Dockerfiles to run `cache-rt` during image build


### `cache-rt` command
Fetches resource types from `https://hub.windmill.dev/resource_types/list` and saves them as JSON to `/tmp/windmill/cache/hub_rt/resource_types.json`. This is run during Docker image build so resource types are available in the container.

### `SYNC_CACHED_RT` environment variable
When set to `true` or `1`, the server will sync cached resource types to the `resource_type` table in the `admins` workspace on startup. The sync:
- Skips resource types that already exist with the same schema and description
- Only inserts/updates changed resource types
- Logs the number of synced and skipped resource types


- [ ] Build Docker image and verify `cache-rt` runs successfully
- [ ] Start server with `SYNC_CACHED_RT=true` and verify resource types are synced to admins workspace
- [ ] Verify existing unchanged resource types are skipped during sync

title: refactor!: v3.0 - functional architecture with performance optimizations
body:
**Major v3.0 release**: Complete architectural rewrite from class-based inheritance to functional, self-contained modules with significant performance improvements.

### Architecture Changes
- **Functional architecture** — Each of 52 languages is now a standalone module exporting `toWords(value, options?)`
- **Removed all base classes** — Deleted `lib/classes/` directory (6 classes)
- **Normalized BCP 47 exports** — `import { en, zhHans, frBE } from 'n2words'`
- **Subpath exports** — `import { toWords } from 'n2words/en'` (~1.4 KB gzipped)

### Breaking Changes
- `import n2words from 'n2words'` → `import { en, es } from 'n2words'`
- `EnglishConverter(42)` → `en(42)`
- UMD files: `dist/EnglishConverter.js` → `dist/languages/en.js`

### New Features
- **Subpath exports** for minimal bundle size (`n2words/en`, `n2words/es`, etc.)
- **Options validation** with helpful error messages
- **TypeScript declarations** generated from JSDoc for all 52 languages
- **Comprehensive type tests** for all 52 languages with option validation
- `lv` (Latvian) and `pl` (Polish) now support `{ gender: 'feminine' }`
- UMD single-language bundles use unique exports (no conflicts when combining)

### Import Methods Reference

**ESM (Node.js / Bundlers):**
```js
// Named imports (tree-shakable)
import { en, es, zhHans } from 'n2words'

// Subpath imports (smallest bundle, single language)
import { toWords } from 'n2words/en'

**Browser (UMD via CDN):**
```html
<!-- All languages -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/n2words/dist/n2words.js"></script>
<script>n2words.en(42)</script>

<!-- Single language (~1.4 KB gzipped) -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/n2words/dist/languages/en.js"></script>
<script>n2words.en(42)</script>

<!-- Multiple languages (no conflicts) -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/n2words/dist/languages/en.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/n2words/dist/languages/es.js"></script>
<script>
  n2words.en(42)  // 'forty-two'
  n2words.es(42)  // 'cuarenta y dos'
</script>


- [x] All tests pass (`npm test`)
- [x] Type tests pass (`npm run test:types`)
- [x] Export tests pass (`npm run test:exports`)
- [x] UMD tests pass (`npm run test:umd`)
- [x] Linting passes (`npm run lint`)

title: feat(deployment): add agent-based dev environment analysis with two-mode dispatch and caching
body:
- Replace the simple Node.js-only `DeploymentService` with a two-mode system: **fast path** (deterministic `package.json` detection) and **agent path** (AI-powered analysis via `IStructuredAgentCaller`) supporting any language/framework
- Add per-repo caching of `DevEnvironmentAnalysis` results in SQLite, keyed by git remote URL (with root repo path fallback), with manual-only invalidation and full manual editing via structured form UI
- Add `NotStartable` deployment state for repos with no server/UI, with inline informational badge showing the agent's reason text
- Add `RepoCacheKeyResolver` for worktree-aware cache key resolution ensuring multiple worktrees of the same repo share a single cache entry

### Architecture Layers (Clean Architecture)

**Domain (TypeSpec):**
- New `DevEnvironmentAnalysis` model with `DevCommand` type, `AnalysisSource` enum (`FastPath`, `Agent`, `Manual`), and `NotStartable` state added to `DeploymentState`

**Persistence:**
- SQLite migration `007_create_dev_environment_analyses` with proper constraints
- `DevEnvAnalysisMapper` for domain ↔ persistence round-tripping (22 mapper tests)
- `SQLiteDevEnvAnalysisRepository` implementing `IDevEnvAnalysisRepository`

**Infrastructure Services:**
- `RepoCacheKeyResolver` — resolves cache key via git remote URL → root repo path → working dir fallback (9 tests)
- `RepoConfigFileReader` — pre-reads key config files (package.json, Dockerfile, pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, go.mod, etc.) for agent prompt context (14 tests)
- `DevEnvironmentAnalyzerService` — two-mode dispatch with auto-detection, fast path reuses existing `detectDevScript()`, agent path uses `StructuredAgentCallerService` (17 tests)
- Refactored `DeploymentService.start()` to accept `DevEnvironmentAnalysis` and handle `NotStartable` (31 tests)

**Server Actions:**
- `analyzeRepository` — triggers analysis with mode selection
- `invalidateDevEnvCache` — manual cache invalidation + re-analysis
- `updateDevEnvAnalysis` — saves user edits to cached analysis

**UI Components (all with Storybook stories):**
- `DeployModeToggle` — Fast/Agent mode selector with auto-detection indicator
- `CacheSummary` — shows cached analysis (language, framework, commands, ports) with Edit/Re-analyze actions
- `DevEnvAnalysisEditor` — structured form for editing all analysis fields (commands list, ports, prerequisites, env vars, canStart toggle)
- `DeploymentStatusBadge` — extended with `NotStartable` state showing info icon + reason text

**Hooks:**
- Extended `useDeployAction` with mode selection, cache state, analyzing progress, and `NotStartable` handling (30 tests)

title: fix(cache): set TUIST_CACHE_ENDPOINT in Gradle cache e2e test
body:
Fixes the Gradle Cache Acceptance CI failure introduced by the dev instance port scoping change (305327caea).

**Root cause:** The `create_cache_endpoints` migration seeds `http://localhost:8087` as the dev cache endpoint. After the port scoping change, the cache server runs on port `8087+suffix` (e.g., 8296), but the seeded endpoint still points to the old hardcoded port 8087. The Gradle plugin discovers this stale endpoint from the server, tries to connect, gets "Connection refused", and Gradle disables the remote cache entirely.

**Fixes:**
- Update the migration to read `TUIST_CACHE_PORT` from the environment when seeding the dev cache endpoint
- Set `TUIST_CACHE_ENDPOINT` in the bats e2e test as a direct override, bypassing server endpoint discovery

- [ ] Gradle Cache Acceptance CI workflow passes
commit_msgs:
fix(cache): set TUIST_CACHE_ENDPOINT in Gradle cache e2e test

The Gradle plugin discovers cache endpoints by calling the main server's
/api/cache/endpoints API. In CI, TUIST_HOSTED=1 causes the server to
query the database for cache endpoints, but none are seeded, returning
an empty list. This causes NoCacheEndpointsException, disabling the
remote build cache entirely.

Set TUIST_CACHE_ENDPOINT directly in the test to bypass endpoint
discovery and connect the Gradle plugin to the cache server.

in the e2e test as a direct override.

title: Fix shared buffer validation for flash attention tile size mismatch
body:
When `tile_size_q > lkp`, the shared L2 buffer (sized `lkp×dk` for K data) cannot hold Q tile data (sized `tile_size_q×dk`). This caused a BD out-of-bounds error during compilation for configs like `LQP=512` with `LKP=64` (`tile_size_q=128 > lkp=64`).

Fix: disable `enable_shared_buffers` when `tile_size_q > lkp`. Q gets its own independently-sized L2 buffer.

Partially addresses #1420 (Issue 3: pass pipeline failures for large tiles).

- [ ] `make run LK=2048 LKP=64 LQ=2048 LQP=512 NUM_HEADS=2` — should no longer crash with BD out-of-bounds (now fails with resource allocation, which is a separate L1 memory issue)
- [ ] `make run` — default non-causal regression
- [ ] `make run LK=2048 LKP=64 LQ=2048 LQP=256 NUM_HEADS=2 EXTRA_PY_FLAGS="--causal"` — causal regression

title: perf(ci): skip container init for changeset PRs
body:
- Service containers (Doltgres, Postgres) in `cypress-e2e` and `create-agents-e2e` were initialized **before** the changeset check ran, wasting ~30s of `ubuntu-32gb` runner time on every changeset PR
- Extracts the changeset check into a lightweight job on `ubuntu-latest` that runs first. The heavy jobs depend on it via `needs:` and skip entirely (including container init) when it's a changeset PR
- Also removes all redundant step-level `if: changeset-check` guards since the job-level `if` already gates everything (-83 lines net)

Affects: `ci.yml` (both `ci` and `create-agents-e2e` jobs), `cypress.yml` (`cypress-e2e` job)

- [ ] Verify CI/Cypress/Create Agents E2E checks still pass on this PR (non-changeset)
- [ ] After merge, verify changeset PRs show the heavy jobs as "skipped" without container init

title: feat(streaming): multi-destination registry + pump.fun and X plugins
body:
- **Multi-destination registry**: Replace single `destination?` field with `Map<string, StreamingDestination>` + `activeDestinationId`, enabling runtime switching between streaming targets
- **New plugins**: Add `@milady/plugin-pumpfun-streaming` (pump.fun) and `@milady/plugin-x-streaming` (X/Twitter) following the existing Twitch/YouTube factory pattern

### Architecture (core)
- `StreamRouteState.destination?` → `destinations: Map<string, StreamingDestination>` + `activeDestinationId?`
- New `getActiveDestination()` helper resolves active destination with first-in-map fallback
- `GET /api/streaming/destinations` now returns all configured destinations with `active` flag
- `POST /api/streaming/destination` now actually switches the active destination (was a no-op placeholder)
- `server.ts` loads all configured destinations into the Map instead of first-wins cascade

### New plugins
- `packages/plugin-pumpfun/` — pump.fun RTMP streaming (user provides URL + key per session)
- `packages/plugin-x-streaming/` — X/Twitter RTMPS streaming (user provides URL + key from studio.x.com)
- Both use `createStreamingPlugin()` factory from `plugin-streaming-base`

### Config
- `PumpfunStreamConfigSchema` and `XStreamConfigSchema` added to zod validation
- `StreamingSchema` updated with `pumpfun` and `x` fields
- `STREAMING_PLUGINS` and `isStreamingDestinationConfigured` updated for auto-enable

### What does NOT change
- StreamManager, Retake plugin, stream persistence, popout/PIP, browser capture, agent actions — all untouched
- Single-destination configs work identically (first destination becomes default active)

title: frontend/explorer: modernize file explorer with antd Table, DnD, and directory tree
body: Major modernization of the file explorer and flyout file panel. ### Core changes - **antd Table with virtual scroll**: Replaces the legacy file listing with `TableVirtuoso` — sortable columns (Name, Size, Date, Type), keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Enter, Escape), virtual scrolling for large directories - **Drag and Drop**: Full `@dnd-kit/core` integration — move/copy files between folders, drop onto breadcrumbs, cross-project drag onto project tabs, long-press activation on touch, Shift held = copy - **Directory Tree**: Toggleable resizable side panel with lazy-loaded tree, drop targets on each folder, live-updates on filesystem changes, starred directories panel, OS-style expand/collapse lines - **Directory Peek**: Inline expandable row showing directory contents as compact chips, with virtualized grid for large directories, drag support, and context menus - **Decoupled navigation**: Explorer and flyout each have independent browsing paths, separate from the Redux `current_path` that tracks the active file tab. Browser-style back/forward history persisted via DKV - **Breadcrumb navigator**: Stable-width layout with press-drag-release interaction, dropdown overflow for deep paths, drop targets on each segment ### Flyout improvements - **Terminal sync**: Flyout terminal follows the flyout's browsing path bidirectionally (cd in terminal ↔ flyout navigation), with sync toggle and manual sync button - **Upload**: Unified Dropzone — single `FileUploadWrapper` handles both drag-drop and upload button clicks, compact overlay preview via CSS - **Type filter**: Dropdown filters by file extension, excludes hidden files from options - **Deferred listing updates**: Buffers filesystem changes, shows "Refresh" banner so the listing doesn't change under the user while reading/selecting. Grace window auto-flushes enrichment data (public paths, starred files) ### UX polish - **Selection**: Shift-click range select, Ctrl/Cmd-click toggle, select-all checkbox - **Context menu**: Right-click with full action set, copy path entries, works on single files, directories, and multi-selection - **Search**: DKV-backed search history with dropdown, terminal mode prefixes (`!` and `/`) - **Settings persistence**: Sort column/direction, tree visibility, and search history persisted per-project via Conat DKV - **Empty state**: Redesigned placeholder with create file/folder buttons and filter badges - **Row styling**: Delimiter lines between rows, highlight for open files, masked-file toggle with badge count - **Batch rendering**: 10ms debounce on listing updates to prevent row-by-row cascade when entering new directories - **i18n**: Column headers and new UI strings use shared labels from `i18n/common.ts` - [ ] File listing renders with sortable columns (Name, Size, Date, Type) - [ ] Keyboard navigation: arrow keys move selection, Enter opens, Escape clears - [ ] Drag files to folders — files are moved; hold Shift — files are copied - [ ] Drag files to a different project tab — cross-project copy dialog - [ ] Drag files from OS → explorer body — upload works with progress preview - [ ] Upload button in flyout — opens file picker, upload works - [ ] Directory tree: toggle, resize, expand/collapse, drop targets, live-update - [ ] Directory peek: expand folder row, click items, context menu - [ ] Breadcrumb navigation: click segments, drop onto segments, overflow dropdown - [ ] Back/forward buttons navigate directory history - [ ] Flyout terminal follows flyout browsing path; cd in terminal updates flyout - [ ] Selection: click, Shift-click range, Ctrl-click toggle, select-all checkbox - [ ] Right-click context menu on files, folders, multi-selection - [ ] Search bar filters files; search history dropdown persists across sessions - [ ] Sort column/direction persists across navigation and page reload - [ ] Hidden files toggle works in table and tree; badge shows count - [ ] Deferred listing: changes show "Refresh" banner, click to apply - [ ] Empty directory shows create file/folder placeholder - [ ] Two browser windows: listing updates propagate across clients - [ ] Build passes: `cd packages/frontend && pnpm tsc --noEmit` and `cd packages/static && pnpm build-dev`

title: fix: properly detect optional mapped types in no-unnecessary-condition
body:
- Fixes the `no-unnecessary-condition` rule incorrectly flagging optional chains on optional mapped types as unnecessary
- Exposes `GetMappedTypeModifiers` in shim to check mapped type optionality
- Only removes short-circuit undefined for non-optional mapped types


The rule was failing on valid-155 test case:

type A = { [name in Lowercase<string>]?: A };
declare const a: A;
a.a?.a?.a;  // Was incorrectly flagged as unnecessary

The issue was that when `getPropertyTypeFromBase` returned `nil` for mapped types with template literal keys (like `Lowercase<string>`), the code was unconditionally removing nullish from the type. This is wrong for **optional** mapped types (`?` modifier) since they genuinely can be undefined.


1. Expose `getMappedTypeModifiers` from TypeScript's checker via `go:linkname` in the shim
2. Check `MappedTypeModifiersIncludeOptional` before removing nullish
3. Only remove short-circuit undefined for non-optional mapped types


- [x] All 293 existing tests pass
- [x] valid-155 (recursive optional mapped type) now passes
- [x] invalid case with nested mapped types (outer optional, inner non-optional) correctly flags second `?.` as unnecessary
