fix: respect per-rig max_polecats config in polecat spawn

The rig-level max_polecats config (gt rig config set <rig> max_polecats N)
was defined as a system default (10) but never read by the spawn path.
The spawn code only had a hardcoded global cap of 25.

Now polecat_spawn checks the rig's max_polecats config (resolved through
wisp → bead → system default layers) and enforces it per-rig before
falling back to the global 25 safety cap.

Also adds countActivePolecatsForRig() to support per-rig counting by
filtering tmux sessions on the rig name from parsed session identity.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix: idle polecats use detached HEAD to avoid branch lock conflicts

When gt done transitions a polecat to IDLE, it syncs the worktree to the
rig's default branch. Previously this checked out the named branch (e.g.
"release"), which git worktrees forbid sharing across worktrees. This
blocked the refinery from checking out release, causing detached HEAD
fallback and PR backlog.

Fix: fetch origin and checkout "origin/<defaultBranch>" which creates a
detached HEAD at the same commit. The reuse path (ReuseIdlePolecat)
already handles detached HEAD correctly — it does ResetHard then creates
a fresh branch from origin/<defaultBranch>.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix: add pre-push hook support for protected branch enforcement

gt done direct-merge pushes now use PushWithEnv with
GT_ALLOW_PROTECTED_PUSH=1 to bypass the pre-push hook that blocks
direct pushes to main/release. The hook is installed per-repo in
.repo.git/hooks/pre-push and covers all worktrees (polecats, refinery,
crew) since they share the hook directory.

This prevents accidental pushes to protected branches (e.g. idle
polecats pushing to release) while allowing authorized paths like
direct-merge convoys and CI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix: witness idle detection + refinery self-healing fallback (P0)

Two fixes for the broken polecat→witness→refinery signal chain:

1. Witness idle detection (manager.go): In the persistent polecat model,
   tmux sessions stay alive after gt done. The old check required no live
   tmux session to detect idle, which never triggered. Now checks
   agent_state=idle AND exit_type present on the agent bead — this means
   gt done completed and wrote exit metadata, distinguishing "done and
   idle" from "crashed and idle".

2. Refinery self-healing (mol-refinery-patrol formula):
   - Reduced await-event backoff-max from 5m to 60s (polls at least once/min)
   - Added GitHub PR polling fallback in queue-scan: when the beads MQ is
     empty, poll gh pr list as a fallback to discover orphaned PRs that the

title: fix: isolate concurrent builds via build_id namespace on git resources
body:
- Concurrent `build()` calls on the same repository collide on shared git resources (integration branch, issue branches, worktree dirs), with the second build silently destroying the first's in-progress work
- Generate a short `build_id` (8 hex chars) at the start of `build()` and thread it through the pipeline so all per-build git resources are uniquely namespaced
- All new parameters default to `""` — fully backward compatible

## What Was Broken

When two builds run simultaneously on the same repo, they share:
1. **Integration branch** — `feature/<goal-slug>`: second build fails or hijacks the first's branch
2. **Issue branches** — `issue/<NN>-<name>`: workspace setup agent explicitly deletes existing branches before recreating, silently destroying the other build's committed work
3. **Worktree dirs** — `.worktrees/issue-<NN>-<name>/`: same filesystem collision


All git resources are now namespaced by `build_id`:
- Integration branch: `feature/<build_id>-<goal-slug>`
- Issue branches: `issue/<build_id>-<NN>-<name>`
- Worktree dirs: `.worktrees/issue-<build_id>-<NN>-<name>/`

The cleanup path derivation (`branch.replace("/", "-")`) continues to map correctly to worktree directories since setup and cleanup use the same convention.

**Files changed:**
- `swe_af/app.py` — generate `build_id`, pass to `run_git_init` and `execute()`
- `swe_af/execution/dag_executor.py` — thread `build_id` through `run_dag()`, `_init_dag_state()`, `_setup_worktrees()`
- `swe_af/execution/schemas.py` — add `build_id` field to `DAGState`
- `swe_af/prompts/git_init.py` — instruct agent to use `feature/<build_id>-<goal-slug>`
- `swe_af/prompts/workspace.py` — instruct agent to use `issue/<build_id>-<NN>-<name>` branch/dir names
- `swe_af/reasoners/execution_agents.py` — pass `build_id` to `git_init_task_prompt` and `workspace_setup_task_prompt`


- [ ] Single build: verify branch names still work normally (no regression)
- [ ] Concurrent builds on same repo: verify each gets unique branches (`issue/abc12345-01-name` vs `issue/def67890-01-name`)
- [ ] Verify cleanup correctly removes each build's namespaced worktrees
- [ ] Verify `execute()` called directly without `build_id` falls back to old naming
commit_msgs:
fix: isolate concurrent builds via build_id namespace on git resources

When two build() calls run simultaneously on the same repository, they
collide on shared git resources: the integration branch (feature/<slug>)
and issue branches/worktrees (issue/<NN>-<name>). The workspace setup
agent even deletes existing branches when they conflict, silently
destroying the other build's in-progress work.

Fix: generate a short build_id (8 hex chars) at the start of build() and
thread it through the entire pipeline so all per-build git resources are
uniquely namespaced:

- Integration branch: feature/<build_id>-<goal-slug>
- Issue branches:     issue/<build_id>-<NN>-<name>
- Worktree dirs:      .worktrees/issue-<build_id>-<NN>-<name>/

The cleanup path derivation (branch.replace("/", "-")) continues to map
correctly to worktree directories because setup and cleanup use the same
naming convention.

All new parameters default to "" for backward compatibility — builds
that call execute() directly without a build_id fall back to the
existing naming convention with no regressions.

Two bugs in the original implementation:

title: feat: hashline edit mode
body:
- Adds `--edit` flag to the MCP server that enables hash-anchored file editing
- When active, `tilth_read` tags every line with a 3-char FNV-1a content hash: `42:a3f|code here`
- New `tilth_edit` tool accepts edits referencing these hash anchors, verifying the file hasn't changed since last read
- Server instructions tell the model to prefer tilth tools for the full read→edit workflow
- Version bump to 0.2.0


# Read (edit mode)
tilth_read → "42:a3f|  let x = 1;"

# Edit (references the hash)
tilth_edit(path, edits: [{ start: "42:a3f", content: "  let x = 2;" }])

# Stale hash? Rejected with current content shown.

## Design decisions

- **Opt-in via `--edit` flag** — set once in MCP config, no per-call ceremony
- **Conditional tool registration** — `tilth_edit` only appears when edit mode is on
- **All-or-nothing hash verification** — reject entire batch if any hash mismatches
- **Reverse-order application** — edits sorted descending so line numbers stay valid
- **Zero new dependencies** — FNV-1a is 5 lines inline


| File | What |
| `src/format.rs` | `line_hash()`, `hashlines()`, `parse_anchor()` |
| `src/edit.rs` | **NEW** — `Edit`, `EditResult`, `apply_edits()` |
| `src/read/mod.rs` | Thread `edit_mode`, conditional hashline output |
| `src/lib.rs` | Register edit module |
| `src/mcp.rs` | `tool_edit()`, conditional tools/instructions |
| `src/main.rs` | `--edit` CLI flag |
| `Cargo.toml` | Version 0.2.0 |
| `npm/package.json` | Version 0.2.0 |


- [x] `cargo build` — clean

- [x] `cargo test` — all pass

- [x] Single-line edit with correct hash — applied
- [x] Multi-line range replacement — applied
- [x] Stale hash — rejected with `isError: true` and current content

## Release

After merge: tag `v0.2.0` on main → triggers release workflow → builds + crates.io publish → then npm publish.

Inspired by [The Harness Problem](https://blog.can.ac/2026/02/12/the-harness-problem/).

title: fix: Handle BaseModelOutputWithPooling from SigLIP get_*_features()
body:
Fixes a runtime error where `get_image_features()` and `get_text_features()` from SigLIP models return `BaseModelOutputWithPooling` instead of raw tensors in newer versions of `transformers`.


In recent versions of the `transformers` library, certain model methods like `get_image_features()` and `get_text_features()` on SigLIP models return a `BaseModelOutputWithPooling` object instead of a raw `torch.Tensor`. This caused the code to fail when attempting tensor operations (like `.norm()`) on the output, resulting in:

AttributeError: 'BaseModelOutputWithPooling' object has no attribute 'norm'


Added a helper function `_extract_tensor()` that handles both return types:
- If the output is a `BaseModelOutputWithPooling`, it extracts `pooler_output` (preferred) or falls back to `last_hidden_state[:, 0]`
- If the output is already a tensor, it returns it as-is

This provides backward compatibility with older transformers versions while supporting the newer API.


- Added `_extract_tensor()` helper function in `headroom/image/trained_router.py`
- Updated `get_text_embeddings()` to use the helper for text feature extraction
- Updated `_get_image_embedding()` to use the helper for image feature extraction

## After Implementation

- Both tensor and `BaseModelOutputWithPooling` return types are now handled correctly
- The SigLIP-based image optimization router works across different `transformers` versions
- All existing tests pass (14 passed, 6 skipped in the embedding/vision test suite)


- [x] Run embedding and vision-related tests: `pytest tests/ -v -k "siglip or embedding or vision"`
- [x] Verify proxy server starts and operates correctly

title: Add proposal for Remote MCP Server Proxy Support
body:
This proposal extends the ToolHive Kubernetes operator to support proxying remote MCP servers with OAuth authentication, bringing the `thv run <remote-url>` CLI capability to Kubernetes.


Organizations can't deploy centralized remote MCP proxies in Kubernetes to gain visibility, enforce policies, and maintain audit logs for employee interactions with external SaaS MCP services (e.g., Salesforce MCP, GitHub MCP).

## Proposed Solution

- **MCPRemoteProxy CRD**: Deploy stateless proxies for remote MCP servers
- **MCPExternalAuthConfig CRD**: Optional token exchange configuration
- **JWT validation** and identity extraction for policy enforcement
- Reuses existing authz, audit, and tool filtering middleware

## Seeking Feedback On

1. Overall architecture and CRD design
2. Security model and token handling approach
3. Integration with existing middleware
4. Edge cases or concerns not covered

Add proposal for Remote MCP Server Proxy Support

This proposal extends the ToolHive Kubernetes operator to support
proxying remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers with OAuth
authentication, bringing feature parity with the existing
`thv run <remote-url>` CLI capability.

Key features:

title: Fix gas coin leak in stress benchmark during epoch transitions
body:
- Fix gas coin leak in `NextOp::Failure` that causes stress benchmark to deadlock at 0 TPS during epoch transitions
- Fix `num_in_flight` metric not being decremented on failure, causing it to drift upward
- Add unit tests verifying payload recycling behavior

### Root cause

When a transaction fails with a `NonRecoverableTransactionError` (including epoch-change timeouts), the `NextOp::Failure` variant is returned **without the payload**. The gas coin is dropped and never returned to `free_pool`. Once enough coins leak, the pool is empty and the tool can never submit new transactions.

The code even acknowledged this: `"May result in gas objects being leaked"`.

### Fix

4 changes in `crates/sui-benchmark/src/drivers/bench_driver.rs`:

1. **Add payload to `NextOp::Failure`**: Change from unit variant to `Failure { payload: Box<dyn Payload> }`
2. **Pass payload through on construction**: `NextOp::Failure { payload }` at the error site
3. **Recycle in main loop**: Decrement `num_in_flight`, push payload back to `free_pool`
4. **Fix drain loop**: Extract payload from `Failure` instead of `continue`-ing past it

This is safe because:
- The transaction timed out without finalizing, so the gas coin is still in its original state
- `make_transaction()` creates a fresh transaction for the current epoch
- The batch/bundle path already works this way — this makes the standard path consistent
- Happy path is completely unchanged

### Impact

- **devnet**: Stress pod stuck at 0 TPS since Feb 7 (~2.5 days)
- **staging/ci**: Same deadlock pattern during epoch transitions
- **private-testnet**: 40 hosts × 150 QPS — epoch transitions can deadlock all hosts simultaneously, requiring manual restarts

After this fix, TPS will dip briefly during epoch transitions but recover automatically within seconds.


### Unit tests (4 new tests)

- [x] `test_failure_variant_carries_payload` — `NextOp::Failure` carries and returns payload
- [x] `test_failure_payload_recycled_to_free_pool` — payload pushed to free_pool, num_in_flight decremented
- [x] `test_drain_loop_extracts_payload_from_failure` — mixed Response/Failure results all recovered
- [x] `test_multiple_failures_dont_leak` — burst of 10 failures all recycled, none leaked

$ SUI_SKIP_SIMTESTS=1 cargo nextest run -p sui-benchmark --lib
  4 tests run: 4 passed, 0 skipped

### Simulation tests (epoch transitions)

- [x] `test_simulated_load_with_reconfig` — 5-second epochs over 60s (~12 transitions) — **PASS (39s)**
- [x] `test_simulated_load_reconfig_restarts` — epoch transitions + random node restarts — **PASS (108s)**
- [x] `test_simulated_load_reconfig_with_crashes_and_delays` — epoch transitions + crashes + delays — **PASS (105s)**

### Code quality

- [x] `cargo build -p sui-benchmark` — compiles cleanly
- [x] `cargo clippy -p sui-benchmark --lib --tests` — no warnings
- [x] `rustfmt` — passed (pre-push hook)

### Post-deploy verification

- [ ] Observe on devnet after deploy: TPS recovers after epoch transitions
- [ ] `no_gas` metric stays near zero
- [ ] `num_in_flight` tracks actual in-flight count

Fix gas coin leak in stress benchmark during epoch transitions

The NextOp::Failure variant did not carry the payload, causing gas coins
to be permanently leaked when transactions failed with non-recoverable
errors (e.g. epoch mismatch timeouts). Once enough coins leaked, the
free_pool emptied and the stress tool deadlocked at 0 TPS.

Also fixes num_in_flight not being decremented on failure, causing the
metric to drift upward.

The fix preserves the payload in NextOp::Failure and recycles it back
into free_pool, matching how the batch/bundle path already works.

to free_pool. These tests catch regressions where the failure path
could silently drop gas coins.

title: fix: outreach quality — unified threads, specific context, tighter engagement gates
body:
Production analysis of 318 outreach messages showed a 2% response rate. The 7 messages that got replies all referenced something specific the person did/said. The 311 that didn't were generic company compliments and open-ended questions.

### Thread unification
- DM handlers now look up `slack_dm_thread_ts` from `person_relationships` so all messages with a person route through one thread
- When a person initiates a DM, the first exchange is saved as the permanent thread for future orchestrator use
- Fixes: every outreach was creating a new disconnected Slack thread

### Compose prompt overhaul
- **Specific or skip**: require referencing something the person actually did, said, or is working on
- **Ban vague compliments**: "your company is interesting" is not specific enough
- **Yes/no CTAs only**: no more open-ended homework questions ("What's pulling your attention?")
- **No hedge language**: ban "might be worth a look", "if you get a chance"
- **One purpose per message**: don't combine profile nudge + WG suggestion + company compliment
- **Profile nudge max once**: never woven into other outreach

### Engagement tuning
- **Cooldowns shortened**: prospect 7d→3d, welcomed 14d→7d, exploring 21d→14d (early stages are highest-intent)
- **Circuit breaker lowered**: 6→4 unreplied messages before stopping
- **Tighter engagement gate**: `workos_user_id` alone no longer counts as meaningful engagement — require observable activity (Slack messages, WG joins, events, profile work, certification)
- **Broader gate scope**: expanded from prospect/welcomed to all stages without prior replies

### Stage progression
- Slack-only users can now advance beyond exploring based on channel activity (20+ messages/30d → contributing)

### Subquery fix
- `getMemberCapabilities()` offerings subquery wrapped in `MAX()` for multi-org users

- [x] All 501 tests pass
- [x] Typecheck passes
- [x] Simulation snapshots updated (shorter cooldowns = more contacts for engaged personas, same circuit breaker behavior for ghosts)
- [ ] After deploy: monitor response rate over 2 weeks (target: 8-10%)
- [ ] Verify thread continuity in production Slack DMs

Every outreach to the same person was creating a separate Slack thread
because handleDirectMessage used event.ts (new message timestamp) as

Now both inbound handlers look up the permanent thread from
person_relationships and route all messages through it. When a person
initiates a conversation before any outreach exists, the first exchange
is saved as the permanent thread for future orchestrator use.

- Update resize() calls to include setZero() for zero-initialization
- Replace memset() with Eigen's setZero() in fast_poloidal.cc
- Enables performance benchmarking for broader Eigen migration

This is the first step in migrating VMEC++ from STL vectors to Eigen
matrices/arrays for better Python integration and potential performance
improvements.

Testing: Code changes follow patterns from eigen_migration_attempt.diff

Migrate FourierBasisFastPoloidal and FourierBasisFastToroidal to Eigen3 (#410)

Add -DNDEBUG to CMake Release flags for Eigen performance

CMakeLists.txt overrode CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE without including
-DNDEBUG, which left Eigen's bounds checking active in Release builds.
This caused a significant performance regression (50-70% slower) after
migrating from std::vector to Eigen::VectorXd, since every operator[]
call in hot DFT loops performed bounds checks.

title: Enhance MFA logging with metrics, timing, and failure details
body:
### **User description** Adds comprehensive logging for MFA operations to improve observability and security auditing. The changes track setup attempts, verification flows, and recovery code usage with detailed context including IP addresses, timing metrics, correlation IDs, and specific failure reasons. ## What Changed This PR enhances the authentication system's logging infrastructure and adds detailed instrumentation across all MFA touchpoints: **Logging Infrastructure** (`apps/web/auth/lib/logging.rb`) Extended `log_auth_event` with a `log_metric` parameter that automatically logs metrics alongside events. This eliminates code duplication and ensures consistent metric generation for key auth events. **MFA Setup Logging** (`apps/web/auth/config/hooks/mfa.rb`) - Categorizes setup attempts as "initiation" (generating secret) or "verification" (confirming OTP code) - Logs success events with recovery code counts and HMAC configuration - Added dedicated route override in `apps/web/auth/routes/mfa.rb` that logs specific validation failures: - `invalid_secret` - HMAC validation failure - `invalid_password` - Password mismatch - `invalid_otp_code` - TOTP verification failure **MFA Verification Logging** (hooks + route override) - Tracks verification attempts with microsecond-precision timing - Records success/failure with calculated duration in milliseconds - Route override logs invalid OTP codes with context before triggering Rodauth's authentication failure flow - All events include correlation IDs for end-to-end request tracing **Recovery Code Logging** (new hooks) - `before_recovery_auth` - Logs when users attempt recovery code authentication - `after_add_recovery_codes` - Tracks code generation/regeneration events - `before_view_recovery_codes` - Monitors when users access their codes (security audit signal) **IP Address Tracking** All MFA-related log events now include `request.ip` for security analysis and abuse detection. ## Review Focus **Security Considerations** - Email addresses are obscured via `OT::Utils.obscure_email` before logging - IP addresses are logged for all MFA operations (setup, verification, recovery) - Recovery code viewing is tracked as a potential compromise indicator - No sensitive data (passwords, OTP codes, recovery codes) appears in logs **Timing & Performance** - Timing uses `Onetime.now_in_μs` for microsecond precision - Duration calculations only occur on verification flows (setup/failure paths) - Session keys `mfa_verification_start` are cleaned up immediately after use - No blocking operations added to critical auth paths **Testing Recommendations** 1. body:

// Before: crashes if not installed
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

async function getAxeBuilder() {
  const module = await import('@axe-core/playwright');
  return module.default;

title: fix(clerk-js): Do not treat 429 responses as authentication failures
body:
429 (Too Many Requests) responses were being caught by `is4xxError` and triggering `handleUnauthenticated`, which signs the user out. This caused a cascading failure pattern observed in production telemetry for a customer.

1. Token fetch fails with a legitimate 4xx (e.g. `authentication_invalid`)
2. `handleUnauthenticated` fires and calls `/touch` to recover
3. `/touch` returns **429** (rate limited)
4. 429 triggers `handleUnauthenticated` **again** (treated as auth failure)
5. Each retry hits 429 → **infinite loop** (30+ retries in 11 seconds observed)
6. User gets forcibly redirected to sign-in


- **`@clerk/shared`**: Add `is429Error` helper alongside existing `is4xxError`
- **`AuthCookieService.handleGetTokenError`**: Exclude 429 from triggering `handleUnauthenticated` — fall through to `degraded` status instead
- **`Clerk.setActive`**: Exclude 429 from triggering `handleUnauthenticated`, and also don't re-throw (swallow like other transient errors)
- **`Clerk.#touchCurrentSession`**: Exclude 429 from triggering `handleUnauthenticated`
- **`Session.getToken` retry logic**: Allow 429 to be retried with exponential backoff instead of immediately giving up (was blocked by `is4xxError` in `shouldRetry`)

### Telemetry evidence (7-day window)

| Event | Count |
| `handleUnauthenticated triggered` | 650 (285 unique sessions) |
| `/touch` returning 429 | Majority of `request failed` errors during cascades |
| Top offending session | 59 `handleUnauthenticated` events from a single session |


- [x] `is429Error` unit tests pass (true for 429, false for all other statuses including null/undefined)
- [x] `is4xxError` unit tests pass (still returns true for 429 — no breaking change)
- [x] All 59 Session tests pass
- [x] All 488 clerk-js core tests pass (36 test files)
- [ ] Verify in staging that 429 from `/touch` no longer triggers sign-out
- [ ] Monitor telemetry for reduction in `handleUnauthenticated triggered` events



  * Fixed handling of rate-limit (HTTP 429) responses so they no longer trigger sign-out; clients now enter a degraded state and retry, preserving signed-in sessions and avoiding recursive unauthenticated loops.

  * Added resiliency tests covering 429 rate-limit scenarios and unauthenticated-edge cases to ensure stable runtime behavior under high traffic.

fix(clerk-js): Do not treat 429 responses as authentication failures

429 (Too Many Requests) responses were being caught by `is4xxError`
and triggering `handleUnauthenticated`, which signs the user out.
This caused a cascading failure: the unauthenticated flow calls
`/touch`, which returns 429 due to rate limiting, which triggers
`handleUnauthenticated` again — creating an infinite retry loop
that forces users to re-authenticate even though their session is
still valid.

Changes:
- Add `is429Error` helper to `@clerk/shared`
- Exclude 429 from triggering `handleUnauthenticated` in
  `AuthCookieService.handleGetTokenError`, `Clerk.setActive`,
  and `Clerk.#touchCurrentSession`
- Allow 429 to be retried in `Session.getToken` instead of
  immediately failing (was blocked by `is4xxError` check in
  `shouldRetry`)

Closes #165, Closes #166

- **Fix #165**: Voice session (long-press Home) now works with Gateway-only connection
  - `SettingsRepository.isConfigured()` returns `true` for Gateway mode
  - Voice session routes messages through the Gateway chat pipeline (`nodeRuntime.sendChat`)
  - Fail-fast health check at session open: shows clear error if Gateway is disconnected
  - Race condition fix: waits for a new assistant message instead of relying on `pendingRunCount`

- **Fix #166**: Self-signed / invalid HTTPS certificates are now supported
  - New "Ignore SSL Certificate Errors" toggle in HTTP settings
  - When enabled, a prominent `errorContainer` warning card explains the MITM risk

  - Users can independently choose whether the voice session (long-press Home) sends messages via **Gateway** or **HTTP**, regardless of the global connection type
  - Defaults to the existing `connectionType` so current setups are unaffected

- **fix(ci)**: Use a shared debug keystore to prevent conflicting app signature errors

  - All own-repo PR builds now share the same signature, so APKs can be installed over each other
  - Fork PRs fall back to a freshly generated keystore (expected — forks cannot access secrets)

title: Fix worktree tests for CI - use explicit 'main' branch

- Changed `git init` to `git init -b main` in the test helper function `createTestRepo` to explicitly set the initial branch name
- Removed duplicate git config commands that weren't running in the correct directory

Use `git init -b main` to explicitly set the initial branch name, ensuring consistency across all environments regardless of git version or system configuration.

title: [12.x] Add DeferredBatch for deferred batch construction in job chains
commit_msgs:
[12.x] Add DeferredBatch for deferred batch construction in job chains

Add `DeferredBatch`, a sibling to `ChainedBatch` that defers batch
construction to execution time. This allows batch contents to depend on
data created by earlier jobs in the chain.

`ChainedBatch` requires all batch jobs to be known at chain construction
time. In many real-world scenarios, a batch's contents depend on data
created by earlier jobs (e.g., an import job creates records, then a
calculation batch processes those records). `DeferredBatch` solves this
by accepting a callable that is invoked at execution time and must return
a `PendingBatch` or `null` to skip.

* **Settings**

commit_msgs:
fix: allow absolute paths in apply_patch when they resolve inside workspace

The absolute path rejection was redundant — the workspace containment
check already prevents writes outside the project directory. Removing
it lets agents use absolute paths without false failures.
fix: delegation tool results lost in UI and history

MCP tool results from delegateToSubagent were not persisted or displayed
properly. Three root causes fixed:

1. SDK bridge timeout (tools-builder.ts): MCP passthrough tools shared
   the 300s timeout meant for SDK built-in tools. Long-running MCP tools
   like observe(waitSeconds=600) would timeout and return {_sdkPassthrough: true}
   instead of the actual result. Fix: MCP passthroughs now use no timeout
   (abort signal handles cleanup).

2. Missing tool summary (tool-result-utils.ts, tool-live-status.ts):
   buildToolSummary had no delegateToSubagent case, falling through to
   generic "keys=..." output. Added cases that extract action, agent name,
   completion status, and response excerpts.

3. Empty expanded view (delegation-tool-ui.tsx): New dedicated UI component
   for delegation results. Extracts content from lastResponse, allResponses,
   result, message, and summary fields. Registered in tool-fallback and
   thread-message-components.
fix: interactive tool persistence, plugin import/settings, and misc fixes

- streaming-progress: persist interactive tool calls (ExitPlanMode,
  AskUserQuestion) in DB so they render on reload in background mode
- plugins: fix import route error handling, settings UI cleanup,
  registry robustness improvements
- chat-provider: thread drop handler and chat provider fixes
- electron-builder: packaging config update
- locales: new translation keys for en/tr
fix: update plugin import test to match current aux file behavior

The route always materializes auxiliary files regardless of characterId
selection. Test expectation was stale after that change.
feat: surface plugin-declared MCP servers in Settings panel

Plugin-provided MCP servers now appear in Settings → MCP Servers with
connection status, tool counts, and plugin attribution badges. The GET
/api/mcp endpoint returns pluginServers alongside user-configured ones,
and the connect route handles plugin:* namespaced reconnection. Servers
are read-only in settings since they're managed by the plugin lifecycle.
fix: reconnect state reconciliation for stuck-active Claude Code tasks

After network outage, SSE reconnect restored transport state but not
agent run state — tasks could show as active but never resume. Two bugs:

1. SSE reconnect handler skipped active-run verification when
   processingRunId was already set, leaving stale runs stuck in UI.
   Now always re-verifies via checkActiveRun (debounced 300ms).

2. Polling error handler cleared processingRunId prematurely during
   disconnect (MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS), causing the reconnect bridge
   to think there was nothing to verify and risking ghost branches
   from premature message refresh. Now preserves processingRunId for
   reconnect re-verification.
fix: improve dark mode contrast across all Claude Code tool UIs

Tool result panels were nearly invisible in dark mode — containers too
transparent, code blocks indistinguishable from background, and diff
colors washed out. Adds proper dark: variants for container backgrounds,
code block surfaces, text colors, diff added/removed indicators, status
badges, and error blocks across all 11 tool UI components.
fix: persist browser mode and other missing settings in API route

The PUT /api/settings handler builds updatedSettings by explicitly
mapping each field from the request body. Several fields were missing
from this mapping, causing the UI to accept changes but never write
them to disk:

- chromiumBrowserMode ("Use my Chrome browser" preference)
- chromiumUserProfilePath
- ttsReadCodeBlocks
- miniOverlayAutoCloseAfterSpeak
- miniOverlayKeepAppFocusedOnCompose
- miniOverlayShowScreenPreview

All six fields now follow the same body-or-current pattern used by
every other setting in the route.

title: fix(cicd): resolve disk space exhaustion in junit and compatibility-images jobs
body:
- **junit job**: Add `cleanup-after-j8` step between the J8 and J14 Docker builds to prune BuildKit cache and dangling images. This was the cause of the `No space left on device` error in [run #21963970482](https://github.com/metasfresh/metasfresh/actions/runs/21963970482/job/63452265227).
- **compatibility-images job**: Reorder to push-then-prune-then-pull pattern — push the 4 built compat images first, free disk, then pull remaining images (db, migration-tool, edi, externalsystems) for retagging. Forward-port of cd089f43e7b from `inner_silence_uat`.

### Root Cause

`ubuntu-latest` runners have ~14GB free disk. The junit job's two sequential `docker buildx build` commands each pull multi-GB base images (Maven repo + compiled code). Without cleanup between them, the J14 build starts with all J8 layers still cached, pushing total usage past the limit.


| Job | Change |
|-----|--------|
| `junit` | New `cleanup-after-j8` step: `docker builder prune -af` + `docker image prune -f` |
| `compatibility-images` | Pushes built images → prunes cache + removes pushed images → pulls remaining images for retagging |

Both cleanup steps include `df -h /` before and after for observability.


- [ ] Verify `test (java)` job completes without disk space errors
- [ ] Verify `compatibility-images` job completes without disk space errors
- [ ] Check cleanup step logs show disk space freed between builds
commit_msgs:
fix(cicd): resolve disk space exhaustion in junit and compatibility-images jobs

The junit job runs two sequential Docker builds (J8 + J14) that each pull
multi-GB base images. All layers from the J8 build remain in the BuildKit
cache when J14 starts, causing disk exhaustion on the ~14GB free ubuntu-latest
runner. Error: "No space left on device" during J8 build.

The compatibility-images job has the same issue: it builds 4 compat images,
then pulls 4 more large images for retagging without freeing disk first.

Fixes:
- junit: add cleanup-after-j8 step (docker builder prune + image prune)
  between the two buildx builds
- compatibility-images: reorder to push-then-prune-then-pull pattern —
  push built compat images first, prune build cache and remove pushed
  images, then pull remaining images for retagging

The compatibility-images fix is a forward-port of cd089f43e7b from
inner_silence_uat which was never cherry-picked to new_dawn_uat.

title: Raise ArgumentError when integer exponent is too large
body:
- Add size limit check for integer exponentiation (`**`) matching CRuby's `BIGLEN_LIMIT` to prevent excessive memory allocation
- Change `pow_ii` return type to `Option<Value>` to propagate errors, and add JIT-side error handling (`testq rax, rax; jeq raise`)
- Add `MonorubyErr::exponent_is_too_large()` helper that raises `ArgumentError: exponent is too large`

commit_msgs:
Raise ArgumentError when integer exponent is too large

Add a size check matching CRuby's BIGLEN_LIMIT (1<<34 bits on 64-bit)
to prevent extremely long or infinite computations for large integer
exponentiation. This affects pow_ii, pow_values, and the JIT path.

Previously, expressions like `100_000_000 ** 1_000_000_000` would
attempt to compute a number with ~27 billion bits, effectively hanging.
Now they raise `ArgumentError: exponent is too large` like CRuby does.

feat: add simplified claude() API and clean up REST endpoints

Introduce a developer-friendly API layer (`claude()`, `claude.agent()`,
`claude.session()`) that eliminates boilerplate — no two-step init,
no sleep() hacks, no env var wiring. Merge duplicate approval endpoints
into a single unified route, add first-class apiKey/baseUrl/permissions

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix: resolve race condition between InboxPoller and receive()

The simplified API's Agent.ask() and Agent.receive() were calling
readUnread() directly, racing with the InboxPoller that also calls
readUnread() on the same inbox. The poller would mark messages as
read before receive() could see them, causing 180s timeouts.

Fix: Use event-based waiting in Agent.ask() and Agent.receive()
instead of polling readUnread() directly. The controller's
InboxPoller already reads the inbox and fires events — the Agent
class listens for these events via wireEvents().

Additional fixes from PR review:
- Add handled guard to prevent duplicate approve/reject calls
  when both autoApprove and onPermission/onPlan are configured
- Store listener refs in boundListeners and clean up via
  unwireEvents() on close/dispose to prevent memory leaks
- Fix resolvePermissions("full") to return undefined instead of
  bypassPermissions (avoids idle detection issues)
- Improve waitForReady() to also listen for agent:spawned and
  message events (not just idle)

fix: filter protocol messages in receiveAny() for consistency

Extract PROTOCOL_ONLY_TYPES constant and apply the same filter in
receiveAny() that receive() already uses. Previously receiveAny()
could return shutdown_approved, plan_approval_response, and
permission_response messages that are meant to be handled via events.

title: fix: use dirname() for cache path — fixes Windows/exFAT
body:
- `fetchDoc()` in `cli/src/lib/cache.js` uses `cachedPath.substring(0, cachedPath.lastIndexOf('/'))` to derive the parent directory for caching fetched docs
- On Windows, `cachedPath` uses backslashes (`C:\Users\...`), so `lastIndexOf('/')` returns `-1`, producing `substring(0, -1)` → empty string → `mkdirSync('')` → `ENOENT` crash
- Replaced with `dirname(cachedPath)` which is already imported from `node:path` and handles both separators correctly

## Repro

On Windows (especially exFAT filesystems):
> chub get svelte/svelte --lang js
Error: Failed to load "svelte/svelte": ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir ''

After fix: fetches and caches correctly.


- [x] Verified `chub get svelte/svelte --lang js` works on Windows (exFAT) after the fix
- [x] Verified `chub get tailwindcss/tailwindcss --lang js` works on Windows (exFAT) after the fix
- [ ] Verify no regression on macOS/Linux (should be no-op since `dirname()` handles forward slashes identically)
commit_msgs:
fix: use dirname() instead of lastIndexOf('/') for cache path on Windows

`cachedPath.substring(0, cachedPath.lastIndexOf('/'))` produces an empty
string on Windows because paths use backslashes. `mkdirSync('')` then
throws ENOENT. `dirname()` from `node:path` (already imported) handles
both separators correctly.

Fixes `chub get` on Windows and exFAT filesystems.

title: fix: remove local LTX files during retention enforcement to prevent unbounded disk usage
body:
Fixes #784 

This PR addresses the issue where local LTX Level 0 files were never cleaned up during compaction, leading to unbounded disk usage on the host running Litestream.


The `EnforceRetentionByTXID` and `EnforceSnapshotRetention` functions would delete LTX files from remote storage (S3, file replica, etc.) but leave the corresponding local cache files in place. Over time, this caused the local `.db-litestream/ltx/0/` directory to grow without bounds, even though the remote replica was properly cleaned up according to the retention policy.


After successfully deleting files from remote storage, both retention enforcement functions now also remove the corresponding local LTX files using `os.Remove()`. The implementation follows existing codebase patterns:

- Uses `os.Remove()` with `!os.IsNotExist(err)` check (matching file/replica_client.go:202)
- Logs errors but doesn't fail the operation (non-critical cleanup after critical remote deletion succeeds)
- Uses `Logger.Error` for failed removals (matching db.go:1479 pattern)


**db.go**
- `EnforceSnapshotRetention`: Added local file cleanup loop after remote deletion (lines 1548-1554)
- `EnforceRetentionByTXID`: Added local file cleanup loop after remote deletion (lines 1597-1603)

**db_test.go**
- Added `TestDB_EnforceRetentionByTXID_LocalCleanup` to verify local files are removed during retention enforcement


- [x] New test `TestDB_EnforceRetentionByTXID_LocalCleanup` passes
- [x] No regressions detected

The test creates L0 files in two batches, compacts each to L1, and verifies that local L0 files from the first batch are properly removed after the second compaction triggers retention enforcement.
commit_msgs:
fix: remove local LTX files during retention enforcement to prevent unbounded disk usage

Fixes #784

Previously, local LTX files were never cleaned up during compaction and
retention enforcement. The EnforceRetentionByTXID and EnforceSnapshotRetention
functions would delete files from remote storage but leave the local cache
files in place, leading to unbounded disk usage over time.

This change adds local file cleanup after successful remote deletion in both
retention enforcement functions. The implementation:
- Removes local files using os.Remove() with !os.IsNotExist() check
- Logs errors but doesn't fail the operation (non-critical cleanup)
- Combines logging and local cleanup in a single loop for efficiency
- Uses Debug level logging to avoid noise

The fix ensures local disk usage is bounded by the retention policy, matching
the behavior of remote storage cleanup.

title: Fix docker exec deadlock for tasks with large output
body:
Problem: `uv run sb run -d terminal-bench-sample@2.0 --task-name fix-code-vulnerability` passes with 100% accuracy but with an agent timeout exception.

Root cause: Docker subprocess commands would deadlock when output exceeded the 64KB pipe buffer size. The code used process.wait() followed by separate stdout.read() calls, creating a circular dependency where the subprocess blocked writing to the full buffer while the parent waited for the process to exit without reading the buffer.

Why this affected fix-code-vulnerability: This task outputs 172KB (2.7x the buffer size) because solve.sh runs 'cat bottle.py' on a 4600+ line file. Other tasks output <3KB and fit within the buffer, avoiding the deadlock.

Why terminal-bench didn't have this issue: Terminal-bench uses subprocess.run() with capture_output=True, which internally calls process.communicate(). This properly reads from pipes while the process runs, preventing buffer deadlocks.

Solution: Replace process.wait() + separate read() calls with process.communicate(), which handles reading from stdout/stderr concurrently with process execution.

Result: Task execution time reduced from 15min (timeout) to ~20sec (success).

title: fix: prevent toexpr from rewriting Const values via st.rewrites
body:
- Fixes a regression in v4.18.4 where `toexpr(O::BasicSymbolic{T}, st)` incorrectly rewrites `Const` values through `st.rewrites`, causing hash-consed constants to be aliased with function argument references
- The old code had a guard `(issym(O) || iscall(O))` in `substitute_name` that prevented constants from being rewritten; the v4.18.4 refactor dropped this guard
- Adds regression test that verifies constants in expression bodies are not aliased with constant-valued function arguments


In v4.18.4, PR #862 refactored `toexpr` for performance. The new `toexpr(O::BasicSymbolic{T}, st)` checks `haskey(st.rewrites, O)` for all `BasicSymbolic` types, including `Const`. The old code routed through `substitute_name` which had a guard:

```julia
function substitute_name(O, st)
    if (issym(O) || iscall(O)) && haskey(st.rewrites, O)  # <-- guard prevents Const lookup
        st.rewrites[O]
    else
        O
    end
end

When `build_function` is called with argument arrays containing constant values (e.g., zeros from erased cache variables in DifferentiationInterface.jl), `handle_let_pair!` adds these constants to `st.rewrites`:

st.rewrites[Const(0)] = :(ˍ₋arg2[12])

Due to hash consing, all `Const(0)` values are the **same object**. So when `toexpr` encounters a literal `0` in the expression body (e.g., off-diagonal entries of a sparse Jacobian), it finds the rewrite and replaces it with `ˍ₋arg2[12]`. At runtime, `arg2` contains actual (non-zero) data, producing incorrect results.


This broke DifferentiationInterface.jl's Symbolics backend when computing Jacobians with cache contexts:
- Fixes JuliaSymbolics/Symbolics.jl#1811
- All 620 DI cachified Jacobian tests now pass (184 were failing)
- All 16876 SymbolicUtils tests pass (no regressions)


- [x] SymbolicUtils test suite passes (16876 pass, 3 pre-existing broken)
- [x] Symbolics.jl test suite passes (pre-existing PyCall segfault only)
- [x] DifferentiationInterface cachified Jacobian tests pass (620/620)
- [x] Added regression test in `test/code.jl` that reproduces the exact scenario

fix: prevent toexpr from rewriting Const values via st.rewrites

In v4.18.4, the refactored `toexpr(O::BasicSymbolic{T}, st)` function
started checking `st.rewrites` for all BasicSymbolic types including
Const values. The old code had a guard `(issym(O) || iscall(O))` in
`substitute_name` that prevented constants from being rewritten.

This caused a bug where hash-consed constant values (e.g., Const(0))
that appeared both in an expression body AND in function argument
arrays (via DestructuredArgs with create_bindings=false) would be
incorrectly aliased. The constant 0 in the expression would be
replaced with a reference to the argument position (e.g., arg2[12]),
producing wrong results at runtime when that argument had non-zero
values.

This manifested as incorrect jacobian computations in
DifferentiationInterface.jl when using Symbolics.jl's build_function
with cache contexts (where cache variables are erased to zero before
building the function).

Fixes JuliaSymbolics/Symbolics.jl#1811

title: fix(java): resolve SQLite 'database is locked' errors across the pipeline
body:
## Root Cause Analysis

**The core bug:** When Maven times out, Python's `subprocess.run()` sends `SIGKILL` to the
Maven parent process only. On Linux, Maven's forked Surefire JVM processes (child processes)
are **not killed** — they become **orphaned**. These orphaned JVMs continue running and
hold the SQLite result file (`test_return_values_0.sqlite`) open, causing
`database is locked` / `SQLITE_BUSY` errors when Python or the Java Comparator reads the
file immediately after Maven is killed.

This is confirmed by:
- All 174 occurrences of "database is locked" in the log affecting only `test_return_values_0.sqlite`
- Errors appearing immediately after Maven timeout (`returncode=-2`) or early Maven exit (`returncode=1`)
- The JVM's SQLite connection is kept alive by `CodeflashHelper.java`'s static connection (only closed by shutdown hook, which doesn't run on SIGKILL)


- **Root cause fix** (`test_runner.py`): Replace all `subprocess.run()` calls for Maven/JVM processes with `_run_cmd_kill_pg_on_timeout()` which uses `start_new_session=True` + `os.killpg()` to kill the **entire process group** on timeout. This ensures no orphaned Surefire JVMs are left behind.
- **Defense-in-depth** (`instrumentation.py`, `parse_test_output.py`, `Comparator.java`, `CodeflashHelper.java`, `ResultWriter.java`): Add `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` + `PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000` and `timeout=30` to SQLite connections. This handles edge cases where Maven exits early (non-timeout failures) before Surefire JVM fully shuts down.


### `codeflash/languages/java/test_runner.py`
- Added `_run_cmd_kill_pg_on_timeout()` helper that kills the entire process group on timeout
- Replaced `subprocess.run()` with it in `_compile_tests`, `_get_test_classpath`, `_run_tests_direct`, and `_run_maven_tests`

### `codeflash/languages/java/instrumentation.py`
- Added `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` and `PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000` to inline SQLite write code

### `codeflash/verification/parse_test_output.py`
- Changed `sqlite3.connect(path)` to `sqlite3.connect(path, timeout=30)` 

### `codeflash-java-runtime/src/main/java/com/codeflash/Comparator.java`
- Added `PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000` before reads

### `codeflash/languages/java/resources/CodeflashHelper.java`
- Added `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` and `PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000` after connection

### `codeflash-java-runtime/src/main/java/com/codeflash/ResultWriter.java`
- Added WAL mode + busy_timeout PRAGMAs

### `tests/test_languages/test_java/test_run_and_parse.py`
- Added `TestRunCmdKillPgOnTimeout` class with 5 tests verifying process group kill behavior

### `tests/test_languages/test_java/test_instrumentation.py`
- Updated snapshot strings to include new PRAGMA lines
- Added `TestSQLiteLockedFix` class

- [x] All 646 Java unit tests pass (excluding pre-existing `test_line_profiler_integration.py` failure about missing Premain-Class)
- [x] E2E test: `codeflash --file Buffer.java --function estimateSizeUtf8` completes without any "database is locked" errors and finds 60% speedup
- [x] `TestRunCmdKillPgOnTimeout::test_timeout_kills_child_processes_not_just_parent` verifies child processes are killed on timeout

fix(java): resolve SQLite 'database is locked' errors across the pipeline

Root cause: The instrumented test JVM holds a SQLite connection open while
writing results.  The Python reader and the Java Comparator were trying to
read the same file without a busy_timeout, causing immediate SQLITE_BUSY
failures (~126 occurrences in codeflash_all_3.log).

Fixes applied:

1. instrumentation.py (_generate_sqlite_write_code):
   Emit PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL and PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000 right after
   each inline connection open.  WAL mode lets readers see the last committed
   state while a writer is active; busy_timeout makes lock collisions retry
   instead of immediately failing.

2. parse_test_output.py (parse_sqlite_test_results):
   Add timeout=30 to sqlite3.connect() so Python waits up to 30 s for a
   transient lock to clear (default was 5 s, which was too short for a busy
   Maven/JVM process).

3. Comparator.java (readTestResults):
   Execute PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000 on the same connection before running
   the SELECT, so the Java Comparator also retries instead of failing with
   [SQLITE_BUSY].

4. CodeflashHelper.java (initializeDatabase) and ResultWriter.java (constructor):
   Same WAL + busy_timeout PRAGMAs added after the initial getConnection() call
   for the long-lived database connections used by these helper classes.

5. Updated codeflash-runtime-1.0.0.jar (rebuilt after Comparator/ResultWriter fix).

tests: add TestSQLiteLockedFix with two assertions —
  • _generate_sqlite_write_code emits PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL and
    PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000 before CREATE TABLE
  • parse_sqlite_test_results uses timeout= in sqlite3.connect()

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix(java): kill entire process group on Maven timeout to prevent orphaned JVMs

Root cause of 'database is locked' errors:
- When Maven times out, subprocess.run() only kills the Maven parent process
- On Linux, Maven's forked Surefire JVM children become orphaned (not killed)
- Orphaned JVMs keep the SQLite result file open, causing SQLITE_BUSY when
  Python reads the file immediately after Maven is killed

Fix: Replace subprocess.run() with _run_cmd_kill_pg_on_timeout() which uses

title: fix(scripts): close pipes on partial RPC client init failure
body:
`startDocsPiClient()` leaks pipe file descriptors when initialization partially fails.


Pipes are acquired sequentially in `startDocsPiClient()`:

```go
stdin, err := process.StdinPipe()   // pipe 1
stdout, err := process.StdoutPipe() // pipe 2
stderr, err := process.StderrPipe() // pipe 3
process.Start()                     // launch

If any step after `StdinPipe()` fails, earlier pipes are never closed:

| Failure point | Leaked pipes |
| `StdoutPipe()` fails | stdin |
| `StderrPipe()` fails | stdin, stdout (read end) |
| `Start()` fails | stdin (write end held open) |

## Proof of bug

Each `*Pipe()` call creates an `os.Pipe()` internally, allocating two kernel file descriptors (read + write). The `Close()` method on the returned `io.WriteCloser`/`io.ReadCloser` releases the caller's end. When the function returns early without closing, the caller's end of the pipe is orphaned -- it stays open until the process exits or the GC finalizer runs (which is non-deterministic and not guaranteed).

Under repeated init failures (binary not found, permission denied), each attempt leaks 1-3 FDs, eventually hitting the process ulimit.


Close previously-acquired pipes at each failure point before returning the error.


- [ ] `docs-i18n` tool starts and translates normally
- [ ] No FD leaks on repeated init failure (can verify with `/proc/self/fd` count on Linux)

Found by [gnosis-polyglot](https://github.com/forkjoin-ai/gnosis) topological scanner (RESOURCE_LEAK rule).
commit_msgs:
fix(scripts): close pipes on partial RPC client init failure

startDocsPiClient() acquires stdin, stdout, and stderr pipes
sequentially. If a later pipe acquisition or process.Start() fails,
previously acquired pipes are never closed, leaking file descriptors.

For example, if StdoutPipe() fails after StdinPipe() succeeded, the
stdin pipe's write-end FD is leaked. Under repeated init failures
(e.g. missing binary, permission denied), this accumulates orphaned
pipe FDs.

Close previously-acquired pipes on each failure path before returning.

Found by gnosis-polyglot topological scanner (RESOURCE_LEAK rule).

title: perf(types): cache gaskv.Store wrappers in Context
body:
- Cache `gaskv.Store` wrappers in a `map[StoreKey]KVStore` on `Context`, eliminating repeated heap allocations from `ctx.KVStore(key)` and `ctx.TransientStore(key)`
- Cache invalidated on `WithMultiStore` / `WithGasMeter` (the only methods that change gaskv inputs)


Every `ctx.KVStore(key)` and `ctx.TransientStore(key)` call allocates a new `gaskv.Store` on the heap (5-field struct, ~40 bytes). Each wraps the same underlying KVStore + same gas meter + same gas config — pure waste to reallocate.

Profiling after #2806 (30s, M4 Max, 1000 EVM transfers/block):

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `gaskv.NewStore` alloc_space | 18,892 MB (#9 top allocator) |
| `gaskv.NewStore` alloc_objects | ~143M objects |
| Top callers | `AccountKeeper.GetAccount` (104.5M), `params.Subspace.kvStore` (46.6M), `bank.getAccountStore` (20.7M) |


`sei-cosmos/types/context.go` (single file):

1. **New field**: `gaskvStores map[StoreKey]KVStore` on Context struct
2. **`NewContext`**: Initialize cache with `make(map[StoreKey]KVStore, 8)`
3. **`WithMultiStore` / `WithGasMeter`**: Invalidate cache (new empty map)
4. **`KVStore` / `TransientStore`**: Check cache first; populate on miss

## Benchmark Results (M4 Max, 1000 EVM transfers/block, 30s profile)

| Metric | Before (after #2806) | After | Delta |
|--------|----------------------|-------|-------|
| TPS (steady-state range) | 8,000–8,800 | 7,800–9,000 | median ~8,400 |
| `gaskv.NewStore` alloc_space | 18,892 MB | 0 MB | **-18,892 MB (eliminated)** |
| `gaskv.NewStore` alloc_objects | ~143M | 0 | **eliminated from top 200** |
| `memclrNoHeapPointers` CPU | 6.96s | 2.11s | **-4.85s** |
| `btree.NewFreeListG` alloc | 36,662 MB | 20,943 MB | **-15,719 MB** |
| `sync.Map nodes` alloc | 33,216 MB | 19,103 MB | **-14,113 MB** |
| `cachemulti.newStoreWithoutGiga` alloc | 39,081 MB | 22,471 MB | **-16,610 MB** |
| Total alloc_space (30s) | 811,276 MB | 457,143 MB | **-354,133 MB (-44%)** |

Note: TPS uplift is modest because freed CPU shifts to idle (usleep/kevent up) — workers complete faster but the bottleneck has shifted elsewhere (likely OCC scheduling / commit pipeline).

### `pprof -alloc_space -diff_base` highlights

-18,298 MB  gaskv.NewStore               (direct savings from this PR)
-17,416 MB  cachemulti.newStoreWithoutGiga (cascading — fewer CMS recreations)
-16,483 MB  btree.NewFreeListG            (cascading — fewer cachekv stores)
-14,798 MB  sync.newIndirectNode          (cascading — fewer sync.Map allocs)
-11,050 MB  state.(*DBImpl).Snapshot      (cascading — less snapshot overhead)
-10,969 MB  sync.newEntryNode             (cascading — fewer sync.Map entries)
 -9,964 MB  vm.NewEVM                     (cascading — less GC pressure)
 -9,241 MB  multiversion.NewVersionIndexedStore

### `pprof -top -diff_base` highlights (CPU)

 -4.85s  runtime.memclrNoHeapPointers (fewer allocs to zero)
 -2.37s  syscall.syscall              (less CGO overhead)
 -1.71s  syscall.syscall6
 -1.46s  runtime.heapBitsSmallForAddr (less heap bookkeeping)
 +3.19s  runtime.usleep               (workers idle more — finished faster)
 +1.61s  runtime.kevent               (same — less work to do)

## Why safe

- Within a single Context, `MultiStore()`, `GasMeter()`, `StoreTracer()` are stable
- `KVGasConfig()` / `TransientGasConfig()` return constants
- `WithMultiStore` and `WithGasMeter` are the only methods that change gaskv inputs — both invalidate
- Map is reference type: copies share cache, but invalidation allocates a fresh map
- Thread safety: each OCC worker has its own Context

title: Fix ContextVar propagation for ASGI-mounted servers with tasks
body:
Fixes background tasks failing with "Background tasks require a running FastMCP server context" when FastMCP is mounted to another ASGI application (FastAPI, Starlette, etc.) or deployed to serverless environments (Lambda, Cloud Run).

**Root cause:** ContextVars set during lifespan don't propagate to request handlers in ASGI environments because they run in sibling async contexts, not parent-child.

**Fix:** `Context.__aenter__` now sets `_current_docket` and `_current_worker` from server instance attributes at request time, ensuring they're available regardless of async context hierarchy.


- `context.py`: Set docket/worker ContextVars from `server._docket`/`server._worker` in `__aenter__`
- `server.py`: Store `_worker` on server instance (was already storing `_docket`)
- `pyproject.toml`: Bump pydocket to >=0.16.6 (includes Redis ACL and py-key-value fixes)

Closes #2671
commit_msgs:
Add debug logging for task lifecycle
Fix ContextVar propagation for nested ASGI lifespan calls

When FastMCP runs with uvicorn, the lifespan is entered twice:
1. FastMCP's outer context (during http_app setup)
2. Starlette's ASGI lifespan (which request handlers inherit from)

The second call was skipping ContextVar setup because _lifespan_result_set
was already True. This caused _current_docket.get() to return None in
request handlers even though server._docket was correctly set.

Fix: Always set ContextVars when entering _lifespan_manager, using the
already-initialized values from self._docket and self._worker.

title: feat(openresponses): add OpenResponses AG-UI integration
body:
Adds a new **OpenResponses** integration that connects AG-UI to any OpenResponses-compatible endpoint (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Hugging Face, OpenClaw). This is a proxy-based integration — it forwards client-provided tools to the LLM and streams responses back as AG-UI events.

### Python SDK (`integrations/openresponses/python/`)

- **`ag_ui_openresponses` package** — full OpenResponses protocol support:
  - Provider auto-detection (OpenAI, Azure, Hugging Face, OpenClaw) from base URL
  - SSE stream parsing and event translation (OpenResponses → AG-UI)
  - Tool call handling with proper event sequencing
  - Reasoning and refusal event translation
  - Multimodal content support (images, files)
  - Stateful mode via `previous_response_id`
  - Runtime config via `forwarded_props` (no hardcoded secrets)
  - JSON config loader with `${ENV_VAR}` resolution
  - Zero-config proxy factory (`create_openresponses_proxy`)

### Deployable Proxy Server (`integrations/openresponses/python/server/`)

A standalone, deployable proxy that turns any OpenResponses-compatible API into an AG-UI endpoint. Includes:

- **Dockerfile** (PyPI install) and **Dockerfile.local** (monorepo source)
- **Named config** system — drop JSON files in `configs/` with `${ENV_VAR}` resolution
- **Restrict mode** — lock down to named configs only, preventing caller overrides
- Platform deployment recipes:
  - **Fly.io** — `fly.toml` config
  - **Railway** — `railway.json` config
  - **Render** — `render.yaml` config

Endpoints:

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `POST /` | Generic | Config via `forwarded_props` |
| `POST /configs/{name}` | Named config | Uses `configs/{name}.json` |
| `GET /configs` | List configs | Returns available config names |
| `GET /health` | Health check | Returns `{"status": "ok"}` |

### Dojo Examples (3 features)

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `agentic_chat` | Basic chat via OpenAI |
| `human_in_the_loop` | Task planning with `generate_task_steps` (frontend-executed) |
| `tool_based_generative_ui` | Haiku generation (frontend-executed tool) |

All examples use `create_openresponses_proxy` with a shared `configs/openai.json` config file.

### E2E Tests

- `agenticChatPage.spec.ts` — greeting + memory retention
- `humanInTheLoopPage.spec.ts` — plan generation + step execution
- `toolBasedGenUIPage.spec.ts` — haiku generation + UI consistency
- CI matrix entry in `dojo-e2e.yml`

### Event Mapping

| OpenResponses Event | AG-UI Event |
|---------------------|-------------|
| `response.created` | `RUN_STARTED` |
| `response.output_item.added` (message) | `TEXT_MESSAGE_START` |
| `response.output_text.delta` | `TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT` |
| `response.output_text.done` | `TEXT_MESSAGE_END` |
| `response.output_item.added` (function_call) | `TOOL_CALL_START` |
| `response.function_call_arguments.delta` | `TOOL_CALL_ARGS` |
| `response.output_item.done` (function_call) | `TOOL_CALL_END` |
| `response.completed` | `RUN_FINISHED` |
| `response.failed` | `RUN_ERROR` |
| `response.reasoning_text.delta` | `THINKING_TEXT_MESSAGE_START` + `THINKING_TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT` |
| `response.reasoning_text.done` | `THINKING_TEXT_MESSAGE_END` |
| `response.refusal.delta` | `TEXT_MESSAGE_START` + `TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT` |
| `response.refusal.done` | `TEXT_MESSAGE_END` |

- [ ] Run example server locally: `cd integrations/openresponses/python/examples && poetry run python -m server`
- [ ] Verify endpoints with curl: `POST http://localhost:8018/agentic_chat/configs/openai`
- [ ] Run Dojo with OpenResponses: `node scripts/run-dojo-everything.js --only dojo,openresponses`

* feat(adk-middleware): robust streaming function call arguments support

Refactor the streaming function call dispatch in EventTranslator to
fix several correctness issues and add opt-in support for Gemini 3's
stream_function_call_arguments mode.

Closes https://github.com/ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui/issues/990

## Breaking Changes

None. All changes are backwards-compatible. The new
`streaming_function_call_arguments` parameter defaults to False.

## What changed

### Streaming FC dispatch split into two explicit modes (#990)

The `is_streaming_fc` condition previously used `func_call.name and
will_continue` which was too broad — it matched partial events that
should be skipped (no accumulated args yet). The dispatch is now split:

- **Mode A** (Gemini 3+ `stream_function_call_arguments`): only active
  when `streaming_function_call_arguments=True` is passed to
  EventTranslator/ADKAgent. Triggers on `partial_args`, first chunk
  (name + will_continue + no args), or end chunk.

- **Mode B** (accumulated args / progressive SSE): triggers on
  `has_args` with `will_continue`, existing tracking, or named FC in
  a partial event. This is the original behavior.

### Name-based dedup replaced with single-use tracking (#990)

`_completed_streaming_fc_names` (a permanent set) suppressed repeat
invocations of the same tool. Replaced with
`_last_completed_streaming_fc_name` (Optional[str]) that clears after
the non-partial event is filtered. TOOL_CALL_RESULT suppression uses
the same single-use mechanism with None guards.

### ADK aggregator workarounds for stream_function_call_arguments

The predictive_state_updates example includes monkey-patches for two
ADK bugs that prevent streaming FC args from working out of the box.
Filed upstream as https://github.com/google/adk-python/issues/4311 —
workaround code is annotated so it can be removed when the fix ships.

### Examples bumped to google-adk>=1.23.0

The examples pyproject.toml now pins `google-adk>=1.23.0` to test
against the latest ADK. The library minimum remains `>=1.16.0`.

### Dojo e2e test comment updated

The predictive_state_updates e2e test remains skipped but the comment
now explains that the demo works without Vertex AI (falls back to
Gemini 2.5 Flash) and documents what credentials enable full streaming.

## Test results

530 passed, 33 skipped (full suite).
3 new tests in test_lro_filtering.py:
- test_mode_a_streaming_fc_with_flag_enabled
- test_mode_a_first_chunk_skipped_without_flag
- test_same_tool_called_twice_not_suppressed

title: Make FBDF/DFBDF stepping non-allocating and fix allocation tests
body:
- Add in-place `calc_finite_difference_weights!` that writes to a pre-allocated `Matrix` buffer instead of creating `MMatrix`→`SArray` (which heap-allocates on every call to `estimate_terk!` and `choose_order!`)
- Add `fd_weights` buffer field to `FBDFCache` and `DFBDFCache`, allocated once at init time
- Update `estimate_terk!` and `choose_order!` (mutable cache variants for both FBDF and DFBDF) to use the in-place version
- Rewrite allocation tests to test `perform_step!` directly via AllocCheck (like Rosenbrock tests) instead of `step!`, since `step!` includes saving operations that naturally allocate
- Add runtime `@allocated` tests for FBDF and DFBDF with `save_everystep=false`

## Results

FBDF and DFBDF now show **0 bytes allocated per step** at runtime, verified across:
- Order ramping (order 1→5)
- Steady-state stepping
- Adaptive dt changes

Steps during order ramping:
  step 1: 0 bytes, order=1
  step 3: 0 bytes, order=2
  step 8: 0 bytes, order=3
  step 14: 0 bytes, order=4
  step 21: 0 bytes, order=5
  step 30: 0 bytes, order=5


- [x] FBDF produces correct solutions (exponential decay, Robertson stiff problem)
- [x] DFBDF produces correct DAE solutions
- [x] `step!(save_everystep=false)` allocates 0 bytes for FBDF
- [x] `step!(save_everystep=false)` allocates 0 bytes for DFBDF
- [x] AllocCheck `perform_step!` static analysis runs (broken for infrastructure-level FunctionWrappers dispatches, same as all other solvers)
- [x] Allocation tests pass: 2 passed, 18 broken (all broken are AllocCheck static analysis shared across all solvers)

- Compute FBDF `fsallast` algebraically from NL solver convergence

Fix PayPal checkout loop when API returns errors (#193)

## Problem
When PayPal NVP API returns an error (e.g., error 10002 - invalid credentials),
the checkout would loop back to /register instead of displaying an error message.
This happened because:

1. `get_checkout_details()` didn't check for ACK=Failure in PayPal responses
2. `confirmation_form()` returned error strings instead of displaying them
3. No logging was present to help debug API issues

## Solution

### Error Handling Improvements
- Added ACK=Failure check in `get_checkout_details()` - now returns WP_Error
  for API errors instead of treating them as valid responses
- Changed `confirmation_form()` to use `wp_die()` instead of returning strings,
  ensuring error messages are actually displayed to users
- Added proper WP_Error handling in `process_confirmation()`

### Logging Improvements
- Added comprehensive logging throughout the PayPal flow:
  - GetExpressCheckoutDetails API calls
  - CreateRecurringPaymentsProfile API calls
  - DoExpressCheckoutPayment API calls
  - All error conditions with specific error codes

### Validation Improvements
- Added null checks for pending_payment, customer, and membership
- Improved error messages with actionable guidance ("Please try again or contact support")
- Fixed HTTP response codes in wp_die() calls (changed '401' strings to 200 integers)

Note: Pre-existing PHPCS errors on lines 423 and 652 are not related to this fix.

Closes #193

title: ci: Optimize GitHub Actions workflow performance
body:
Reduces CI overhead across 12 workflow files through four strategies:

- **Blobless partial clones** — Many jobs used `fetch-depth: 0` (full clone of all commits, tags, and file blobs). Most only need commit history for version tagging via `git describe`. Adding `filter: blob:none` tells git to fetch commits and tags but download file blobs only on demand at checkout, reducing initial clone size while preserving versioning. All 13 bare `fetch-depth: 0` occurrences now use blobless clones.
- **NuGet package caching** — Added `actions/cache` to 7 build jobs, saving ~1-2 minutes per job by avoiding redundant package downloads. This was the biggest measurable improvement.
- **Scoped artifact uploads** — `siteextension_release` was uploading the entire workspace; now uploads only the build output. Updated `deploy_siteextension` download path to match.
- **Sparse checkout** — 6 validation jobs in `post_deploy_agent` now check out only the directory they need.

- [x] Verify versioning works correctly with blobless clones (`Versioning.targets` git describe)
- [x] Verify `post_deploy_agent` sparse checkouts work (next release cycle)
- [x] Trigger `siteextension_release` manually to verify scoped artifact upload/download

title: perf(evm): skip redundant initial Snapshot in OCC executor path
body:
- Skip the redundant initial `Snapshot()` call in the OCC executor path

## Stack
7/19 — depends on perf/cache-gaskv-context (replaces auto-closed #2819)
commit_msgs:
perf(evm): skip redundant initial Snapshot in OCC executor path

In the OCC executor path, each EVM transaction creates 3 CacheMultiStore
layers:

  1. prepareTask: CMS with VersionIndexedStore wrappers (OCC isolation)
  2. NewDBImpl: Snapshot() creates CMS wrapping #1 (GetCommittedState baseline)
  3. Prepare: Snapshot() creates CMS wrapping #2 (EVM revert support)

Layer #2 is redundant because no state changes occur between NewDBImpl
and Prepare (called by go-ethereum's StateTransition.Execute). Prepare's
Snapshot provides the same GetCommittedState baseline.

Add NewDBImplWithoutSnapshot() that skips the initial Snapshot, used only
in the OCC hot path (app.go executeEVMTxWithGigaExecutor). The original
NewDBImpl is preserved for all other callers (tests, RPC, ante handlers)
that may write state before the first explicit Snapshot.

Also add defensive guards on GetCommittedState and flushEvents for the
case where snapshottedCtxs is empty.

Results (M4 Max benchmark, diff vs previous):
- DBImpl.Snapshot alloc: -9.8 GB
- cachemulti.newStoreWithoutGiga: -10.5 GB
- Total alloc_space: 457 GB → 313 GB (-31%)
- Idle CPU (usleep+kevent): 42.9s → 30.1s (-30%, workers busier)
- TPS steady-state: 7,200-8,600 (median ~8,000)

title: release-26.2: logictestccl: fix as_of flake by increasing closed timestamp target
body:
Backport 1/1 commits from #166111 on behalf of @mw5h.

----

The TestCCLLogic_as_of test has been repeatedly flaking (deflaked 6+
times) because follower_read_timestamp() returns now()-4.2s by default,
which in race builds can land mid-bootstrap — after database creation
but before table creation — producing "relation t does not exist"
instead of the expected "database test does not exist".

Rather than continuing to widen error regexes (whack-a-mole), this
patch increases kv.closed_timestamp.target_duration to 1m for the
follower read portion of the test. This makes follower_read_timestamp()
go back ~62s, reliably predating cluster bootstrap even in slow builds.
The setting is reset to 3s before the bounded staleness tests that
follow.

Fixes: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/166055

Epic: none
Release note: None


----

Release justification: Test only fix

title: feat(prompts): add 'Never Give Up' persistence to worker/fixer agents
body:
Adds explicit instructions to worker and fixer agents to CREATE missing resources instead of giving up when something doesn't exist.

**Changes:**
- `full-workflow.json`: Added to worker's `initial` and `subsequent` prompts
- `worker-validator.json`: Added to worker's `system` prompt
- `debug-workflow.json`: Added to fixer's `system` prompt

## The New Instruction

## NEVER GIVE UP - CREATE WHAT'S MISSING

If something doesn't exist that SHOULD exist:
- Missing file → CREATE IT with proper implementation
- Missing function → ADD IT to appropriate module
- Missing test → WRITE IT
- Missing config → CREATE IT with sensible defaults

"I couldn't find X" is NOT an acceptable outcome. Either find it or CREATE it.

## Why This Matters

Workers and fixers were sometimes giving up when they couldn't find a file or function they expected. This caused task failures when the agent could have simply created what was missing. This explicit instruction makes the "create it" behavior the expected default.

Test expected 14s (2s + 4s + 8s = 3 delays) but implementation only has

The delay formula is: baseDelay * 2^(attempt-1)

title: fix(sessions/claudecode): keep final streaming token count for duplicate entries
body:
Claude Code's streaming API writes the same `messageId:requestId` pair to the JSONL log multiple times while a response is being generated:
- Early writes contain **partial** `output_tokens` (e.g. 31)
- The final write contains the **complete** `output_tokens` count (e.g. 300)

The previous `HashSet`-based dedup kept the **first-seen** entry, causing systematic token undercounts for every streaming response.


Replace `processed_hashes: HashSet<String>` with `HashMap<String, usize>` that maps each dedup key to its **index** in the `messages` vec. When a duplicate key is encountered, compare `output_tokens` and update the existing entry in-place if the new value is larger.


- `sessions/claudecode.rs`: `HashSet` → `HashMap<String, usize>` for `processed_hashes`; dedup logic updated to keep max `output_tokens`
- Added `test_deduplication_keeps_max_output_for_streaming_duplicates`: three streaming writes for the same `messageId:requestId` collapse to one entry with the final token count

## Test

running 3 tests
test sessions::claudecode::tests::test_deduplication_allows_same_message_different_request ... ok
test sessions::claudecode::tests::test_deduplication_keeps_max_output_for_streaming_duplicates ... ok
test sessions::claudecode::tests::test_deduplication_skips_duplicate_entries ... ok
commit_msgs:
fix(sessions/claudecode): keep final streaming token count for duplicate entries

Claude Code's streaming API writes the same messageId:requestId multiple
times while streaming — the first entry has a partial output_tokens count
and the last entry has the final, complete count. The previous HashSet-based
dedup kept the first-seen entry (partial), causing systematic token undercounts.

Switch processed_hashes from HashSet<String> to HashMap<String, usize> mapping
each dedup key to its index in the messages vec. When a duplicate is found,
update the existing entry in-place if the new output_tokens is larger.

Add test_deduplication_keeps_max_output_for_streaming_duplicates to verify
that three streaming writes for the same messageId:requestId collapse to one
entry retaining the max output_tokens (300, not the partial 31).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix(claudecode): use per-field max merge for streaming duplicates

Instead of only updating when output_tokens increases, merge all token
fields using per-field max. This fixes undercounting when later streaming
entries have corrected input/cache values but same output.

Adds regression tests for:
- Same output but higher input (per-field merge)
- Higher-first/lower-later (max preservation)
fix(claudecode): defer dedup index insert to prevent stale index panic

processed_hashes.insert() was called before the model check, so entries
with model=null registered an index without pushing a message. Later
duplicates would index out of bounds or corrupt an unrelated message.

Move insert to right before messages.push() so index is only recorded
when the message is guaranteed to exist.

This PR adds a new user preference that allows customizing the spacing between notes in timelines. Users can choose from four spacing options to suit their viewing preferences.


### Four Spacing Options
- **極狭い (Extremely Narrow)**: 3px gap (2px on mobile) + ~50% reduced internal padding
- **狭い (Narrow)**: 6px gap (4px on mobile)
- **普通 (Normal)**: 16px gap (10px on mobile) - Default
- **広い (Wide)**: 28px gap (18px on mobile)

Settings → General → Timeline and Note → Note Spacing

- Responsive design with automatic mobile adjustments via `@media` queries

title: perf: Fix SQL editor typing lag by memoizing DatabaseTree
body:
- Wraps `DatabaseTree` component with `React.memo()` to prevent unnecessary re-renders


The SQL editor was experiencing significant lag when typing, especially in projects with many database tables/views (~500ms per keystroke in some cases).

**Root cause:** `EditorScene` subscribes to `queryInput` via `useValues(multitabEditorLogic)`, causing the entire component tree to re-render on every keystroke. This cascaded to `DatabaseTree` which re-rendered `LemonTree` with potentially thousands of nodes.


Wrap `DatabaseTree` with `React.memo()`. Since the only prop (`databaseTreeRef`) is a stable ref, the component will skip re-rendering when the parent re-renders due to `queryInput` changes.


- [x] Tested locally with 500 fake view nodes - typing is now snappy
- [ ] Test in production on projects with many tables/views

perf: Wrap DatabaseTree with memo to prevent re-renders on keystroke

The SQL editor was experiencing significant lag when typing, especially
in projects with many database tables/views. Root cause: EditorScene
subscribes to queryInput, causing re-renders on every keystroke. This
cascaded to DatabaseTree which re-rendered the entire tree (potentially
thousands of nodes).

Wrapping DatabaseTree with React.memo prevents re-renders when the
parent re-renders, since the ref prop is stable.

title: Add `release-python.yml` workflow for trusted publishing
body: ### Related Issues/PRs Relates to # ### What changes are proposed in this pull request? Add a `release-python.yml` GitHub Actions workflow that publishes Python packages (`mlflow`, `mlflow-skinny`, `mlflow-tracing`) to PyPI using [trusted publishing](https://docs.pypi.org/trusted-publishers/) (OIDC-based, no API tokens needed). Key features: - `workflow_dispatch` with inputs for package, ref, and destination (PyPI or TestPyPI) - Actor permission check (admin/maintain required) - Environment-gated publish job (`pypi`/`testpypi`) for approval workflows - PR trigger (paths: `release-python.yml`) to validate the build on changes to the workflow itself ### How is this PR tested? - [x] Manual tests ### Does this PR require documentation update? - [x] No. ### Does this PR require updating the [MLflow Skills](https://github.com/mlflow/skills) repository? - [x] No. ### Release Notes #### Is this a user-facing change? - [x] No. #### What component(s), interfaces, languages, and integrations does this PR affect? Components - [x] `area/build`: Build and test infrastructure for MLflow #### How should the PR be classified in the release notes? Choose one: - [x] `rn/none` - No description will be included. The PR will be mentioned only by the PR number in the "Small Bugfixes and Documentation Updates" section #### Is this PR a critical bugfix or security fix that should go into the next patch release? What is a minor/patch release? - Minor release: a release that increments the second part of the version number (e.g., 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0). Minor releases are expected to contain larger changes, such as new features and improvements. Non-critical bug fixes and doc updates can be included as well. By default, your PR should target the next minor release. - Patch release: a release that increments the third part of the version number (e.g., 1.2.0 -> 1.2.1). Patch releases are typically only performed when there has been a major regression or bug in the latest release. For the sake of stability, your PR should not be included in a patch release unless it is a critical fix, or if the risk level of your PR is exceedingly low. - [ ] This PR is critical and needs to be in the next patch release - [x] This PR can wait for the next minor release

- Output `[ZYLOS_TASK]` blocks for Claude to execute via C4

## Design

Follows v2 proposal architecture:
- Skills directory: `~/.claude/skills/<component>/`
- Data directory: `~/zylos/components/<component>/`
- Commands output task blocks for AI execution (Scenario B)
