zylos install telegram              # Official component
zylos install kevin/whatsapp        # Third-party
zylos upgrade telegram              # Single component
zylos upgrade --all                 # All components
zylos uninstall telegram --purge    # Remove with data
zylos list                          # Show installed
zylos search bot                    # Search registry

title: fix: web terminal resize + mobile menu + session management
body:
- **Terminal resize**: Web terminal was not resizing because `tmux attach -f ignore-size` excludes the client from window size calculation. Added explicit `tmux resize-window` call after `pty.Setsize()` so programs inside the session observe updated dimensions.
- **Mobile menu**: On Galaxy Fold and similar devices, the hamburger menu opened then immediately closed. - **Session management from web UI**: Added two new API endpoints and corresponding UI controls:
  - `POST /api/session/quick-create` — creates a new session under a group with auto-generated name and Claude as default tool (mirrors TUI "N" shortcut)
  - `POST /api/session/{id}/stop` — kills the tmux session and removes it from the session list

  - "×" button on session rows for delete
- **Service worker cache**: Bumped cache version to ensure clients pick up frontend changes.

fix: prevent mobile menu from closing immediately on open

When the hamburger menu opens on mobile, it auto-focuses the filter
input after 60ms. On devices like Galaxy Fold, this triggers the
virtual keyboard, which fires a visualViewport resize event that
detects keyboard-open state and calls closeMenuForMobile().

Fix by focusing the first menu item (a button) instead of the filter
input, avoiding the keyboard trigger entirely.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix: mobile menu closes immediately on Galaxy Fold and similar devices

Three issues combined to make the hamburger menu unusable on mobile:

1. Opening the menu did not blur the active element (often xterm.js's
   hidden textarea), so the virtual keyboard stayed up or reappeared,
   triggering a viewport-shift that was mis-detected as a keyboard
   event and closed the menu via closeMenuForMobile().

2. closeMenuForMobile() had no grace period, so any viewport jitter
   within the first few hundred milliseconds of the menu opening
   (toolbar hide, keyboard dismiss animation) could close it.

3. The backdrop click handler could fire from the same touch gesture
   that opened the menu on some Android browsers.

Fix by blurring the active element on menu open, adding a 400ms guard
to closeMenuForMobile(), a 300ms guard to backdrop clicks, and bumping
the service-worker cache version to ensure clients pick up the changes.

title: Fix generalization of call-argument lambdas causing type errors
body:
See https://roc.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/231634-beginners/topic/Unexpected.20type.20mismatch.20with.20parameterised.20function/near/577730388

Lambdas passed as call arguments (e.g. `list.fold_rev(dest, |item, acc| ...)`)
were independently generalized at an inner rank, setting their type vars to
rank 0. When those vars were then unified with outer scope vars via Rank.min
in merge, the outer vars were pulled to rank 0, preventing the enclosing
function from generalizing. This caused spurious TYPE MISMATCH errors when
a polymorphic function with nested lambdas was tested from within its own
module (via expect), while working correctly from external modules.

Skip generalization for standalone lambdas that are direct call arguments,
since they are consumed immediately and don't need independent generalization.
Their type vars remain at the enclosing scope's rank and generalize together
with the enclosing function.

in merge, the outer vars were pulled to rank 0, preventing the enclosing
function from generalizing. This caused spurious TYPE MISMATCH errors when
a polymorphic function with nested lambdas was tested from within its own
module (via expect), while working correctly from external modules.

Skip generalization for standalone lambdas that are direct call arguments,
since they are consumed immediately and don't need independent generalization.
Their type vars remain at the enclosing scope's rank and generalize together

Merge branch 'main' into fix-unexpected-type-mismatch

Signed-off-by: Anton-4 <17049058+Anton-4@users.noreply.github.com>
fix: resolve imports for all modules before code generation

The evaluator backends only re-resolved imports for the current module
being compiled, but Monomorphize follows cross-module calls and uses
cached import indices from dependency modules. When the comptime
interpreter and code-generation evaluator use different module array
orderings, stale cached indices in dependency modules point to the
wrong module, causing an out-of-bounds panic in isDefNode.

Re-resolve imports for every module in all_module_envs so all cached
indices are consistent with the array Monomorphize will use.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix: only suppress call-arg lambda generalization inside functions

The checking_call_arg flag unconditionally suppressed generalization
for all call-argument lambdas, which fixed the polymorphic list reverse
test but regressed issue 9075 (y inferred as Error instead of Dec).

Only suppress generalization when the call-arg lambda is nested inside
another function (rank > outermost). At the outermost rank, allow
generalization so the enclosing value's type is properly generalized
for instantiation at use sites, preventing error propagation from
destroying type information.

title: refactor: Clean up search architecture, remove experimental contextualize endpoint
body:
This PR cleans up the search architecture by removing the experimental contextualize endpoint and clarifying the vector-first search strategy.


### Removed Contextualize Endpoint
- **Removed** `contextualize` MCP tool from search-server.ts (~4KB reduction)
- **Rationale**: Contextualize is better suited as a skill (LLM-powered analysis) rather than a static endpoint
- **Created** issue #132 to track future contextualize skill implementation
- **Benefit**: Search API already provides vector search with configurable limits; skill can do smart synthesis

### Clarified Search Architecture  
- **Disabled** FTS5 fallback paths in SessionSearch.ts
- **Added** deprecation warnings where FTS5 code remains
- **Clarified** that search is vector-first (Chroma), not keyword-first
- **Benefit**: Clearer architecture, no confusion about search strategy

### Documentation Cleanup

title: Levenberg-Marquardt optimizer for deformable registration (v1.5.0)
body:
## Levenberg-Marquardt optimizer for deformable registration (v1.5.0)

FireANTs now ships a **Levenberg-Marquardt (LM)** optimizer for greedy and SyN deformable registration — a second-order method that adapts its own damping at every iteration with no manual tuning required.

### What's new

**`optimizer='levenberg'` in `GreedyRegistration` / `SyNRegistration`**

reg = GreedyRegistration(
    scales=[8, 4, 2, 1],
    iterations=[200, 150, 100, 50],
    fixed_images=fixed_batch,
    moving_images=moving_batch,
    loss_type="fusedcc",
    optimizer="levenberg",
    optimizer_lr=0.75,
reg.optimize()

The optimizer maintains a damping parameter λ that is automatically updated each iteration:
- **loss increases** → λ × `lambda_increase_factor` (retreat to a safer step)
- **loss decreases** → λ × `lambda_decrease_factor` (allow a more aggressive step)

All three hyper-parameters have sensible defaults and can be overridden via `optimizer_params`:

| Parameter | Default | Role |
| `lambda_init` | `1e-2` | Starting damping (also accepts `'auto'`) |
| `lambda_increase_factor` | `1.5` | Growth factor on bad steps (must be > 1) |
| `lambda_decrease_factor` | `0.975` | Shrink factor on good steps (must be < 1) |

A tiled Hessian approximation (`tile_size > 1`) is also available for locally-varying curvature estimates.


See the new **[How To: Levenberg-Marquardt optimizer](docs/docs/howto/levenberg-marquardt.md)** guide, which covers default usage, parameter explanations, and a self-contained evaluation script with Dice score logging.

### Files changed
- `fireants/registration/optimizers/levenberg.py` — `WarpLevenbergMarquardt` implementation
- `fireants/registration/deformation/compositive.py` — wires up `'levenberg'` optimizer choice
- `docs/docs/howto/levenberg-marquardt.md` — new how-to guide
- `tests/test_optimizer_comparison.py` — optimizer comparison tests

title: feat: Set up comprehensive Python testing infrastructure
body:
# Set up Python Testing Infrastructure


This PR establishes a comprehensive testing infrastructure for the InfLoRA continual learning project. The setup follows modern Python development practices using Poetry for dependency management and pytest for testing.

### Key Changes Made:

- **Package Management**: Added Poetry configuration in `pyproject.toml` with all project dependencies migrated from the conda environment
- **Testing Framework**: Configured pytest with comprehensive settings including coverage reporting, custom markers, and strict configuration
- **Directory Structure**: Created organized test directory structure:
  - `tests/` - Main test directory
  - `tests/unit/` - Unit tests directory  
  - `tests/integration/` - Integration tests directory
  - `tests/conftest.py` - Shared fixtures and test configuration
- **Test Fixtures**: Comprehensive fixtures for ML testing including:
  - PyTorch tensors, models, optimizers, and dataloaders
  - NumPy arrays and random seeding
  - Mock objects for testing without dependencies
  - Sample configurations and data structures
  - Memory buffers and LoRA configurations
- **Coverage Reporting**: Configured 80% coverage threshold with HTML and XML reports
- **Development Environment**: Updated `.gitignore` with testing artifacts and development files

## Testing Infrastructure Components

### pytest Configuration
- Test discovery patterns for `test_*.py` and `*_test.py` files
- Custom markers: `unit`, `integration`, `slow`
- Coverage reporting with term-missing, HTML, and XML formats
- Strict configuration and verbose output

### Coverage Settings
- Source directories: `methods`, `models`, `utils`
- Exclusions for test files, cache, and boilerplate code
- 80% coverage threshold requirement
- HTML report generation in `htmlcov/`

### Shared Fixtures (`conftest.py`)
- **Configuration fixtures**: Sample configs, temporary directories, file handling
- **PyTorch fixtures**: Tensors, models, optimizers, datasets, dataloaders
- **NumPy fixtures**: Arrays with proper seeding for reproducible tests  
- **Mock fixtures**: Models, optimizers, loggers, wandb integration
- **ML-specific fixtures**: Memory buffers, LoRA configs, task data, checkpoints, metrics
- **Environment fixtures**: Device handling, CUDA cleanup, random seeding

## Instructions for Running Tests

### Basic Commands
# Install dependencies
poetry install

# Run all tests
poetry run pytest

# Run with coverage
poetry run pytest --cov

# Run specific test types
poetry run pytest -m unit          # Unit tests only
poetry run pytest -m integration   # Integration tests only
poetry run pytest -m slow          # Slow tests only

# Run tests with verbose output
poetry run pytest -v

# Generate coverage report
poetry run pytest --cov --cov-report=html

### Test Organization
- Place unit tests in `tests/unit/`
- Place integration tests in `tests/integration/`
- Use provided fixtures from `conftest.py` for consistent test setup
- Mark tests appropriately with `@pytest.mark.unit`, `@pytest.mark.integration`, or `@pytest.mark.slow`

## Validation

The setup includes comprehensive validation tests (`tests/test_setup_validation.py`) that verify:
- ✅ pytest functionality and fixture loading
- ✅ PyTorch and NumPy integration (with graceful fallbacks)
- ✅ Mock object functionality
- ✅ Test markers and configuration
- ✅ Directory structure creation
- ✅ Coverage reporting setup

All validation tests pass, confirming the testing infrastructure is ready for development.

## Dependencies Added

### Testing Dependencies (dev group)
- `pytest` ^7.1.2 - Main testing framework
- `pytest-cov` ^4.1.0 - Coverage reporting
- `pytest-mock` ^3.11.1 - Mock utilities and fixtures

### Main Dependencies
All existing dependencies from `environment.yaml` have been migrated to Poetry format with compatible version specifications.


- The testing infrastructure is designed to work with optional dependencies (torch/numpy) for flexible CI/CD environments
- Coverage is configured to exclude test files, cache directories, and boilerplate code
- Poetry lock file is included and should be committed (not in .gitignore)
- HTML coverage reports are generated in `htmlcov/` directory
- All test artifacts are properly excluded via `.gitignore`

title: feat(ce-compound): add discoverability check for docs/solutions/ in instruction files
body:
The `docs/solutions/` knowledge store only compounds value when agents can find it. Today, only plugin-mediated workflows (ce:plan via learnings-researcher) know to search there. Agents in fresh sessions, other tools (Cursor, Copilot), or collaborators without the plugin have no reason to discover it.

Both ce:compound and ce:compound-refresh now run a discoverability check after their main work completes. If the project's instruction file (AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md) doesn't surface the knowledge store to agents, the skill suggests a minimal addition — with consent before editing.

## What gets added

The addition adapts to the AGENTS.md\/CLAUDE.md\'s existing structure. Two examples from testing:

**When AGENTS.md\/CLAUDE.md has a directory listing or architecture section** — a single line is added:

app/
  models/        # ActiveRecord models
  controllers/   # Request handling
  views/         # ERB templates
docs/
  solutions/     # Documented solutions to past problems (bugs, best practices, workflow patterns), organized by category with YAML frontmatter (module, tags, problem_type)

**When AGENTS.md\/CLAUDE.md has a documentation section with bullet entries** — a bullet is added:

```markdown
## Documentation

- `docs/adr/` — Architecture Decision Records
- `docs/api/` — OpenAPI specs (auto-generated from code annotations)
- `docs/runbooks/` — Incident response procedures
- `docs/solutions/` — Searchable knowledge store of previously solved problems, organized by category with YAML frontmatter (`module`, `tags`, `problem_type`); relevant when implementing or debugging in documented areas

**When AGENTS.md\/CLAUDE.md is flat with no sections** — a line is appended matching the existing style:

Use `bun test` to run tests.
Prefer Tailwind utility classes over custom CSS.
This is a Next.js 14 app with App Router.
`docs/solutions/` contains categorized write-ups (YAML frontmatter with tags, problem_type, component) of past bugs and decisions, relevant when implementing or debugging in documented areas.

The tone is always informational ("relevant when...") rather than imperative ("check before...") to avoid redundant reads when the plugin's own workflows already search `docs/solutions/`.

## Key decisions

- **Semantic assessment, not string matching.** The check evaluates whether an agent reading the file would learn three things: (1) the store exists, (2) enough about its structure to search effectively, (3) when it's relevant. The file could express this many different ways without ever using the literal path `docs/solutions/`.
- **Shim detection.** One file may just `@`-include the other (e.g., `CLAUDE.md` containing only `@AGENTS.md`). The check identifies which file holds substantive content and targets that one.
- **Prefer existing sections.** The skill strongly prefers adding a single line to an existing architecture/directory/documentation section over creating a new headed section.
- **Consent-gated editing.** In interactive modes, explains why discoverability matters and uses the platform's question tool to get user approval. In autofix mode (compound-refresh), includes a report recommendation without editing.


- Tested across 12 fixture scenarios covering: shim files (both directions), directory listings, flat files, files that already mention the store, files that mention the path but not the spirit, files using different terminology, minimal files, complex multi-section files, no files, and both-files-substantive
- Ran 2 iterations — iteration 1 identified imperative tone and unnecessary new-section creation, iteration 2 confirmed fixes landed (7/7 tone issues resolved, 3/3 section issues resolved)

fix(fix_services): add threading lock around LASTTRY and isReloadingMon

on_epoch and on_bcap_sys_log run from different threads (main loop vs
bettercap event handler). Both read and write self.LASTTRY without
synchronization, creating a race where two recovery actions fire
simultaneously. Similarly, isReloadingMon can be checked and set by

title: Add MPP+SDL2 hardware acceleration for high-performance video decoding
body:
This PR implements hardware-accelerated video decoding and rendering using Rockchip MPP decoder and SDL2 for maximum FPS performance on RK3588 platforms.

## Performance Improvements

- **129 FPS achieved** (up from 50 FPS) - **158% improvement**
- Target FPS: ~170 FPS (matching mp4_hw_dec_sdl2 example benchmark)

### Optimizations Implemented

1. **Removed MPP decoder FPS limit** - Allow full-speed decoding
2. **Removed main loop delay** - Eliminate unnecessary usleep() calls
3. **NV12 format direct pass-through** - Avoid YUV↔RGB conversion overhead
4. **SDL2 hardware rendering** - GPU-accelerated display with OpenGL/ES

## New Components

### New Nodes

- **vp_mpp_file_src_node**: FFmpeg demuxer + MPP hardware decoder
  - Uses FFmpeg for container parsing (demuxing)
  - Uses Rockchip MPP for H.264/H.265 hardware decoding
  - Outputs NV12 format directly for zero-copy rendering

- **vp_sdl2_des_node**: SDL2 hardware renderer destination
  - Accepts NV12 format frames directly
  - Hardware-accelerated texture upload and rendering
  - FPS overlay display with visual bar indicator

### New Executable

- **rk_videopipe_opt**: Enhanced main program with two modes
  - Mode 0: Full AI pipeline (YOLO + tracking + pose + classification)
  - Mode 1: High-performance decode + display only (MPP → SDL2)

## Key Bug Fixes

1. **MPP decoder initialization bug** (`mpp_decoder.cpp:69`)
   - Fixed local variable shadowing class member `mpp_ctx`
   - Changed `mpp_create(&mpp_ctx, ...)` to `mpp_create(&this->mpp_ctx, ...)`

2. **vp_frame_meta assertion removed**
   - Allow empty cv::Mat for NV12 mode (data provided via nv12_data pointer)

3. **MPP library linking**
   - Changed from hardcoded path to library name `rockchip_mpp`
   - Allows system linker to resolve correct version (.so.0 vs .so.1)

## Exit Behavior Improvements

- ✅ **Ctrl+C works properly** - Added SIGINT/SIGTERM signal handlers
- ✅ **Auto-exit on video end** - Program exits when source finishes
- ✅ **ESC key support** - Works in both windows (data flow + SDL2)
- ✅ **Window close button** - SDL2 window close event handled


# High-performance mode (129+ FPS)
build/rk_videopipe_opt -f video.mp4 -m 1 -fps

# Full AI pipeline mode
build/rk_videopipe_opt -f video.mp4 -m 0 -fps

- [x] Verify SDL2 hardware rendering (OpenGL/ES)

## Documentation

- `USAGE_WITH_BOARD.md` - Detailed usage with interface description
- `MPP_SDL2_SUMMARY.md` - Implementation summary
- `PLAN_MPP_SDL2_OPTIMIZATION.md` - Development plan

title: fix: patch DOM-based XSS and account-linking CSRF in Vercel connect flow
body:
The Vercel connection flow has two chained security vulnerabilities (VERIA-212, CVSS 7.4 High):

1. **DOM-Based XSS**: The backend validates the `next` redirect URL and correctly returns `""` for malicious inputs (e.g. `javascript:` URIs). However, the frontend uses `sessionInfo?.next_url || nextUrl` — since `""` is falsy in JS, the `||` operator falls back to the raw, unvalidated URL parameter, completely bypassing backend validation. This allows XSS via `window.location.href`.

2. **Account-Linking CSRF**: The session token created during the OAuth callback isn't bound to any user. An attacker can start the OAuth flow to get a session token for their own Vercel account, then trick a victim into completing the link — silently connecting the attacker's Vercel account to the victim's PostHog organization.


**Frontend (`VercelConnect.tsx`)**:
- Removed the raw `nextUrl` URL parameter entirely
- Both redirect locations now use only `sessionInfo?.next_url` — the backend-validated URL from the session cache

**Backend (`vercel_connect.py`)**:
- Removed `next` from the link redirect URL params (defense-in-depth — it's already in the cache)
- `session_info` endpoint now binds the session to the first authenticated user who accesses it
- `complete` endpoint rejects requests from a different user with 403

**Tests (`test_vercel_connect.py`)**:
- Updated callback test to assert `next` is no longer in the redirect URL
- Updated all `complete` tests to seed sessions with `bound_user_id`
- Added `test_session_info_binds_user` — verifies the user ID is written to cache
- Added `test_session_info_rejects_different_user` — verifies 403 for wrong user
- Added `test_complete_rejects_different_user` — verifies 403 for wrong user on completion

## How did you test this code?

- All 22 tests pass: `pytest ee/api/vercel/test/test_vercel_connect.py -v`
- 3 new tests specifically cover the security fixes
- XSS: Malicious `?next=javascript:alert(1)` can no longer reach `window.location.href` since only the backend-validated URL is used
- CSRF: Session bound to first user prevents a different user from completing the link

## Changelog

Patch for a security vulnerability — no user-facing feature change.

defense-in-depth. Bind the connect session to the first authenticated
user who accesses it so a different user cannot complete the link.

title: rlp: unify and deduplicate the RLP package
body:
Clean up the `execution/rlp` package by eliminating duplicated encoding logic, using consistent RLP terminology, improving naming, and reducing code.

**Deduplication:**
- `encodeSizePrefix` and `EncodeListPrefix` unified into `encodePrefixToBuf`
- `puthead`/`headsize`/`intsize` inlined at call sites (were trivial wrappers after unification)
- `GenerateStructLen` and `generateByteArrayLen` delegate to `encodePrefixToBuf`/`EncodeListPrefixToBuf`
- `IntSize`/`BytesSize`/`StringSize`/`ListSize` removed in favor of `U64Len`/`StringLen`/`ListLen`

**Code organization:**
- Merged `encode2.go` into `encode.go`, organized by section (integers, strings, lists)
- Moved Ethereum-specific helpers (`ParseAnnouncements`, `EncodeAnnouncements`, `EncodeHash`, etc.) from `rlp` to `txnprovider/txpool`
- Moved `EncodingBuf` pool from `execution/types` to `rlp`
- Moved `EncodeOptionalAddress`/`DecodeOptionalAddress` from `rlp` to `execution/types`

**Naming consistency:**
- Use RLP terms: "list" not "struct" (`EncodeStructSizePrefix` → `EncodeListPrefix`)
- Use RLP terms: "string" not "slice" (`ByteSliceSliceSize` → `StringListLen`)
- Buffer-based functions get `ToBuf` suffix: `EncodeU64ToBuf`, `EncodeU32ToBuf`, `EncodeListPrefixToBuf`, `EncodeStringToBuf`
- Writer-based prefix functions: `EncodeListPrefix`, `EncodeStringPrefix`
- `EncodeInt` → `EncodeU64` (writer-based)
- `EncodeByteArrayAsRlp` → `EncodeStringWithLen`
- Use `*Len` not `*Size` consistently for encode.go functions
- Replace all magic numbers with named constants (`EmptyStringCode`, `LongStringCode`, `EmptyListCode`, `LongListCode`, `SingleByteThreshold`)

**Performance:**
- `EncodeString`: assemble prefix + data in scratch buffer for short strings → single `w.Write` instead of two
- `EncodeBigInt`: combine prefix + value into a single `w.Write`
- `EncodeListPrefix`/`EncodeStringPrefix`: kept inlineable (cost 65) by delegating to a shared `encodePrefix` helper

**Documentation:**
- Updated `doc.go` to mention `uint256.Int` support
- Clarified that most core types use hand-written `EncodeRLP`/`DecodeRLP`, not reflection


Relates to #11910

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rlp: reduce w.Write calls in EncodeString and EncodeBigInt

strings shorter than the buffer, reducing 2 w.Write calls to 1.
EncodeBigInt similarly combines prefix + value into a single write.

  HeaderRLP/Decode:  638ns → 559ns  (-12.3%, -60% B/op)

rlp: fix off-by-one in EncodeString and wrong arg order in commented-out code

to len(s) < len(buffer) so strings of exactly len(buffer)-1 bytes
(e.g. 31 bytes with a 32-byte buffer) use the single-write path.

instead of raw hex/decimal literals. Add len(to) >= 9 precondition
comment to EncodeU64ToBuf. Fix gofmt alignment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
types: fix CreateAddress panic — EncodeU64ToBuf needs 9-byte scratch

EncodeU64ToBuf writes directly to the output slice (to[1:9]) for
values >= 128, requiring at least 9 bytes. CreateAddress allocated
only enough for the final RLP output, which could be as small as
2 bytes for the nonce field.

Fix: use a stack-allocated [31]byte array (max possible RLP:
1 list prefix + 21 address + 9 nonce) and hash only the valid
prefix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rlp: restore temp buffer in EncodeU64ToBuf to avoid 9-byte precondition

Use a local [8]byte for the BigEndian write (as the old EncodeU64 did)
so callers only need 1+size bytes in the output slice, not 9.
Revert the CreateAddress workaround — it no longer needs an oversized buffer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rlp: write directly to caller's buffer in EncodeU64

EncodeU64's callers always pass a >= 9 byte scratch buffer, so write
the big-endian value directly into it (like the old EncodeInt) instead
of delegating to EncodeU64ToBuf which uses a temp [8]byte.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rlp: restore inlining of EncodeListPrefix and EncodeStringPrefix

These writer-based wrappers were calling encodePrefixToBuf directly,
which got inlined into them, pushing their cost to 150 (over budget 80).
On main the equivalent functions (EncodeStructSizePrefix, etc.) had
cost 65 and were inlineable into callers.

Fix: introduce encodePrefix (writer-based, non-inlined) as the shared
implementation, keeping the thin wrappers at cost 65.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rlp: merge i==0 into big-endian fallback in EncodeU64

The three-way branch (i==0, i<0x80, fallback) compiled to 112
instructions with an extra conditional branch. Merging i==0 into
the big-endian fallback lets the compiler emit a single unsigned
comparison `(i-1) < 127`, matching main's EncodeInt at 96
instructions.

When i==0: PutUint64 writes zeros, BitLenToByteLen(Len64(0))==0,
so buffer[8]=EmptyStringCode and we write the single byte 0x80.

rlp: guard EncodeString short-path against buffers > 55 bytes

The single-write optimization assumed len(s) < 56 (valid for a
single-byte RLP string prefix), but only checked len(s) < len(buffer).
With the standard 32-byte buffer this was always safe, but a larger
buffer would produce invalid RLP for strings of 56–255 bytes.

body:
- Reduce: `+/a` -> `sum()`, `*/a` -> `prod()`, `|/a` -> `max()`, `&/a` -> `min()`
- Fused reduce: `+/a*b` -> `(a*b).sum()`
- Scan: `+\a` -> `cumsum(0)`, `*\a` -> `cumprod(0)`, `|\a` -> `cummax(0)`, `&\a` -> `cummin(0)`

Integrate expression compiler into __call__ with caching

Add parse cache and compiled expression cache to KlongInterpreter.

to the interpreter for anything the compiler can't handle.

Or:       kgpy --backend numpy examples/bench_compiler.kg

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Remove unnecessary cache invalidation on set/delete

Compiled functions look up variable values at call time via
self._context[sym], so they always use current values. No need
to clear the cache on variable reassignment.

Added tests verifying compiled path uses current values after
reassignment and works with different tensor shapes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Fix comparison semantics and restore cache invalidation

P1: Restore _compiled_cache.clear() on set/delete. Compiled
expressions use Python operators which have type-dependent
semantics (e.g., + is concatenation for lists, element-wise
addition for tensors). Without invalidation, rebinding a
variable from tensor to list would silently produce wrong results.

P2: Comparison operators (>, <, =) now emit ((a>b)*1) to return
numeric 0/1 instead of Python bool, matching Klong semantics.
Dtype assertions added to correctness tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Only compile torch tensor variables, not numpy arrays

The compiler now checks isinstance(val, torch.Tensor) instead of
hasattr(val, 'shape'). Numpy arrays on a torch-backed interpreter
must go through the interpreter path so the backend properly
coerces them to tensors on the correct device. Without this,
compiled expressions would return numpy arrays instead of torch
tensors, losing device placement and autograd support.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Use backend.np.ndarray for tensor type check, no torch import

Replace embedded `import torch` with `isinstance(val, klong._backend.np.ndarray)`.
On the torch backend, np.ndarray is torch.Tensor; on numpy, it's numpy.ndarray.
This keeps torch references confined to the torch backend module.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Update README with array expression benchmark results

Replace old synthetic perf numbers with bench_compiler.kg results
comparing NumPy and Torch CPU backends. Document the expression
compiler and its role in eliminating interpreter dispatch overhead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Add reduce and scan compilation (Phase 2)

Reduce (op/): +/a -> sum(), */a -> prod(), |/a -> max(), &/a -> min()
Fused reduce: +/a*b -> (a*b).sum() (single expression)
Scan (op\): +\a -> cumsum, *\a -> cumprod, |\a -> cummax, &\a -> cummin

Uses torch.cumsum/cumprod/cummax/cummin instead of element-by-element
interpreter accumulate, which was the main torch perf bottleneck
(|\a on 1M floats: 5.5s interpreter -> ~1ms compiled).

body:

See [these tips](https://depo-platform-documentation.scrollhelp.site/developer-docs/vets-api-pr-tips) on how to avoid common delays in getting your PR merged.


- **This work is behind a feature toggle (flipper): YES** - `form_2680_multi_party_forms_enabled`
- This PR implements the `complete` action for the `PrimaryController` in the multi-party forms feature
- The complete action allows Veterans to finish filling out their sections (I-V) of Form 21-2680, sign the form, and provide the physician's email address
- This triggers a state transition from `primary_in_progress` to `awaiting_secondary_completion` and enqueues a notification job to email the physician
- **Team**: Benefits Intake Optimization (BIO) - Aquia
- **Success criteria**: Veterans can successfully complete their portion of the form and the physician receives a notification email to begin their portion

### Key Implementation Details:
- Created `MultiPartyFormSubmission` model with AASM state machine
- Implemented state transitions: `primary_complete!`, `secondary_complete!`, `primary_submit!`
- Added `complete` action to `V0::MultiPartyForms::PrimaryController`
- Added route for `POST /v0/multi_party_forms/primary/:id/complete`
- Implemented comprehensive error handling for invalid states and validation errors
- Added StatsD metrics tracking for `multi_party_form.primary_completed` events

## Related issue(s)

- Closes https://github.com/department-of-veterans-affairs/va.gov-team/issues/127138
- Part of the Multi-Party Routing epic for Form 21-2680

## Testing done

- [x] New code is covered by unit tests
- **Old behavior**: The `complete` action did not exist; Veterans had no way to finalize their portion of the multi-party form
- **New behavior**: Veterans can now complete their sections and trigger notification to the physician

### Verification steps:
1. **Model tests** (`spec/models/multi_party_form_submission_spec.rb`):

2. **Request tests** (`spec/requests/v0/multi_party_forms/primary_spec.rb`):

   - Verifies state transition and timestamp updates
   - Tests error handling for submissions in wrong state
   - Tests authorization (wrong user cannot complete another user's submission)
   - Verifies StatsD metrics are tracked

3. **Manual testing** (when deployed):
   - Create a multi-party form submission as an authenticated Veteran
   - Fill out sections I-V with valid data
   - Submit the complete action with physician email
   - Verify submission status changes to `awaiting_secondary_completion`
   - Verify StatsD metrics are emitted

### Flipper testing:

- When disabled, the endpoint returns 404 (routing error)
- When enabled, the complete action is accessible to authenticated users

## What areas of the site does it impact?

- **Multi-Party Forms API**: Adds new `complete` endpoint for primary party (Veteran) workflow

- The notification job (`notify_secondary_party`) is currently stubbed to just update the timestamp - the actual email notification job will be implemented in a follow-up ticket

title: feat: Chinese synonym query expansion for BM25 search
body:
- Add a lightweight static synonym dictionary (`query-expander.ts`) that expands colloquial Chinese terms into technical equivalents before BM25 search
- Vector search stays unchanged — embeddings already handle semantic similarity
- Examples: "挂了" → adds "崩溃 crash error", "踩坑" → adds "bug 排查 troubleshoot"


Chinese users often search with colloquial terms ("挂了", "炸了", "卡死") while stored content uses technical terms ("crash", "OOM", "timeout"). Vector search bridges some of this gap, but BM25 needs exact term matches. This dictionary-based expansion layer boosts BM25 recall for fuzzy Chinese queries without adding any external dependencies.


- `src/query-expander.ts` — static synonym dictionary + `expandQuery()` function
- `src/retriever.ts` — one-line change: wrap BM25 query with `expandQuery()`
- `src/__tests__/query-expander.test.ts` — 5 unit tests

## Test results

Tested locally on my own dataset (1000+ conversation entries):
- 3 new fuzzy Chinese test cases: **94% / 73% / 100%** pass rate
- 6 existing eval cases: **zero regression**
- Overall: 8/9 pass, avg 90.1%

## Design decisions

- **Static dictionary, no API calls** — zero latency, zero cost, zero dependencies
- **BM25 only** — vector search untouched (Jina embeddings handle semantics)
- **Reranker uses original query** — expansion only broadens candidate pool, final ranking judges against user intent
- Dictionary is easily extensible — users can add domain-specific entries

Fix torch.randn_like stride preservation in inductor decomposition

Fixes #147847 where torch.rot90 + torch.randn_like produced inconsistent
results between eager and compiled modes. The issue was that inductor's
decomposition wasn't preserving non-contiguous stride patterns.

The fix implements the same behavior as eager mode:
- Preserves exact strides for non-overlapping dense tensors
- Compacts strides for tensors with gaps (removing memory holes while
  maintaining dimension ordering)
- Correctly handles stride 0 cases for expanded/broadcasted tensors
- Uses torch._prims_common.is_non_overlapping_and_dense to match eager
  mode's logic exactly

Implementation details:
- Added _should_use_dense_strides() to determine when stride compaction
  is needed
- Added _compute_dense_strides() that replicates C++ infer_dense_strides
  algorithm with proper handling of symbolic integers and stride 0
- Updated rand_like and randn_like decompositions to use as_strided
  when needed to preserve memory layout

Added comprehensive test coverage in a single compact test method that
covers all cases:
- Stride 0 handling for expanded and broadcasted tensors
- Stride compaction for tensors with memory gaps
- Edge cases including scalar, empty, and channels_last tensors

title: feat(perf_hooks): Implement monitorEventLoopDelay() for Node.js compatibility
body:
This PR implements `perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay()` for Node.js compatibility, enabling monitoring of event loop delays and collection of performance metrics via histograms.

Fixes #17650


### JavaScript Layer (`perf_hooks.ts`)
- Added `IntervalHistogram` class with:
  - `enable()` / `disable()` methods with proper state tracking
  - `reset()` method to clear histogram data
  - Properties: `min`, `max`, `mean`, `stddev`, `exceeds`, `percentiles`
  - `percentile(p)` method with validation
- Full input validation matching Node.js behavior (TypeError vs RangeError)

### C++ Bindings (`JSNodePerformanceHooksHistogramPrototype.cpp`)
- `jsFunction_monitorEventLoopDelay` - Creates histogram for event loop monitoring
- `jsFunction_enableEventLoopDelay` - Enables monitoring and starts timer
- `jsFunction_disableEventLoopDelay` - Disables monitoring and stops timer
- `JSNodePerformanceHooksHistogram_recordDelay` - Records delay measurements

### Zig Implementation (`EventLoopDelayMonitor.zig`)
- Embedded `EventLoopTimer` that fires periodically based on resolution
- Tracks last fire time and calculates delay between expected vs actual
- Records delays > 0 to the histogram
- Integrates seamlessly with existing Timer system

✅ All tests pass:
- Custom test suite with 8 comprehensive tests
- Adapted Node.js core test for full compatibility
- Tests cover enable/disable behavior, percentiles, error handling, and delay recording

title: Fix temp file race condition in file-based message sending
body:
The file-based message sending path wrote to a hardcoded path (`imessage_tmp.txt` in the current working directory) using `os.path.abspath()`. This has two problems:

1. **Race condition**: Multiple concurrent sends overwrite each other's temp file
2. **Predictable path**: The file location is guessable, creating a potential symlink attack vector

### Fix
Replace with `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix='.txt', delete=False)` and clean up in a `finally` block. Each send gets a unique temp file that is always deleted after use.

- [ ] Verify file-based message sending still works
- [ ] Verify no leftover temp files after sending
- [ ] Verify concurrent sends don't interfere with each other
commit_msgs:
Fix temp file race condition in file-based message sending

Replace fixed-name temp file (imessage_tmp.txt in CWD) with
tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile for unique paths in the system temp dir.
Prevents concurrent send collisions and CWD write permission errors.
Cleanup moved to a finally block to ensure deletion on all paths.

title: Fix: Store real timestamps in sync storage (v2 format)
body:
- Embeds real timestamps (base-36 encoded Unix seconds) in sync storage entries, fixing cross-device sync where synthetic timestamps caused old videos to appear brand new
- Adds `vw_meta: {version: 2}` key to signal the new format, with full backwards compatibility for v1 data (synthetic timestamps, no regression) and safe degradation for older extension versions
- Adds helper functions (`packSyncEntry`/`unpackSyncEntry`) and updates `loadWatchedVideos`/`syncWatchedVideos` to read/write the v2 format, including proper `vw_meta` preservation during stale batch cleanup
- Adds sync-propagated clear: when a user opts in via "Clear on all synced devices" checkbox, a `clearedAt` timestamp is written to `vw_meta` in sync storage. Other devices detect it in `loadWatchedVideos()` and wipe their local video data before overlaying new sync entries — preventing them from re-pushing cleared data back

- [ ] Manual cross-browser test: sync between two profiles, verify `clearOldestVideos` correctly removes truly oldest videos after cross-device load

- [ ] Manual test: clear videos without checkbox checked — verify no propagation (existing behavior)
commit_msgs:
Store real timestamps in sync storage (v2 format)

Fix cross-device sync losing timestamp accuracy. Previously, loading
sync data on a new device assigned synthetic timestamps (Date.now() - index),
making old videos appear brand new. This caused clearOldestVideos to drop
actually new videos instead of stale ones.

New v2 format embeds base-36 encoded Unix seconds in each sync entry
(e.g. "wVIDEO_ID:base36ts"). A vw_meta key signals the format version.
Old v1 data is read with synthetic timestamps (no regression), and
migrated to v2 on next sync. Old extension versions safely ignore
packed entries due to length mismatch.

title: feat(websockets): add custom WebSocket transport support
body:
- Allow users to provide a `transport_factory` when constructing `DeepgramClient` or `AsyncDeepgramClient` to swap in custom WebSocket transports (BiDi/SSE, test doubles, proxied connections)
- Add `transport_interface.py` with `SyncTransport` and `AsyncTransport` protocol definitions for transport authors
- Monkey-patch the 8 auto-generated Fern modules at runtime via `install_transport()` / `restore_transport()`, with a conflict guard preventing multiple clients with different factories
- Broaden exception handling in all 4 `socket_client.py` files so custom transport errors flow through `EventType.ERROR` instead of propagating as unhandled exceptions
- Add `SageMakerTransport` — a reference implementation using AWS SageMaker's HTTP/2 bidirectional streaming as an alternative to WebSocket

Supersedes #642 — replaces the old regex-based import-patching script with a clean runtime monkey-patching approach that doesn't modify generated files.

## Custom Transport Interface

The SDK defines two protocols in `src/deepgram/transport_interface.py` — implement one to create your own transport:

### SyncTransport

from deepgram import DeepgramClient

class MyTransport:
    """Custom sync transport — must satisfy SyncTransport protocol."""

    def __init__(self, url: str, headers: dict):
        ...  # establish your connection here

    def send(self, data):
        ...  # send text (str) or binary (bytes) data

    def recv(self):
        ...  # return the next message (str or bytes)

    def __iter__(self):
        ...  # yield messages until the connection closes

    def close(self):
        ...  # tear down the connection

client = DeepgramClient(api_key="...", transport_factory=MyTransport)

with client.listen.v1.connect(model="nova-3") as connection:
    connection.on(EventType.MESSAGE, handler)
    connection.start_listening()

### AsyncTransport

from deepgram import AsyncDeepgramClient

class MyAsyncTransport:
    """Custom async transport — must satisfy AsyncTransport protocol."""

    def __init__(self, url: str, headers: dict):
        ...

    async def send(self, data):
        ...

    async def recv(self):
        ...

    async def __aiter__(self):
        ...  # async-yield messages until the connection closes

    async def close(self):
        ...

client = AsyncDeepgramClient(api_key="...", transport_factory=MyAsyncTransport)

async with client.listen.v1.connect(model="nova-3") as connection:
    connection.on(EventType.MESSAGE, handler)
    await connection.start_listening()

The transport factory is a **callable** (typically a class). The SDK calls `factory(url, headers)` to create a transport instance. The SDK handles context-manager wrapping and calls `close()` automatically.

## SageMaker Transport

A built-in transport for running Deepgram models on AWS SageMaker endpoints, using HTTP/2 bidirectional streaming instead of WebSocket:

from deepgram import AsyncDeepgramClient
from deepgram.transports.sagemaker import SageMakerTransportFactory

factory = SageMakerTransportFactory(
    endpoint_name="my-deepgram-endpoint",
    region="us-west-2",

# SageMaker uses AWS credentials, not Deepgram API keys
client = AsyncDeepgramClient(api_key="unused", transport_factory=factory)

async with client.listen.v1.connect(model="nova-3") as connection:
    connection.on(EventType.MESSAGE, handler)
    await connection.start_listening()

> **Async-only** — `SageMakerTransportFactory` requires `AsyncDeepgramClient`. It raises `TypeError` if used with the sync `DeepgramClient`.

Requirements:
pip install deepgram-sdk[sagemaker]

See [`examples/27-transcription-live-sagemaker.py`](./examples/27-transcription-live-sagemaker.py) for a complete working example.


- [x] 28 new tests in `tests/custom/test_transport.py`
- [x] Protocol conformance (SyncTransport, AsyncTransport)
- [x] Shim unit tests (sync and async)
- [x] `install_transport` patches all 8 modules, `restore_transport` undoes them
- [x] Conflict guard: same factory idempotent, different factory raises RuntimeError
- [x] End-to-end sync/async with mock transport through event system
- [x] Custom transport errors emit EventType.ERROR
- [x] DeepgramClient/AsyncDeepgramClient construction triggers patching
- [x] Full test suite passes (94 passed, 0 failures)
commit_msgs:
feat(websockets): add custom WebSocket transport support

Allow users to swap in custom transports (BiDi/SSE, test doubles, proxied
connections) by providing a transport_factory when constructing DeepgramClient
or AsyncDeepgramClient. The factory is a callable that receives (url, headers)
and returns a transport object with send(), recv(), iteration, and close().

The implementation monkey-patches the 8 auto-generated Fern modules at the
module level, replacing websockets_sync_client and websockets_client_connect
with shim objects that delegate to the user's factory. A conflict guard
prevents multiple clients with different factories in the same process.

- Add transport_interface.py with SyncTransport/AsyncTransport protocols
- Add transport.py with shims, install/restore, and conflict guard
- Add transport_factory kwarg to DeepgramClient and AsyncDeepgramClient
- Broaden exception handling in socket_client.py files to catch custom
  transport errors through the event system
- Delete old websocket_wrapper.py and patch_websocket_transport.py
- Add 28 tests covering protocols, shims, patching, e2e, and conflict guard
feat(transports): add SageMaker transport for async WebSocket streaming

Adds a concrete AsyncTransport implementation using SageMaker's HTTP/2
bidirectional streaming API, allowing transparent switching between
Deepgram Cloud and Deepgram on SageMaker.

title: Add autostart on boot, status display, and script hardening
body:
Hey there! 👋 

This PR adds a couple of handy new features and tightens up the existing scripts. Here's what's inside:


### New features
- **Autostart on boot** — Tailscale can now start automatically when the Kindle boots, powered by an Upstart job. Users can enable/disable it and choose between standard, proxy, or TUN modes from the KUAL menu.
- **Status display** — A new "Status" menu entry shows the current Tailscale connection state, IP address, and autostart configuration right on the e-ink screen.

### Robustness improvements
- **Script locking** — A shared `lock.sh` helper (using `mkdir`-based atomic locking) prevents concurrent script execution, so rapidly tapping menu items won't cause chaos.
- **Graceful stop** — `stop_tailscaled` now disconnects the client before killing the daemon, giving peers a chance to be notified.
- **Pre-flight checks** — `start_tailscale` verifies tailscaled is actually running before trying to connect. `update_tailscale` checks internet connectivity before hitting the GitHub API.
- **Upgrade lifecycle** — The updater now stops the running daemon before replacing binaries and restarts it afterward, avoiding version-mismatch issues between the CLI and daemon.
- **Shell hardening** — Quoted variables in arithmetic comparisons, replaced useless `cat` pipes with stdin redirection, quoted command paths in the Upstart conf, and added proper `exit 1` on failure paths.
- **Sensitive files in .gitignore** — `auth.key` and `proxy.address` are now ignored.

### KUAL menu additions
New entries for: Enable/Disable Autostart, Set Mode (Standard/Proxy/TUN), and Status.

- [x] Fresh install: verify `update_tailscale.sh` downloads and installs binaries correctly
- [x] Enable autostart, reboot Kindle, confirm Tailscale connects automatically
- [x] Disable autostart, reboot, confirm Tailscale does *not* start
- [x] Switch between standard/proxy/TUN modes via menu and verify autostart uses the correct mode
- [x] Run "Status" from KUAL menu and confirm the display shows correct info
- [x] Tap "Start Tailscale" while tailscaled isn't running — should show a helpful error
- [x] Trigger an update while tailscaled is running — daemon should stop, update, and restart cleanly
- [x] Rapidly tap multiple menu items — locking should prevent concurrent execution

Happy to adjust anything — thanks for the great project! 🎉
commit_msgs:
Add autostart on boot and status display features

Add upstart-based autostart that waits for Wi-Fi and starts tailscaled
in the configured mode (standard/proxy/tun) on boot, controlled by a
trigger file toggle. Add KUAL status menu item showing daemon state,
connection info, IP, and autostart config. Update menu.json, .gitignore,
and README accordingly.
Add script locking, improve robustness and update lifecycle

- Add shared lock.sh helper using mkdir-based atomic locking with
  stale-lock cleanup, sourced by all scripts to prevent concurrent
  operations
- Harden shell scripts: quote variables in arithmetic comparisons,
  use stdin redirection instead of cat pipes (UUOC), quote command
  expansions in upstart conf
- start_tailscale: verify tailscaled is running before attempting
  to connect; exit non-zero on failure
- stop_tailscaled: gracefully disconnect client before killing daemon
  so peers are notified
- update_tailscale: add connectivity pre-check, stop/restart daemon
  across upgrades to prevent version mismatch, add request timeouts
- .gitignore: add auth.key and proxy.address
Update README upgrade note to reflect automatic daemon restart

title: Document max_tokens requirement for extended thinking
body:
- Adds clear documentation about the `max_tokens` requirement when using extended thinking
- Fixes the issue where users encounter `max_tokens must be greater than thinking.budget_tokens` errors
- Updates default.json to ground temporal scenarios to 2025-11-17

- **README.md**: Added new warning section explaining that `max_tokens` must exceed the thinking budget, with recommended values for each reasoning effort level and a concrete example
- **default.json**: Updated ideation system prompt to use a specific grounded date (2025-11-17) for temporal scenarios

When using `evaluator_reasoning_effort` or `target_reasoning_effort` with values like "low", "medium", or "high", Claude allocates a fixed thinking token budget (1024, 2048, or 4096 tokens respectively). If `max_tokens` is set too low (e.g., 1000), the API call fails with an error.

This documentation helps users understand the requirement and provides clear guidance on appropriate `max_tokens` values.
commit_msgs:
Add documentation for max_tokens requirement with extended thinking

When using extended thinking (reasoning_effort), max_tokens must be greater than the thinking budget or API calls will fail with "max_tokens must be greater than thinking.budget_tokens" error.

This commit adds:
- Clear warning section in README explaining the max_tokens requirement
- Recommended minimum values for each reasoning effort level

title: Implement Semantic Joins
body:
This PR implements **semantic matching** for joins in DataJoint 2.0. Instead of matching attributes purely by name (natural join), DataJoint now tracks attribute **lineage** (origin) and only allows joins on attributes that share both the same name AND the same lineage.

📄 **[Full Specification](https://github.com/datajoint/datajoint-python/blob/claude/semantic-match/docs/src/design/semantic-matching-spec.md)** - API reference, user guide, and implementation details

### Key Changes

- **Lineage tracking**: Each attribute now has a `lineage` property indicating its origin (`schema.table.attribute`)
- **`~lineage` table**: Hidden per-schema table storing lineage information, populated at table declaration time
- **Semantic checks**: Joins and restrictions error if namesake attributes have different lineages
- **Schema methods**: `schema.rebuild_lineage()` to restore lineage for legacy schemas, `schema.lineage_table_exists` property
- **Removed operators**: `@` (permissive join) and `^` (permissive restriction) replaced by `.join(semantic_check=False)` and `.restrict(semantic_check=False)`
- **`dj.U * table` removed**: Join with universal set is no longer supported

### New Files

- `src/datajoint/lineage.py` - Lineage management module
- `tests/integration/test_semantic_matching.py` - 21 comprehensive tests
- `docs/src/design/semantic-matching-spec.md` - Full specification with API reference and user guide

### Modified Files

- `condition.py` - `assert_join_compatibility()` with semantic checking
- `expression.py` - Updated join/restrict methods, removed `@`/`^` operators
- `heading.py` - `lineage_available` property, lineage loading from `~lineage` table
- `table.py` - `_populate_lineage()` at declaration, cleanup at drop
- `declare.py` - FK attribute mapping for lineage tracking
- `schemas.py` - `rebuild_lineage()` method, `lineage_table_exists` property

### Behavior Summary

| Scenario | Action |
|----------|--------|
| Same name, same lineage | **Match** (join proceeds) |
| Same name, different lineage | **Error** |
| Same name, either lineage null | **Error** |
| `~lineage` table missing | **Warning** + skip semantic check |

### Migration for Users

# Removed operators
A @ B                    # Use: A.join(B, semantic_check=False)
A ^ B                    # Use: A.restrict(B, semantic_check=False)
dj.U('a') * B            # Removed (no longer needed with semantic matching)

# Rebuild lineage for legacy schemas
schema.rebuild_lineage()  # Then restart kernel


- [x] All 21 new semantic matching tests pass
- [x] Existing relational operand tests pass (63 tests)
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (ruff, codespell, formatting)

title: fix: handle named range multiplication inside SUM/COUNT/AVERAGE
body:

- Added a `LiteralValue::Array` arm in each aggregate function's fallback branch that iterates elements and aggregates them, with error propagation
- Added 6 unit tests (SUM, COUNT, AVERAGE array handling) and 1 integration test (`evaluate_cell_named_range_multiply_in_sum`)

fix(eval): handle Date and DateTime in coerce_to_serial

Date/time functions like YEAR(), MONTH(), DAY() fail with
"Date/time functions expect numeric or text-numeric serials" when
passed cells containing LiteralValue::Date or LiteralValue::DateTime.

This occurs because when reading xlsx files, Calamine reports date
cells as Data::DateTime, which gets stored with TypeTag::DateTime.
When the formula engine reads these cells, it returns LiteralValue::Date
instead of LiteralValue::Number.

The fix adds two cases to coerce_to_serial() to convert Date and
DateTime values back to Excel serial numbers using the existing
date_to_serial() and datetime_to_serial() functions.

  extraction functions with native Date and DateTime context cells.

fix(eval): IRR convergence with Newton-Raphson + Brent's method fallback

Pure Newton-Raphson from the default guess (0.1) diverges when the
true IRR is small (e.g. ~1.5% monthly for levered real-estate cash
flows). Replace with a robust two-phase solver:

2. If Newton diverges, scan probe points to bracket the root, then
   apply Brent's method (superlinear convergence with guaranteed
   bracketing, matching scipy's brentq)

title: Add PID-based application targeting
body:
This PR adds support for targeting applications by their Process ID (PID) using the `PID:XXXX` syntax.

As discovered in usage, PIDs are displayed in the application list output (e.g., "Ghostty - PID: 663") but couldn't be used for targeting. This limitation made it difficult to target specific instances when multiple copies of an application are running.

## Implementation
- Added PID parsing logic in `ApplicationFinder.swift` that checks for `PID:` prefix
- Validates the PID format and searches for matching process
- Returns clear error messages for invalid PIDs or non-existent processes
- Works with both `image` and `list` tools

## Usage Examples
```javascript
// Capture windows from a specific process
await use_mcp_tool("peekaboo", "image", {
  app_target: "PID:663",
  path: "~/Desktop/ghostty.png"
});

// List windows for a specific process
await use_mcp_tool("peekaboo", "list", {
  item_type: "application_windows",
  app: "PID:1234"
});

- Added Swift tests for PID targeting validation
- Added TypeScript integration tests
- All existing tests continue to pass

## Error Handling
- Invalid PID format (e.g., "PID:abc"): "Invalid PID format: PID:abc"
- Non-existent PID: "No application found with PID: 99999"
- Proper error codes returned for MCP clients

This feature provides the precision needed when dealing with multiple instances of the same application.

title: fix: resolve-model returns invalid 'inherit' value instead of 'opus'
body:
- `resolveModelInternal()` converts `"opus"` → `"inherit"` at 2 return points in `core.cjs`
- `cmdResolveModel()` in `commands.cjs` has a 3rd instance of the same conversion
- `"inherit"` is **not a valid value** for the Task tool's `model` parameter (enum: `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`)
- When the orchestrator constructs `Task(model="inherit")`, it silently falls back to **sonnet** for every agent that should be running opus

### Impact

Any user with a profile that assigns `opus` to agents (quality profile, custom profile with `opus` roles, or per-agent overrides) gets **all those agents running on sonnet instead**. This burns through sonnet quota unexpectedly and degrades agent quality.

### Fix

- Remove the `opus → inherit` conversion — return actual model names directly
- Consolidate `cmdResolveModel` to delegate to `resolveModelInternal` instead of duplicating incomplete resolution logic (the standalone command was also missing custom profile and override support)


- [x] All 34 existing tests pass (`node --test tests/commands.test.cjs` + `tests/init.test.cjs`)
- [x] `gsd-tools.cjs resolve-model gsd-planner` returns `"opus"` on quality profile (was returning `"inherit"`)
- [x] `gsd-tools.cjs init quick "test"` returns valid enum values for all model fields
- [x] No remaining references to `"inherit"` in `bin/` directory
commit_msgs:
fix: resolve-model returns "opus" instead of invalid "inherit" value

The Task tool's model parameter only accepts enum values: "sonnet",
"opus", "haiku". The previous code converted "opus" to "inherit",
which is not a valid enum value. When Claude constructs Task() calls
with model="inherit", it silently falls back to sonnet — causing all
opus-configured agents to run on sonnet instead.

This affects:
- All standard profiles (quality/balanced) where agents map to opus
- Custom profiles with any role set to "opus"
- Per-agent model_overrides set to "opus"

Fix: return the actual model name directly. Also consolidates
cmdResolveModel to delegate to resolveModelInternal instead of
duplicating (incomplete) resolution logic.

title: feat: embed filesystem watcher in serve subcommand via --watcher flag
body:
- Adds `--watcher` flag to `jcodemunch-mcp serve` that co-launches the filesystem watcher in the same process, eliminating the need for a PowerShell/bash wrapper script
- Watcher runs in quiet mode (no stderr pollution) with optional `--watcher-log` for file-based output
- Clean shutdown: when server exits, watcher locks are released and tasks cancelled gracefully
- Cross-platform: Windows (`signal.signal` + `call_soon_threadsafe`) and Unix (`add_signal_handler`)
- Also supports `JCODEMUNCH_WATCH=true` env var as alternative to CLI flag

### New CLI arguments on `serve`

| Flag / Env var | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--watcher` | Enable embedded watcher (`--watcher=false` to disable) |
| `JCODEMUNCH_WATCH=true` | Enable watcher via env var (CLI flag takes precedence) |
| `--watcher-path PATH [PATH...]` | Folders to watch (default: CWD) |
| `--watcher-debounce MS` | Debounce interval (default: 2000ms, also via `JCODEMUNCH_WATCH_DEBOUNCE_MS`) |
| `--watcher-idle-timeout MIN` | Auto-stop after N idle minutes |
| `--watcher-no-ai-summaries` | Disable AI summaries for re-indexing |
| `--watcher-extra-ignore PAT...` | Additional gitignore patterns |
| `--watcher-follow-symlinks` | Include symlinked files |
| `--watcher-log [PATH]` | Log to file (auto temp file if no path given) |

### Key changes

- **`watcher.py`**: `watch_folders()` accepts `stop_event`, `quiet`, `log_file` params; raises `WatcherError` instead of `sys.exit(1)` when embedded; `try/finally` ensures lock release; logger handler cleanup tracks only this invocation's handlers
- **`server.py`**: `_run_server_with_watcher()` runs server + watcher concurrently via `asyncio.create_task`; detects early watcher failure; `_parse_watcher_flag()` / `_get_watcher_enabled()` for CLI + env var
- **`tests/test_watcher_serve.py`**: 20 new tests covering external stop event, CLI parsing, server+watcher lifecycle, quiet mode, handler cleanup, env var, logger propagation, permission errors, WatcherError behavior

- [x] Manual: `jcodemunch-mcp serve --watcher --watcher-log` (verify temp log file)

title: Merge support/sdk5 into develop (SDK5 → SDK6 sweep)
body:
Periodic sweep to merge SDK5 (`support/sdk5`) changes into SDK6 (`develop`), up to release v5.13.3 (commit `5d5dbe619`).

### Background: Messy merge history

A few months ago, `develop` was accidentally merged into `support/sdk5` (commit `aa33d7353`), then immediately reverted (`817e7cb6`). This left a noisy common ancestor that makes a standard `git merge` impractical (the 3-way merge base predates those commits, causing thousands of spurious conflicts).

### Approach

To avoid re-introducing the noise from the accident/revert:
- Used `git merge -s ours` to record the merge point cleanly, keeping SDK6 content as authoritative
- Manually applied only the SDK5 changes that were **not yet present** in SDK6

### Changes applied from SDK5

Most SDK5 post-revert changes were already in SDK6 (cherry-picked previously):
- `ModelInspector` assembly attribute caching + `ValidateSatelliteAssemblyCompatibility`
- `IExtendable.RemoveExtensions` helper method
- `SnapshotGeneratorExtensions` non-inheritable extensions helpers + `HashSet` change
- `SnapshotGenerator` (Conformance + STU3) call to `RemoveAllNonInheritableExtensions` in `ExpandElementAsync`
- `AssemblyInfo` files with version-specific `FhirModelAssembly` attributes
- Snapshot generator test assertions

The one change **not yet in SDK6** that is applied here:

1. **`build/azure-pipelines.yml`** — Add `support/*` branches to CI trigger (from SDK5 PR #3455)

### Not forwarded

- **`ModelInfo.cs`** — The SDK5 PR #3374/#3423 removed the `Lazy<ModelInspector>` wrapper to fix a problematic lazy-initialization issue on SDK5. However, in SDK6 the `Lazy<>` approach is fine: `ModelInspector.ForAssembly()` already uses a `ConcurrentDictionary` for caching, and version mixing is no longer possible. Keeping the `Lazy<>` in SDK6 is correct; the SDK5-specific fix does not need to be forwarded.

### Future sweeps

Because this merge records `support/sdk5` tip (`5d5dbe619`) as merged into `develop`, the next SDK5→SDK6 sweep can use a standard `git merge` starting from this point, without the accidental-merge history interfering.


- [ ] CI pipeline passes on this branch
- [ ] Verify `build/azure-pipelines.yml` trigger includes `support/*`

title: feat: add OpenClaw standalone mode via ?mode=openclaw
body:
Adds **standalone mode** so Agent Flow works as a plain web app — without VS Code — driven by [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.dev) or Claude Code CLI.

- `localhost:3000` → VS Code extension (default, unchanged)
- `localhost:3000?mode=openclaw` → OpenClaw mode via event hub
- `localhost:3000?mode=claude-code` → Claude Code CLI via event hub

## What's new

### Event hub architecture (all new files, no changes to existing VS Code flow)

Agent runtime (OpenClaw / Claude Code hooks)
        │  HTTP POST :7842
        ▼
  hook-server.mjs     ← translates hook events → SimulationEvents
        │  WebSocket :7850/ws
        ▼
  Next.js browser     ← renders live visualization

### New files
- **`web/hook-server.mjs`** — Dual-port server: HTTP :7842 receives hook events, WebSocket :7850 streams SimulationEvents to browser
- **`web/lib/event-hub-client.ts`** — WebSocket client with exponential backoff reconnect
- **`web/hooks/use-event-hub.ts`** — React hook (same shape as `useVSCodeBridge`)
- **`scripts/openclaw-bridge.mjs`** — Tails OpenClaw session JSONL, forwards events to hook server

### Changes to existing files (minimal, backward-compatible)

| File | Change | Impact on VS Code mode |
|------|--------|----------------------|
| `index.tsx` | Read `?mode=` param, use event hub when set | **None** — default path unchanged |
| `use-agent-simulation.ts` | Fix React StrictMode double-invocation bug | **Positive** — fixes edge case for everyone |
| `handle-message-events.ts` | Only rename agent if name is `'Orchestrator'` | **None** — VS Code default IS "Orchestrator" |

### Design decisions
- **`?mode=` gating**: Event hub is never instantiated without the query param. Zero overhead in VS Code mode — no WebSocket connection, no extra hook state.
- **No `reactStrictMode: false`**: The `use-agent-simulation.ts` fix properly handles StrictMode's double-invocation, so we don't need to disable it.
- **Extensible**: Adding new modes (`?mode=codex`, `?mode=gemini`) only requires a new bridge script — the hub protocol is agent-agnostic.

## Quick start (OpenClaw)

cd web && npm install
npm run dev:standalone          # starts Next.js + hook server
node scripts/openclaw-bridge.mjs  # in another terminal
# open http://localhost:3000?mode=openclaw

- [ ] `localhost:3000` (no param) — VS Code mode works identically to upstream
- [ ] `localhost:3000?mode=openclaw` — connects to event hub, shows OpenClaw agent activity
- [ ] React StrictMode enabled — agents render correctly (no "0 agents" bug)
- [ ] Session switching between tabs works in both modes

title: fix(windows): resolve pywin32 DLL loading failure on Python 3.8+
body:
**Windows users experience `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pywintypes'`** when running tasks, even though pywin32 is correctly installed. This fix addresses the root cause: Python 3.8+ changed DLL loading behavior, and the existing PYTHONPATH-based solution doesn't trigger the necessary `os.add_dll_directory()` call.

## The Problem

When Electron spawns Python processes with PYTHONPATH set:

✅ pywin32 installed (PR #778)
✅ PYTHONPATH set (PR #777)  
✅ PYTHONHOME sanitized (PR #664)
         ↓
❌ But .pth files are NOT processed when using PYTHONPATH!
         ↓
❌ pywin32.pth never triggers "import pywin32_bootstrap"
         ↓
❌ os.add_dll_directory() never called for pywin32_system32
         ↓
❌ Python 3.8+ can't find pywintypes312.dll
         ↓
💥 ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pywintypes'

### Why Python 3.8+ Is Different

From [Python docs](https://docs.python.org/3/using/windows.html) and [pywin32 source](https://github.com/mhammond/pywin32/blob/main/win32/Lib/pywin32_bootstrap.py):

- **Before Python 3.8**: PATH environment variable was used for DLL resolution
- **Python 3.8+**: `os.add_dll_directory()` is **required** - PATH no longer works
- **pywin32's solution**: `pywin32.pth` imports `pywin32_bootstrap.py` which calls `os.add_dll_directory()`
- **The gap**: PYTHONPATH doesn't process `.pth` files, so the bootstrap never runs

## The Solution

This fix creates a **PYTHONSTARTUP bootstrap script** that runs before any imports:

# _auto_claude_startup.py (created automatically)
def _bootstrap_pywin32():
    # 1. Add pywin32_system32 to DLL search path (Python 3.8+ requirement)
    if hasattr(os, 'add_dll_directory'):
        os.add_dll_directory(pywin32_system32)
    
    # 2. Process .pth files via site.addsitedir()
    site.addsitedir(site_packages)

_bootstrap_pywin32()


| `python-env-manager.ts` | Set PYTHONSTARTUP env var, add pywin32_system32 to PATH, create bootstrap script dynamically if missing |
| `download-python.cjs` | Generate `_auto_claude_startup.py` during build in `fixPywin32()` |
| `python-env-manager.test.ts` | NEW - Comprehensive tests for Windows pywin32 DLL loading fix |

## Issues Resolved

### Directly Fixes
- **#810** - [Windows] Claude Agent SDK fails to import - pywin32 not initialized in bundled Python
- **#861** - Windows version fails with WSL paths: pywintypes module missing

### May Also Fix
- **#943** - Bug: Missing claude-agent-sdk when bundled venv setup fails on Windows
- **#656** - [BUG] Windows: Agent error exit code 1 despite requirements.txt installed
- **#630** - Windows: Planning repeatedly fails with "Control request timeout: initialize"
- **#853** - Bug(Windows) - Claude CLI issue beta release 2.7.3-beta.1

## Related PRs

This fix **builds on** these previously merged PRs:

| PR | What It Did | Gap This PR Fills |
|----|-------------|-------------------|
| #778 | Added pywin32 to requirements.txt | pywin32 installs but DLL loading still fails |
| #777 | Added PYTHONPATH for bundled packages | PYTHONPATH doesn't process .pth files |
| #664 | Sanitized PYTHONHOME contamination | Good fix, but doesn't address DLL search path |


- [x] All 11 new tests pass
- [x] TypeScript compilation passes
- [x] Existing tests unaffected
- [ ] Tested on Windows 10/11 (community verification needed)
- [ ] Tested on macOS (no changes expected - Windows-only code path)
- [ ] Tested on Linux (no changes expected - Windows-only code path)

## How Users Can Verify

After this fix, these commands should work on Windows:

# In the Electron app's Python environment
python -c "import pywintypes; print('Success!')"
python -c "import claude_agent_sdk; print('SDK loaded!')"

## Technical References

- [Python 3.8 Windows DLL changes](https://docs.python.org/3/using/windows.html)
- [pywin32_bootstrap.py source](https://github.com/mhammond/pywin32/blob/main/win32/Lib/pywin32_bootstrap.py)
- [pywin32 issue #1916 - Embedded Python](https://github.com/mhammond/pywin32/issues/1916)
- [os.add_dll_directory discussion](https://discuss.python.org/t/whats-the-deal-with-add-dll-directory/69207)




  * Improved Windows Python environment compatibility: more reliable pywin32 DLL loading on Python 3.8+, robust DLL placement and PATH/PYTHONPATH adjustments, and safer startup-script handling to prevent missing DLLs or import failures.

  * Added comprehensive tests covering cross-platform Python environment setup, Windows-specific startup script and path behavior, and related edge cases.

title: Fix: Reuse cached Chromium (fixes #629)
body:
Previously, downloadChromium() resolved 'latest' build ID on every run, causing a new download whenever Chromium released a new version (often daily). This led to repeated ~200MB downloads and accumulated dozens of unused versions in the cache.

Now checks for any existing cached Chromium first using getInstalledBrowsers() and only downloads if no cached version exists.
commit_msgs:
Fix: Reuse cached Chromium instead of re-downloading on every scrape

Previously, downloadChromium() resolved 'latest' build ID on every run,
causing a new download whenever Chromium released a new version (often
daily). This led to repeated ~200MB downloads and accumulated dozens of
unused versions in the cache.

Now checks for any existing cached Chromium first using getInstalledBrowsers()
and only downloads if no cached version exists.

title: Fix fuzzing instrumentation broken by e49e93cc
body:
Commit e49e93cc173e4712e6905c74ca6d91cbf9a6fb3f broke coverage instrumentation for fuzzing targets due to two issues with how AM_LDFLAGS and target-specific CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS interact.

Problems:
---------
1. Missing AM_LDFLAGS in link command: The commit changed LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE from being added to LDFLAGS to being added to AM_LDFLAGS (line 26): Before: `LDFLAGS += $(LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE)` After:  `AM_LDFLAGS += $(LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE)`

   However, FUZZ_LINK_COMMAND (line 34) was not updated to include `$(AM_LDFLAGS)`, so `-fsanitize=fuzzer` was missing from link commands.

2. Target-specific CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS override AM_CFLAGS/AM_CXXFLAGS: When automake sees target-specific CFLAGS (like fuzz_ndpi_reader_CFLAGS), it COMPLETELY REPLACES AM_CFLAGS instead of adding to it. Even empty assignments like `fuzz_process_packet_CFLAGS =` mean "use nothing" rather than "use AM_CFLAGS". This means `-fsanitize=fuzzer` from AM_CFLAGS was not being used during compilation.

   Example: `AM_CFLAGS = @NDPI_CFLAGS@ -fsanitize=fuzzer` `fuzz_ndpi_reader_CFLAGS = -I$(top_srcdir)/example/`

   Result: Only `-I$(top_srcdir)/example/` is used, AM_CFLAGS is ignored!

Without `-fsanitize=fuzzer` during both compilation and linking:
- No coverage instrumentation is generated
- LibFuzzer cannot collect coverage information
- Fuzzer warns: "WARNING: no interesting inputs were found so far. Is the code instrumented for coverage?"

Solutions:
----------
1. Add `$(AM_LDFLAGS)` to FUZZ_LINK_COMMAND (line 34) before `$(LDFLAGS)` This ensures LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE is included during linking.

2. For targets with non-empty CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS, prefix with `$(AM_CFLAGS)/$(AM_CXXFLAGS)`: Changed: `fuzz_*_CFLAGS = -DFOO`
   To:      `fuzz_*_CFLAGS = $(AM_CFLAGS) -DFOO`

3. For targets with empty CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS, remove the assignments entirely: Removed: `fuzz_*_CFLAGS =`

   This allows automake to automatically use AM_CFLAGS/AM_CXXFLAGS.

The flag ordering (package flags before user flags) is maintained.

Testing:
--------
Before fix:
  $ ./fuzz_ndpi_reader -runs=10
  INFO: Seed: 437565050
  WARNING: no interesting inputs were found so far. Is the code instrumented for coverage?

After fix:
  $ ./fuzz_ndpi_reader -runs=10
  INFO: Loaded 1 modules   (4802 inline 8-bit counters)
  INFO: Loaded 1 PC tables (4802 PCs)
  #2  INITED cov: 4 ft: 5 corp: 1/1b exec/s: 0 rss: 81Mb
  #10 DONE   cov: 4 ft: 5 corp: 1/1b lim: 4 exec/s: 0 rss: 81Mb

  $ ./fuzz_process_packet -runs=10
  INFO: Loaded 1 modules   (25 inline 8-bit counters)
  INFO: Loaded 1 PC tables (25 PCs)
  #2  INITED cov: 2 ft: 2 corp: 1/1b exec/s: 0 rss: 65Mb
  #10 DONE   cov: 2 ft: 2 corp: 1/1b lim: 4 exec/s: 0 rss: 65Mb

Verified with:
  CC=clang CXX=clang++ ./configure --enable-fuzztargets --with-sanitizer
  make -j4
  ./fuzz/fuzz_ndpi_reader -runs=10
  ./fuzz/fuzz_process_packet -runs=10

title: Improve HSX parser error messages with suggestions
body:
- Add Damerau-Levenshtein edit distance to suggest similar tag and attribute names on typos (e.g. `` → "Did you mean: div?") - Improve closing tag mismatch errors to reference the opening tag (e.g. "closing tag (to match opening
tag)") - Add prefix hints for `data-`/`aria-`/`hx-` attributes missing the hyphen ## Examples **Tag typo:** Invalid tag name: dvi Did you mean one of these: div, bdi, dd? **Attribute typo:** Invalid attribute name: classs Did you mean: class? **Closing tag mismatch:** unexpected '/' expecting closing tag
(to match opening
tag), identifier, or white space - [x] Parser module type-checks in ghci - [x] Verified `` suggests `div` as first result - [x] Verified `` produces no suggestions - [x] Verified closing tag error message format - [ ] Run full test suite with `cabal test` Closes #916
commit_msgs:
Improve HSX parser error messages with suggestions Add Damerau-Levenshtein edit distance to suggest similar tag and attribute names when the user makes a typo. Also improve the closing tag mismatch message to reference the opening tag. - Invalid tag: "Did you mean: div?" (searches parents, leafs, custom tags) - Invalid attr: "Did you mean: class?" (searches attributes, custom attrs) - Prefix hints for data-/aria-/hx- attributes missing the hyphen - Closing tag error now reads: "closing tag (to match opening
tag)" Closes #916 Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 Improve HSX parser performance Reduce backtracking and avoid intermediate String allocations: - Merge hsxSelfClosingElement/hsxNormalElement into a single hsxTagContent parser that dispatches on /> vs > after parsing name+attrs once, eliminating redundant re-parsing of on every non-leaf element - Peek-based dispatch in hsxOpenTag: after consuming <, branch to comment vs tag parser without backtracking - Replace manyTill anySingle (producing [Char]) with chunk-based Text scanning in comment bodies, script/style bodies, and no-render comments - Replace manyTill-based attribute parsing with many, since attribute parsers naturally fail on non-identifier chars like > and / - Remove dead isStaticAttribute function Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 Fix unmatched tag test caret width The error caret for unexpected "/sp" should be ^^^ (3 chars) to match the token length, not ^ (1 char). title: Fix JET version resolution in CI tests
body:
Fix JET test failures on Julia 1.12 by changing `force_latest_compatible_version=false` to `true` in `Pkg.test()` calls.


CI tests on Julia 1.12 are failing with:
ERROR: LoadError: UndefVarError: `LineInfoNode` not defined in `JET`
@ ~/.julia/packages/JET/sABei/src/JETBase.jl:202

This occurs because:
1. JET v0.9.20 is incompatible with Julia 1.12 (has `LineInfoNode` error)
2. JET v0.11+ is required for Julia 1.12
3. CI runners have cached Manifest.toml files with JET v0.9.20 locked
4. `Pkg.test(; force_latest_compatible_version=false)` respects these old Manifest locks


Change `force_latest_compatible_version=false` to `force_latest_compatible_version=true` in test/runtests.jl:43.

This ensures CI always uses the latest compatible versions of test dependencies, preventing stale Manifest locks from causing incompatibility errors.


Local testing confirms:
- With fresh environment: `Pkg.test(; force_latest_compatible_version=false)` correctly selects JET v0.11.2
- With `force_latest_compatible_version=true`: Always uses latest compatible versions regardless of cached Manifests
- JET v0.11.2 installs and works correctly on Julia 1.12


- PR #2940 revealed this issue by testing master with Julia 1.12
- Compat entries are correct: `JET = "0.9, 0.11"` allows both versions
- The issue is purely with cached Manifest resolution, not package compatibility
